author: coderdan
body:
Fixes cipherstash/stack#708. Stacked on #909 (→ #908 → #907 → #906) — this PR's diff is the last commit only.

## The gap

`encryptedSupabase` derived every column's encryption config by introspecting the database's domain types, so it **always** needed a direct Postgres connection. That ruled out Workers, Edge Functions and the browser — environments where the Supabase client is otherwise perfectly usable — and cost a second, more privileged credential even on Node, where the caller already had an authenticated Supabase client.

**The rule this ships:** *declare your schemas and it runs anywhere; omit them and we discover them for you, which needs a database connection and is therefore Node-only.* That inverts the current design — introspection becomes the Node convenience, declaration becomes the portable path.

## Two mechanisms, and fixing either alone leaves it broken

The issue treats "a Worker or the browser" as one case. It isn't, and the two blockers are independent:

| | Postgres connection | Native binary |
|---|---|---|
| Worker / Edge | fine | **blocks** |
| Node | works, costs a 2nd credential | fine |

**Introspection.** Passing `schemas` skips it entirely — no connection, no `pg`, no `databaseUrl`. The gate is the **database URL, not the absence of `schemas`**: if a URL resolves, introspection still runs and a `schemas`-passing caller still gets the drift check. That is what keeps every existing caller byte-identical (all 551 unit and 44 type tests passed unchanged once I got this right — my first cut gated on `!schemas` and two existing tests caught it immediately), and it makes "pass `databaseUrl` as well" the way to declare types *and* keep verification.

**The native engine.** `src/index.ts:1` was the sole runtime edge dragging `@cipherstash/protect-ffi` **and** `@cipherstash/auth` (both Node-API) into the graph — statically, so they load whether or not you encrypt anything. The new `@cipherstash/stack-supabase/wasm-inline` entry binds the WASM `Encryption` instead; the shared factory moves to `src/create.ts` with the encryption client left open.

The **introspector is injected for the same reason**, and this one is easy to miss: `introspect` reaches `pg` via a dynamic `import('pg')`, and a dynamic import is still *a specifier in the bundle*. Statically importing that module would have put `import("pg")` into the edge build for a bundler to resolve against a dependency the runtime will never have. Injecting keeps it out of the graph — a property assertable on the emitted file rather than hoped for. The edge entry therefore passes `null` and **refuses a `databaseUrl`** rather than ignoring it.

## What declared mode gives up — loudly

* **`select('*')` and bare `select()` are refused.** `allColumns` comes only from introspection, and an unexpanded `*` reaches PostgREST without the `::jsonb` casts. The refusal already existed for `allColumns === null`, so declared mode inherits it.
* **`from()` on an undeclared table throws**, blaming the declaration rather than an introspection pass that never ran.
* **The drift check is absent** — a wrong declared domain surfaces as a `23514` CHECK violation on first write instead of at construction.
* **`queryDomainsRequired` is forced, not detected**, since the EQL version is read by introspection. Forcing is the fail-loud direction.

## A bug found on the way

`buildAndExecuteQuery` had a fallback marked *"shouldn't happen but fallback"* that sent a **raw `*`** to PostgREST when a read was awaited with no `.select()` call — bypassing the refusal `select('*')` has always performed, so every encrypted column came back with no `::jsonb` cast. Reachable today on the introspected path too (`await supabase.from('users').eq(...)`), not just in declared mode. Both spellings of "give me everything" now go through one guard.

Also: `process.env.DATABASE_URL` was read unguarded. On a runtime with no `process` that is a `ReferenceError`, not `undefined` — it would have thrown during construction before declared mode could help. Same defect class as the adapter-kit logger in #799.

## Evidence, not assertion

The design comment notes the Workers claim was only ever backed by an export-map resolve. I did not want to add another unbacked claim, so:

* **`e2e/wasm/supabase-declared.test.ts`** runs the emitted entry under **real Deno**, `ffi: false`, no database anywhere. It proves the module graph loads with no native binding and no `pg`, that construction succeeds from declared schemas alone, and that the refusals fire. It joins the existing credentialed WASM job (which already builds protect-ffi's wasm); the job now builds `stack-supabase` too.
  I ran it locally after building protect-ffi's wasm: the graph loads and reaches the credential check, and the **`databaseUrl`-refusal case is deliberately credential-free** and passes locally — I moved it off `requireEnv` precisely so one real assertion is reproducible outside CI. The credentialed case needs CI's secrets.
* **`__tests__/wasm-entry-edge-safety.test.ts`** scans the *emitted* bundle for specifiers that must not be there (`@cipherstash/stack` root, `protect-ffi`, `auth`, `pg`), strips comments first so prose about those specifiers cannot fail it, and carries a **positive control** asserting the native entry *does* import them — without which a renamed output file would pass everything while proving nothing. Verified to fail: pointing the wasm entry back at the native engine turns 2 of its 4 tests red.

## Scope — what I deliberately did not do

The design called for export **conditions** (`workerd`, `edge-light`, `browser`) on `.`. I shipped only the explicit `./wasm-inline` subpath, matching the precedent `@cipherstash/stack` already sets. Conditions would reintroduce the trap the design itself flags: TypeScript applies none of them, so a bare-specifier edge consumer gets **native types over a wasm runtime** — `databaseUrl` allowed, `.withLockContext()` available, each a runtime throw. An explicit subpath has no such gap. Vercel Edge (#806) and the Workers smoke test (#808) stay open; browser stays unclaimed and is blocked on #804 regardless.

`pg`'s peer range moves `>=8` → `>=8.16.3`, the floor where `pg` works on Cloudflare via `pg-cloudflare`.

## Heads-up for whoever picks up the rest

The issue's design comment says the spec lives at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-supabase-portable-runtime-design.md` and four plans under `docs/superpowers/plans/`, git-excluded and present "only in the working tree of `feat/supabase-portable-runtime`". **That branch no longer exists** — not locally, not on origin, no stash, no worktree, and the spec is not in `docs/superpowers/specs/`. Plan 1 survived as merged code (#799); the written reasoning behind the rest is gone, and the design comment on #708 is now the only record. Worth knowing before anyone goes looking.

## Verification

`@cipherstash/stack-supabase` 551 unit + 44 type tests, `@cipherstash/stack` 1050, `stash` 1334 — all green. Biome clean. Built both entries and confirmed the emitted `dist/wasm-inline.js` imports only `@cipherstash/stack/{wasm-inline,adapter-kit,eql/v3,errors}` — no root, no native, no driver.

author: kvnalb
body:
Closes #39. `--year {2020, 2025}` and a hardcoded ReviewArena read become explicit arguments.

```
--papers PATH          CSV needing only a paper_id column; other columns pass through
--text-dir DIR         repeatable; directories of <paper_id>.txt
--text-parquet-year N  the ReviewArena backend
--run-name TAG         output naming, default the papers-file stem
```

Two text backends behind one `sizes()`/`get()` interface, so the population resolver doesn't know where text comes from.

## Why this is more than an interface tidy-up

I asserted, in this runner's docstring, in #34, in PR #35 and in #38, that 2018 and 2019 have no local full text, and encoded it as `choices=[2020, 2025]`. **It was wrong.** The text is in `data/OpenReview/`, laid out as `fulltext/<paper_id>.txt` across two run directories:

| year | usable | pool | coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 915 | 935 | 97.9% |
| 2019 | 1,402 | 1,419 | 98.8% |
| 2020 | 2,180 | 2,213 | 98.5% |
| **total** | **4,497** | **4,567** | **98.5%** |

Rejects included, median 49,123 chars. That total equals `committee_rating`'s count exactly, so it is the same text the 9-call pipeline consumed.

I got there by globbing for `local_fulltext.json` under `*/papers/*/` — the layout `pipeline_xray.py` documents — finding one file, and never opening the directory that had it. Hardcoding the years turned a bad search into a structural constraint, which is the actual argument for this change.

**Consequence:** the baseline runs on the full primary sample, **4,497 papers across three years, 1,517 accept / 2,980 reject**, not 2,212 papers of 2020. Fig 2's third bar covers the same sample as the council's, so no 2020-only caveat and no restricted comparison. Roughly double the calls previously scoped.

## Two bugs fixed while wiring it

**The prompt's `{year}` now comes from each paper's row.** A mixed-year run was telling the model a 2018 submission was a 2020 one — it changes what the model is asked to judge, and it would have done so silently. Caught in the dry run: paper `rJIN_4lA-` is 2018, its PDF header reads "ICLR 2018", and the prompt said 2020. `demo()` pins it for all three years.

**`build_population` counts what it drops** (70 no text, 0 under the char floor) instead of leaving a short output row count to be explained after the fact.

## Normalization: checked, not assumed

`to_archive_text()` strips markdown heading markers so ReviewArena text matches the archive's shape. The archive `.txt` files carry **zero** such markers, so it is a no-op on them. One code path, and both regimes read the same bytes.

## Verification

- `demo()` stays offline, and now exercises `DirText` and `build_population` against a temp directory, asserting a paper with no text and one under the char floor both drop
- Dry run against the real archive: 4,567 in → 4,497 scoreable, per-year counts as above, prompt year matching the paper
- No API calls made

## Follow-up

Docstrings and issue text asserting "2018 and 2019 have no local full text" still need correcting in #34 and #38.

A two-column showcase was nested inside a two-column act, so three columns of text shared one row and the media panel sat stranded in the leftover space.

The act now introduces itself across the full width (heading left, case right), then hands over to the showcase below with the whole page to work with. Media takes the larger share of that grid, and recessed items sit at 45% rather than 35% so they read as quieter rather than broken.

body: ## What changed Overview and Tracker leaked into the same page again. The hide rules only ran when `data-frame` was phone or tablet, and tablet used `display: contents`, which can ignore `display: none` on children in Safari. **Every frame now:** - **Overview** — Left to spend (desktop compact strip) + calendar. No All / Expenses / Income bar. No Monthly spending. - **Tracker** — filter + Monthly spending. No calendar. ## How to try it - [x] `npm test` - [ ] Phone and desktop: Overview has no spending card; Tracker has no month grid - [ ] Planner and Privacy unchanged ## Notes for reviewers No leftover-math or encryption changes. QC now requires the hides on `html[data-shell]` without a frame prefix.

author: athurg
body:
定时同步取回信头之后，顺手把这批新邮件的正文也拉回来写进缓存，点开直接命中本地，省掉一次网络往返。

## 怎么取

- 只跟着 `history` 带回来的新邮件走，和新邮件通知同一条线：首次全量那几百封走的是回溯拉取，不经过这里——否则加个账号就先下几百封正文，用户还一封都没打算看；
- 每轮上限 10 封、最新的先取。合盖一夜再打开可能一次涌进上百封，那时候取回最可能先点开的那几封就够了；
- 跳过草稿、垃圾邮件、废纸篓；按当前「会话/单封」设置决定缓存键，和界面读的是同一把；单封模式下缓存已有就不重取，会话模式必须重取（新来的那封还不在旧缓存里）；
- 排在同步流程最后：位点、欠账补取、收件箱对账这些关乎邮件会不会丢的事，一件都不等它。取失败就结束本轮，不逐封重试拖长这一轮同步。

## 顺带的整理

正文的「拉取 → 渲染 → 换内联图 → 落缓存」从 `MessageDetailModel` 抽成 `MessageBodyLoader`，界面打开和后台预取共用一条路。写成两处的话，「内联图没换全就不落盘」这类规矩迟早会在两边分家。

`MailCache` 新增 `hasThread`：只问存过没有，不读也不 touch——用 `thread(...)` 去问会把文件使用时间推到此刻，没人打开过的邮件会因为被预取查过而在缓存回收时显得很新。

## 验证

装上新构建后监控活动日志，一次真实的新邮件到达走完了整条路：同步发现新邮件 → batch 取信头 → 紧接着自动发出 `messages/<id>?format=full`（期间无人点开），正文落到 `Cache/<账号>/message/<id>.json`。之后打开这封即为纯本地读取。

author: vansin
body:
来自 #1066 的审计。**盲区在取集，不在判据。**

## 问题

    .github/scripts/check-bun-install-pin.py:69-71（改前）
      def is_dockerfile(path: str) -> bool:
          name = Path(path).name
          return name == "Dockerfile" or name.startswith("Dockerfile.")

前缀式（`Dockerfile.mock`）收，**后缀式（`playwright.Dockerfile`）不收**。实测：

    is_dockerfile 收 **226** 个
    文件名含 "Dockerfile" 的 **233** 个
    🔴 差 **7** 个，全在 `agent-network/tests/docker-e2e/`：
       agent-node.Dockerfile · dashboard.Dockerfile · playwright.Dockerfile
       issue-88 / issue-115 / issue-117 / issue-122.Dockerfile

## 当时没漏掉真问题 —— 这一格我追到底了

用**门自己的** `USES_INSTALLER` 逐个查那 7 个：

    门内 226 个里，用 `bun.sh/install` 的 **38** 个   ← 已知阳性，量具有效
    门外 7 个里，用 `bun.sh/install` 的 **0** 个

⇒ 是「**没人守**」，不是「**已失守**」。
但只要有人往 `agent-network/tests/docker-e2e/playwright.Dockerfile` 里
加一句 `curl bun.sh/install`，这道门**看不见**。

## 改了什么

**① `is_dockerfile` 加一条后缀式**，并把起因写进 docstring（下一个人不必重新考古）。

**② 自测补取集夹具** —— 这是 #1066 里我自己提的要求：
原来的 6 条用例全在喂 `unpinned()`（判据），**没有一条碰 `is_dockerfile()`（取集）**。

    ckname("tests/x/Dockerfile.mock", True)          # 前缀式
    ckname("tests/x/playwright.Dockerfile", True)    # 🔴 后缀式，本次之前漏
    ckname("tests/x/dockerfile-notes.md", False)     # 名字里有 dockerfile 但不是
    ckname("tests/x/README.md", False)

## 见证红 → 见证绿

自测 13/13 **不算数**。把 `is_dockerfile` 改回原样（对真代码变异）：

    FAIL 取集 tests/x/playwright.Dockerfile   [got=False want=True]
    selftest: 12/13 ok        rc=1

**只有后缀式那一条红**，其余 12 条不动 —— 说明新夹具钉的正是这个盲区，没有误伤。
复原后 `13/13  rc=0`，`diff` 确认文件**逐字复原**。

## 基线不动

    scanned 233 tracked Dockerfile(s); 37 still install bun unpinned; baseline lists 37
    no new unpinned bun installer.        rc=0

取集从 226 扩到 233，**没有引入任何新违规**，与「那 7 个都没用 installer」的测量一致。
⇒ **这个 PR 不改任何地板数字**，纯粹是把门的视野补齐。

## 它自己那条空取集守卫我保留了

    :117-119
      if not dockerfiles:
          print("FAIL: 一个 Dockerfile 都没扫到 —— 取集塌了,拒绝通过", file=sys.stderr)
          return 2

防的是「0 命中被读成 0 问题」。和 `check-docs-integrity.py` 的同款写法，是本仓的好范例。

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- The zod schema compiler from #36956 can only be turned on with the `BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_EXPERIMENTAL_ZOD` environment variable. The React Compiler has `bun build --react-compiler` and `Bun.build({ reactCompiler: true })`. The zod compiler needs the same surface.
- #36956 also fell 499 commits behind main. Only `test/bun.lock` conflicted.

### Fix
- Carries the #36956 commits forward (merged onto main, lockfile regenerated) and adds `bun build --zod-compiler` and `Bun.build({ zodCompiler: true })`. The option goes `BundlerOptions.zod_compiler` -> `BundleOptions.zod_compiler` -> `features.zod_transform`, next to the `react_compiler` plumbing.
- The variable still turns the transform on in every transpiler. A build enables it when the option or the variable is set. `--no-bundle` transforms too and imports `__zod` from `bun:wrap`, like every transpile-only helper.
- Five transform fixes from review: string arguments folded by `--minify-syntax` are read whole. A boolean node with checks no longer compiles, so `z.boolean().min(5)` raises zod's own error on the first parse. Macro-remapped zod imports are left to the macro. `__zodState` ignores a state written by another copy of the helper. A literal held by reference never settles a union and never matches an array by identity.
- Verified: `test/bundler/bundler_zod.test.ts` (every case uses the option, plus cases for the JS API, the variable, `--no-bundle` and each fix). Also `zod-transform.test.ts`, `react-compiler.test.ts` and `bun-types.test.ts`.

### Background
- The transform (`src/js_parser/zod.rs`) rewrites `z.object({...})` into `__zod(() => z.object({...}), ir)`. `__zod` (`src/runtime.js`) returns a stand-in whose own `parse` and `safeParse` run a validator compiled from the IR. It builds the real schema from the thunk when a parse fails or anything else on it is used, so errors always come from zod.
- `features.zod_transform` is the parser switch. `ParseTask.rs` sets it for bundles, `transpiler.rs` for the runtime and `--no-bundle`.
- Design notes, measurements and limitations of the transform are in the #36956 description and review thread.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

Rebased onto main at 6d13a3a9bf (8a2564cc86). One conflict: main bumped the runtime transpiler cache to version 26 (the new ModuleInfo wire format) while this PR had also claimed 26. The zod entry is version 27 now, on top of main's 26. `test/bun.lock` was regenerated from main's lockfile with `bun install` in `test/`. No other file needed a manual resolution.

The request came from the core team in chat: add the zod compiler to the bundler the way the React Compiler is added.

Other approaches that were considered for the option:

- Injecting `import "zod/compile"` (zod's own runtime compiler, global mode) in front of every module that imports zod. It is implemented and tested on the branch `farm/782b84e1/zod-compiler`. It compiles every schema with exact parity, but at runtime through `new Function`, and it needs a zod that ships `zod/compile` (4.5 canary as of this writing). It is not part of this PR. It could become a follow-up, for example for schemas this transform leaves alone.
- Making the option replace the environment variable for builds. Kept the variable as an additional switch so `bun run` and `bun build` agree when somebody sets it.

The option is documented in `packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts`, the `bun build --help` text, `docs/snippets/cli/build.mdx` and `completions/bun-cli.json`.

The internal feature keeps the `zod_transform` name from #36956. Only the user-facing option is called the zod compiler, to match `--react-compiler`.

Before the option commit, the merged branch builds on current main and the two #36956 suites pass unchanged (15 tests). With it: `bundler_zod.test.ts` 19 pass, `zod-transform.test.ts` 4 pass, `react-compiler.test.ts` passes, `bun-types.test.ts` 15 pass.

One reviewed divergence is documented rather than changed: `z.enum(arr)` followed by a mutation of `arr` is observed by the compiled schema, where zod copies the array at construction. The schema is built lazily, so a copy in the reference slot only moves the divergence to the fallback path, and bailing would drop the transform from every tree containing `z.enum(SOME_CONST)`. The note is in the header of `src/js_parser/zod.rs`.

The rope bug reproduced with `bun build --zod-compiler --minify-syntax`: `z.literal("a" + "b")` compiled to `"vs":["a"]` and accepted `"a"`, `z.enum(["x" + "y"])` accepted `"x"`, `.startsWith("pre" + "fix")` accepted `"pre-rest"`, and `.default("d" + "ef")` returned `"d"`. The macro remap reproduced with a bunfig `[macros.zod]` table: the build emitted `__zod(() => object(), ...)` and the macro never ran. Each regression test fails on the commit before its fix and passes after it.

</details>

author: jacorbello
body:
## The drift

`internal/api/authz.go` never looked at `Session.EndedAt`. `poker.withSession` and `standup.withSession` both answer `409 {"error":"this session has ended"}` for any write on a closed session — but the two facilitator routes on `/api/sessions/{id}` went straight through.

So on a closed session, `POST /api/sessions/{id}/facilitator` returned 204 and the role moved. `POST .../facilitator/claim` did answer 409, but only by accident of the claim eligibility rule, and with the wrong message.

## The fix

`rejectEnded` is its own middleware rather than part of `requireSessionMember`, so the three deliberate exceptions can opt out: `GET /`, `GET /export.csv` and `POST /reopen` still work on an ended session — reopen exists for nothing else, so it now sits outside the group. Status code and error string are copied verbatim from `internal/poker/routes.go` so all three sites agree.

`DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` also sits outside the `rejectEnded` group, and stays idempotent: closing an already-closed session is still a no-op `204`, enforced in the handler, which skips the write when `EndedAt` is already set. Only transfer and claim answer 409 on an ended session. `requireFacilitator` still guards close and reopen.

Not done here, deliberately: the three duplicated authz ladders are left alone. A `ponytail:` comment on `rejectEnded` records the duplication and the upgrade path — consolidating them is a routing refactor and the wrong diff to mix with a behaviour fix.

## Failing tests first

New `internal/api/authz_test.go`, run before the fix:

```
=== RUN   TestEndedSessionRejectsFacilitatorTransfer
    authz_test.go:37: transfer on ended session: got 204, want 409
--- FAIL: TestEndedSessionRejectsFacilitatorTransfer (0.12s)
=== RUN   TestEndedSessionRejectsFacilitatorClaim
    authz_test.go:54: claim on ended session: got error "the facilitator is still here — the role can be claimed after they have been gone a minute", want "this session has ended"
--- FAIL: TestEndedSessionRejectsFacilitatorClaim (0.14s)
=== RUN   TestEndedSessionStillReadable
--- PASS: TestEndedSessionStillReadable (0.19s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/lets-parley/parley/internal/api	0.460s
```

`TestClosingAnAlreadyClosedSessionIsIdempotent` pins the close path, and failed the same way before its fix:

```
    authz_test.go:104: second close: got 409, want 204 (idempotent); body=map[error:this session has ended]
--- FAIL: TestClosingAnAlreadyClosedSessionIsIdempotent (0.14s)
```

`TestEndedSessionStillReadable` passing before and after is the point: it pins the exceptions so the fix cannot over-reach.

## After

`go test -p 1 -race ./...` fully green; `go vet ./...` clean.

author: devinjameson
body:
## Summary

- keep editable playground previews hidden, inert, and untabbable until their iframe finishes loading
- preserve the same iframe across the loading transition, while keying different preview URLs as different entities
- extend the deployed SSR and SSG smoke tests to verify iframe identity, hydration, accessibility state, and interaction

## Why

The editable WebContainer playgrounds expose server-rendered or statically generated controls before Vite finishes loading and evaluating the cold client dependency graph. In live measurements, controls could remain visibly inert for roughly four to six seconds. Warm reloads and production-built embeds became interactive within tens of milliseconds, so Foldkit hydration is not the long pole.

The parent now keeps an opaque loading panel over the mounted iframe until its native load event. This removes the misleading visible-but-dead interval without adding a flaky timing threshold or claiming that iframe load is a formal hydration protocol.

## Verification

- full repository pre-push gate
- website unit tests: 460 passed
- website typecheck, lint, formatting, and production build
- local live SSR and SSG playground smoke: 2 passed
- mutation check: keying by loading state detached the captured iframe and failed the identity assertion
- mutation check: removing the URL key failed the focused key regressions

author: nrmeyers
body:
UAT cycle 2 bug hunt (AgentAlloy 9.2.1), run through the full SDD lifecycle
(intake → spec → design → plan → build → qa → ship). Four genuine defects fixed,
each with a regression test, plus the README accuracy vehicle and a repo-hygiene
change.

## Fixes

**B4 (+B1) — proxy gate trusted a stale `/proj` token**
`src/agentalloy/api/proxy_context.py`: the proxy-side gate resolved the repo from
the `/proj/<token>` URL discriminator, which goes stale when the session's real
working directory has moved. It now resolves the session's actual `repo_root`
instead. Fixing B4 also resolves B1 (same stale-token root).

**B6 — synchronous rerank calls blocked the shared event loop**
`src/agentalloy/api/proxy_signal.py`: `check_transition_trigger` made up to two
sequential blocking rerank HTTP calls on the event loop while the rest of gate
eval was offloaded. One blocking call froze every repo on the shared proxy
simultaneously. Now offloaded with `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`. (Consistent
with D14: this is blocking socket I/O to a separate process, not the in-process
DuckDB writes D14 keeps inline.)

**B3 — `contract init --body-file` double-emitted frontmatter**
`src/agentalloy/install/subcommands/contract.py`: passing a body file with its own
YAML frontmatter produced double frontmatter and empty structured fields. It now
merges the body frontmatter over the template.

**B2 — code-index 409 misreported as a start failure**
`src/agentalloy/install/code_index_wiring.py`: a 409 (already running) was
surfaced as a failure. Now handled correctly.

## Vehicle + hygiene
- **README.md** (the cycle's target task): refreshed for 9.2.1 — skills badge
  711→355, version badge v9.0.0→v9.2.1, "39 packs"→"41 packs", tier 10→9.
- **Anomaly log untracked**: `docs/uat-bug-hunt-anomalies.md` is UAT scratch and
  should not live in the repo — removed from git tracking and added to `.gitignore`
  (local copy kept).

## Tests
Each fix carries a regression test: `tests/proxy/test_proxy_context.py`,
`tests/proxy/test_proxy_signal.py` (incl. `TestTransitionTriggerOffEventLoop`),
`tests/contracts/test_contract_init_scaffold.py`,
`tests/install/wiring/test_code_index_wiring.py`. Full suite green (the 2
`test_upgrade.py` failures are environmental — `uv`/`agentalloy` not on host PATH —
and pass with a PATH shim).

body:
## What

Eleven specs still built the visitor subject by hand — writing a
`grappa-subject` envelope into `localStorage` with `nick` and
`network_slug` fields the server had already stopped sending. They are
now absorbed onto the verbs that already exist in
`cicchetto/e2e/fixtures/cicchettoPage.ts`: **no new API, no new field**.

- Nine take `bootVisitorContext(browser, seed)`.
- `issue375` and `issue557` take `bootVisitor(page, seed)` instead,
  because they attach a `websocket` listener *before* the boot
  navigates — the context-level verb would navigate too early for them.

**11 files, +76/-211.** Residual `nick`/`network_slug` inside a
`kind: "visitor"` literal under `e2e/tests`: **0 files, 0 fields**
(counted by grouping per literal BODY, not per file — a per-file count
gave the wrong number twice, because `issue282` has a clean subject and
an unrelated `nick:` in a vhost-view stub).

Stacked on #1545, which introduced the shared verb; that has landed, so
this branch now sits directly on `main` with its own two commits.

## Evidence

Bench for every runtime number below: worktree `w1-1397-bv`, sitting
exactly on the base commit. Bench restored afterwards (clean tree).

- **Baseline** (base commit, the eleven specs): rc=0, **16 passed**.
- **Treatment** (this branch): rc=0, **16 passed, same 16 titles**
  (compared after stripping `file:line`, which necessarily moves).
- **Positive control, runtime**: flipping `registered: false` → `true`
  on the ephemeral seed of `issue126` gives rc=1 and **exactly 1 red
  out of 16** — and it is `detach-btn toHaveCount(0)` failing with
  `Expected: 0 / Received: 1`. So the seed shape is load-bearing and
  the suite can see it.
- **Positive control, static**: re-adding `nick` at a new call site
  yields **exactly one** `TS2353 … 'nick' does not exist in type
  'VisitorSeed'`.
- `scripts/bun.sh run check` rc=0 over the **whole** chain (biome && tsc
  && tsc -p e2e/tsconfig.json), 0 `error TS`, 59 CSS warnings unchanged.
- `scripts/design-notes-gate.sh` rc=0; DN marker `#1397-e2e-visitorseed`
  is unique (`grep -Fxc` = 1) and the boundary shape on the file is
  marker / blank / `---` / blank / heading, with no blank before the
  marker.

## What I decline to claim

- **I do not claim the full integration suite is green.** It was never
  run for this branch; only the eleven specs were.
- **I do not claim the type is the guarantee.** TypeScript's
  excess-property check fires on *literals* only — a caller passing a
  variable gets no error. What closes the drift is that the envelope is
  now *constructed* in one place, not that `VisitorSeed` exists.
- **I do not claim a re-run after restoring the mutant.** The evidence
  that the bench is back to the measured state is an empty `git status`
  and an empty `git diff HEAD` on the commit the treatment was measured
  on, not a fresh green run.
- **Pre-existing, not introduced here:** on `webkit-iphone-15` visitor
  contexts are not iPhone-emulated, because `browser.newContext()` does
  not inherit the project's `use` block. Identical before and after this
  change.

<!-- Programmatic LoC summary. Do not edit by hand; rewritten on every commit. -->

| Test | 8 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​522 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​230 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​292 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

Fixes STA-2802 / #11027.

## The report

Several teammates connect desktop clients to one always-on remote Orca server. When one teammate creates and opens a new remote workspace, everyone else's client jumps to it and starts rendering that teammate's live agent session. Field nuance: it is **intermittent** — ordinary navigation between workspaces does not drag anyone.

## Why it was intermittent

Plain navigation was already isolated. `worktree.activate` resolves `navigation: 'caller'` for any paired client (`resolveRuntimeNavigationTarget` keys off `clientKind`), so neither the host renderer nor sibling clients are notified. That is why clients "usually look independent".

`worktree.create` had no such notion. When `args.activate === true` the runtime called `notifyActivateWorktree`, which fanned the `activateWorktree` client event out to **every** subscribed connection via `emitClientEvent`. Every client renderer handles that event by running `activateAndRevealWorktree` — a forced project + workspace switch, sidebar reveal and pane focus.

The renderer only sends `activate: true` on the remote create path when a **startup command** exists, i.e. "new workspace + agent". That is the exact trigger, and it matches the screenshot (an observer watching someone else's Claude Code session).

## The fix

Address create-activation the same way activate already is. `worktree.create` gains an optional `navigation` param, and the RPC layer resolves the target from `clientKind`:

* create over a **paired desktop/web client** (`clientKind: 'runtime'`) → `caller`: no host-renderer navigation, no sibling-client fan-out. The creator already navigates from its own RPC result, which carries `setup` / `startup` / `defaultTabs`, so nothing is lost — and the creator's own "user moved on, keep it in the background" logic is no longer overridden by the echoed event.
* create **in-process or from the CLI** → `all`, unchanged. The CLI now sends `navigation: 'all'` explicitly with `--activate`, because it pairs as a runtime device but has no viewer of its own — without that, `orca worktree create --activate` against a *remote* runtime would have become a silent no-op.
* create from **mobile** → `all`, unchanged, deliberately. A phone has no terminal-provisioning renderer, so for a blank create (no startup command) the host renderer is what runs the repo's `setup` and default tabs off this activation event. Scoping mobile would drop that work; moving it into the runtime is a separate change.
* `navigation: 'clients'` / `'host'` / `'all'` remain expressible for the existing explicit-follow contract.

Shared model state is untouched: `reposChanged`, `worktreesChanged`, terminal side-effects, agent output and lifecycle all still reach every client.

## Rollout: host first

This fix is enforced by the **host**, because the host is the only party that knows who issued the create — on `origin/main` the `activateWorktree` event carries no originator field at all. That has a consequence worth stating plainly in release notes:

* **Old client + new host → fixed.** An observer is protected without updating anything.
* **New client + old host → still broken.** Nothing breaks or hangs; the old host simply keeps its old broadcast behavior.

So **shipping clients alone fixes this for nobody** — the always-on server must be updated. Support triage for "my window still jumps" should check the *host* version, not the client's.

A client-side fallback was considered and rejected: with no originator on the event, a new client cannot distinguish a teammate's create from its own, or from a legitimate `orca worktree create --activate` reveal, so suppressing it would break the CLI reveal this PR deliberately preserves.

## Wire compatibility

Host-side only; no frame shape changes. Under Rule 3 this is "a frame the host stops sending on an existing path":

* **old client + new host** — protected without updating, and its create still self-navigates (that has been renderer-side since #4729, well before the reported 1.4.158).
* **new client + old host** — unchanged old behaviour; the new optional `navigation` param is ignored by an old host (Rule 1).

## Evidence

Baseline `origin/main` 4ec6bbf588.

**Two-client integration** (real `OrcaRuntimeService` + real `OrcaRuntimeRpcServer`, two E2EE-paired devices over WebSockets, real RPC dispatch):

| | observer client B's stream after A creates |
|---|---|
| main / fix reverted | `['worktreesChanged', 'activateWorktree']` ❌ |
| candidate | `['worktreesChanged', 'reposChanged']` ✅ |

The oracle is fence-ordered, not timing-based: a `reposChanged` emitted after the create must be the next frame each client sees, so an interleaved activation frame fails deterministically. It also asserts the host notifier was not called, includes repeated ordinary-navigation negative controls, and covers both the headed-notifier and headless `orca serve` runtime shapes plus the in-process/CLI reveal non-regression.

**Headed Electron E2E** — the desktop app as the remote server with two independently paired web clients in separate partitions:

* candidate: observer stays on its own worktree, and the created workspace still appears in its sidebar ✅
* fix disabled: the observer's `data-rendered-active-worktree-id` resolves to the workspace the other client just created ❌

```
pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts \
  src/main/runtime/multi-client-navigation-isolation.integration.test.ts \
  src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/worktree-create-navigation.test.ts
pnpm run test:e2e:multi-client-navigation
```

Also green: `src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.test.ts` (1183), `src/cli` + `src/main/runtime/rpc` (2321), `typecheck:node`, `oxlint`, `check:reliability-gates`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`.

Registered as reliability gate `runtime.multi-client-view-isolation`.

## Scope

Deliberately not included: host-originated CLI creates still reveal on every client (a headless server's only viewer depends on that); mobile creates keep the all-surface reveal for the provisioning reason above; and no per-client view-state store was introduced — the deterministic evidence points at one broadcast, not at shared global selection state.

`activateWorktree` is the only `RuntimeClientEvent` that can move a viewer — every other member is handled with an early return in the renderer's client-event dispatch, and mobile does not consume the event at all.

**Known gaps:** no live Windows-server run yet (the report's topology); the Electron journey drives the store create action, so the composer's *automatic* self-navigation on create is proved by `worktree-creation-flow.test.ts` and the host-side `worktree.spec.ts` composer journey rather than by this journey.

## Adjacent gaps found in review, deliberately left out

Independent review turned up two more places where a paired caller can still steer the **host** (never a sibling client, and never across worktrees). Both are recorded in the gate's `knownGaps` and are follow-ups rather than part of this fix:

* `terminal.create` receives `clientKind` and drops it, so an explicit `presentation: 'focused'` from a paired connection still activates the host renderer (`rpc/methods/terminal.ts` → `orca-runtime.ts` `activate: presentation === 'focused'`). `terminal.focus` and `agent-session` already downgrade this for paired callers, so the fix is precedented — but the Orca client always sends `presentation: 'background'`, so this is unreachable from the product UI, and closin

## Summary

@bruschill's cleanup from #2321, rebased onto current main. Original commit and authorship preserved; #2321 had gone conflicting after #2326 touched the same file.

Removes the unreachable tvOS map Menu callback path and an unused duplicate Disconnect button. 34 lines, no behaviour change.

## Verification that the path really is dead

Checked on current main before resolving:

- `escapeMap` is only ever *passed* (`onMenuExit: escapeMap`), never called.
- `onMenuExit` is only invoked by `menuPressed`.
- `menuPressed` is attached to **no** gesture recognizer — no `addGestureRecognizer`, no `allowedPressTypes`, no `UIPress` handling anywhere in the file.
- The map is `isUserInteractionEnabled = false` and `canBecomeFocused = false`, so it never holds focus to escape from in the first place.

Menu at the map root continues to be handled by the system (returns to the Home Screen), which is the behaviour #2313 was closed to preserve.

## One thing worth knowing

The conflict was in `escapeMap`, because #2319 had added the empty-map focus fallback (`recenterFocused = true` when no nodes are located) *inside* it. Since `escapeMap` is unreachable, **that accessibility improvement has never executed** — it went in inert. Deleting it here loses nothing that was running, but if that behaviour is still wanted it needs a real trigger, which is a separate change rather than something to preserve in dead code.

## Testing

tvOS scheme builds with no unused-symbol warnings.

author: badrishc
body:
## What
Disable dependency install/postinstall scripts when installing the Docusaurus website dependencies, as supply-chain security hardening.

- `website/.npmrc` → `ignore-scripts=true` (covers `npm` usage / defense in depth)
- `website/.yarnrc` → `ignore-scripts true` (**the effective setting** — Yarn Classic, used by the website and CI, ignores `.npmrc`'s `ignore-scripts` key)

## Why
`postinstall` scripts are a common npm supply-chain attack vector. Skipping them removes that arbitrary-code-execution path during `yarn install`.

> Note: `.npmrc` alone is a no-op under Yarn Classic (verified empirically — lifecycle scripts still ran). `.yarnrc` is required for the hardening to actually take effect for the website build.

## Validation
Matches CI (node 22, `working-directory: website`):
- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` → `warning Ignored scripts due to flag`
- `yarn build` → `[SUCCESS] Generated static files in "build"` (exit 0)

Only `core-js` (funding message) and macOS-only `fsevents` use install scripts in this tree — both safe to skip, so the build is unaffected.

## Behavioral impact
Every `yarn install` (local + CI) now skips dependency lifecycle scripts.

Closes #2077

author: yoshiofthewire
body:
Closes the question `ci.yml` has carried in its matrix comment for several
runs: **the API 36 failures were this job's own keyguard handling, not the app.**

## What was wrong

The job arms a keyguard deliberately — `locksettings set-pin 1234`, because
`EnrollmentVault.ensureKey()` returns false without a secure lock screen — and
then dismissed it with three unverified `input` events. On API 36 they never
landed:

```
mDreamingLockscreen=true
isKeyguardShowing=true
mKeyguardShowing=true
KeyguardShowing=true  DismissalRequested=false  Occluded=false
```

`DismissalRequested=false` means `wm dismiss-keyguard` never even registered. The
PIN was typed into the lock screen wallpaper, and **no Activity can reach RESUMED
behind a keyguard** — which is every one of the 8 failures.

A modern lock screen needs a **swipe** to raise the PIN bouncer. `keyevent 82` did
that job on API 31/34 and does not on 36.

Note the shape of this: the `set-pin` step immediately above carries a comment
saying *"Prove it took, rather than assuming. A silent failure here reads
downstream as a Keystore bug and costs an afternoon."* The step three lines below
it — the one that decides whether any UI test can run at all — was asserted by
nothing, and its silent failure cost rather more than an afternoon.

## The app is exonerated

No `FATAL EXCEPTION`, no ANR, nothing in logcat but normal operation. `ci.yml`'s
other branch — *"a user-facing data-loss bug in the default configuration"* — does
**not** apply. Rotation, fold and process death are fine for Android 16 users.

## Two dead ends, recorded so nobody re-derives them

- **Not "tests that call `Activity.recreate()`."** `FoldLockBehaviourTest.aLiveResizeDoesNotEngageTheAppLock`
  failed at a *plain launch* before recreating anything, and `InboxRailTest` launches
  the same Activity via `ActivityScenario.launch` and passed throughout. The common
  factor was the keyguard.
- **Not a stale `androidx.test`.** `core:1.7.0`, `ext:junit:1.3.0`, `espresso:3.7.0`
  fail identically with the keyguard up. That bump is now separated into #63 on its
  own merits.

## The part I want reviewed most

The wait polls for **two** conditions, not one. A dismissed keyguard is not the same
as a system that will resume activities:

- the run that first went green did so because an unrelated `adb logcat -c` added a
  few hundred milliseconds after the dismissal;
- the run before it — same dismissal, no delay — **failed with the keyguard already
  down**.

So the loop now waits for a resumed activity to exist as well, making that settling
explicit rather than incidental. A fix that works by accident is one refactor away
from silently reverting, which is the same shape as the bug it replaces.

Assertion strictness is deliberate: the keyguard check is **fatal** but fires only on
a *positive* `mKeyguardShowing=true`, so an API level naming the field differently
cannot fail a leg over a diagnostic. The resumed-activity check only warns, for the
same reason.

## API 36 promoted to required

`continue-on-error` is gone. It was advisory only while the failure was unexplained.

⚠️ **Residual risk, stated plainly:** this is verified green **twice on the same
commit**, not across weeks. If 36 flakes after this, the fix is the settle wait and
the answer is to strengthen it — read the keyguard dump the emulator step now prints
before suspecting the app. I would rather this gate and occasionally need attention
than sit advisory and hide the next real regression, but that is a judgement call and
reverting one line puts it back.

logcat is captured around every run, including passing legs: a green leg's log is the
control that makes a red one readable.

author: wwdhogo-sv
body:
승격 심사를 제대로 하려고 준비 상태를 점검하다가 두 가지를 찾아 고쳤습니다.

## ① 봉인 해시가 한 번도 대조되지 않고 있었습니다

`tools/lockbox_audit.py` 는 스스로 세 가지 질문에 답한다고 적어 두었고 그 셋째가 **"디스크의 데이터가 봉인 당시 그대로인가(sha256)"** 입니다.

그런데 대조가 `lockbox_manifest` 키가 있을 때만 돌았습니다. **그 형식을 쓰는 것은 이미 소진된 세 벌뿐**이고, 아직 봉인된 9벌은 자기 매니페스트의 `output.sha256` 에 해시를 적는 형식입니다.

결과 — 감사는 9벌 전부를 `해시미확인` 으로 내보내면서 `--strict` 에서 **정상 종료**했습니다.

> ★위험은 "해시가 틀렸다" 가 아니라 **"틀렸는지 아무도 모른다"** 였습니다.
> 승격 심사에서 "후보가 이 데이터를 본 적 없다" 를 뒷받침하는 물증이 이 해시입니다.

**고친 뒤:**

```
봉인 유지 9건 · 실제로 쓸 수 있는 것 9건 · 해시 검증된 것 9건
불일치 0 · 파일없음 0
```

**봉인 데이터 12벌 전부 봉인 당시 그대로입니다. 변조 없습니다.**

## ② 승격 기준이 네 파일에 흩어져 있었습니다

```
tools/consolidate_formal_validation.py        FRR 3% · 아는 5% · 미지 10%
tools/evaluate_candidate_external_holdout.py  MAX_BOT_ASR 0.05 · MAX_HUMAN_FRR 0.03
tools/aim_lofo.py                             FRR_BUDGET 0.05 · 기준 ≤10%
docs/PROMOTION_STATUS_20260810.md             표에 손으로 적은 값
```

`training/promotion_gate.py` 로 모았습니다.

★**기준을 새로 정하지 않았습니다.** 기존 두 도구가 이미 같은 값을 쓰고 있었고, 그 값을 그대로 옮겼습니다. 기준을 바꾸는 것은 별도의 결정이어야 합니다.

### 핵심 — 재지 않은 항목은 불합격입니다

`None` 을 통과로 처리하면 **"안 재봤다" 가 보고서에 "문제 없다" 로 찍힙니다.** 승격에서 그 방향의 실수는 봇을 들여보낸 뒤에야 드러납니다. 반대 방향은 한 번 더 재면 됩니다.

### 전제조건 둘을 더 겁니다

- **봉인 해시가 대조됐나** — 아니면 점수가 아무리 좋아도 근거가 못 됩니다
- **실사용자 shadow 관측이 최소치를 넘었나** — 오프라인 점수만으로 켜면 실사용자 오탐을 한 번도 안 보고 켜는 셈입니다

### 지금 숫자를 넣어 보면

```
불합격  사람 오탐 (참가자 최악): 3.4% (기준 ≤3%)
합격    아는 봇 통과율: 1.4% (기준 ≤5%)
불합격  미지 계열 통과율 (최악): 41.3% (기준 ≤10%)

판정: ★승격 불가
```

## 시험

새로 9개. 마지막 하나는 **기준 표류 감시**입니다 — 다른 도구의 상수가 갈라지면 거기서 걸립니다. 도구 쪽 기준을 바꾸려면 이 시험도 같이 고쳐야 하고, 그 순간 "기준을 바꾸는 중" 임이 드러납니다.

```
263개 전부 통과
```

## 함께 보시면 좋은 것

`docs/PROMOTION_READINESS_20260818.md` 에 오늘 점검한 내용을 정리했습니다. 실서비스가 `active` 로 돌고 있어 **승격 근거가 될 shadow 관측이 한 건도 안 쌓이고 있었다**는 것도 여기 있습니다. 그 부분은 catchap-infra#66 으로 이미 `shadow` 로 내렸습니다.

author: chuckbuilds
body:
## Summary

Fixes an unattended failure mode on low-memory boards where the Pi becomes
completely unreachable — SSH refuses connections, the panel goes dark — while
still answering pings and serving the web UI, so it looks healthy from outside.
Only a power cycle clears it. Diagnosed on a 1GB Pi 3B+; it reproduced twice,
about 90 minutes after each boot.

## What actually happens

The display process settles near 600MB RSS of 905MB usable. When the remaining
headroom runs out, `fork()` starts failing, and since almost anything needs a
new process, the symptoms do not read as "out of memory":

- `sshd` accepts the TCP connection and closes it before sending its banner (it
  forks a session per connection)
- the web UI keeps answering — already resident, forks nothing
- ping stays at 0% loss — handled in the kernel
- the panel goes dark, and the service cannot be respawned
- `fake-hwclock`'s periodic save stops running, so the clock is wrong after the
  next boot

## Changes

**Service resilience**

- `PluginHealthTracker._load_health_state()` returned the cached value verbatim.
  A non-dict entry makes every caller raise `AttributeError: 'list' object has
  no attribute 'get'` during `DisplayController.__init__`, so the process dies
  before the display loop starts — an unattended restart loop that survives
  reboots, because the bad entry is persisted. Observed in the field. Non-dict
  entries are now discarded with a warning and defaults rebuilt.
- `ledmatrix.service` used `Restart=on-failure`, so an exit with status 0 left
  the unit stopped and the panel dark indefinitely. Now `Restart=always`.
- `ledmatrix-wifi-monitor.service` used `StandardOutput=syslog`, which systemd
  has marked obsolete and rewrites on every load.

**Memory**

- `MemoryCache` had a fixed 1000-entry ceiling. Entries are parsed API payloads
  of tens of KB, so one ceiling cannot serve both a 512MB Zero 2 W and an 8GB
  Pi 5. Now scaled from `MemTotal` — 150 entries at <=1GB, 1500 at >=8GB —
  overridable with `LEDMATRIX_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`.
- `requirements_are_satisfied()` returned False for **any** requirement with
  extras, so a plugin depending on `python-socketio[client]` re-ran pip on every
  single start: ~8s, a network dependency, and a 100-200MB spike — repeated for
  each restart during a crash loop. Extras are now resolved one level deep
  against installed metadata, keeping the conservative "anything unverifiable
  falls through to pip" contract.
- `MemoryMax=85%`, as a percentage so one unit file suits every board. This
  needs the memory cgroup controller, which Pi firmware disables by default —
  `first_time_install.sh` now adds `cgroup_enable=memory` to `cmdline.txt`, and
  the unit documents how to verify it took effect. Without it systemd accepts
  the setting and silently ignores it.
- `first_time_install.sh` also enables persistent journald storage (capped at
  64M). Default storage is volatile, so every reboot destroys the logs that
  would explain the reboot.

**Docs** — `docs/LOW_MEMORY_BOARDS.md`, linked from the docs index and
cross-referenced from `SSH_UNAVAILABLE_AFTER_INSTALL.md`, since "I can't SSH in
any more" is how most people will meet this.

## Note on scope

The memory ceiling is a safety net, not a cure. On a 1GB board this workload
genuinely wants ~67% of RAM, so any ceiling safe enough to protect the system is
one it may reach. It converts "the board becomes unreachable until someone pulls
the plug" into "one service restarts". Running fewer plugins is the real remedy,
which is what the doc says.

## Testing

- Full suite against `main`: **identical failure sets** (2777 passing; 84
  pre-existing failures are Windows path/file-locking issues, unrelated). Failure
  lists were diffed rather than compared by count — one run showed 85 vs 84, which
  was a flaky test.
- `systemd-analyze verify` on the patched unit with placeholders expanded, on the
  Pi — clean.
- `bash -n` on `first_time_install.sh`.
- Extras resolution verified against real installed metadata on the affected Pi:
  resolves `python-socketio[client]` to `requests` + `websocket-client`, finds both
  installed, returns satisfied.
- RAM scaling verified on the affected board: selects 150 entries where it
  previously used 1000.

  * Plugin installation now more accurately verifies optional dependencies.

author: kotisolo
body:
## Summary
Addresses the HIGH-impact "group roles are all-or-nothing" gap from the audit. Groups previously had a binary admin/member split with hardcoded behavior: editing group info and adding members were always admin-only with no way to loosen that, and sending messages had no restriction at all with no way to tighten it (e.g. into an announcement-only channel).

Adds three admin-configurable per-group policies, each `'everyone'` or `'admins'`:
- **Who can send messages** — new capability, lets a group act as an admin-only announcement channel.
- **Who can edit group info** — previously always admin-only; can now be opened up to all members.
- **Who can add members** — same.

Defaults are chosen to exactly match the prior hardcoded behavior (`send: everyone`, `edit_info: admins`, `add_members: admins`), so existing groups are completely unaffected until an admin explicitly changes a setting.

- New `PATCH /api/groups/:groupId/permissions` (admin-only) endpoint.
- Server-side enforcement added to the message-send, group-edit, and add-member endpoints — admins always pass regardless of policy, matching how these are checked in every other group endpoint.
- Client: a "Group permissions" section in the group info panel (admin-only, three tap-to-toggle rows), and the group compose box shows a locked banner instead of the message input when the current member isn't allowed to send.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` passes cleanly; `node -c server/src/server.js` syntax check passes.
- [x] Full API test with two throwaway accounts (admin + member) and a real group: member could send/nothing-restricted by default (`201`); admin restricted `sendMessagesPolicy` to `admins` → member's send now `403` with the expected message, admin's send still `201`; member's group-edit attempt `403` under the default `admins`-only `editInfoPolicy`; admin loosened it to `everyone` → member's edit now `200`.
- [x] Full browser UI test: logged in as the admin, opened Group Permissions in the group info panel, confirmed default values render correctly, toggled "Who can send messages" to "Only admins" and confirmed the panel reflects it immediately; logged in as the member, opened the same group, confirmed the compose input is replaced by the "Only admins can send messages in this group" locked banner.
- [x] Test accounts, group, and messages cleaned up from the database afterward.

body: ## Summary Follow up #186 so semantic dot paths inside each intrinsic-array item are rendered as nested, collapsible tree nodes instead of flat labels. For example, a collected point containing: ```text photometry.g.psf.mag time.mjd ``` now renders under the array item as: ```text [57] photometry g psf mag error time mjd ``` The same applies to `color_points`, `magnitude_rate_points`, `feature_vector_points`, and other mapping-valued array items. ## Root cause #186 made sequences structural, but each collected array item is itself a mapping whose keys are still canonical semantic dot paths. `_render_value()` treated that mapping as already nested and therefore rendered keys such as `photometry.g.psf.mag` literally. ## Fix Before rendering a mapping-valued sequence item, pass that item through the existing `_tree()` dot-path builder. This reuses the renderer's existing path/value collision handling and keeps array items collapsed while making their semantic substructure collapsible. ## Regression coverage The existing CI-covered smoke renderer test now: - exercises `time.mjd`, `photometry.g.psf.mag`, and `photometry.g.psf.mag.error` inside `points` - verifies `time`, `photometry`, `g`, and `psf` are nested nodes - verifies feature-vector `g.value` becomes nested `g -> value [N]` - explicitly rejects flattened labels such as `time.mjd` and `photometry.g.psf.mag` ## Scope Two files only: - `alertissimo/data_layer/presentation/portfolio_html.py` - `tests/test_smoke_scenarios.py` No normalization, collector, ontology, provider, endpoint, payload, orchestration, or CI-workflow changes.

author: cjimti
body:
The portal's script page showed an owner their automation's contract, its parameters, its approval and its run history, and let them act on none of it. Running one meant leaving the page and asking an agent to call `run_script`. Editing was a blind save: the author wrote a change, could not check that it parsed, could not see what capabilities it now reached, could not execute it once, and sent it to an administrator who then approved code neither of them had run. Every parameter was a text box, including the ones naming a connection whose full set the platform already holds.

This is the owner's loop on the page they are already looking at: run it, check an edit, and pick a value from the set the platform can offer.

## Running one now

`POST /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/runs` binds the supplied values against the approved version's contract, checks any connection parameter against the grant, and enqueues. It queues exactly what `run_script` queues, so a worker executes it under the script principal with the grant its approval bound; the run history below the form is where it is followed.

Whether a run is admitted at all is `script.RefuseNewRun`'s answer (`pkg/script/run.go`), the same one `run_script` obeys and the contract document reports, so the page cannot run something those two call unrunnable. A script with nothing approved, or one disabled, deprecated or superseded, gets no Run control at all rather than a button that fails when pressed.

A run's `trigger` now records which of the three producers created it: `tool` for `run_script`, `schedule` for a fire, and `portal` for one an owner asked for on the page. The three execute identically. The distinction is not decorative on one axis: `internal/platform/scriptexec/notify.go` mails a failure only for `TriggerSchedule`, whose requester is nobody, so a portal run's failure stays on the page where its requester is looking.

The history re-reads itself every three seconds while any run is pending or running and stops the moment nothing is, so a queued run reaches its terminal state on screen without a reload and a page of finished runs costs one request.

## Checking an edit before asking for approval

`POST /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/validate` parses the edited source and reports the capabilities, connections and destinations it would reach, with the correction for each finding. It executes nothing and stores nothing. Where a list is known to be short because a call computes its target instead of naming one, the report says so.

`POST /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/dry-run` executes the edit under the caller's own identity and persona with the draft limits, persisting nothing: `platform.export` previews, no asset is versioned, no object is delivered, and the approved-version pointer is untouched. The no-new-authority property is structural rather than a promise, because the draft's session carries the caller's own identity and every platform call it makes crosses the same authentication, authorization, rate limiting and audit their own call would.

Both surfaces that run a draft go through one implementation, `internal/platform/scriptdraft`, extracted from `scriptlayer/rundraft.go`. The `manage_script run_draft` tool and the portal route differ only in where the identity was read from.

## What a reviewer now sees

Each dry run leaves an account of itself: the run id (which is also its session id, so the audit rows it wrote are reachable from it), who ran it, when, how it ended, the bounded log it captured, and the shape of the outputs it would have written. A dry run still persists nothing it produced; what is stored is the record that one happened.

The account is keyed by the SHA-256 of the source that executed rather than by a version id, because an author dry-runs an edit before saving it. The digest links the account to whichever version later carries that exact code, in either order, and to no other version. `GET /api/v1/admin/scripts/{id}/versions/{version}` carries it, and the review drawer shows it beside the version it describes.

Its absence is shown as loudly: a version nobody has dry-run says so, because approving one means that code first executes unattended.

## Choosing a value the platform can offer

`connection` joins the closed parameter type list (`pkg/script/param.go`). It binds as a string, and it is a type of its own because the platform holds the whole set of values it can take and an approved version's grant names the subset a given script may use.

`GET /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/connections` serves that set, and which set depends on what will execute. A run or a schedule fire is confined to the approved version's granted connections; a dry run executes as its caller and reaches what that person's persona reaches. The two are labelled with their source, because serving one under the other's name would offer values the run then refuses. The enumeration applies the same persona predicate `list_connections` applies (`internal/platform/connscope` over `pkg/connview`), so the values a form offers and the values a tool call may name are one set. An administrator is enumerated unrestricted.

A value outside the applicable set is refused where it was entered rather than at the query it would have failed on: `script.CheckConnectionParams` runs at the portal run route, at the schedule route (`BuildSchedule`, since every fire of such a schedule would fail identically and unattended), and in `run_script`. An optional connection parameter must declare a default, for the same reason an optional enum or date must: there is no meaningful empty connection, and a run binding one is refused by the grant.

One parameter form now serves all three surfaces on the page — run now, dry run, and the schedule's bindings — so a parameter cannot render as a picker in one place and a text box in another. `enum` and `bool` render as choices through the same control. Each form scopes its control ids (`script-param-<form>-<name>`), since a DOM id may appear once in a document.

## Schema

Migration `000114_script_portal_run_loop` does two things. `script_runs.trigger_kind` gains `portal`, extending the check the scheduler last widened in `000100`. `script_dry_runs` is created to hold the accounts, keyed by `(script_id, source_sha256)` with a second index on `(script_id, requested_by)`; `source_sha256` is `BYTEA`, because a raw SHA-256 is not a UTF-8 string.

Growth is bounded at write rather than by a sweeper: an author keeps the newest twenty accounts per script, trimmed in the same transaction as the insert, so the table is bounded by the authoring loop rather than by how many times somebody pressed the button. The down migration relabels `portal` runs as `tool` before narrowing the constraint, which keeps the runs and loses only the label.

## What is bounded, and what is not

A draft run had no concurrency bound: the one-run-at-a-time lever belongs to the approved-run worker, and an interpreter heap cannot be capped. With the path reachable from a form in a browser, the runner holds four execution slots and answers a request that cannot get one within five seconds as `503` with a retry rather than queueing it. The bound is small rather than one because an author iterating is interactive work.

`docs/scripts/security.md` records both the mechanism and what it does not cover: a draft run still has no per-request rate limit of its own, and a dry run's log is stored and now reaches a reviewer. Neither widens who may read the underlying data, because a draft run reaches only what its caller already reaches.

## Surfaces

| Route | Does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/runs` | Queue one run of the approved version |
| `POST /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/validate` | Parse an edit and report what it would reach |
| `POST /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/dry-run` | Execute an edit as the caller, persisting nothing |
| `GET /api/v1/portal/scripts/{id}/connections` | The set a connection parameter c

author: michaelsowah
body:
Schema now exists exactly when the feature that owns it is provisioned or enabled — never as
  a side effect of boot — and every migration operation is locked, truthful, and recorded.

  ## What's in this release

  - **Pack manifests are the sole schema inventory.** All 12 library packs declare
    `extra.glueful.migrations` (8 core descriptors with effect verifiers, 4 explicit `"none"`);
    providers register nothing. Framework 1.80 enforces declaration unconditionally.
  - **Provision is one locked, failure-aware complete pass** over the app schema, every core
    pack descriptor, and every shipped-enabled engine. A failed migration fails provision
    naming the file. The create-admin catch-up now applies only the dependent-grants lane —
    its first-pass ordering retry is obsolete (render's permission seed moved to the
    dependent tier, fixing a real single-pass ordering failure the retry papered over).
  - **Extension toggling works in production, truthfully**: SPA and CLI drive the shared
    schema executor — migrate-first, lock-serialized, persisted operation records surfaced
    through the API and UI. The extensions list shows per-package schema state
    (ready/pending/divergent/none/undeclared) with reasons and the CLI equivalent.
  - **Capabilities gate on their owning engine**: effective = requested AND available, with
    the six engine-owned capabilities declaring their Composer owner and failing closed
    (reason + remedy) when the engine is missing, disabled, or schema-unready.
  - **One system-scoped capability switchboard** (`capability.<id>.enabled`) with an
    operator-only management surface; the Settings › General search toggle reads and writes
    through the same authority (legacy `search_enabled` row retired on first write).
  - **Tenancy enablement migrates through the executor's protected lane**
    (`protected_migrate` operations) while its state machine keeps sole custody of the
    provider-state write.
  - **Legacy seams removed**: the alias/normalization machinery is gone — **pre-beta.3
    installs are not upgradable in place** (re-provision, or rewrite ledger `source` values
    by hand; see docs/upgrading.md).

  ## Dependencies

  `glueful/framework` ^1.80 (v1.80.1 locked) plus the adopted extension minors: aegis ^1.15,
  audit ^1.4, commerce ^1.13, email-notification ^1.13, i18n ^1.2, import-export ^1.2,
  media ^1.2, meilisearch ^1.7, payvia ^2.8, subscriptions ^2.3, tenancy ^2.1, users ^2.4.

  ## Verification
  
  Full PHP suite 3,380 tests · distribution smoke · SPA 2,236 tests + type-check ·
  `composer boundaries` · `composer phpcs` · fresh-provision acceptance on an isolated
  PostgreSQL schema · cross-policy acceptance matrices (`SchemaProgramAcceptanceTest`) ·
  dist archive verified (admin bundle ships; internal docs/config excluded).

author: piedras77
body:
Fixes #14. Website half; paired with [gaudi-agents-functions#54](https://github.com/GaudiAICompany/gaudi-agents-functions/pull/54), which adds the endpoint. **Merge that one first** — this PR points at it.

## Root cause

Not missing env vars. They were set correctly, in both GitHub secrets and the Static Web App settings — they point at a host that no longer exists:

```
FUNCTION_API_BASE = https://gaudi-backend-staging-a7f6fwfybma7fjfa.westus3-01.azurewebsites.net
```

NXDOMAIN via Google DNS, and absent from `az functionapp list` in both subscriptions. Every CTA fetch dies at DNS resolution before sending a byte. That value is baked into the live heygaudi.ai HTML right now.

The endpoint itself only ever existed in `piedras77/gaudi-backend`, a **personal** repo whose function app has been deleted — which is why an org-wide search finds nothing. There's an orphaned `ASP-gaudibackendgroup-9d65` App Service plan (0 sites) still sitting in a `gaudi-backend_group` resource group: the shell it left behind.

## 🔴 The function key was public — rotate it

`?code=${apiKey}` was built client-side, so `FUNCTION_API_KEY` shipped in the query string of a `fetch` and was readable in the page source of **every deployed page**. That key also worked on the other routes of the function app it belonged to.

Treat it as compromised: rotate it, then delete `FUNCTION_API_BASE` and `FUNCTION_API_KEY` from repo secrets *and* from the SWA application settings (along with a leftover `dummy = remove` entry).

## What changed

The site now holds **one plain URL and no credential**. The backend owns the database secrets and decides what gets written.

- All CTAs route through one helper, `lib/capture-lead.ts`
- `FUNCTION_API_BASE`/`FUNCTION_API_KEY` removed from every page component
- No `api/` folder here on purpose — a second backend means a second secret store to audit

**Two call sites had no error handling at all.** On `/es` and `/inspections` the thrown fetch also killed the `cal.com` redirect that ran after it — part of why this went unnoticed for so long. Both are guarded now.

**Logging.** Browser consoles are effectively public, so each submission logs exactly one line carrying no address and no credential:

```
[cta] failed source=Get started requestId=<uuid> status=429 code=RATE_LIMITED durationMs=812
```

`status=no-response` means the request never reached a server — DNS, TLS, offline. That's what this outage looked like, and it was previously indistinguishable from a server 500. The same id is shown to the visitor as `Ref:` and appears in the backend's traces, so a screenshot is enough to find the matching one.

## ⚠️ Config: it must be set in GitHub, not Azure

`NEXT_PUBLIC_LEAD_CAPTURE_URL` — a repo **Variable**, not a Secret (a public endpoint URL isn't one). Passed straight to the build step; the `.env.production` file step is gone.

This is a **static export**, so `next build` compiles the value into the JS bundle, and that build runs in GitHub Actions. Static Web App *application settings* are **runtime** settings, readable only by managed functions — and there are none. By the time Azure serves the site there's no process left to read a setting. Proof, straight out of the artifact:

```
out/_next/static/chunks/app/page-*.js:
  agentic-back-office-dev-…azurewebsites.net/api/capture_cta_email
```

This is the same misunderstanding that leaked the key: the value sat in Azure settings *and* GitHub secrets, but only the GitHub one ever reached the browser. `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` documents the distinction so it doesn't recur.

## Setup

- [ ] Add repo **Variable** `NEXT_PUBLIC_LEAD_CAPTURE_URL` = `https://agentic-back-office-dev-c6dzhceedgffcse8.westus3-01.azurewebsites.net/api/capture_cta_email`
- [ ] Rotate `FUNCTION_API_KEY`, then delete both old secrets and the SWA settings
- [ ] Merge and deploy gaudi-agents-functions#54 first

Pointing at dev is fine and is a one-value flip later — the site is decoupled from which backend it uses. Both function apps are Flex Consumption with no always-ready instances, so an idle app bills ~nothing.

## Verification

`npm run build` passes; the URL inlines correctly and `out/` contains neither the dead host nor `?code=`. `npx tsc --noEmit` reports only two pre-existing `window.gtag` errors, unrelated.

The endpoint itself is verified end-to-end against the real database in the backend PR (10/10, test rows cleaned up).

Not yet exercised: a real browser submission through a deployed SWA preview. That needs the variable set and the backend merged — worth doing on the preview build before this lands.

## Note

`package.json` / `package-lock.json` include a `@supabase/supabase-js` addition that was already in the working tree, not from this change. The site itself doesn't use it — only the untracked `local_scripts/`. Drop it if that isn't going to be committed.

author: matthewdaw
body:
## The gap

Neither existing path covers an idea judged on the strength of a run that should never have been adjudicated:

- `retriable-ideas` — only **parked** ideas whose `reactivation_trigger` has fired
- `invalidate-adoption` — only ideas rejected under an adoption the ratchet invalidated

An idea **rejected because its run was truncated** is neither. It stays rejected forever — the worst possible record, because a rejection is precisely what a future session reads as a question already settled.

## What happened

A graph-convolution arm was starved by a 30-minute wall-clock budget. The deadline is set once for the whole run but checked inside *each fold's* epoch loop, so once it passed, every remaining fold broke at epoch 0 and was scored as an **untrained** model:

| seed | score | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.6183 | trained |
| 1 | 0.6273 | trained |
| 2 | 0.4123 | budget expired partway |
| 3 | 0.0491 | untrained (all folds 0.0154) |

The mean over trained *and untrained* folds — 0.4268 — was adjudicated as a **−0.2766 rejection of the entire graph model family**. That is the family the skeleton-action-recognition literature converged on, and the one this campaign's own adopted arm (bone vectors, 2s-AGCN's second stream) is evidence for.

**Voiding the trial did not fix it.** The trial became `voided`, but the *idea* stayed `rejected`, so the arm could never be re-queued and the false record stood.

## Deliberately narrow

Not a way to relitigate a verdict you dislike. The prior verdict is preserved under `reopened_from`, not erased — a reader must be able to see the idea was judged once, on what, and why that judgement was discarded, or reopening is indistinguishable from quietly deleting an inconvenient result. Repeated reopens accumulate, so an idea that keeps being reopened is visible as such. Stale `rejection_reason` fields are cleared, since an untried idea still carrying one reads as rejected to anything scanning meta.

`--reason` required, as with `supersede-trial` and `reset-ratchet`.

## Tests

325 passed, 6 new.

## Summary

- Make V060 a no-op for sentences that have no W tier, matching its documented scope for segmented XML.
- Accept canonical language-valued variety labels such as Truku in orthography rule sidecars, using the same inventory accepted by V152.
- Ignore `~` only when it occurs between CJK characters in a source gloss, where it is an open semantic-argument placeholder rather than a reduplication boundary.

The root causes are three narrow validator assumptions: treating an absent optional W tier as an alignment mismatch, validating rule-sidecar varieties against a smaller label set than related registry checks, and treating every gloss tilde as morphological notation even in CJK teaching glosses.

The CJK exception does not affect ordinary Leipzig-style forms such as `CAU~walk`.

author: danfiedler-msft
body:
## Summary

This PR pins GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs for improved security and reproducibility and adds a 7 day cooldown to Dependabot configuration for GitHub Actions. This work is described in more detail at https://aka.ms/action-pinning.

## Why?

Pinning actions to commit SHAs prevents supply-chain attacks where a tag could be moved to point to malicious code. This is a recommended security best practice per the [GitHub Actions security hardening guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions).

This change mitigates the risk of tag retargeting to malicious code as seen in incidents like the [tj-actions/changed-files action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised) or [codfish/semantic-release-action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/supply-chain-compromise-codfish-semantic-release-action) and improves the integrity and reproducibility of the CI/CD pipeline.

## What changed?

**Action pinning:** Third-party action references in `.github/workflows/` that used mutable tag-based references (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`) have been updated to full-length commit SHAs with a version comment (e.g., `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`) using the [pinact](https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) tool. References that were already pinned to a SHA, or that used immutable release tags, were left unchanged.

**Dependabot configuration:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has been updated to ensure a `github-actions` package-ecosystem section is present with a `cooldown` configuration (`default-days: 7`). If the file did not exist, it was created. If a `github-actions` section already existed, only the `cooldown` block was added or its `default-days` value was increased to 7 if it was lower. The 7-day cooldown provides a window for the community to detect and report compromised releases before they are automatically proposed as updates, reducing exposure to supply-chain attacks via newly published malicious versions.

## Is this safe to merge?

Yes. The pinned SHAs correspond to the same commits that the existing tags pointed to. No behavioral changes in action execution are introduced. You can verify the pinned SHA value using the GitHub REST API (e.g., the commit hash for `actions/checkout@v7` can be found in the `sha` property in the JSON response for `GET https://api.github.com/repos/actions/checkout/commits/v7`).

## Additional Information

For more information, please see https://aka.ms/action-pinning

| # | File | Query key | Endpoint | Role | Interval | Socket coverage? | Authorized? | Data used? | Classification |

| 12 | technician/pages/Messages.tsx *(whole page removed)* | activity-feed-tech | GET /messages | TECHNICIAN | on mount only | N/A | **No -- same 403** | No (always empty state) | **REMOVED** |
| 13 | components/DirectMessages.tsx | dm-conversations | GET /direct-messages/conversations | All (shared component, only while messaging page is open) | 30s | No | Yes | Yes | KEEP (no socket exists; genuine sole update mechanism) |

Also inventoried and confirmed **not** network polling: `ConnectionBanner.tsx`/`NotificationBar.tsx`'s 300-500ms `setInterval` (a local, self-terminating poll of `getSocket()` waiting for the socket to attach -- zero HTTP/socket-server traffic), and `Reports.tsx`'s 1s UI clock ticker. No manual (non-React-Query) `setInterval`/`setTimeout` loop calling `api.*` was found anywhere.

## Confirmed cause of Technician /messages 403

`packages/backend/src/routes/messages.ts:19`: `router.get('/', requireRole('ADMIN', 'SCHEDULING'), ...)` -- TECHNICIAN was never in the allowed-role list. The route's own SCHEDULING-branch logic further scopes visibility to customer/visible-appointment audit logs only, and there is zero technician-specific branch anywhere in the file -- this is deliberate, role-scoped design (audit-trail visibility limited to ADMIN and, filtered, SCHEDULING), not an oversight. No other backend endpoint represents equivalent data for a Technician. Per the mission's explicit instruction not to broaden authorization without clear business-rule evidence, and finding none, the fix is (A): remove the unauthorized request and the page/nav entry that depended on it entirely.

## Exact fix chosen

- `technician/components/Sidebar.tsx`: removed the `activity-feed-tech` `useQuery` (and its derived `newMessages`/`lastSeenMessages` computation and the `messages` badge entry), and removed the `{ to: "/technician/messages", ... }` nav link.
- `technician/pages/Messages.tsx`: deleted (the page could never show real content -- every mount 403'd).
- `App.tsx`: removed the `TechMessages` import and its `<Route path="messages" .../>` registration.
- `technician/components/Layout.tsx`: removed the now-dead `/technician/messages` entries from the page-title and help-key lookup maps.
- **No backend change.** `routes/messages.ts` authorization is untouched.

## Requests removed/reduced/kept

- **Removed:** the Technician Sidebar's recurring `GET /messages` badge query (previously fired once per mount, `staleTime`-refetched on window refocus after 30s -- non-periodic but recurring, always a 403), and the Technician Messages page's own `GET /messages` fetch (previously fired every time a technician navigated to that page -- always a 403).
- **Reduced:** none. Every socket-covered query (urgent badges, activity-feed) was already using the minimal appropriate design (socket-primary + 30s fallback, or staleTime-only) from prior work this session -- there was no over-polling to reduce.
- **Kept:** all 10 other queries in the inventory above, each confirmed to either lack any socket coverage to leverage (notification/DM-unread badges, DM conversation view -- genuine fallbacks) or to already be in the reduced/optimal form (urgent badges, activity-feed for Admin/Scheduling).

## Before/after idle requests per minute by role

Counting only genuine fixed-interval (`refetchInterval`) polling, per this session's own established measurement convention:

| Role | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Admin | 6/min (dm-unread + urgent + notif, 3 x 2/min) | 6/min (unchanged) |
| 1 Scheduling | 4/min (notif + dm-unread, 2 x 2/min) | 4/min (unchanged) |
| 1 Technician | 6/min (urgent + notif + dm-unread, 3 x 2/min) **+ 1 guaranteed 403 on every mount, + further 403s on every window-refocus event thereafter (non-periodic, so not folded into the /min figure -- but real, recurring, and unauthorized)** | 6/min (unchanged) **+ zero 403s, eliminated entirely** |

The fixed-interval `/min` figure for Technician does not change, because the removed query was `staleTime`-based, not `refetchInterval`-based, so it never had a clean periodic cadence to begin with -- it fired on mount and on each subsequent window-focus event, an amount that scales with actual user behavior, not a fixed timer. The real, honest improvement is not a reduction in polling frequency (there wasn't excess frequency to cut) but the complete elimination of a request that was **guaranteed to fail every single time**, on every Technician session, for the lifetime of the deployment until now.

## Example: 1 Admin + 1 Scheduling + 2 Technicians (idle)

**Before:** 6 + 4 + (6 x 2) = **22 requests/minute** (matching this session's earlier read-only performance audit's independently-derived figure) **+ at least 2 guaranteed 403s (one per technician, on mount) + additional 403s per technician on every window-refocus event thereafter.**

**After:** 6 + 4 + (6 x 2) = **22 requests/minute** (unchanged) **+ zero 403s.**
