## Physical source architecture

No second D9/database/warehouse/resolver/reader/API was created. The adapter reuses existing `history_store.append_partition`, `ImmutableHistoryConflict`, and `partition_descriptor` under the deployment-supplied D9 WARM/history root.

The D8 runtime source was deliberately not modified by this task. Qualified D8 `sqlite.spool` PENDING rows are forwarded only when bound to terminal cycle evidence, `OBSERVED_STATE` capability ledger evidence, and complete cycle-local checkpoint-v2 integrity evidence.

Checkpoint-v2 source binding requires:
- exact checkpoint attempt bound to an `OBSERVED_STATE` capability ledger row;
- ledger SHA-256 binding;
- expected observation count;
- contiguous ordered positions;
- unique observation membership;
- membership SHA-256;
- per-member payload SHA-256;
- aggregate payload SHA-256;
- exact cycle/capability/observation identity;
- exact equality of checkpoint cycle-local payload and spool envelope.

The D8 global `observation_id` remains the WARM record identity:
`sha256(provider|series_id|provider_timestamp_at|payload_fingerprint)`.
Checkpoint membership remains recovery evidence, not market observation identity.

The forwarder imports no provider acquisition surface and performs no provider reacquisition, provider fallback, synthetic fill, silent substitution, or Git transport.

## D9 WARM mapping

- Binance Spot M5 -> `FIXED_GRID`
- Kraken Spot M5 -> `FIXED_GRID`
- Binance USD-M M5/current -> series-bound: perp OHLCV fixed-grid, current/depth sampled state `SAMPLED_SCHEDULE`
- Deribit perpetual/current -> `SAMPLED_SCHEDULE`
- options -> `SAMPLED_SCHEDULE`
- liquidity -> `SAMPLED_SCHEDULE`
- Kraken futures analytics -> `SAMPLED_SCHEDULE`

D8-origin WARM stores the exact validated D8 envelope and explicitly does not claim a provider-native row. In particular, missing provider-native Binance fields are never fabricated.

Preserved fields include provider, canonical series identity, provider timestamp, payload/fingerprint, exact observation_id, known_at, retrieved_at/collected_at, cycle/run provenance, source revision, runtime contract/revision, finality, and lifecycle/gap semantics.

## Crash/ACK semantics

Transport: `AT_LEAST_ONCE`.
History materialization: effectively once by exact immutable observation identity + idempotent D9 append.

A. Crash before WARM commit -> D8 remains `PENDING`.

B. WARM committed, crash before D8 ACK -> D8 remains `PENDING`; retry validates the exact already-present WARM identity, creates zero duplicate rows, then ACKs.

C. WARM durable + exact read-back + collection-run evidence + ACK -> selected D8 rows transition `PENDING -> FORWARDED` in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction.

No partial/global false `FORWARDED` mark is allowed if the selected batch does not reach global ACK.

## Gap/finality lifecycle evidence

`OBSERVED_STATE` materializes exact checkpoint-bound observation envelopes. `COLLECTION_GAP`, provider failures, validation failures, `NOT_DUE`, and `DISABLED_BY_POLICY` remain explicit D9 collection-run lifecycle evidence. Gap-only terminal cycles are exported even when no PENDING market observation exists. No carry-forward or synthetic observation is created.

## Internal HOT seam

`D8ToD9Forwarder.read_hot_snapshot()` remains an internal read-only physical source seam with contract `d8-hot-internal-physical-source/1.0.0`. It is `agent_facing=false`; no `/latest`, `/market-data`, `/agent-data`, second resolver or second reader was added. The canonical consumer remains semantic request -> canonical resolver -> ResolutionPlan -> canonical reader.

author: kinqsradio
body:
## ADR-041 D8 Phase 36 — fetch_url + web_search (host-side egress) + in-app-browser extraction

The two host-side egress tools leave the switch for a new `handlers/websearch.ts`. Both are **refused on a pentest turn** (host egress bypasses the scope-pinned sandbox — an SSRF vector) and both **prefer the in-app browser** (real Chromium + the user's session) when present, falling back to the HTTP crawler / configured search provider.

**New host surface:** `pentestMode` (agent.ts:1209) + `browserControlPort` (agent.ts:1294).

**Why a module extraction rides along:** the browser-fetch helpers (`looksStructuredUrl` / `fetchViaInAppBrowser` / `fetchHtmlViaInAppBrowser` + their internal `BrowserFetchPort` / `InAppBrowseOptions` / `openOrReuseBrowseTab`) were defined *inside* `runtime.ts`. A handler importing them from `runtime.ts` would cycle back through the dispatch shim — the same problem the Phase 17 `sourceSafety` extraction solved. The block references only JS builtins, so it moves **verbatim** into `websearch/inAppBrowser.ts` with zero new imports; `fetch-via-browser.test.ts` now imports from there. `runtime.ts` drops the block + both cases + the exclusive websearch imports, and `egressDecision` is split out of the shared execPolicy import (`decideExecutionPolicy` stays for `run_command`).

Bodies are the former switch cases verbatim (`this.*` → `ctx.host.*`).

**Verification:** tsc clean; full core suite green (**4688, 0 fail**); inert-value-sweep ceilings hold; dispatch test covers the pentest-refusal (both) + the empty-query guard.

Switch: 7 → 5 cases.

author: codhenley
body:
Two fixes to `reconcile_dispensed_items.py`, found while investigating why its first live run failed:

1. **False-positive variance (the actual cause of the failure):** `vetspire_total()` summed ALL of Vetspire's `usageReport` order items, but that report also includes non-inventory line items (exam fees, consult charges, radiograph/injection admin fees) that have no `productId`/product record at all — confirmed by sampling (215 of 7,057 qty in one location's 18-day window, ≈3%, matching the reported variance almost exactly). `backfill_date_range.py` and the other writers correctly never capture these — they were never real dispensed products. The reconciliation now excludes them the same way, so it's a true apples-to-apples comparison instead of a permanent ~3-4% false alarm that would train everyone to ignore its red X.
2. **Timezone bug:** `end = date.today()` reads the GitHub Actions runner's UTC clock — the exact bug already fixed everywhere else in this pipeline (see `vetspire_intraday_sync.py`). Switched to `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("America/Chicago")).date()`.

author: bmarshall511
body:
Owner-reported twice: *"In the moment has no navigation… no way to review or edit answers given for other categories"*, and *"the questions are too long — short, easy to answer, and specifically about dirty talk"*.

Reading the code first turned up worse than was reported.

## The two reports

**In the moment** is now a six-category strip that never leaves the screen. Switching is navigation, not a purchase: an answered category re-opens for free with its choices intact, and nothing is discarded to go somewhere else. `edge`, `sexting` and `phone` were written by the engine and reachable from nowhere.

**The questions** are one line under 20 words with 3–5 tappable answers written for that exact question, plus a folded "say more". The prompt's interpretive angle is gone — a reading about a person belongs in their profile, labelled as one, not as a question they answer about themselves mid-test.

## Five defects nobody had reported

| | |
|---|---|
| **A pass's six answers collapsed into one** | Every question was stamped under the bare *ambiguity* id, and last session's own fix — making `stampTurn` replace by item so an answer could be edited — turned that from a harmless append into silent destruction. Six answers typed, one on disk. The review screen showed a single card because that was all there was, and the synthesis got a sixth of its richest input. |
| **A moment's options were never saved** | `options: []` hardcoded at the stamp, so an answered moment could never be re-opened or re-picked — a "done" category could only spend again on five *different* moments. |
| **Half the categories unreachable** | The engine writes six; the screen offered three. |
| **A skip counted as an answer** | It recorded `''`, which is a string. |
| **A failed analysis said nothing** | `runSynthesis` returned no reason on a parse failure and the bridge discarded `ok`/`reason`/`message` regardless, then completed the take and redirected to a report with no profile in it. Three of four phases got this fix; the fourth is the one reported three times. |

It now names which failure it was, stays put, and offers a retry **and** an explicit `acceptDegraded` finish — never completing on a failure alone is a trap for anyone over budget.

## Also

The folded "What you told it" in the report (your answers appeared nowhere), the take's running spend in the rail (admin-only by construction), comparable rail units, an area jump for the 36-area words step, and the "three more"/"all three" copy drifts.

## Verified live

Against the owner's own vault through `createCoreBridge` — the real handlers, not the engine functions — at 132 marks / 245 boundaries:

```
PASS  questions are short — longest 13 words (was ~54); 8/11/10/11/11/13
PASS  answers are tappable — 6/6 carry 2+ options
PASS  every answer survives — 6 of 6 on disk (was always 1)
PASS  the options survive with them
PASS  sexting → moments          (a category the UI never offered)
PASS  an answered moment keeps its choices — 4 options on disk (was 0)
PASS  wrote the analysis — 2450 chars; completed the take
```

The answer-loss guard is verified to **fail** when reverted (*"expected 3 but got 1"*).

Gate: typecheck ×3, lint, format, **2390 core + 1684 desktop** unit, **216 E2E** (the lone failure is the documented accumulated-load flake — 3/3 in isolation on a clean tree).

body:
# Knowledge flush — 8 insight(s)

8 queued candidates → **7 new pages** (two candidates share one mechanism and were
merged into a single page), 7 existing pages amended with reciprocal `related:`
links, 5 domain indexes updated, `log.md` appended.

## Verified best-practice

### 1. `inspect.getsource` on a class from a path-loaded module → `verified`

**Claim:** a module loaded via `spec_from_file_location`/`module_from_spec`/`exec_module`
without `sys.modules` registration makes **class** introspection fail with
`TypeError: … is a built-in class`, while **function/method** introspection works.

**How verified:** reproduced locally 2026-08-18 on CPython **3.9.6, 3.11.13, 3.13.11,
3.14.6** — the headline behaviour is identical on all four: class → `TypeError:
<class 'aw.Handler'> is a built-in class`; `m.Handler.do_GET` and `m.select` → source returned; after
`sys.modules[spec.name] = m` the class call returns source. Mechanism read directly from
the shipped `inspect.py` (3.14.6) `getfile`: the class branch resolves through
`sys.modules.get(object.__module__)`, the function branch falls through to
`object.__code__.co_filename`. The registration line was confirmed to be part of the
standard library's own documented recipe.

**Sources checked (opened this session):** docs.python.org/3/library/importlib.html
("Importing a source file directly" recipe, `sys.modules[module_name] = module`),
docs.python.org/3/library/inspect.html, docs.python.org/3/reference/import.html,
local `inspect.py` source.

### 2. Unpacked Chromium extension reload → `verified`

**Claim:** after editing a content script, the host-page refresh alone re-injects the
cached copy; the extension itself must be reloaded too.

**How verified:** Chrome's official Hello-World tutorial was opened and states "After
saving the file, to see this change in the browser you also have to refresh the
extension", with its reload table listing content scripts as "Yes (plus the host page)".
`chrome.runtime.getManifest()` (used for the running-build marker directive) was
confirmed on the official runtime API page. The `#dev-reload-button` shadow-root path is
labelled in-page as a **measured internal detail, not a documented API**, with instructions
to re-derive it when it stops matching. Field evidence: okta-autofill, page-refresh-only →
field stayed empty; extension reload → flow completed.

**Sources checked (opened):** developer.chrome.com get-started tutorial,
develop/concepts/content-scripts, reference/api/runtime.

### 3+8. Browser-automation console capture gaps → `verified` (merged page)

**Claim A (candidate 8):** a collector attached after navigation loses load-time records.
**Claim B (candidate 3):** extension content-script logs live in an isolated execution
context that a main-world collector never reports.

**How verified:** Claim A **independently reproduced this session** (Aside CLI
1.26.810.1915 / daemon 1.26.818.1059) against a local `python3 -m http.server` page whose
inline script logs one `log` and one `error`: `openTab` → `[]`; after `sleep(800)` → `[]`;
after `console.clear()` + `reload()` + `sleep(300)` → both records. Claim B's mechanism is
documented — Chrome content-scripts page ("An isolated world is a private execution
environment that isn't accessible to the page…") and CDP `Runtime.consoleAPICalled`
carrying `executionContextId`, "Identifier of the context where the call was made"; the
default/isolated/worker distinction is carried in `executionContextCreated`'s `auxData`
("Embedder-specific auxiliary data"), and the page now says so rather than presenting it
as a documented field of its own. The tool-specific miss stays labelled as a field
measurement.

**Correction made:** a drafted `playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page` citation was **dropped**
— the fetch did not surface the `console` event section, so the claim could not be
confirmed from it.

**Sources checked (opened):** chromedevtools.github.io Runtime domain,
developer.chrome.com content-scripts. (playwright.dev opened, not confirmable → removed.)

### 4. Correlated SubLink duplicated by derived-table pull-up → `verified`

**Claim:** a derived table carrying no aggregate/LIMIT/DISTINCT/set-op is flattened, its
select-list SubLink is substituted into every referencing aggregate, and PostgreSQL does
not CSE SubPlans — so N outer references cost N evaluations per row; `OFFSET 0`,
`MATERIALIZED`, or `LATERAL` fix it.

**How verified:** the harvested evidence was second-hand (a worker's measurement the
harvesting session could not re-run). **Reproduced from scratch this session** on a
throwaway local cluster, PostgreSQL **16.11** (Homebrew), 5 driving rows:

| Shape | Plan |
|---|---|
| Unfenced derived table, read by `bool_or` + `sum` | `SubPlan 1` + `SubPlan 2`, each `loops=5` (10 evaluations) |
| `OFFSET 0` inside the derived table | one `SubPlan`, `loops=5` |
| `WITH … AS MATERIALIZED` | one `SubPlan` under a `CTE` node |
| Plain `WITH` (not materialized) | **two** `SubPlan` nodes — a plain CTE is not a fence |
| `LEFT JOIN LATERAL` | no `SubPlan` — Nested Loop Left Join |
| Derived table with `GROUP BY` | one `SubPlan` |
| 1 / 2 / 3 outer references | 1 / 2 / 3 `SubPlan` nodes |

The plain-CTE and reference-count rows are additions the candidate did not contain.
Doc quotes obtained verbatim: `OFFSET 0` "is the same as omitting the `OFFSET` clause"
(queries-limit), and the folding/`MATERIALIZED`/push-down-restriction sentences
(queries-with). The pull-up predicate is cited **by location** (`is_simple_subquery()` in
`prepjointree.c`) and explicitly marked as measured-not-quoted, because the only doxygen
rendering available returned a paraphrase rather than the source comment.

**Sources checked (opened):** postgresql.org queries-limit.html, queries-with.html;
local EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs.

### 5. Expectation sets with one distinct value → `verified`

**Claim:** when every case expects the same literal, a hardcoded constant at the assembly
point is observationally identical to the wired computation, so adding assertions cannot
kill it; a delete probe only proves key presence.

**How verified:** **reproduced with a minimal control** (CPython 3.9.6, `unittest`):
3 cases all expecting `"HAS_VACANCY"` → constant mutant **survived** (0 failures);
adding one case expecting `"UNSURVEYED"` → same constant **killed** (1 failure); wired
baseline green in both sets; a delete probe reddened via `KeyError`, i.e. on key presence
alone. Field measurement (rtb-unified NEWRTB-2786, 2046-test api suite) retained as the
production instance.

**Correction made:** the Stryker and PIT quotes were **re-fetched rather than inherited** —
the real sentences are "When all tests passed while this mutant was active, the mutant
survived. You're missing a test for it." and "Survived means the mutation was not detected
by the covering test." A third drafted citation (testing.googleblog.com) was dropped as
unopened.

**Sources checked (opened):** stryker-mutator.io mutant-states-and-metrics, pitest.org
basic_concepts; local reproduction.

### 6. ORM-generated test schema hides model-vs-DB drift → `field-tested`

**Claim:** with `ddl-auto: create-drop`/`create`/`update` the test schema is generated
from the entity model, so an entity-vs-database drift cannot exist there and "add a
reproducing test" is unachievable; verification must move to a migration-built DB with
`validate` or an `information_schema` gate.

**How verified — and why not `verified`:** the knobs are documented (Spring Boot: JPA
databases "are automatically created **only** if you use an embedded database"; the
`ddl-auto` ↔ `hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto` mapping; "If you are using a higher-level database
migration tool, like Flyway or Liquibase, you should use them alone to create and
initialize the schema"; Jakarta `@Column.nullable` = "(Optional) Whether the database
column is nullable"). The **consequence** — that the drifted state is unconstructible in a
generated schema — follow

author: isma-l154
body:
Closes #28.

## The bug

`build` and `check` both began with `wrangler types --check`. `wrangler.jsonc` points `main` at `.svelte-kit/cloudflare/_worker.js` — **which `vite build` is what produces.** When that file exists, `wrangler types` emits three extra lines:

```ts
interface GlobalProps {
    mainModule: typeof import("./.svelte-kit/cloudflare/_worker");
}
```

So the generated output depended on whether a build had already run:

| state | `_worker.js` | `wrangler types --check` |
|---|---|---|
| fresh clone, or CI | absent | passes |
| after any local `vite build` | present | **fails, permanently** |

The error tells you to run `wrangler types`, and doing so produces a file that then fails in CI instead. The build was gated on the output of the command it was gating.

**It was also gating nothing.** CI called `npx svelte-check` and `npx vite build` directly to sidestep it, with a comment calling it "a local development aid". That divergence is precisely why this survived — no pipeline ever ran the broken script.

## The fix

- `build` → `vite build`; `check` → `svelte-kit sync && svelte-check`.
- **CI now runs `npm run check` and `npm run build`** instead of working around them, so the commands a developer runs are the commands that have to pass.
- Regenerating binding types stays as `npm run gen` (which already existed). The README now says when to run it, and that it wants a clean tree — same `GlobalProps` reason.

Losing the check costs little: `worker-configuration.d.ts` only moves when bindings move, and a stale one already fails `svelte-check` the moment code uses the new binding — a truer signal than an alarm that fires whether or not anything is wrong.

## Verification

Diagnosis confirmed by moving `.svelte-kit/cloudflare` aside and back: `--check` passed with it gone, failed with it restored, on the same unchanged file.

Then both scripts run in **both** states:

| | `npm run check` | `npm run build` |
|---|---|---|
| built state (used to fail) | 885 files, 0 errors | built in 8.44s |
| clean state (`.svelte-kit` removed) | 885 files, 0 errors | ✔ done |

`worker-configuration.d.ts` is untouched by this PR. Lint clean, 232 unit tests pass.

This PR is also its own test of the CI change — the checks below are the first run of `npm run check` and `npm run build` in the pipeline.

author: thefacelessdon
body:
## The defect

The Berd profile shipped in 0.0.46 recorded:

```yaml
owner_ruling: "PENDING — no Sovereignty-loop ruling recorded yet; this profile is
               validation output, not an adoption decision"
```

and validated clean. §9.12's Phase-7 gate says every `rent`/`mitigate` waiver *"matches a recorded owner ruling"* — but the check was only non-empty-string. **The gate was satisfied by a value asserting the gate's own condition was unmet.**

Same defect class as 0.0.45, one level down: the spec declares a gate; the enforcement cannot fail it.

## Why the fix isn't "reject PENDING"

That text was *correct behaviour*. The 0.0.14 guard-rail forbids an agent recording a Sovereignty-loop ruling on the human's behalf, and the profile author obeyed it — honestly, in the only field available. The problem is that free text can't be gated, so honesty and fabrication are indistinguishable to the validator.

So the fix makes ruled-vs-unruled **structural**:

```yaml
ruling:
  status: ruled          # ruled | pending
  by: "Harper (harper@face.works)"
  date: "2026-08-05"
  note: "Model-layer rent accepted; harness and state remain sovereign."
```

- `ruled` requires `by` + an ISO `date`.
- `pending` requires both be **absent** — a ruling is recorded or it is not; there is no half-recorded state.
- **The Phase-7 gate now fails** when a `pending` profile is reached through `conformance.claimed: true`. Claiming conformance asserts the tenant world is ready to be operated, which a rented or mitigated shell cannot be until its owner has ruled.
- **`claimed: false` with a profile declared** now validates the profile structurally *without* the Phase-7 gate. Validation output can be kept under review before it is claimed — which is exactly the Berd profile's state, and gives the honest `pending` state somewhere to live rather than making it unusable.
- `owner_ruling` is **deprecated, still accepted**, read as `ruled`. Every v1.5.0/v1.6.0 profile stays valid with a deprecation warning.

Both in-repo profiles migrated: Claude Code → `ruled`; **Berd → `pending`, and now structurally unclaimable until you rule.**

## Design note — the field is `date`, not `on`

`on` is the natural name and it is unusable. **YAML 1.1 parses a bare `on:` key as the boolean `true`** — the validator caught it mid-implementation, reporting `unknown keys: true`. The trap is now named in the spec, in the schema, and in a dedicated validator error placed *ahead* of the generic unknown-key check, so a future editor who tries `on:` gets told why instead of a confusing message:

```
[error] shell_sovereignty.waiver.ruling uses the key 'on', which YAML parses as
        the boolean true — use 'date'
```

## Verification

Five rejections:

| Case | Message |
|---|---|
| pending under a live claim | `Phase-7 gate: … 'pending', so this profile is validation output and MUST NOT be reached through conformance.claimed: true (§9.12)` |
| half-recorded ruling | `status is 'pending' but declares by — a ruling is recorded or it is not` |
| non-ISO date | `ruling.date must be an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD): "Aug 2026"` |
| the `on:` trap | `uses the key 'on', which YAML parses as the boolean true — use 'date'` |
| `ruling` + `owner_ruling` both set | `declares both ruling and owner_ruling — use ruling` |

Two acceptances: the legacy string (with deprecation warning), and the same pending profile under `claimed: false`, reported honestly:

```
[ok] RuntimeConformance: NOT claimed — profile checked as validation output on 'berd'
     shell sovereignty: harness=mitigate / state=mitigate / model=rent
                        — waiver covers: harness, state, model (ruling: PENDING)
```

## Process

Spec, schema and validator moved together per `AGENTS.md` rule 2. `sync-canon` re-run for the `PROTOCOL.md` edit per the rule added in 0.0.47.

`make protocol-check` ok · 60/60 tests · canon in sync

## Still open

- **The multi-harness hedge is claimed but never verified** (from the #51 review) — a profile whose `harness_options` are *all* `rent` validates identically to one with real alternatives, though FS-400.8 frames multi-harness as a sovereignty hedge.
- `bin/validate-tokens` fails on `main` — FVI-400 motion table.
- The "4 days" retraction missed three live sources, one of which is a release-readiness checklist item telling someone to verify it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jonnyeclectic
body:
## What and why

A cold `boost search` at real scale (458 taps, 71,600 entries) measured **0.94 s, of which BM25 scoring was 18 ms**. The rest was packaging: `catalog.all_entries()` parsed every tap cache on the machine (~100 MB of JSON, 0.32 s) to build a `live` map whose entries only the final k hits display; `_passage` windowed a snippet for all 39,726 scored docs to show 60 (0.11 s); and `dense.ready()` imported numpy via sqlite_vec just to answer "no vector store" (0.12 s).

`retrieve(entries=None)` — the CLI, MCP and eval path — now ranks off the index's own doc metadata, feeds the full ranked list through `dedupe_by_content` with shadow entries carrying exactly the two fields `source_rank` reads (tap, curated — from one `registry.list_taps()` snapshot, never a second config read), and materialises real entries for just the survivors' taps. The contract is **byte-identical-or-fall-back**: any survivor that fails to materialise reruns the query through the explicit-`entries` path, which is unchanged. Snippets window on returned hits only, on both paths; dedupe promotion copies the kept hit wholesale so the deferred raw snip survives it. `dense.ready()` stats the store before importing the backend. `_load_raw` keys its cache on `(mtime_ns, size)` — the stamp `catalog._cached_tap` already uses.

**Measured after: 0.94 s → 0.49 s cold.** The eval gate reproduces main's exact figures (recall 0.852 · hit@1 0.473 · MRR 0.605 · nDCG 0.657 over the 20-tap/10,152-entry pinned corpus) — empirical proof of ranking parity, not just parity by construction.

Complement of the shipped `cache-the-catalog-entry-set-across-rag-queries` (PR #114), which only amortised warm repeats. The v7 snip-out-of-JSON move stays deliberately deferred: the roadmap item (`docs/roadmap/items/cold-search-reads-the-whole-catalogue.md`) records the adversarial-review findings (migration clobber race, mixed-version reindex thrash) and the single format bump it should ride with.

## Checks

- [x] `make check` passes locally (lint · eval · test · smoke · mutation). Notes from the sandboxed run: the two `TestServe` functional tests fail locally on a sandbox `socket.bind()` denial (documented pre-existing; CI runs them), and mutation ran scoped over every changed function (~90%+ killed; survivors verified equivalent) with CI's full sweep as the arbiter.
- [x] Behaviour changes have tests. `tests/unit/test_rag_fastpath.py` is a full-Hit parity battery (ties, cross-tap duplicate promotion, kind filters, snippets) plus laziness pins (`all_entries` must never be called on the fast path; only touched taps load) and fallback coverage; `tests/unit/test_dense_ready_order.py` pins stat-before-import.
- [x] No third-party imports added under `boost_cli/` — the runtime is stdlib-only.
- [x] Layers respected: `core/` imports neither `commands/` nor `cli`.

## phaze-w84zt — decompose `routers/shell.py`'s two brain methods

**Score: 2.04 → 4.14 (defect score, improved — not a drop). max_ccn: 70 → 12. Both brain
methods gone.** Full before/after detail (including the history-based markers that
worsened as expected) is posted as a comment on phaze-w84zt; summary below.

Note: the bead title/description quotes an early "worst file in the repo at 1.0/10"
framing that a follow-up comment on the bead retracted as stale (coverage had not yet been
ingested into the index when it was filed) — the real baseline used throughout this PR and
its report is **2.04/10**, confirmed against the live main-branch index before writing this
body.

### What changed

Pure refactor of `src/phaze/routers/shell.py` — extract-and-name, not split-into-package
(the file has only two public routes, `GET /` and `GET /s/{stage}`, behind two enormous
private functions):

- **`_derive_summary_overview`** (227 lines, CCN 70, cognitive 73, 15 params) → ~15 named
  units (flow-tile builders, attention-queue assembly split into failure/capacity groups,
  a 3-stage recommended-action chain) plus a `SummaryOverviewInputs` dataclass replacing
  the 15-parameter keyword-only signature. No successor exceeds 53 NLOC or CCN 12.
- **`_render_stage`** (142 lines, CCN 31, cognitive 52) → one async context-builder
  function per stage (`_analyze_stage_context`, `_files_stage_context`,
  `_discover_stage_context`, …), dispatched through a `_STAGE_CONTEXT_BUILDERS` map, plus
  `_render_stage_fragment` for the three-way `HX-Target` fragment dispatch. Largest
  successor is 34 NLOC, CCN ≤7. The function itself no longer appears in repowise's
  findings at all.
- The five 4-operator `if` conditionals (original lines 471/500/508/516/524) are now two
  named predicates, `_stage_ready_to_start_work` and `_stage_paused_with_pending_work`,
  called at all five original sites.

  why broad is correct (their docstrings already explained the degrade-safe contract; the
  comment is now also right at the `except` line itself, per the acceptance criteria).

### Byte-identical proof (pure refactor claim)

Built a temporary (never committed) parity harness: loaded the pre-refactor `shell.py` via
`git show HEAD:...` as a second module, monkeypatched it into `phaze.main.create_app`'s
router wiring, and hit both routes through the **same DB session and seeded data** as the

body across **38 URL variants** — full page, htmx fragment, all three narrow-swap targets
(`files-table-view` / `propose-workspace-list` / `changes-workspace-list`),
history-restore, and the unknown-stage 404 — after freezing the one live
`datetime.now(UTC)` read on the page (admin_agents.py's "refreshed at" stamp, unrelated to
shell.py) so two near-simultaneous captures couldn't differ on that alone.

**Result: all 38 variants byte-identical.**

### Test changes

- `tests/shared/core/test_shell_routes.py` — **unchanged**, 62/62 pass.
- `tests/shared/core/test_summary_overview.py` — **updated**, not left alone. It's a
  white-box unit test of `_derive_summary_overview`'s signature, and the bead's own

  argument). The diff there is exactly three things: one import, a 3-line comment, and the

  `_derive_summary_overview(progress, **args)` to
  `_derive_summary_overview(progress, SummaryOverviewInputs(**args))` — same 14 values,

| Marker | Before | After |

| defect score | 2.04/10 | **4.14/10** |
| max_ccn | 70 | **12** |

History-based markers (**not** this bead's work, reported for completeness): change_entropy

- Full suite: `uv run pytest tests/` → **7103 passed, 2 skipped, 151 deselected** on an

  `phaze test database: 'phaze_w84zt_559db72d_test' on localhost:5433 (from

author: owenchen07
body:
> Stacked on #94 (review dashboard filtering) — this PR targets `INTS26-Support-Dashboard-Filtering`, so please merge that one first. The diff here is search only.

## Notion ticket link
[Support Dashboard Search](https://app.notion.com/p/uwblueprintexecs/Support-Dashboard-Search-3b310f3fb1dc800ab446f35396c77407)

## Implementation description
Search on the review dashboard moves from a client-side pass over the loaded page to the database, so it covers every applicant rather than only the 25 rows on screen.

**Backend** — `getReviewDashboard` gains a `search` term, matched case-insensitively against the applicant's full name:
* First and last names are separate columns, so the term is matched against them joined with `concat_ws(' ', first_name, last_name)` using `ILIKE`.
* The term is trimmed and internal whitespace collapsed, so `"  Jane   Doe  "` behaves as `"Jane Doe"`. Empty or whitespace-only input omits the clause entirely.
* LIKE wildcards in the term are escaped — otherwise typing `%` matches every applicant.
* Column references are qualified (`applicant.first_name`), since `users` also has `first_name`/`last_name` and would make this ambiguous if the reviewer join ever stops being `separate: true`.

**Where the term lives** — `search` is a field on `ReviewDashboardFilters` rather than its own argument. `reviewDashboardApplicantRecordIds` already accepts `filters`, so search reaches side panel navigation for free; a separate argument would have to be threaded through both queries and would otherwise leave the panel navigating rows the table isn't showing.

**Frontend** — a `useDebouncedValue` hook (500ms) feeds the settled text into the query while the input keeps the raw value, and the client-side `visibleRows` filter is removed. As a side effect this also fixes the next-page control, which previously stayed enabled when a search emptied the visible rows.

## Steps to test
1. Go to `/admin/review` and type a full name (e.g. `Talia Okafor`) into the search box.
2. Confirm matching applicants appear, and that results are not limited to the page you were on.
3. Try lowercase (`talia okafor`) and padded input (`  Talia   Okafor  `) — both should match.
4. Clear the input; the full applicant list returns.
5. Open DevTools → Network, filter `graphql`, and type a name at speed: one pair of requests should fire ~500ms after you stop, not one per keystroke.
6. Combine search with a filter and confirm both apply.
7. With a search active, open a row's side panel — the counter total should equal the number of matches.

Verified against seeded data (391 records):

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `undefined` / `""` / `"   "` | 391 rows (default list) |
| `"Talia Okafor"` | 1 row |
| `"talia okafor"` | 1 row (case-insensitive) |
| `"  Talia   Okafor  "` | 1 row (whitespace handled) |
| `"okafor"` / `"tal"` | 1 row (partial matching) |
| `"%"` / `"_"` | 0 rows (wildcards escaped) |
| `"a"` + position=Developer | 153 rows (composes with filters) |

Navigation ids matched row counts in every case.

## What should reviewers focus on?
* Matching is substring rather than strict full-name equality, so `doe` and `jane d` also match. That's a superset of the AC — say the word if you want it tightened.
* `concat_ws` + `ILIKE` can't use a plain index. Fine at current data size; if the applicant table grows a lot, a `pg_trgm` index on the concatenated name is the follow-up.
* The debounce is 500ms (top of the ticket's 300–500ms range) — one constant at the top of `pages/admin/review/index.tsx` if it feels off.

author: brickbots
body:
The 2.6.2 release notes described main as of #619. Five commits have landed since the branch point with `release`, and the notes covered only the lens ones (#624, #625, #628). This adds the other two and corrects two figures that #628 left stale.

## What was missing

### #622 — nearby ranking (ADR 0030)

New `## Fixes` section. The `BallTree` behind both the object list's **Nearby** sort and the chart's nearby-DSO marker layer was built and queried as `[ra, dec]` against sklearn's haversine metric, which reads dimension 0 as latitude. Separations were right only between objects on a shared meridian, and worse towards the poles.

Also covered: the `NEAREST_LIST_CAP = 200` window and what it costs the user, the great-circle staleness trigger replacing per-axis degrees (and `MAX_TIME` 2 s → 10 s), the carousel counting `_menu_items_sorted` rather than the source, the cursor policy (top row follows the pointing, a scrolled cursor pins to its object), and the `serialize_ui_state` truthiness fix that had been silently blanking the remote web interface's object-details view for every object opened from a Nearby list.

### #623 — observed-objects cache

One chunked, catalog-grouped query instead of a lookup per listing, and one shared `ObservationsDatabase` per UI process. Includes the measured numbers and why grouping by catalog code is load-bearing (SQLite will not drive a two-column index from a row-value list, so a single logged WDS listing dragged ~131k rows into every chunk).

## Corrections to existing text

Two figures survived #628's 13.04 mm measurement:

- the worked example in "Lens Selection" still said a 12 mm on an imx296 images **17.8°**. It derives **16.38°** — the table three paragraphs below already said so. The argument is unaffected; 16.38° is still outside the old `[8.0, 16.0]`.
- Known Sharp Edges still said the 12 mm's effective focal length was "the nominal 12.0 standing in for a measurement nobody has made, flagged in the data as `effective_focal_length_measured=False`". It is measured, and the flag is true. What remains open on #612 is the SQM zero point and the f-number, which the bullet and the follow-up entry now say.

## Also added

- **Why #628 mattered to self-heal**: at the nominal 12.0 a 12 mm unit fitted 7.9% from derived, outside the 5% identification tolerance, so `identify_lens_from_fitted_fov` returned `None` on every frame and affected units would have solved on the wide assumed gate forever without ever promoting. At 13.04 mm that error is −0.07%.
- The single-sample caveat on 13.04 mm, as a sharp edge.
- The failed-solve log line, which hardcoded `FOV est: 12.0°, max err: 4.0°` and had been describing a window the solver had not used since #609.
- `SortOrder.RA` gaining an implementation — the enum, the marking-menu branch and the "Sorting by RA" message all existed, but `sort()` had no branch, so selecting it announced a sort and left the list alone. Recorded as a sharp edge that it is still not offered in the Quick Menu.
- `ObjectsDatabase.get_object_ids_by_listings()`, the `get_nr_of_menu_items()` override, and ADR 0030 (including why it was renumbered off 0029).

## Verification

Every figure quoted was checked against the code in this worktree rather than carried over from the source PRs:

- the FOV table (imx296 16.38 / 13.71 / 8.26, imx462 12.44 / 10.40 / 6.26, hq 20.43 / 17.12 / 10.33) recomputed from `optics.OpticalTrain`
- the assumed-lens gates (imx296 `15.25 ± 3.59`, imx462 `11.57 ± 2.73`, hq `[8.78, 11.88]`) recomputed from `optical_train_for_profile(profile, None)`
- test counts collected per suite; **1,305 unit + smoke passing** measured locally, replacing the stale 1,285
- the `logconf_default.json` root-logger `ERROR` claim read from the file

Docs only — no code changes.

body:
## Summary

- 統計実行が完了すると、演習サマリ（Panel 02）が「演習統計サマリ」へ、演習詳細（Panel 03）が「キャラ別統計」へ差し替わる。単一実行の表示は変わらない。
- 演習統計サマリ: スコア統計（平均±95%CI・中央値・標準偏差・min/max・P05/P95）、日次ベスト指標（E[best-of-5]・日次ベスト中央値・75%/90%保証ライン・有効サンプル）、単発ヒストグラムと日次ベスト分布 F(x)⁵ の重ね描き、完走内訳、ブレイク回数分布、再現条件（seed・チャンクサイズ・Catalog revision）。
- キャラ別統計: ベストスコア上位N（10/25/50、既定10）比較、キャラ別与ダメージ（寄与率・上位N平均・共通スケールの分布バー）、ユニット別ブレイク回数（分位点の分布バー・0回の割合・帰属しない残差の脚注）、全run生データCSVダウンロードと統計サマリJSONコピー。

Closes #542

## Scope

- In scope: 統計可視化パネル2枚、上位Nセレクタ、手書きSVGチャート、CSV/JSONエクスポート、page配線、`UI-AC-043`・テストID台帳の追記、component/E2Eテスト、visual baselineの追加。
- 併せて必要になった変更: `EvaluationAggregate` へ試行ごとの出所（`runs`）とチャンクサイズを追加（`runs.csv`互換のCSV列に要る。連結後の標本からは復元できない）、`StatisticsRunSubmission` へ送信時の味方ユニット定義ID（列の名前づけに要る）。
- Out of scope: API変更（#537 で完了済み）、本番Cloud Runでの評価エンドポイント有効化（#543）、単一実行の表示。
- Rules: `Q-TEX-16`（サーバーは統計量を返さない）、`Q-TEX-18`（期限到達の部分結果）、`R-MEM-04`／`R-CFS-01`（帰属しないブレイクの残差）、`UI-AC-043`、`UI-API-004`。

## Test evidence

- Red: `pnpm --filter ui exec vitest run src/features/exercise/evaluation-chunk-plan.test.ts` — `merged.aggregate.runs` が `undefined` で失敗（試行ごとの出所を持たないため）。
- Red: `pnpm --filter ui exec vitest run src/features/exercise-stats/ExerciseStatisticsSummary.test.tsx` — module未作成で失敗。
- Red: `pnpm --filter ui exec vitest run src/app/BattleSimulatorPage.exercise.test.tsx -t "UI-CT-091"` — 「演習統計サマリ」の見出しが無く失敗（3件）。
- Green: `pnpm --filter ui exec vitest run` — 91 files / 1,122 tests passed。
- Green: `pnpm --filter ui exec playwright test tactical-exercise --grep-invert @visual` — 8 passed。
- `bash scripts/run-quality-gates.sh` — exit 0（darwin）。`ui:e2e:visual` は baseline が Linux 専用のため **skip**。
- visual regression は PR CI で検証済み。初回実行では 4 枚目の baseline が無く失敗し（既存3枚は pass ＝ 通常戦闘の画面に意図しない変化なし）、その run が生成した actual screenshot を `desktop-1440x900-statistics-chromium-linux.png` として追加した。追加後の run は `ui / UI Quality Gate` `Quality Gate Result` ともに pass。

## Documentation and contracts

- `docs/ui-design/01_UI要求・画面設計.md`: §5.4 の後続参照を解消、§7.4「統計実行の演習統計サマリ」・§8.5「統計実行のキャラ別統計」を追加、`UI-AC-043` を起票。
- `docs/ui-design/02_フロントエンドアーキテクチャ設計.md`: `features/exercise-stats` が component を持つようになったことを反映。
- `docs/ui-design/04_コンポーネント・状態管理設計.md`: 統計可視化パネルの state 方針（上位N は local state・列の名前は送信時の編成から）。
- `docs/ui-design/06_UIテスト戦略.md`: `UI-UT-STR-001〜004`／`UI-UT-CSV-001〜004`／`UI-CT-087〜091`／`UI-E2E-016` と visual baseline 4 枚目の方針。
- API契約・Event・Catalog への影響なし。UIの内部型（`EvaluationAggregate`・`StatisticsRunSubmission`）のみ拡張。

## レビュー後の変更（ブレイク回数の可視化）

初版は runあたりのブレイク回数を `0/1/2/3+` の積み上げバーで出していたが、粒度が粗すぎるとの指摘を受けて作り直した。1試行あたりの総ブレイクは20〜30回に達し（今後さらに増える）、しかも枠によって数回しか取らないユニットと20回以上取るユニットに分かれるため、畳んだ内訳では多く取る枠がすべて「3回以上」の一色に潰れ、比較したい差がまさに消えていた。

- ブレイク回数を与ダメージと同じ `min–P25–中央値–P75–max`（◆＝上位N平均）の分布バーへ揃えた。スケールはブレイク回数の全ユニット共通で0起点に取り、「右端に寄る枠」と「左端に留まる枠」の差がそのまま図の位置になるようにした（桁が違うので与ダメージとは別スケール）。
- 共通スケールは最も多く取る枠に合わせて伸びるため、数回しか取らない枠の箱は潰れて0との差が読めない。分位点から復元できない「1回もブレイクを起こさなかった試行の割合」を数値で併記した。
- 与ダメージとブレイク回数の要約が同じ形になったため、列の散らばりを `summarizeColumn` へ括り出し、分布バーも1つの component にした（`AllyUnitBreakRunCounts` は退役）。
- Panel 02 のブレイク回数分布も同じ前提で目盛りを間引く（上限8本・両端は必ず残す）。回数の種類が15を超えると数字が重なって読めなくなるため。
- E2Eの評価mockが列数をリクエストの味方編成から決めるようにした。固定1列で返していたため、2体編成のE2Eが「応答の列が編成より少ない」契約違反の経路を通っていた。標本も1体目18〜22回・以降0〜2回の偏りのあるものへ変え、visual baseline は味方2枠で撮り直した（同一定義を複数枠へ置いたときの列名 `#1`／`#2` も写る）。

併せて、JSXへ直接書いた日本語の長文を文字列式へ移した。JSXのテキストは行の折り返しが半角スペースへ潰れるため、整形のたびに文中へスペースが入っていた（`上振れが ベストスコアを`）。

## Risks

- CSVのユニット別列は編成順の1始まり（`unit_<n>_damage` / `unit_<n>_break_count`）で、列名に定義IDを含めない（同じ定義を複数の枠へ置けて衝突するため）。列と定義IDの対応は統計サマリJSONの `units` にしかない。
- 上位Nの再集計とスコア統計は最大2,000試行の並べ替えを通る。page側は `useMemo` で編成編集ごとの再計算を避けているが、パネル内の上位N切り替えは毎回集計し直す（実測で問題になる規模ではない）。

author: sailordave17
body:
Refs #12, Refs #121, Refs #100

Two changes for sun legibility, from digging into the photographs added to #12 on 2026-08-19.

## What the analysis found

Perceived luminance in sunlight is **emitted + reflected**, so bright sun adds a constant floor
under the text and the background alike. Modelling that against this repo's own palette constants
(`R = lux·ρ/π`) puts the levers in an order nobody would guess from the issue:

| lever | gain in contrast delta |
|---|---|
| clean / protect the crystal (5% → 2% reflectance) | **2.46×** |
| let auto-brightness reach the panel's sunlight range (600 → 1000 nits) | **1.66×** |
| darken the amber state | 1.29× |
| navy → pure black background | **1.02× — nothing** |

The brightness gain is exactly the nits ratio and holds at every illuminance tested (1.61–1.66×
from 20k to 120k lux), because the contrast delta scales linearly with peak nits and the reflection
floor cancels out of the comparison.

**Changing the background colours buys about 2%.** The prescription carried on #12 and #121 —
*"if any state fails, `Theme.kt` colors adjusted and re-tested"* — is aimed at the one lever that
barely moves. Amber is the sole exception, and it is the weakest state even indoors at 4.77 : 1.
That is why this branch does not retune `Theme.kt`.

## 1. The final-ten flash (`65afb23`)

The countdown numerals animated to `alpha = 0.3`. The trough is **2.02 : 1** against the red
background — under the 4.5 : 1 bar **in a dark room**, before sunlight enters the picture. In sun it
goes to roughly 1.07 : 1.

The pulse moves to the background; the digits hold full white and their contrast now *rises* at the
trough, 11.40 : 1 → 19.04 : 1. A whole-screen luminance pulse is also a stronger peripheral cue than
a thin-stroke one.

## 2. The brightness override (`ddefd45`)

#65 forces the panel to "maximum" during the sequence. #100 measured that this switches the
automatic strategy **off** and pins 600 nits, while automatic reaches 1000 nits at 7033 lux —
crossover around 3000 lux, direct sun 10,000–100,000. Above the crossover the feature written for
sun legibility was making the screen dimmer than doing nothing.

No app API can request the high-brightness range, so this releases the override above the crossover
rather than trying to ask for more, with hysteresis at 2000/3000 lux. Below the band it is kept —
worth up to 8.6× indoors — and a watch with no light sensor keeps the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

Neither #12 nor #121 is discharged by this branch, and both stay open.

- **Met** — *"digit contrast against the flashing red state is checked; flashing must not obscure the
  numbers"*. Measured at 2.02 : 1, found failing, and remedied. This is the criterion nothing could
  answer, because the digits were the only text on the screen with no contrast guard at all.
- **Deferred to #277** — *"either `Theme.kt` is adjusted and re-tested, or the audit records
  explicitly that every state passed unchanged"*. The numbers say three of the four backgrounds are
  the wrong lever (1.02x), and amber is the one exception worth taking (1.29x, and the weakest state
  indoors at 4.77 : 1). #277 carries that single colour change with the measurement behind it. It is
  split out rather than taken here because epic #196 records the owner directive *"the watch's
  colors, same colors for now"*, so retuning a state background is an owner call and not a side
  effect of a legibility branch. The same marker is on #12 and #121 in band.
- **Still gated on the watch and real sun** — the per-state photographs, and the wrist-glance test.
  This branch changes what those tests will be run against; it cannot stand in for them.

## Verification

- `sh githooks/pre-push` — all three steps green (`declared-surface` needs a real interpreter; the
  `python3` on PATH here is the Windows Store alias stub).
- 413 shared tests, 0 failures, on a `--rerun-tasks` run after the file-watcher reported a suite it
  had not compiled.
- **Mutation pass, 5 mutations, red counts predicted before running and matched 5/5**: dropping the
  flash-frame expansion (1), greying the digits (2), dropping the ambient hysteresis (1), letting the
  flash run past the gun (1), refusing on a null lux reading (1). Sources snapshotted outside the
  repo and the restore verified by sha256 — `git checkout --` here would have reverted to
  `origin/develop` and deleted the branch's work.

**Not measured:** that releasing the override lets this panel actually reach its high-brightness
range in the field. The mechanism is measured on #100 and the arithmetic follows, but the end-to-end
result needs the watch, real sun, and a `dumpsys display` read.

author: koeylp
body:
## What this changes

A just-sent image did not appear until the page was reloaded.

**Root cause.** The backend acks a message on the Redis buffer write and persists `chat_message.asset_id` in a **spawned task afterwards** (`crates/chat_realtime/src/broker/bridge_message.rs` — `add_messages_to_room` runs inside an `actix::spawn`). The optimistic bubble renders instantly and requests the bytes before that row exists, so `ChatMessage::find_by_asset_id` returns `None` and `media_proxy` answers **404**. Browsers never retry a failed image load, so it stayed broken until a reload — by which time the row had landed and the identical URL returned 200.

Proven in the backend access log, the same shape for every upload:

```
GET /api/v4/media-proxy/22270cf9-… 404   <- first render
GET /api/v4/media-proxy/22270cf9-… 404
GET /api/v4/media-proxy/22270cf9-… 200   <- after reload
GET /api/v4/media-proxy/0bd23c65-… 404
GET /api/v4/media-proxy/0bd23c65-… 200
```

Neither the `/api/media/[assetId]` route nor the stored envelope was at fault; both behave correctly. This is a timing race between *acked* and *persisted*.

Worth noting it hit **recipients too**, not only the sender: the message is broadcast from the same handler that spawns the persist, so another participant could also render before the row existed. A sender-only fix would have left half the bug in place.

**1. Bounded retry on media load failure** — the necessary fix, covering both sides. Three attempts at 500ms / 1s / 2s (~3.5s), then a graceful fall-through to the "preview unavailable" state — which `ChatMessageBubble` did not have at all before this. The policy is a pure, unit-tested module rather than being inlined into each component; the React glue is thin.

**2. Instant local preview for the sender** — the sender already has the bytes, so waiting on a server round trip to see their own image is the wrong shape. An object URL is held keyed by `assetId` and rendered for their own message, then handed back to the ordinary retry-hardened URL.

The lifecycle is the risky part of (2) and is handled deliberately: the entry **self-releases after 20s** rather than depending on component unmount, `register` revokes any prior URL under the same key so a double registration cannot strand a blob, and `release` revokes before forgetting. 20s is generous against the retry policy's ~3.5s worst case, so the handoff is not itself a race. No room/session scoping is needed because `assetId` is a server-issued UUID and only the uploading tab ever registers one — a recipient never has the bytes to create one.

## How this was verified

- `pnpm test:unit` — 33 files / 285 tests (from 31 / 269; +16, none lost)
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` clean · `pnpm lint` 0 errors / 610 warnings (baseline) · `pnpm build` exit 0

## Not verified

No live browser reproduction — that needs a real authenticated session and creating an account was out of scope. The race itself is proven from the server log above and the retry policy is unit-tested, but nobody has watched an image appear without a reload in the running app. That is the one thing left to confirm by hand.

## What changed

- adds a tenant-scoped, privacy-safe patient acquisition event model and durable schema
- preserves opaque attribution through public availability, booking submission, and appointment scheduling
- adds normalized source, intent, campaign, and landing-page reporting with funnel and drop-off metrics
- adds an admin-only Patient Acquisition dashboard in the Portal

## Why

Practices need to connect marketing activity to actual booking outcomes without storing patient identity or form contents in analytics. This introduces the focused acquisition layer that later aggregate integrations can build on.

## Architecture

The existing public booking path flows from IntakeService to SchedulingService, with booking approval handled in SchedulingService. This change reuses that path: IntakeService forwards only allow-listed attribution fields, SchedulingService records tenant-scoped idempotent events, and the Portal reads an authorized aggregate report. No parallel CRM or patient analytics store is introduced.

author: felipemarcelino
body:
Décimo primeiro workstream da Sprint 1. Depende do WS-10 (PR #14, na main).

## O que entra

- **E2E**: três mensagens fragmentadas entram pelo webhook e uma resposta ordenada sai no fake client, atravessando broker, Redis e Postgres reais.
- **Injeção de falhas (§38)**: reentrega pós-commit, publicação duplicada, perda de Redis no meio da janela, desconexão de broker durante publish.
- **Correlação (Q131)** atravessando fronteiras de processo.
- **Fixtures de containers** movidas para `tests/conftest.py`, compartilhadas entre suítes.

## Dois defeitos que só apareceram por escrever isto

1. **O agregador não tinha agendador de flush real.** `FlushScheduler` recebia um transporte injetado e só os testes forneciam um — em produção não havia quem publicasse o gatilho. Agora existe `RabbitMQFlushScheduler`, publicando com expiração por mensagem na fila de delay.

2. **`fileConfig` do Alembic desabilita loggers existentes por padrão.** Rodar migration no processo **desligava todo o logging da aplicação** — qualquer entrypoint que migra antes de servir rodaria sem log nenhum. O teste de correlação achou isso ao observar que nenhum estágio logava.

E um terceiro, menor: o caminho feliz não logava nada. Pipeline que só loga falha não é rastreável, e a Q131 existe justamente para que uma interação seja seguível ponta a ponta.

## Nota de teste

As duas suítes declaravam as mesmas filas com argumentos diferentes (tiers em milissegundos aqui, em minutos ali) e o RabbitMQ recusa redeclaração divergente fechando o canal. Cada suíte agora deleta e redeclara a própria topologia.

## Testes

**8 E2E**: três fragmentos → um batch → uma execução → uma resposta; todo `outbox_event` chega a `PUBLISHED`; mensagem de workflow reentregue não gera segunda execução nem segunda resposta; publicação duplicada consumida três vezes gera um batch; Redis limpo no meio da janela ainda responde com os dois fragmentos; broker fora deixa a linha `PENDING` e ela publica quando volta; e o trace da interação aparece nos logs do worker e do dispatcher, com os três traces de request alcançáveis a partir do batch.

`make check` limpo: 475 testes.

author: akiojin
body:
Closes #3684

## 問題

canonical Work への start attach が成立している session に対し、similarity 経由の `workspace.join`（candidates が提示する stale duplicate への join）が同一 container の duplicate Work へ claim attach を追加し、session が 2 つの Work に attach された状態になる。以後 `workspace.ensure` が「already attached to noncanonical Work」で fail-closed になり、`workspace.update` / settlement receipt / `pr.create` 系が生涯拒否になる（2026-08-19 00:17Z SPEC #3287 で実測、復旧経路なし）。

## 根本原因

1. `workspace.candidates` は「自 session が attach していない Work」を similarity 順で提示するため、同一 container の stale duplicate が最上位候補として露出する
2. `workspace.join` に canonical-container guard が無く、同一 container の noncanonical Work への二重 attach を無条件で許す
3. `workspace.ensure` は duplicate attach を検出しても self-heal せず fail-closed する（works.json は event fold の純関数で detach 手段が無い）

## 変更内容

- **AC-1（入口の遮断・3層）**: `workspace.join` に same-container duplicate guard を追加（canonical Work id を明示して拒否）。`workspace.candidates` から same-container duplicate を除外。event fold 層（`would_reject_session_attach`）で、他の incomplete Work に attach 済み session の同一 container duplicate への Claim を拒否 — rebuild 時に既存の汚染 store も治癒する
- **AC-2（self-heal）**: `workspace.ensure` が claim-provenance の同一 container duplicate attach を検出した場合、fail-closed ではなく `detach_same_container_duplicate_claims` で attach を解除してから進行。terminal 化した duplicate に残る汚染 ref も解除対象（実測で Discard 後も旧 session が復旧不能だったケースをカバー）
- **AC-3（consolidation 導線）**: `workspace.prune` に第3パス `classify_same_container_duplicate_works` を追加し、canonical と共存する same-container duplicate を検出して discard を提案・適用。ensure の ambiguous 拒否メッセージに `workspace.prune` への導線を明記
- **AC-4（回帰テスト）**: 実測インシデント（canonical start attach + stale duplicate claim → ensure fail-closed）を fold / CLI join / candidates / ensure self-heal / ensure 拒否メッセージ / prune の各層で再現するテストを追加（新規9件）

設計上、active な未 attach duplicate に対する ensure の fail-closed 契約（`workspace_ensure_docker_rejects_nonhistorical_or_current_paused_shadow`）は維持し、復旧は prune 導線に一本化した。Detach event kind の追加（intake 互換面の拡張）と fold の同一 container attach 全面拒否（歴史 replay 挙動の反転）は blast radius が大きく不採用。

## 検証

- `verify.run` PASS — record `vrr-ab75fde1459b454693a7f1c8f3d9602a`（owner #3684）
  - `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` PASS
  - `cargo test -p gwt --lib`: 2660 passed / 0 failed
  - `cargo test -p gwt-core`（全 target）: 全 PASS
- `cargo test -p gwt --test workspace_cli_test`: 38 passed
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p gwt-core -p gwt --no-deps` PASS
- User Verification: n/a（GUI 影響なし・CLI/バックエンドのみ）

## Rollback / Follow-up 境界

- 本 PR は単独で revert 可能。event schema・store format の変更なし（fold の拒否規則と projection 修復のみ）
- 既存の汚染 store は (a) ensure 実行時の self-heal、(b) rebuild 時の fold 拒否、(c) `workspace.prune` の duplicate discard のいずれでも治癒する

author: vzvince
body:
## Problem

The OpenAPI V1 `POST /openapi/v1/collaboration/groups` endpoint did not carry the `originator` concept that legacy `POST /groups` relies on (caller↔originator authorization). It instead gated the caller against the **driver** (`ensure_collaboration_eligible(driver)` in the V1 facade) and hardcoded `originator = caller principal`.

Two compounding issues:

1. The V1 facade checked **caller↔driver**, not caller↔originator — diverging from the legacy identity model and from the documented V1 intent (the `GroupManagement::for_v1_openapi` doc: *"A dedicated V1 instance validates collaboration from the selected driver, after the V1 facade has verified Principal-to-driver eligibility."*).
2. `for_v1_openapi()` was never set in production wiring — `server.rs` builds `GroupManagement` without it, so production V1 create-group actually ran the *legacy* core branch while the `bcs-app-group` tests ran the V1 branch. A silent prod/test divergence, and the likely root cause of the `create_group_auth_failed` symptom: with `originator` hardcoded to the human caller, the legacy branch also re-imposed caller↔driver gating on the driver.

## Solution

Add an optional `originator` to V1 create-group and authorize **caller↔originator** (self or a caller-owned Bot); drop caller↔driver. Give the V1 facade its own `for_v1_openapi` `GroupManagement` instance so production matches the tests' driver-anchored core branch, leaving legacy `POST /groups` untouched.

- **Contract/DTO:** `originator: Option<String>` on `CreateCollaborationGroup` (service-api) and on the V1 `CreateGroupRequest::Normal` wire field, threaded via `From`.
- **V1 facade (`bcs-app-group`):**
  - `authorize_originator` — admits only the caller-self (`human_<staff_no>`) or a registered Bot the caller owns (`created_by == caller.user.id`); else `403`. Stricter than legacy `authorize_originator` (which lets any human designate any originator).
  - `ensure_driver_is_registered_bot` — structural validity only (driver must be a registered Bot Actor); explicitly *not* a caller↔driver relationship gate.
  - `ensure_originator_can_reach_driver` — runs only when the originator is a caller-owned Bot distinct from the caller; requires the driver to be `public` or `friend(originator_bot, driver)`. When the originator is the human caller itself, the driver is ungated against the caller by design.
  - Removed `ensure_collaboration_eligible(driver)` from `create_collaboration` (the caller↔driver check). `create_dm` keeps its target-eligibility check.
- **Wiring (`bcs` bootstrap):** `GroupManagement` now derives `Clone`; each compose path (`server.rs:1966`, `:3353`, `:3966`, and the shared `build_use_case_bundle`) twins its legacy instance via `.clone().for_v1_openapi()` and feeds that twin to `build_openapi_v1_state` only. Legacy HTTP routes keep the un-flagged instance in every path.
- **Core (`bcs-group`) unchanged** except the `Clone` derive.

Net behavior (now matching the V1 tests, and production):

- `originator` omitted ⇒ defaults to the human caller.
- driver ungated against the caller; driver↔originator friendship required only when the originator is an owned Bot.
- participants stay driver-anchored (`friend(driver, participant)`), as the `bcs-app-group` tests already expected.

## Validation

- `cargo build -p bcs` (binary + all touched crates): clean.
- `cargo test -p bcs-app-group`: 56 passed — incl. 8 new originator-policy tests (self/owned-bot accepted; unowned-bot/unregistered/other-human rejected; owned-bot originator requires driver reachable; driver ungated vs caller when originator is human). One existing caller↔driver test was repurposed to lock in the dropped check.
- `cargo test -p bcs-api-http`: 29 passed — incl. 2 new DTO contract tests (originator omitted / explicit), plus a flaky unrelated JWT-logging unit test that passes in isolation and on retry.
- `cargo test -p bcs-group`: green (`Clone` derive regression check).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps`: red on **pre-existing** deny lints — `unwrap` in `bcs-service-api/src/core/group.rs:94` and `expect` in `bcs-app-group/src/lib.rs:887` (the state-machine runtime block), plus `collapsible_if`/`too_many_arguments` style nits — all in lines this branch did not author. The added code is `?`-based (no new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`); no new lint errors introduced. Per the repo rule ("limit edits to lines that must change"), the pre-existing lints were left untouched.
- Not run: the server binary smoke or `scripts/test.sh` e2e.

## Compatibility and risk

- **Wire:** `originator` is optional; clients omitting it see unchanged behavior (originator defaults to the caller).
- **Service-contract:** new `Option<String>` field on `CreateCollaborationGroup`; ~24 struct literals in `bcs-app-group/tests/v1_group_service.rs` were updated with `originator: None` to keep compiling. Only one production construction site (`bcs-api-http` DTO `From`).
- **Production runtime:** enabling `for_v1_openapi` for the V1 facade is the intended, test-backed behavior (the tests always used it); this change makes production match tests rather than introducing new behavior. Legacy `POST /groups` behavior is unchanged because it keeps its own un-flagged instance in every compose path.
- **No DB migration** — `group.originator` already persists in `bcs_groups`.
- **Rollback:** revert the four commits; the field remains optional at the wire level, so clients are unaffected.

## Spec

- Plan (authoritative): `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-v1-create-group-originator.md`.
- Earlier draft (superseded — assumed production stays on the legacy branch): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-v1-create-group-originator-design.md`. The plan's header records the supersedence.

author: china-sz
body: ## Background Follow-up to an engine state-model audit. Three issues confirmed in `core/runtime` / `core/adapter/llm` are fixed here. ## 1. `CreateApproval` swallowed persistence errors (bug fix) `Engine.CreateApproval` ignored the `approvals.Create` DB error (`_ =`). When the INSERT failed: - the in-memory waiter channel was still registered and `permission.ask` was still published, so the UI showed approve/reject buttons; - but `SessionManager.DecideApproval` resolves against the DB row (`Approvals().Get` first), so every click errored; - the turn hung in `WaitApproval` until cancelled. Now `CreateApproval` returns `(string, error)`, cleans up `approvalWait`/`approvalMeta` on failure, and the gate in `TurnRunner` fails the tool call with an explicit `approval could not be persisted: …` message instead of asking. Regression test: `TestCreateApprovalPersistFailureCleansWaiters`. ## 2. Audit trail for repaired LLM tool-argument JSON (new) The OpenAI-compatible adapters repair damaged tool-call argument JSON (unescaped quotes, raw newlines, trailing commas) via `repairJSONObject`. Previously the repaired form silently entered the flow and the original bytes were dropped — the one case that most needs an audit trail (the runtime rewrote model output) had none. - `port.ChatToolCall` gains `RepairedFrom`, set by both adapters (`parseArgs` now also returns the pre-repair bytes on successful repair). - `TurnRunner` records a `tool.args_repaired` stream event (`ToolArgsRepairedPayload`: call ID, tool name, raw arguments) plus a server log line. - Turn JSONL stays untouched: audit/diagnostic types belong to stream events per the turnlog whitelist contract (`turn_log.go` `Append` doc). Tests: `TestRunPublishesToolArgsRepairedAuditEvent`, `TestParseArgsCleanInputHasNoRepairRecord`, extended repair tests. ## 3. Removed vestigial in-memory `turnMessages` path (cleanup) Cross-turn LLM history is reconstructed from turn-log JSONL on disk; the engine's `turnMessages` map was cleared at the end of every turn and only kept alive for tests (its own comment said "retained for tests"). Removed: - `Engine.turnMessages` map, `clearSessionTurnMessages`, `commitTurnMessages`, `buildTurnMessages` - `salvagePairedTurnDelta` wrapper (`keepCompleteToolPairs` stays — it is the production pairing logic used by `enforceToolPairing`); salvage tests retargeted at `keepCompleteToolPairs` directly Net: −347 lines. ## Testing - `go test ./core/adapter/llm/... ./core/runtime/... ./core/store/turnlog/... ./test/integration/...` — all pass - `go build ./...` — clean - Pre-existing failures not touched by this PR: 4 tests in `core/service` (market/git/weixin) and `check-layers` violations fail identically on the base commit.

body:
Closes #57.

## Summary

Docs systematically understated the provider set (10 exist; README listed 7). This PR completes the registry (perplexity was the only provider without `register.go`), documents all 10 providers everywhere, fixes the wrong cells in the PROVIDERS.md matrix, and adds a test that verifies the matrix against each provider's actual `Supports()` so it can't drift again.

## Changes

**Code**
- `providers/perplexity/register.go` — registers the perplexity factory via `init()`, matching the other nine providers. `providers.List()` (with subpackages imported) now returns `[anthropic azurefoundry gemini huggingface ollama openai perplexity voyageai xai zai]`

**README**
- "Why Iris", Project Structure, Supported Providers table, and the import block now cover all 10 providers (+ `contrib/`)
- `providers.List()` example blank-imports the subpackages, documents the empty-without-imports trap, and shows the correct sorted output

**docs/PROVIDERS.md**
- Matrix: new **Azure AI Foundry** row and **Images** column; corrected cells against `Supports()` (OpenAI embeddings/images = Yes, Anthropic reasoning = Yes, Ollama embeddings = Yes, Gemini images = Yes); note on Perplexity `FeatureWebSearch`
- New **Azure AI Foundry** detail section (endpoints, Entra ID auth, env vars, usage example)

**Drift guard**
- `TestProvidersDocMatrixAccuracy` parses the matrix and asserts each cell: `Yes` ⇔ `Supports()` true; `Yes*` ⇔ `Supports()` true **or** any catalog model `HasCapability` (e.g. OpenAI reasoning on GPT-5.x); `No` ⇔ `Supports()` false. Runs in the normal test suite, so capability changes that don't update the docs fail CI

## Acceptance criteria (from #57)

- [x] Perplexity registers in the registry
- [x] README tables/structure list all 10 providers
- [x] PROVIDERS.md matrix matches `Supports()`, includes AzureFoundry and an image column

## Testing

- New matrix-accuracy test found and verified every corrected cell (it initially caught the OpenAI `Yes*` cells, which now pass via model-catalog evidence)
- Full `go test ./...` green (23 packages), build/vet/gofmt clean

## Out of scope

- OpenAI provider-level `FeatureReasoning`/`FeatureBuiltInTools`/`FeatureResponseChain` declarations (matrix documents them as `Yes*`; tracked in #67)
- CLI factory support for perplexity/voyageai/azurefoundry (#66)

author: akashlevy
body:
## Problem

The range analysis stopped at a flip-flop output, which is the one place a pipelined datapath cannot afford it. A dot product registers each lane term before the accumulate tree, so every adder in that tree saw an operand of unknown range and was priced at the **declared** accumulator width -- 128 bits where the value needs 40 -- while real synthesis charges nothing for those upper bits, all of which are copies of the sign.

Predicted area then tracks the declared width instead of the data. That inverts the cost ordering between two designs whose only difference is how wide their accumulator is declared, which is what a sawtooth in an area-vs-datapath-width sweep looks like.

## Change

`-cross-flops` bounds `Q` by the union of everything the register can hold: its data input, an async load, a reset value, and a defined init. Three details beyond the union:

- **Blasted registers.** A register reaches this pass split into one-bit cells in any flow that blasts flops for per-bit reporting, so no cell drives the whole word and the whole-output test never matches one. The word the data inputs form is reassembled instead -- but only across bits that capture on the same event, since skewed bits could pair a negative high bit with a positive low word, which no single reachable value of the data word allows.
- **The negation cap belongs on the range, not the register.** A 128-bit accumulator holding an 8-bit value is the case most worth handling, and a width test on the register is exactly what refuses it. The cap that keeps every endpoint negatable now applies to the range carried out.
- **An all-undefined init is the absence of one**, not "any value". That is where the assumption lives.
- **A forced constant is read in the word's own signedness.** An unsigned register reset to `8'h80` holds 128, not -128; folding it in as -128 under-approximates the low end of the union and can narrow an operand below the width the reset value itself needs. That is the second commit, with D8 covering it.

## Soundness

Sound for every state reachable after reset; **not** from an arbitrary power-up state, where a register that has never been written can hold a value outside the range its data input can produce and the narrowed operand reads only its low bits. Hence the flag, default off, and the `NOT equivalence-preserving from an arbitrary power-up state` paragraph in `help opt_signif`.

Group D of `tests/opt/opt_signif.ys` pins both halves with the solver. `equiv_opt` cannot answer the question -- its induction step assumes only that the two register words agree, and a value they could agree on is outside the reachable range, so it has to report a difference. So D1 does bounded model checking from a zero initial state to prove equivalence, then runs the same miter with `-falsify -set-init-def` to prove the assumption is a real one rather than an unproven claim.

## Tests

New Group D (`tests/opt/opt_signif.ys`), all passing:

| Test | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | registered products feeding an adder: off by default, 32+32 -> 8+8 with the flag, plus both solver checks |
| D2 | the same shape with the flops blasted to one-bit cells |
| D3 | the range crosses two register stages |
| D4 | a word split across two registers, with and without a shared clock |
| D5 | an accumulator behind registered terms keeps its feedback operand at 32 (B2 with the flag on) |
| D6 | a reset value that widens the union past the word, paired with a small one that does not |
| D7 | a blasted 128-bit register whose value needs 8 bits |
| D8 | a blasted unsigned register whose reset has its MSB set, with a small-reset control |

Nothing outside the flag changes: a flop is only indexed as a driver when `-cross-flops` is given, so with the flag off no new code path is reachable and Groups A-C are untouched.

Silimate/preqorsor#2253 turns this on in the flow and carries the measurement: over a 50-design block-scaled dot product family, rank correlation against asap7 ground truth goes 0.53 -> 0.98.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: hokiepokedad2
body:
Stacked on #731 — base is `fix/730-preserve-unmodelled-tracking-fields`, so merge that first.

The backend half of per-alarm delivery scope. PoracleNG 5.1.0 lets an alarm carry its own scope instead of inheriting the profile's single pin and area list; this carries it through PoracleWeb. UI is a separate PR.

## What an alarm can now say

- **Within N km of a place** — `override_location_label` plus a distance
- **Only in these areas** — `override_areas`, no distance
- **Neither** — inherits the profile, exactly as before

Modelled on all ten alarm types, their `*Create` / `*Update` DTOs, and the mapping extensions. Saved places over PoracleNG's `/locations` API at `GET/POST /api/location/places` and `DELETE /api/location/places/{label}`.

Delete surfaces PoracleNG's 409 `referencing_rules` rather than flattening it — the useful answer to "why can't I delete Work" is which alarms to repoint. Worth knowing: an orphaned label is *not* fatal downstream (`resolveOverride` falls through to the pin), so this guard is PoracleNG being helpful rather than protecting an invariant.

## The user-geofence problem, and why the fix is sound

`validateOverrideFields` checks every `override_areas` entry against `GetAvailableAreas`, which filters on `UserSelectable` for non-admins. PoracleWeb serves user-drawn geofences with `userSelectable: false` on purpose, to keep them out of the bot's `!area` picker. So naming your own geofence fails the **whole write** with 400 "area not permitted" — it rejects, where `setAreas` silently strips.

Matching does not consult that flag:

```go
// processor/internal/matching/generic.go:146
func resolveOverride(label string, ruleAreas []string, human *db.Human) (…) {
    effectiveAreas = human.Area
    if len(ruleAreas) > 0 { effectiveAreas = ruleAreas }
}
// → areaOverlap(effectiveAreas, matchedAreaNames): a name comparison, nothing more
```

`userSelectable` gates selection only. So the permitted names go to PoracleNG normally, the full list is written into the row's column afterwards, and state is reloaded (PoracleNG reloads on its own mutations; a direct write is not one, and the periodic fallback is 60s).

This is the same class of workaround as the existing `HACK: trusted-set-areas` sites and is tagged to match, so `grep -rn "HACK: trusted-set-areas"` still lists every reversion point. Verified against 5.1.0's matcher rather than inferred from the shape of the code.

## Where it lives

`UserOwnedOverrideAreaProxy`, a decorator over `IPoracleTrackingProxy`, not the ten alarm services. The outbound body already carries the areas, the distance and the tracking type, which is everything the decision needs; the service-layer version meant ten new constructor parameters, ten copies of the logic, and edits to every test that constructs a service. It also means quick-pick apply and profile import are covered without being touched, which is where guards have slipped past before (#548, #565).

`IUserAreaDualWriter.SetAlarmOverrideAreasAsync` does the column write. Table names come from a fixed allowlist because a table cannot be a SQL parameter; an unknown tracking type throws rather than reaching the query. Raw SQL with unquoted identifiers so it parses on SQLite for the repository tests, and `UPDATE` rather than the `ExecuteDeleteAsync` shape MariaDB rejects.

Uid resolution pairs on content for multi-row bodies rather than by index, because PoracleNG reorders batch responses — the thing `BulkUidRemap` was written for (#443).

## A regression this PR had to fix in #730's own helper

Modelling the fields broke five of #730's tests, and they were right to break. Once `Monster` declares `OverrideAreas`, every serialized alarm carries it as an explicit `null` whether or not the caller ever read it, so `PreserveUnmodelled` saw a stated value and let it overwrite the stored one — reintroducing the exact erasure #730 exists to prevent.

`null` now means "not stated, keep what is stored". Clearing is an empty array or empty string, which is what PoracleNG reads as empty (`normalizeOverrideAreas` maps an empty slice to nil, `nullIfEmpty` maps `""` to NULL) and the same split the models already use for `gym_id`. Both directions have a test; the clearing one is there because otherwise a scope could be set and never taken off.

## Tests

`UserOwnedOverrideAreaProxyTests`, 12 cases. Each refusal has its legitimate twin — all three incoherent scopes are refused, all three coherent ones go through — because a guard with only refusal tests is free to refuse everything and still pass.

- An owned geofence is stripped from the PoracleNG write and written directly.
- A mixed list keeps the admin area on the normal path **and** writes both names to the column, so the public area is not quietly lost.
- Admin-only areas never touch the database.
- An ordinary write with no override costs no geofence lookup — every alarm write goes through this seam and must not pay for a feature it does not use.
- A missing row after the write raises rather than leaving an alarm that silently covers the whole profile.

Full suite: 1915 passed, 0 failed.

## Not covered

Bulk creates that carry per-alarm overrides resolve uids by content pairing, which is sound but has no fixture yet; nothing generates that shape today (the Where sheet edits one alarm at a time, and bulk distance does not touch areas). Worth a test when quick picks learn to carry a scope.

author: darischen
body:
You asked what surfaced and didn't get fixed. Two things. One is fixed here; the other is blocked by your nightly run and recorded.

## The one I left half-done

ADR 119 created `market_date()` and applied it to `v_positions` **only**. Two consumers stayed on `CURRENT_DATE`, both computing the staleness the banner reads:

- `capitalscan/handlers/_db.py::trading_days_since`
- `web/lib/screen.ts` `META_SQL`

**Measured live at 2026-08-19 03:06 UTC:**

```
last bar            2026-08-17
staleness (wrong)   2 sessions     ← CURRENT_DATE
staleness (right)   1 session      ← market_date()
```

`MonitoringThresholds.stale_after_days` is 2 and the banner fires **above** it, so the wrong value was one session away from raising a full day early. That's the exact failure mode a staleness banner exists to avoid — and I'd written a comment saying so in the component while leaving the bug in place two files over.

`capscan_ro` can call the function; verified before switching the web app, which reads through that role.

## A guard, because this is the fourth time

`CURRENT_DATE` appeared in four places and got fixed in three separate passes. A class of defect that keeps returning needs a test, not a third careful reading.

`test_market_date_is_the_only_today.py` fails the moment it reappears in production code, **at any hour**. A behavioural test would pass for seventeen hours a day and fail for seven, which is worse than none.

Its allowlist is checked in both directions — an entry that stops matching describes something that was fixed and has to be deleted, the same rule `threshold_lint.KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS` follows.

Test files are excluded deliberately: `test_threshold_lint.py` reconstructs the pre-ADR-095 view to prove its matcher sees the string, and the guard quotes it in its own assertions. Scanning them would make it flag the tests written to enforce the rule, which is how a guard gets deleted instead of obeyed.

## Recorded, not fixed: `events.sector`

**NULL on all 13,479,819 rows.** `tickers.sector` has 502 populated, so the data exists and was never copied onto the event.

`v_events` gets it right — joins `tickers`, selects `t.sector`. `v_screen` and `v_screen_live` project the dead column, so a consumer reading sector off them can't tell "null" from "genuinely unknown".

The fix is a view join, not a backfill — copying onto 13.5M rows is a large write for data a join already has, and it goes stale on the next reclassification. **`cscan nightly` is running and CLAUDE.md forbids migrating against a live writer**, so it's an Open items entry. The web route's dead read is removed so nothing depends on the null in the meantime.

## Verification

    ruff check / format / mypy   clean
    pytest unit+property         1825 passed, core coverage 95.83%
    npm test / typecheck / build clean, 15 tests

- **6.1** `resolveCredentialRecord` requires `invoker: CredentialInvoker` at the type level and returns `ResolvedCredential`; D4 order: pin loud → invoker's own `user-oauth` → workspace-level rows in creation order. Foreign-pin and foreign-only cases fail closed with the re-exported `CredentialNotConnectedError` (matched on `code`, never message); nothing connected stays `undefined`.
