author: admaloch
body:
## Summary

**Phase 3 now explicitly supports one API process/container.** Redis remains the production ingestion backend and provides durable queueing within that topology, but horizontal API-process/container scaling is not claimed or supported.

This PR implements the confirmed queue/concurrency fixes from Audits #22–#24 under that architectural decision:

- Production Compose ships `uvicorn --workers 1`; docs and a deployment test guard against reintroducing multi-worker API processes.
- Embedding rate limiting is process-scoped and applied per embedding HTTP batch (thread-safe token bucket shared across RQ worker threads).
- Redis queue shutdown, spill-dir config, bounded DLQ, resilient `/status` metrics, and extraction/chunking offloading from the API event loop.
- Startup stale-document reconciliation retained for the supported single-process topology (no distributed coordination added).

Also includes prior branch work on retry/timeout hardening and ingestion idempotency (migration 011, provider timeouts, queue retry-capacity fix).

## Test plan

- [x] Targeted queue/concurrency tests (58 passed)
- [x] Full backend suite (662 passed, 4 skipped)
- [x] `test_production_topology.py` asserts shipped prod compose uses `--workers 1`

body:
## Description

Adiciona um guia de contribuição para o Tá Preenchido e organiza os templates de issue/PR do projeto.

Inclui:

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` com regras de issues, sagas, branches, commits, PRs, changelog e publicação;
- template de feature request com labels e assignee padrão;
- template de pull request com referência direta à issue;
- entrada no `CHANGELOG.md` no padrão com issue em `UNRELEASED`.

## Related Issue

Closes #3

## Motivation and Context

A saga de melhorias precisa de um padrão claro para organizar subissues, branches vinculadas no GitHub Development, commits granulares e PRs apontando para a branch da saga.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Validação manual:

- revisei o conteúdo final do `CONTRIBUTING.md`;
- conferi que o `CHANGELOG.md` segue o padrão com `## [UNRELEASED]`, seção `### Adicionado` e link da issue;
- conferi que a branch está vinculada à issue #3 no GitHub Development.

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

Não aplicável.

## Types of changes

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

## Checklist:

- [x] My code solves the related issue or at least one of its tasks.
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] My change requires a change to the documentation.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I have updated the **CHANGELOG** document.
- [x] I have read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed, or manual validation is documented above.

author: alex-bair
body:
**Description:**

After the `linked_collections` mechanism support was added in https://github.com/estuary/connectors/pull/5038, a user set up a capture with 40,500+ bindings and noticed backfill throughput was significantly slower than anticipated. Captures have never needed to work with that many bindings before, so it's little surprise that there are strategies sprinkled throughout the code that are slow at that scale.

This PR is a coterie of performance improvements for SQL captures so they're more performant in the new `linked_collections` world. The improvements are described in each commit along with benchmarks, but a brief summary of the changes in `sqlcapture/capture.go` is below:
- Avoid allocating in the sort comparator by comparing the `Schema`/`Table` directly instead of using `StreamID.String()`.
- Stop building a list in the main loop guard. Instead of using `if BindingsCurrentlyBackfilling() != nil` which allocated and sorted every backfilling binding just to see if any existed, we perform an exit early scan.
- Use an `iter.Seq` for the binding state predicate, requiring callers to compose with `slices.SortedFunc`, `slices.AppendSeq`, or returning early as necessary.
- Make the removed binding check no longer O(N^2) by using an existence map instead of scanning every binding inside a loop over every state entry.

On my machine, I measured the overall improvements as:
|   |  before | after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| per backfill chunk | 591.80 ms, 225 MB, 11.8M allocs | 15.73 ms, 655 KB, 2 allocs |
| startup binding reconciliation | 33.6 s | 10.5 ms |

Motivating Slack thread: [link](https://estuaryworkspace.slack.com/archives/C03Q2NRFKDL/p1787100817430129)

**Notes for reviewers:**

~~Additionally, I updated a stale comment that indicated a loop could be removed a couple days after a late 2024 migration. I _almost_ removed it, but Claude figured out that the loop is still necessary so `source-mysql` can detect primary key updates.~~

There may be additional performance improvements we need to make as captures start exercising the `linked_collections` mechanism and increasing the number of bindings

**Checklist:**

- [ ] If fixing a regression, I have linked the PR that introduced the regression: [insert link]
- [ ] If there are user-visible changes, `CHANGELOG.md` has been updated (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entries))
- [ ] If there are user-facing behavior changes, documentation has been updated (see [documentation conventions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SRC9VS9zyCzWl3n4HXHbc4wPB1eLxJHkA2rtu9ZNokM/edit?usp=sharing)), or the docs PR is linked here: [insert link]

author: local-variable
body:
Adds the dev-load-only observation harness that resolved [Settle the five live-session unknowns from the sale-detection research](https://github.com/local-variable/EMM/issues/18).

The harness is **observation only**. It polls per frame and writes *transitions* — bell condition, watched addons, the active Retainer, the retainer market container, and every Retainer's posting count, expiry and gil — plus listeners on both chat event streams. Polling was chosen over addon lifecycle callbacks because the load-bearing question was **ordering**, and separate callback streams destroy it.

Nothing here writes to the game. The one control that touches the retainer run at all is spelled out rather than folded into a general switch, and it takes a postprocess turn, reads it, and hands back immediately.

## Why it is being merged rather than left on a branch

It is the base for the write-path dry run specified on [Write path — the postprocess window and the first act](https://github.com/local-variable/EMM/issues/39), and the project restructure in [Extract the Core module and stand up the test seam](https://github.com/local-variable/EMM/issues/22) should land on top of it rather than be rebased over it later.

## What it established

Five of six unknowns settled live, and four claims in the research note were wrong — including the listener it recommended. The corrections are recorded in full on the ticket's resolution comment, which stands on its own. The load-bearing ones for later work:

- Offline sales are **not** replayed on the chat channel, so detection time rather than sale time is permanent.
- The chat event **misses the sale that empties a Retainer** — the one a bell-return notification depends on — so the log-message stream filtered by id is the correct listener.
- The market container and its parallel price array are populated at the postprocess instant, but the price array **lags the container by about 50 ms**, so a snapshot is only trustworthy when priced slots equal occupied slots.
- Market expiry is refreshed by merely opening a Retainer, so expiry is unreachable for an automated setup.
- The scheduler exposes no busy signal, so the conservative rule stands: do nothing at the bell until handed a turn.

author: actuallypanda56
body:
Closes None.

## What changed

The grill, the audit and the orchestrator now check a settled product decision against the platform
before it is built on.

The grill says it in the same message as the answer it questions, so the card never carries it. The
orchestrator does the same for a decision handed over mid-day, outside any grill. The audit gets a
sixth check for the same thing where the diff shows it, and `ask` is now the verdict when a diff
departed from a `grilled` answer *because* that answer fights the platform — until now that was
`hold`, which blocked the departure and left the decision standing.

Two triggers, and nothing else fires it: WinUI or Windows App SDK refuses the answer, or the app
would behave unlike every other Windows app in a way the person who asked would not have meant.
`.claude/skills/winui/` is what says so, and a recollection is not. Taste is not a finding.

## Why

The loop was built to obey product decisions and had no way to question one. A decision that could
not be built as stated would be written on the card as settled, and the audit would then hold any
PR that did the buildable thing instead — so the one agent placed to catch it was the one enforcing
it.

Nothing here overrides the user. They answer again, and that answer is the one that stands,
including when it is the one they already gave.

## Additional notes

Nothing in `CLAUDE.md`, which is at its 175-line ceiling. It also fails that file's own test: this
is needed when a product decision is made or judged, not on every task.

A named cost that is accepted goes on the card in the answer's own line. That is a deliberate
exception to the grill's "question, answer, never why" — without it the next session raises the
same objection and the user pays for it twice.

author: gustavo-cerqueira
body:
## What happens today

`generateSummary()` sends `max_tokens: 100` and `temperature: 0.3` to `gpt-5.4-nano`. The GPT-5 family rejects both — it requires `max_completion_tokens`, and accepts only the default temperature — so every request comes back **HTTP 400**.

`if (!res.ok) return null` throws the status away, and the function never throws, so the `Auto-summary failed (non-critical)` branch in `server.ts` cannot fire either. The result is a feature that fails 100% of the time and reports nothing.

Measured on one install before the fix: **198 recorded peer registrations across 201 MCP log files, zero `Auto-summary:` lines and zero failure lines.** It had never worked once. The p50 time from connection start to `Registered as peer` was 1.345s on a warm broker — the request was going out and being rejected; only the reason was invisible.

## Changes

- send `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`, drop `temperature`
- add `reasoning_effort: "low"` — reasoning tokens come out of the same budget, so a small cap can starve the answer
- add `verbosity: "low"`, strip markdown emphasis, cap the length at a sentence boundary; the summary lands in a `list_peers` table and the model otherwise answers in three padded sentences
- log the HTTP status and response body when the call is rejected
- log the exception the `catch` used to swallow
- log a 200 that carries no content, with `finish_reason`
- log when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is absent instead of returning `null` in silence
- request timeout 5s to 8s

Everything still goes to stderr with the existing `[claude-peers]` prefix, so stdout stays clean for the MCP protocol.

## Verification

`bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. Live against the API after the fix:

```
elapsed=1346ms
summary="The developer is likely working on the ez2set project, specifically updating
projects/ez_harness_dashboard/server.mjs in the dev branch…"
```

Failure paths, exercised deliberately:

```
[claude-peers] auto-summary: OPENAI_API_KEY is not set in this process; skipping
[claude-peers] auto-summary: OpenAI returned HTTP 401 {"error":{"message":"Incorrect API key provided…
```

## One note on the length cap

The first attempt cut the text with a sentence-splitting regex, `/[^.!?]+[.!?]+(\s|$)/g`, and it silently ate the opening clause: a file name like `server.mjs` has a dot with no whitespace after it, the match fails there, and the engine restarts past the text it already scanned. Output began mid-sentence with `", routes, middleware…"`. Truncating from the end instead cannot lose the beginning.

author: benhof
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip manages AI agents and their governed tool access.
> - The heartbeat runtime builds the MCP server list for each agent run.
> - The runtime profile resolver used only company and agent bindings.
> - An issue or project profile could therefore fail to restrict a broader agent profile.
> - PR #11605 adds local stdio connections to the same runtime delivery path.
> - This pull request adds the missing run context to profile resolution.
> - The benefit is an exact, narrow runtime tool list for issue-scoped and project-scoped work.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #11605

**What happened?**

A heartbeat run with an issue-scoped deny-by-default tool profile received the broader agent tool list. The regression fixture returned six installed connections instead of the five connections allowed by the issue profile.

**Expected behavior**

The runtime must use the narrowest matching profile. An issue profile must take priority over agent, project, and company profiles. A project profile must take priority over broader company profiles.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Install six tool connections for one agent.
2. Bind broad profiles for all six connections to the agent or company.
3. Bind a deny-by-default profile with five included connections to the run issue or project.
4. Build the heartbeat runtime MCP server list with the issue and project context.
5. Observe that the old code returns all six connections.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Parent commit `9ecc4ce2fa7ba9091e6640f1006b00fd436ce5a8` from #11605.

**Deployment mode**

Local development from source with embedded Postgres tests.

## What Changed

- Pass the run issue ID and project ID to runtime MCP profile resolution.
- Match issue and project profile bindings in `getEffectiveProfilesForAgent`.
- Reuse the existing narrowest-scope precedence function.
- Add real-database regressions for issue-over-agent and project-over-company precedence.
- Keep the local stdio delivery behavior from #11605.

## Verification

- RED: the two new regressions failed with six returned connections instead of five.
- GREEN: `npx -y pnpm@9.15.4 exec vitest run server/src/__tests__/heartbeat-runtime-mcp-servers.test.ts` passed 5 of 5 tests.
- `npx -y pnpm@9.15.4 exec vitest run server/src/__tests__/tool-access-policy-service.test.ts` passed 35 of 35 tests.
- `npx -y pnpm@9.15.4 --filter @paperclipai/server typecheck` passed.

- The candidate worktree was clean after verification.

- This is a dependent draft. It contains the commits from #11605 until that pull request merges.
- The optional project ID fallback uses trusted heartbeat run context. The primary issue path uses the database-backed issue and project IDs.
- A narrower issue or project profile now intentionally removes tools granted only by broader profiles.

> For core feature work, check [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md) first and discuss it in `#dev` before opening the PR. Feature PRs that overlap with planned core work may need to be redirected — check the roadmap first. See `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

OpenAI Codex with `gpt-5.6-sol` in high-reasoning mode. The agent used repository tools, Git, code execution, real-database tests, and an independent verification pass.

author: mutexdev
body:
From release run [32209615608](https://github.com/mutexdev/lite_api/actions/runs/32209615608).

## Linux — a self-inflicted timeout

Nothing stalled this time. `archive.ubuntu.com` was just slow:

```
Fetched 56.1 MB in 11min 42s (79.9 kB/s)
Selecting previously unselected package bubblewrap.
##[error]The action 'Install Linux build dependencies' has timed out after 12 minutes.
```

The download completed, unpacking began, and the 12-minute bound from c94df10 killed it **ten seconds later**. That bound was sized against a stall, not against a bad-but-working mirror.

A slow mirror is not an error and must not be retried into one, so the install keeps no timeout wrapper of its own — restarting a download that is progressing just discards the bytes already fetched. It gets room instead: 25 minutes at the step, job bounds raised to match, `Acquire::Retries=3` so apt rides out a dropped connection mid-download, and two install attempts for a genuine transient. The update loop keeps its per-attempt timeout, because a stall there still needs one.

## macOS — better diagnostics

When no `Developer ID Application` identity is present, the step now prints `find-identity`'s own listing and states the requirement, instead of leaving the answer in a hex attribute blob forty lines up. Identity names are embedded in every binary we ship, so there is nothing to withhold from the log.

## Windows progress

The `WritePrivate` fix in #3 worked: `sync <dir>: Access is denied` went from **65 occurrences to 0**, and Windows went 94 → 61 failures. It is 61 rather than 32 because clearing that error lets ~29 tests run further and fail at their real assertion.

The remaining 61, measured from the run log:

| Cause | Count |
|---|---|
| **Product enforces POSIX permissions** — `workspace migration artifact permissions are invalid` | 21 |
| Test asserts a POSIX mode (`mode 666, want 600`) | 14 |
| Other — PAC proxy, OpenAPI drift, JS require shims, concurrent rename | 11 |
| `file://` remote URL built from a Windows path | 9 |
| Path / drive-letter handling (exec path, `/etc/passwd`, `.aws`) | 4 |
| Genuinely unsupported (unix socket, terminal session) | 2 |

**35 of those 61 are a single unmade decision**: what owner-only file permissions mean on Windows. The product refuses to proceed at all — that top row is production code rejecting its own artifacts, not a test being fussy — because it requires 0600 and Windows reports 0666.

author: connorshea
body:
AI Disclosure: Generated with Claude Code, Opus 5. Tested and reviewed by me.

Ten call sites across nine rules checked whether an identifier is a specific global with:

```rust
ctx.scoping().root_unresolved_references().contains_key(&ident.name)
```

That asks whether the **name** is unresolved **somewhere in the file**, not whether **this reference** is global. Any file that shadows the global in one scope and uses the real global in another gets a false positive on the shadowed use:

```js
function f(myLogger) {
  const console = myLogger;
  console.log(1);        // reported by `no-console` — this is the bug
}
console.log(2);          // the real global, elsewhere in the file
```

`ctx.is_reference_to_global_variable(ident)` already exists for this and is used at ~50 other call sites. It is `reference.symbol_id().is_none()` — one field read instead of hashing the name into the unresolved-references map — and it honours the user's `globals: { X: "off" }` config.

### Rules fixed

| rule | shadowed code that was wrongly reported |
| --- | --- |
| `eslint/no-console` | `const console = myLogger; console.log(foo)` |
| `eslint/no-constant-binary-expression` | `const String = MyString; String(x) ?? y` |
| `eslint/no-new-native-nonconstructor` | `const Symbol = FakeSymbol; new Symbol()` |
| `eslint/prefer-object-spread` | `const Object = MyObject; Object.assign({}, a)` |
| `eslint/symbol-description` | `const Symbol = FakeSymbol; Symbol()` |
| `eslint/valid-typeof` | `const undefined = u; typeof x === undefined` |
| `promise/avoid-new` | `const Promise = FakePromise; new Promise(fn)` |
| `unicorn/new-for-builtins` | `const String = MyString; new String('x')` |
| `unicorn/prefer-global-this` | `const window = fake; window.foo` |

Each rule gets a pass test in that shape. Both halves matter — without a second, genuine use of the global the name lookup already returns false, so a single-scope test would pass before the fix too.

Three of these ship a fix or suggestion (`prefer-global-this`, `valid-typeof`, `no-console`), so the false positive was rewriting or deleting code the user owns.

### Real-world impact

Base vs. branch over four corpora (vscode, sentry, material-ui, actual), each rule isolated with `-A all -A nursery -D <rule> --format=json --no-ignore --disable-nested-config`, diagnostics normalised to `(file, span, code, message)`:

**0 added, 23 removed.** Every removal is `prefer-global-this` on a genuinely shadowed `window`:

- `vscode/src/vs/base/browser/dompurify/dompurify.js` (16) — `let window = arguments.length > 0 ? arguments[0] : getGlobal()`
- `material-ui/packages-internal/core-docs/src/Demo/DemoSandbox.tsx` (5) — `function IsolatedDemo({ children, cssVarPrefix, colorSchemeNode, window })`, a destructured prop
- `sentry/src/sentry/templates/sentry/error-page-embed.js` (2) — `(function (window, document, JSON) { ... })(window, document, JSON)`, the classic IIFE parameter

In each file the real global references outside the shadowing scope are still reported.

### Notes

- `no-console` uses `ident.is_global_reference(ctx.scoping())` rather than the context helper. An existing fail case pins that `globals: { console: "off" }` must still report, and the context helper treats `"off"` as "not a global". The other eight sites use the context helper, so they now respect that config, but this one doesn't.
- Five upstream ESLint pass cases that were commented out in `no-constant-binary-expression` now pass and are re-enabled (`function Boolean(n) { return n; }; Boolean(x) ?? foo` and friends). Two others in that list stay commented — they are `function foo(undefined) { ... }`, which is a separate problem: the rule matches `undefined` by name via `Expression::is_undefined()`. Left a TODO pointing at it.

author: melbinjp
body:
`ComposioHQ/composio` draws its repository layout in a fenced `text` block:

```
ts/                TypeScript SDK workspace
  packages/core/       @composio/core
  packages/providers/  Provider adapters
  packages/cli/        Composio CLI
python/            Python SDK and provider packages
```

`looks_like_a_tree` said no. Its indentation-only branch requires every line to be a single
token, and requires some line to END in a slash. Both fail here, because the description
column sits where the slash would be. So the block fell through to the plain path reader,
which took `packages/providers/` as a path from the repository root and reported it deleted.

`ts/packages/providers` exists.

**The trigger is why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating.** A path is only reported
as deleted when history holds a commit that removed it, and composio moved `packages/` under
`ts/` on 2025-06-16. A directory that never sat at the root produces no finding at all. So
the misreading fires precisely on the projects that reorganised, which are the ones whose
layout diagrams are most likely to be stale and most worth checking.

## Strictly additive

The new branch is reached only when the existing one declines, and it is confined to the
**first token** of each line: every one must be path-shaped, carrying a slash or a file
extension, and at least one must end in a slash.

| block | still not a diagram |
|---|---|
| `Options:` / `--verbose be loud` | first token is not path-shaped |
| `python -m pytest` | first token is a bare word |
| `alpha.py the first` / `beta.py the second` | nothing ends in a slash |
| `src/ source` / `build/ output` / `make run it` | one bare word among the paths |

`parse()` already read the entry name as `name.split(" ")[0]`, which is why nothing below
the detector had to change to understand the description column.

## Measured, not reasoned

- **106 of 110,615 fenced blocks** across 217 repositories newly read as diagrams, which is
  0.1%. Every one of a twelve-block sample is a real layout: scrapy, sanity, gsd-core,
  rustfs, SparkyFitness, llmgateway, hive and others.
- **68 repositories re-swept against recorded results.** Batch 10 moved exactly one,

author: ovaistariq
body:
Kills the eviction-suite flake that has failed CI **seven times in three days** across four PRs (#216, #219, #228, #229), each time costing a rerun cycle.

## Why the sleep could never work

The check reads the oldest keys to bump their LRU recency, then triggers eviction and asserts the bumped keys survived. It waited with `sleep 8` for "a few flush intervals". But the bumps are queued by the read path and persisted asynchronously — the batch is time-gated (`accessTimeLRU` + `DefaultAccessUpdateDelay`) and written by a background ticker — so the delay is not bounded by the ticker period. No sleep length is a guarantee; CI simply lost the race periodically.

## The deterministic replacement

`accessUpdater.Stop()` drains the update channel and flushes unconditionally before the process exits:

```go
case <-a.done:
    a.collectUpdates()
    a.flushBatch()
    return
```

So a **graceful restart is the guarantee** — no timing assumption at all. The access index lives in RocksDB and survives restart (the suite's own "Restart persistence" test asserts exactly that property), so what's under test is unchanged; only the synchronization becomes deterministic.

## Also fixed

`restart_server` passed `server_args` where `start_server` expects its `cleanup` argument, so the **first server flag was silently swallowed** — a latent bug that would have dropped `-disk` from the restarted command line. It now passes `cleanup=false` explicitly, which is also the only correct value for a restart.

## Verification

Eviction suite run 4× locally: LRU and FIFO protection pass every time, all 8 subtests green.

author: realsyncdynamics-spec
body:
| Commit | Thema |
| --- | --- |
| `a98c4ac` | Transparenzpflichten nach Art. 50 VO (EU) 2024/1689 (seit 02.08.2026 in Kraft) |
| `f74c6af` | englisches Impressum-Alias `/legal/imprint` als 301 |
| `f8a6c6f` · `fd54332` · `d9fa079` | Soft-404-Versuch, Loop-Fix, **Rücknahme** — netto bleibt die Prerender-Abdeckung |
| `c489c98` | Merge von `main` (`d8fe81f`) |

Vorab eine Korrektur an der Ausgangsanalyse: mehrere dort gemeldete Lücken bestehen nicht. `ai-disclosure` ist bereits vollständig verdrahtet (Synthese → Renderer → Blueprint-Analyse → Observation-Analyse → Remediation-Agent → Runtime-Scan), und die Ed25519-Signatur ist nicht „nur presence" — `provenance/index.ts:128` verifiziert mit `crypto.subtle.verify` und liefert den Public Key extern aus.

---

# Teil 1 — Art. 50 EU AI Act (`a98c4ac`)

## 1.1 Falsche Norm (13 Stellen)

„Art. 52" bezeichnete durchgehend die Transparenzpflicht. Art. 52 der finalen Verordnung regelt jedoch die Einstufung von GPAI-Modellen mit systemischem Risiko — inhaltlich eine andere Norm. Betroffen waren neben Kommentaren auch drei nutzersichtbare Disclosure-Texte:

- `src/components/AssistentQuickChatModal.tsx:212`
- `src/components/audit/AuditCopilotPanel.tsx:282`
- `src/features/governance/risks/RiskCenterView.tsx:282/284/384`

Die Änderung an bestehendem Text wurde nach CLAUDE.md §10 vorab freigegeben.

## 1.2 Art. 50 Abs. 1 — Offenlegung im Governance-OS-Chat

`GovernanceChatSidebar` nutzt `useAgentChat`, rendert aber nie `AIDisclosureNotice`. Die Offenlegung stand dort nur in der ersten Antwort des Systems — also erst *nach* Beginn der Interaktion. Der Hinweis sitzt jetzt über der Nachrichtenliste. Reine Ergänzung mit der vorhandenen Komponente, keine neue Optik.

## 1.3 Art. 50 Abs. 2 — maschinenlesbare Kennzeichnung

Der Renderer lieferte bisher nur `data-ai-disclosure` am Hinweisblock aus; der erzeugte Inhalt selbst war nicht gekennzeichnet.

Neu in `packages/siteos-core/src/render/renderer.ts` (Beispiele ohne spitze Klammern, weil die GitHub-API sie aus dem Text filtert):

| Ebene | Ausgabe | Wo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block | Attribut `data-ai-generated="true"` | am Wurzelelement jedes generierten Blocks |
| Seite | `meta` mit `name="ai-generated"`, `content="true"` | im Kopf jeder Seite mit generiertem Inhalt |
| Seite | `meta` mit `name="ai-generated-model"` | ebenda, Wert aus `origin.model` |

Der Block-Marker sitzt bewusst **nicht** am Wurzelelement des Dokuments: eine Seite mischt erzeugte und redaktionelle Blöcke. Der Hinweisblock selbst bleibt ungekennzeichnet — er stammt vom Builder, nicht vom Modell.

## 1.4 Publish Gate (`docs/architecture/target-architecture.md` §7)

`buildDeploymentArtifact` wurde von keiner Edge Function aufgerufen; es gibt noch keinen Publish-Pfad. Genau der Zeitpunkt, zu dem das Gate laut Zieldokument davor gehört.

Neu: `packages/siteos-core/src/deploy/publish-gate.ts` — Contract-Typ nach §7 im abhängigkeitsfreien Kern, `derivePublishable()` als **einzige** Ableitung (G2), `evaluateTransparency()` gegen Blueprint **und** Artefakt, `preparePublish()` als einziger Einstieg, fail-closed bei `backend_preservation: unknown` (G3), `evaluation_id` aus dem Artefakt-Hash (G6).

Gate-Verstöße sind bewusst **kein** `RuntimeFinding`: Befund-Codes und Scoring-Gewichte sind laut CLAUDE.md versionsrelevant, und eine Ja/Nein-Entscheidung darf keine Score-Werte verschieben.

Offen und in `target-architecture.md` vermerkt: serverseitige Auswertung (G1) und Persistenz der Evaluation (G5) als eigene Edge Function.

---

# Teil 2 — Impressum-Alias `/legal/imprint` (`f74c6af`)

Datenschutz und AGB haben je einen deutschen **und** einen englischen Pfad (`/legal/datenschutz` + `/legal/privacy`, `/agb` + `/legal/terms`). Das Impressum hatte nur den deutschen. Wer über `/legal/privacy` einsteigt, probiert folgerichtig `/legal/imprint` — und landete über den SPA-Fallback auf der Startseite mit HTTP 200. Ein Abruf ohne JavaScript liest daraus „Seite existiert, aber ohne Impressum", und § 5 DDG verlangt gerade die leichte Erreichbarkeit. Genau diese Verwechslung ist in zwei externen Prüfberichten aufgetreten.

**Am Deploy verifiziert:** `/legal/imprint` → 301 → `/legal/impressum` → 200 mit vollständigem Impressum im rohen HTML. Die Berichte lagen in der Sache falsch — Impressum und AGB werden vollständig ausgeliefert, es fehlte nur das Alias.

---

# Teil 3 — Prerender-Abdeckung (`d9fa079`, netto)

**`PRERENDER_PRIORITY_MIN` 0.6 → 0.4.** Die Schwelle ließ 26 der 115 Sitemap-Seiten ohne statisches HTML; die trugen im Roh-HTML Titel und Canonical der Startseite. Jetzt sind alle 115 gerendert, jede mit eigenem Canonical. Prerender: **115 statt 89**, 0 failed.

## Was ich versucht und zurückgenommen habe

Der Plan war, den SPA-Fallback auf ein `noindex`-404-Dokument zu legen, damit unbekannte URLs sich nicht mehr als indexierbare Startseite ausgeben. Zwei Anläufe, beide am Preview-Deploy gescheitert:

1. **Ziel `/404.html` → Endlosschleife.** Cloudflare Pages kanonisiert `.html`-URLs per 308 auf die endungslose Form; `/404` traf erneut auf `/*`. `curl` bricht nach 50 Sprüngen ab.
2. **Ziel `/404` (endungslos) → die ganze Site wurde `noindex`.** Der Pages-Build der Git-Integration läuft mit `npm run build` → `prerender:**safe**`, also nicht-strikt. Fällt der Prerender dort aus — und im Preview-Container tat er das —, liegt keine der 115 Seiten statisch vor, und jede echte Seite bekommt das 404-Dokument. Belegt: `/`, `/pricing` und `/impressum` lieferten `robots: noindex, nofollow`.

Punkt 2 ist strikt schlimmer als das Problem: ein Soft-404 kostet Indexierung für Müll-URLs, das hier hätte die ganze Site deindexiert. Deshalb zurück auf `/*  /index.html  200`, verifiziert am Deploy (alle Seiten wieder `index, follow` mit eigenen Titeln).

**Der Soft-404 bleibt damit bestehen** — abgedeckt durch den `noindex` in `NotFoundPage`, sobald JavaScript läuft. Eine saubere Lösung braucht einen strikten Prerender im Pages-Build oder eine Allowlist über alle 459 Router-Pfade. Beide Sackgassen stehen als Kommentar im `_redirects` und als Test, damit der nächste Versuch nicht dieselben Wände findet.

---

# Merge von `main` (`c489c98`)

`main` hatte mit #1095 dieselbe Datei angefasst wie Teil 3: `scripts/prerender.mjs`. Dort kam `stripRuntimeOnlyState()` dazu (entfernt Reveal-Animationszustand aus den Snapshots), hier die Konstante `PRERENDER_PRIORITY_MIN` — getrennte Stellen, konfliktfrei. Beide zusammen greifen sinnvoll ineinander: die Snapshot-Hygiene gilt jetzt auch für die 26 Seiten, die durch die gesenkte Schwelle neu prerendert werden.

Der Merge wurde hereingeholt, weil `mergeable_state` über eine Stunde auf `unknown` feststand und ein Reviewer nicht mergen kann, was GitHub nicht bewertet. Nach dem Push steht er auf `unstable` (mergebar, Checks laufen).

---

## Nebenbefunde (nicht behoben)

- **`prerender:safe` produziert im Pages-Build nicht zuverlässig Output.** Das ist der eigentliche Befund hinter Teil 3 und verdient eine eigene Entscheidung.
- `src/App.tsx:1041` rendert für „AI Use Case Registry" einen `EnterprisePlaceholderPage` („folgt in Phase 3"), während `ai_act_risk_inventory` + `AiSystemRegistryView` bereits existieren — Abgrenzung ungeklärt.
- `renderPage` nutzt für `/` durchgehend `seo.defaultTitle`; `page.title` der Startseite ist wirkungslos.

## Tests

28 neue Tests aus diesem PR — 24 in `test/siteos/publish-gate.test.ts`, 4 in `test/config/legal-route-aliases.test.ts` (inkl. einem, der das Fallback-Ziel gegen erneutes Umstellen absichert). Die Gesamtzahl unten enthält zusätzlich die mit `main` hereingekommenen Tests.

```
npm run lint    grün
npm test        3118 passed | 104 skipped | 96 todo
npm run build   grün (115 prerendered, 0 failed)
```

author: saucam
body:
Unblocks **#295**, whose `daemon-check` is red. The failure is not #295's fault — it touches no fleet code.

## What actually failed

Not an assertion mismatch — a `TypeError`:

```
undefined is not an object (evaluating 'Object.keys(server.instance._registeredTools)')
  at src/tests/collaboration.test.ts:2374
```

`_registeredTools` is a **private field of the MCP SDK's `McpServer`**. Reading it goes wrong two ways, and the second is what bit us:

1. It breaks on any SDK upgrade that renames or restructures internals.
2. `src/tests/provider-claude.test.ts:56` installs a process-global `mock.module("@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk", ...)` whose fake `createSdkMcpServer` returns `{ instance: { tools } }` — **no `_registeredTools`**. Bun's module mocks leak across files within a run, so whether this test saw the real SDK or that fake depended entirely on which file the runner reached first.

Locally `collaboration.test.ts` is 4th and `provider-claude.test.ts` is 14th, so it passes. CI's readdir order differs, and it threw.

## Why it's not #294 or #295

- #295 changes `config.ts`, `daemon/guard/*`, `session.ts`, docs — no fleet code, no dependency files
- #294 (fleet board) touched no `fleet.ts`
- the test passes on `main` locally, and both SDKs are lockfile-pinned (`claude-agent-sdk@0.3.220`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0`), identical local and CI

It's a latent order-dependent bug that surfaces whenever file ordering shifts — which adding any test file can do. #295 adds `src/daemon/guard/repeat-tool.test.ts`.

I confirmed the leak mechanism directly: two synthetic files in the same run, one registering that mock and one importing the SDK. Alone the second sees `_registeredResources,…,_registeredTools,…`; after the mock it sees `tools` — exactly the CI shape.

## The fix

Fix the coupling, not the symptom. `buildFleetMcpServer` now builds through an exported `fleetToolDefinitions()` and passes that array through verbatim; the test asserts on those definitions instead of reaching into the SDK.

That still proves what the old test set out to prove — that `pick()` **actually filters what reaches the model**, not merely that the constant is well-formed — while being immune to both the SDK's internals and the mock leak.

Adds a second test pinning the seam the split introduces: `fleetToolDefinitions` would be worthless if the builder stopped calling it. That one asserts only the SDK's **public** config shape, so it holds under a real or mocked SDK.

## Verification

- previously-failing order (`provider-claude` first) — **227 pass, 0 fail**
- reverse order — **227 pass, 0 fail**
- full suite — **2311 pass, 0 fail**; lint + typecheck clean

## Note for #295

Merge `main` into it after this lands and its `daemon-check` should go green.

## Worth knowing separately

`provider-claude.test.ts`'s mock is still process-global and still shape-unfaithful. Nothing else reads `_registeredTools` today (I checked — this test was the only consumer), so this PR closes the live issue. But the next thing to reach into a mocked SDK object hits the same trap. Making that mock mirror the real shape would be a reasonable follow-up; I left it out to keep this fix to the failing path.

author: kaeawc
body:
## Problem

[On Merge run 32199674792](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/actions/runs/32199674792) failed on **Validate Documentation Links** with `0 Errors 🚫` but **42 Timeouts ⏳**. Every timed-out URL is a `github.com` self-link — the repo's own issues, `actions/workflows/*`, and badge URLs. Lychee checks ~2300 links; the burst of unauthenticated requests to `github.com` hits GitHub's rate limit and times out (timeouts fail the job). No documentation link is actually broken.

## Fix

Lychee routes `github.com` links through the GitHub API — which is authenticated and not throttled — instead of raw HTTP scraping whenever `GITHUB_TOKEN` is present. This PR supplies it in both the CI and local paths:

- **`.github/workflows/merge.yml`** — inject `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` into the *Validate Links* step.

author: adinailson88
body:
## Contexto

O Lote 8H-B1 ([PR #247](https://github.com/adinailson88/classificacao-chamados/pull/247), mesclada) criou e testou exaustivamente `src/persistir_estado_automacao.py`: um helper que persiste uma unica chave de `dados/estado_automacao.json` sempre a partir de um worktree temporario no SHA remoto mais recente, sem `git pull`/`rebase`/`stash`/`-X theirs`/`-X ours`. Este lote adota o helper nos 4 workflows que escrevem nesse arquivo.

## O que muda em cada workflow

**`comparar_modelos.yml`** e **`multimodelo_classificacao.yml`** — nao tinham nenhum outro artefato Git proprio. O bloco antigo (`guard_automacao.py --registrar` + `git add`/`commit`/`pull --rebase --autostash -X theirs`/`push` com retry manual) foi **substituido integralmente** por:
```
python src/persistir_estado_automacao.py --chave <chave> --valor '${{ needs.guard.outputs.valor_atual || '0' }}' --aplicar
```
Nenhum `git commit`/`git push`/`git pull` restante nesses dois arquivos.

**`avaliacao_final.yml`** — separa responsabilidades. O commit existente passa a stagear **somente** `docs/dados/avaliacao_final.json` e `docs/dados/analise_erros.json` (`dados/estado_automacao.json` saiu do `git add`). Um step novo, que so roda se o commit anterior tiver sucesso (ou for no-op), persiste o marcador via helper.

**`transformer_ft.yml`** (job `persistir_estado`) — o commit operacional passa a stagear **somente** `docs/dados/bertimbau_training_state.json`, com a allowlist/default-deny do job ajustada para esse unico caminho. Um step novo, apos esse commit ter sucesso, persiste o marcador via helper. Nada mais no job muda: guarda, `valor_atual`, coluna O, `TRANSFORMER_SELECT=none`, separacao operacional/cientifica do Lote 8G-B — todos preservados.

## O que NAO muda neste lote (intencional)

`avaliacao_final.yml` e `transformer_ft.yml` continuam usando `git pull --rebase --autostash -X theirs`/`git pull --rebase -X theirs` para os **outros** arquivos que cada um comita (os dois JSONs derivados; `bertimbau_training_state.json`). Isso e aceitavel pelo escopo deste lote — fica para o fechamento posterior do 8H. O que este B2 garante e que **nenhum dos quatro workflows resolve mais `dados/estado_automacao.json` por merge textual**.

Nenhuma logica cientifica, o proprio helper (`src/persistir_estado_automacao.py`), `guard_automacao.py`, `dados/estado_automacao.json`, `dashboard.yml` ou qualquer outro workflow foram tocados.

## Testes

- `tests/test_estado_automacao_workflows.py` (novo): confirma estaticamente, para os 4 YAMLs, que cada um chama o helper com a chave e `--aplicar` corretos, o `--valor` referencia a saida certa da guarda, `guard_automacao.py --registrar` nao e mais chamado para essa chave, nenhum `git add` inclui `dados/estado_automacao.json`, o `git add` proprio de `avaliacao_final`/`transformer_ft` fica restrito aos seus artefatos, e o step do helper vem depois do commit do artefato proprio.
- `tests/test_transformer_ft_governanca.py` (atualizado): o teste que antes exigia `git add docs/dados/bertimbau_training_state.json dados/estado_automacao.json` agora exige somente `docs/dados/bertimbau_training_state.json`, mais verificacao de que o helper e chamado com `--chave transformer_ft --aplicar`. Os demais testes de governanca do 8G-B (permissoes, guarda, workflow experimental, artifacts) nao foram enfraquecidos.

Suite completa do repositorio: `906 passed`. `python src/verificar_artigo_congelado.py`: `21/21` integro. `git diff --check`: limpo.

Nenhum workflow foi disparado, nenhum acesso a Google Sheets ou secret durante os testes, nenhum push real para `main`.

author: mfethe1
body:
fix(desktop): stop the claude-spawn test reading a poisoned resolve cache

`claude_spawn_uses_the_probed_cli_executable` has been failing on developer
machines for a long time and passing in CI, which reads like a timing flake.
It is not. It is deterministic, and the determinism is easy to miss because
what decides it is test *order*.

`resolve_command` caches results in a process-wide map keyed on the **command
name alone** — `HashMap<String, Option<PathBuf>>` — with no PATH in the key and
no expiry. The test plants a fake `claude` in a temp directory, points PATH at
it, and asserts `configure_runtime_cli` picked that file up. It took the PATH
mutex but never touched the cache, so if any earlier test had already resolved
a real `claude`, the lookup was served from cache and the assertion compared a
real install against the temp fake and failed.

That explains the whole shape of it:

- **Passes in isolation.** Cache is empty, so the fake resolves.
- **Fails under `--test-threads=1`.** Deterministic order puts a poisoning test
  first — 2443 passed / 1 failed, every run.
- **Looks random in a normal run.** Parallel scheduling decides whether that
  test lands first.
- **Never fails in CI.** No Claude Code on the runners, and only successful
  resolutions are cached, so there is nothing to leak.

The leak also ran the other way: the test cached its temp-directory path and
left it there after `TempDir` was dropped, handing a dangling path to every
later test. The neighbouring `is_batch_shim` tests already carry a comment
about being written to avoid exactly that poisoning — the workaround was in the
tree, the cause was not.

## The fix

`PathOverride` (test-only, beside `lock_path_mutex`) takes the mutex, swaps
PATH, and clears the resolve cache on both entry and exit. Restoration moved
into `Drop`, so a panicking assertion no longer leaves the process with a
temp-directory PATH — the old code restored by hand before the assert, which
worked here but is not a property the next test author gets for free.

The rest of the PATH-mutating tests were audited and are fine: they either call
`resolve_command_uncached` deliberately, or use command names unique to the
test, or resolve nothing. This was the only one on the cached path, so the
change is one test plus the shared guard.

## Verification

x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, `cargo test --manifest-path desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
--lib -- --test-threads=1` — deterministic order, so this is a before/after, not
a sample:

- before: **2443 passed, 1 failed**
- after: **2444 passed, 0 failed**

`claude` resolves on this machine (`AppData\Roaming\npm\claude.ps1`), which is
the precondition CI lacks and developers have.

author: blakematthews-dev
body:
## Why

Targets `fix/develop-traversal-commit-lint` so **#447 stays the merge vehicle** for the baseline restoration.

The core-test failure was extracted by reproducing the suite locally rather than through the Actions log endpoint. The exact failing assertion is:

```
pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for DurableRunRecord
  Value error, adjacent TraversalCommits must link resulting and prior state hashes
```

**It is a `develop` regression.** It reproduces on develop's tip (`7e29554a`) with 22 core-test failures, all in `graph/durable_runs` and `runs/`. #447's remaining production diff is not what breaks it.

### The root cause is broader than #447's description states

#447's body attributes this to pause/wait/HITL. That is not what the failing tests hit. The canonical failure is `test_run_sync_dag_completes_in_one_walk` — a plain two-node synchronous DAG with **no pause, wait, or HITL anywhere in the walk**.

Instrumenting the real failing run to diff commit #1's resulting state against commit #2's prior state gives exactly one field:

```
### DIFFERS: visit_counts
  commit1.resulting: {"n1": 1}
  commit2.prior    : {"n1": 1, "n2": 1}
```

`_ensure_frontier_node_runs` materializes the next frontier's NodeRuns and durably checkpoints a `graph_state` with bumped `visit_counts`. Since `graph_state_hash` digests the *entire* `GraphExecutionState` dump, that ordinary mutation lands between commit N's resulting state and commit N+1's prior state, so adjacent commits cannot hash-link. Every multi-node walk fails record validation.

**#447's `TraversalCheckpoint` bridge is the correct repair** — it keys off a pre-advance state-hash difference rather than off pause specifically, so it already covers this ordinary path. Verified independently: 22 failures → 0.

### What this PR contains

One test. No production change.

The existing bridge coverage exercises only the HITL metadata case, so a regression that reintroduced direct adjacent linking for non-pause frontiers would pass the named tests and only show up as 22 mysterious failures elsewhere. This adds an end-to-end test asserting that a plain sync DAG walk produces two commits, that the second *cannot* link directly to the first, and that it is bridged by a persisted `TraversalCheckpoint` whose state hash matches the commit's prior state.

Rebased onto #447's current head (`f72adcda`). Earlier revisions of this branch also carried a `ruff format` fix, the `pr447-core-diagnostic.yml` removal, and a test-side `mappingproxy` workaround — all three were solved in parallel on #447 itself, and the `_freeze_json` production fix in `20996aeb` is the better answer to the third, so they were dropped rather than duplicated.

### Note for follow-up (not changed here)

`_checkpoint_bridge` verifies `checkpoint.state_hash == commit.prior_state_hash`, but never verifies the checkpoint chains back to the *previous commit's* `resulting_state_hash`. A checkpoint can therefore bridge from arbitrary state, which weakens the provenance guarantee the commit chain is meant to provide. Flagging rather than changing it — it is a contract question, not a blocker for restoring the baseline.

## Feature freeze (until `v1.0.0` is tagged)

- [ ] This PR is a **tracked item** in [`docs/product/V1-RELEASE-PLAN.md`](../docs/product/V1-RELEASE-PLAN.md) — workstream/item: `____`
- [x] …or it is a **stabilization / deployability fix** for a tracked item (allowed). New features are not.

## Checks

- [x] Base branch is `fix/develop-traversal-commit-lint` — deliberately stacked onto #447 so that PR remains the single merge vehicle into `develop` per [`ADR-095`](../docs/adr/ADR-095-four-tier-branch-model.md)
- [x] Tests at the right layer per [`ADR-032`](../docs/adr/ADR-032-contracts-as-acceptance-criteria.md)
- [x] No decision or doc claim changes — the bridge contract is unchanged

### Local verification on `f72adcda` + this test

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| core suite | **6199 passed, 0 failed** |
| `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` | pass |
| `mypy` (9 packages) / `mypy --strict` core | pass |

Only `maistro-evolve/tests/benchmarks/test_swebench.py` (2 tests) fails locally, solely because this container has no Docker socket (`dial unix /var/run/docker.sock`). Unrelated to this diff; passes on GitHub runners.

author: merrickphan
body:
Three findings from @merrickphan, all correct.

## "Can these all be 100%?"

They could. Four of six components were presence checks — `thesis` 20/20 for a thesis-shaped paragraph in the first third, `conclusion` 10/10 for a last paragraph labelled one. Two now carry a quality axis:

- **`topic-not-thesis`** halves the thesis. "This essay will discuss the effects of X" has oriented the reader and claimed nothing. Half rather than zero — the paragraph *is* in the right place.
- **`summary-without-point`** vetoes `statesClaim`, so a paragraph that only relays sources stops counting toward governing claims.

Both compound with the existing positional halvings.

**This narrows the saturation; it does not remove it.** `warrant` and `governingClaims` still read a role vector that is marker matching whenever the relay classifier is unavailable — which is always, because `classify-structure` is not deployed. A draft can still max `warrant` by writing "therefore" once per paragraph. That remains the largest lever in this feature and it is already written (`ai/structureClassifier.ts`, relay `feat/classify-structure`).

## "How is the support 0%, relevance 0%, recency 0, and quality 0?"

Because all four are computed over the sources that cleared the relevance floor, and none did. A `0` meaning *nothing was read* rendered identically to a `0` meaning *the literature is against you* — over a correctly cited biographical sentence.

`problemKindsFor` has drawn exactly this distinction since 2026-08-16 (`nothingFound` gates `cited-unverified`). The score display never got the same treatment, so the accusation the problem kinds refuse to make was being made by the number underneath them. There is now no number, no track and no metric grid in that state — the card says what was searched and that those four indexes hold scholarly articles.

## "Obviously by the end, it is completely supported by everything above"

`new-claim-in-conclusion` fired on any detected claim in the closing paragraph — the one move a conclusion exists to make. Now gated on `conclusionDrawsOnBody`, measured as vocabulary overlap with everything above it, at a deliberately low bar (half). A false positive here tells a student to delete the best sentence in their essay.

## On the word lists

`summary-without-point` is structural, not lexical. Counting sourced sentences backstopped by a reasoning-marker regex was the first version, and it flagged a paragraph closing *"the agreement between two biographers working from different archives is what makes the figure usable"*. Every word added to catch that widens a pattern used to **excuse** a paragraph. It now asks whether the writer contributed any sentence of their own at all.

## Measured

- 895 unit tests, 17 e2e, typecheck and build clean.
- The Hepburn essay is **unchanged at 78** with identical components — none of the new rules fire on it.
- Verified in the harness: that biographical sentence draws no score, no track, no metric grid, no horizontal overflow.

## What

Adds a PascalCase naming policy to `Meziantou.Framework.Yaml`:

- `YamlKnownNamingPolicy.PascalCase = 6` (appended, so existing values keep their numbers)

- The source generator compiles the naming policy files via explicit `<Compile Include>` items, so `YamlPascalCaseNamingPolicy.cs` also had to be linked in `Meziantou.Framework.Yaml.SourceGenerator.csproj`; without it the generator project fails to build.

### CI/regression gates

author: bonemantgrm
body:
## Production failure

The current Spanish Comprehensive run reaches final assessment-report generation at 83% and then fails closed with:

`v2_production_publication_failed:ValueError:unrecognized Spanish presentation contract: Technical maturity remains based on exact-commit technical controls. Evidence-Adjusted readiness is 93/100 versus technical maturity 93/100. NICO retains 639 review-required candid...`

English report generation completes.

## Root cause

The Spanish v87 renderer already has the exact dynamic translation contract for the observed 93/93, 639-review-candidate summary, and the existing regression uses that exact production-shaped sentence. The failure is therefore not a missing translation.

The remaining defect is soft-whitespace drift. v87's structured contracts intentionally use full-match validation, but multiline values are split on CR/LF before structured matching. If production wraps the otherwise valid summary across a newline or repeated whitespace, the first fragment starts with a protected structural prefix but cannot satisfy the full sentence regex, so the fail-closed guard raises `unrecognized Spanish presentation contract`.

That explains why the same visible sentence passes the single-line regression but fails in production.

## Fix

- Keep v87's strict full-match/fail-closed contract unchanged.
- At the already late-bound v88 Spanish compatibility boundary, collapse soft whitespace only when the normalized value is independently recognized by v87's authoritative structured translator.
- Feed that recognized normalized English contract back through the canonical field translator so existing field validation remains active.
- On the secondary presentation surface, pass the v87-produced Spanish value through the existing surface guard.
- Unknown or changed structured prose is delegated unchanged and still fails closed.
- No global translation/replacement loops are expanded.
- English rendering is untouched.

## Regression coverage

Adds the exact 93/93, 639-review-candidate production summary with embedded line wrapping and proves:

- canonical Spanish translation completes;
- the secondary presentation surface completes;
- normalized input reaches the existing translator without CR/LF drift;
- an unknown soft-wrapped contract still raises the existing fail-closed `unrecognized Spanish presentation contract` error;
- rollback, exit-criteria, detached-worker reassertion, English behavior, human-review, and blocked-delivery boundaries remain intact.

## Preserved boundaries

No score, evidence, finding, candidate, authorization, approval, persistence, or delivery semantics change. Client delivery remains blocked until authorized human approval. Existing failed runs remain immutable historical evidence.

## Production closure

After merge and exact-SHA deployment, recover/rerun the blocked Spanish Comprehensive assessment. It must advance past final report generation, produce the same report truth as English in `es-MX`, reach human review, and remain blocked from client delivery until approval.

author: miere
body:
Pure refactor — no backend gains or loses a heartbeat here. Groundwork for #116.

## Why

`ToolWatcher`, `ErrToolCeiling` and the timing defaults lived in `internal/agent/acp`, which was fine while ACP was the only backend with a heartbeat. #116 gives the claudecode backend one, and a second copy would be a copy of precisely the thing that must not drift.

**The ceiling error is the sharper reason.** `internal/slack/gateway` matched:

```go
errors.Is(event.Error, acp.ErrToolCeiling)
```

to drop a session binding whose agent cannot be told to stop. That behaviour isn't ACP's — it's what the relay owes *any* backend that can't cancel an in-flight tool. Keyed on an ACP-owned value, a claudecode ceiling would have rendered as a plain turn failure and silently left a wedged session bound.

## What moved

`ToolWatcher`, `ErrToolCeiling`, `DefaultToolHeartbeatInterval`, `DefaultToolCeiling` → `internal/agent`. The relay now matches the backend-neutral error.

The **intervals** move deliberately, not just for tidiness: `AGENTS.md`'s backend-parity rule says the user-visible experience must not depend on which backend answers, and a tool reaped at 90s on one backend and 10min on another is exactly that dependency.

`acp.ErrToolCeiling` stays as an alias so this package's own callers read naturally. Same value, so `errors.Is` against either name matches both — nothing downstream needed touching.

`TaskStatus.Terminal()` replaces the package-local `isTerminalToolStatus`. It belongs on the type: whether a status ends a tool call is a property of the status, not of whoever is watching it.

## Tests

The watcher's own tests move to `internal/agent` alongside it, plus coverage for two things not previously asserted: the empty-id drop (an anonymous update must not collapse into one phantom tool that never retires) and `Terminal()` (an *unrecognised* status must not silently retire a running tool).

`acp` keeps the tests that are genuinely about ACP's *use* of the watcher.

`go build`, `go vet`, `archcheck`, and `go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/slack/gateway/...` all clean.

author: martin-ez
body:
`MapTile` stored its position as a `Vec2` of floats, so the coordinates design invariant 3 calls the truth were themselves carrying rounding, and every system built on adjacency would have inherited it.

Tiles now hold integer axial coordinates, and `world_position` is the one conversion out of them. The half-width shift on odd rows is no longer a special case inside that conversion — it falls out of the axial-to-pixel formula — so the parity branch is gone and the grid stands where it stood.

A `neighbours()` accessor is deliberately not here. This is a binary crate built under `-D warnings`, nothing can call such a method until #3 places a building on a tile, and a method whose only callers are behind `#[cfg(test)]` is a `dead_code` error rather than a warning. The adjacency the issue asks for is held instead by a test that names the six axial steps as integers, and the accessor can land with the first consumer that needs it.

### Changes

- `MapTile` stores `HexCoordinates { q: i32, r: i32 }` in place of a `Vec2`.
- `world_position` derives the world `Vec3` from those integers, with no parity branch and no epsilon.
- `HexCoordinates::from_offset_row` builds them from the offset-row rectangle `setup` walks, keeping the map's shape where it is generated.

Tracks #30

Fixed a bug in `make_annotated_video.m` where it was attempting to read non-existent struct fields `kin.v_smooth` and `kin.z_smooth`. These are internal variable names inside `kd_kinematics`, not actual struct fields. The correct field names are `kin.v` and `kin.z`.

## Changes
- **src/make_annotated_video.m**: Updated field references from `kin.v_smooth` → `kin.v` and `kin.z_smooth` → `kin.z`, with explanatory comments
- **docs/QUANTITIES.md**: Added documentation table clarifying the mapping between internal variable names and saved struct field names, including the note about this bug

## Details
The `kd_kinematics` function saves smoothed velocity as `kin.v` and depth as `kin.z` (aliased from `kin.depthRod_cm`). The variables `v_smooth` and `z_rod` are local variables within `kd_kinematics` and were never struct fields. Reading `kin.v_smooth` or `kin.z_smooth` would return nothing, causing the video annotation to fail silently. This fix ensures the correct fields are accessed.

- **`curation/faction-map.json`**: `detail_source_faction_code` added to all 30 records —

  feature's own authoring rule (an entry without it would be adopted into every Space Marine
  chapter's scope and collapse six per-chapter identifiers into one).

**This PR must merge AFTER its sibling, `009-release-1-pr-a` (#27).** Confirmed by hand this
session: this PR's `curation/faction-map.json` content fails JSON-Schema validation against

author: oxoxdev
body:
## Summary

Two backend defects in the workflow editor stack, both about a save that looks fine but isn't:

- **Config accepted at save, fails at run.** The per-kind config gate had arms only for `condition`/`http_request`/`switch`/`tool_call`, then `_ => {}` — so a `transform` with no `config.set`, a `split_out` with no `config.path`, a bad-typed `output_parser`, a non-URL `http_request.url`, or a `sub_workflow.workflow_id` that names no saved workflow all saved clean and were silent no-ops (or hard failures) at run. Now every kind is validated at save.
- **Errors were an unstructured blob.** Every 400 flattened problems with `join(" ")` into one string with no field paths, and the edge validator named the edge by *index* (`edge #N starts at \`old-id\``) not by the node. Now a new `WorkflowInvalid { problems: [{node_id, field, message}] }` variant carries structured problems; the HTTP envelope emits an additive `problems` array (only for this variant); the edge message names the endpoint.

**This is the backend half of #1016.** The frontend half (cascade a node-id rename into edges, prune by row key, consume `problems` to highlight the offending node) is **deferred** — it lives entirely in `WorkflowCreateDialog.tsx`, which graycyrus's open PR #1020 is rewriting; doing it now would guarantee a hard conflict. It will land as a follow-up rebased on merged #1020. The backend ships first: the additive envelope keeps today's frontend working, and the failure is now a fixable 400 with the node/field named.

## API Or Behavior Changes

- Saving a workflow with an unschema'd/invalid node config now returns **400** at save (previously accepted, failed at run). New kinds gated: `transform` (`config.set`), `split_out` (`config.path`), `output_parser` (type-checks present keys; a schema-less identity parser is still accepted), `http_request.url` (now a real http/https URL check), `sub_workflow.workflow_id` (must name an existing workflow).
- 400 responses for workflow validation now carry an additive `problems: [{nodeId, field, message}]` array (new `code: "workflow_invalid"`); every other error is unchanged (no `problems` key) — backward compatible.
- The dangling-edge error names the endpoint node instead of `edge #N`.
- `merge` stays schema-free by design.

## Tests

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `--no-deps --features openhuman,tinycortex --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo build --locked --features openhuman,mcp,telegram --all-targets` + `cargo check --locked --all-features --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo test --lib` — `company::workflow_create` (81), `company::workflow_file` (81), `server::error` (4)

Red-first (fail pre-fix, pass after): a `transform` with no `config.set` (and `split_out` with no `config.path`) is now rejected naming the node + field; an `http_request` with `url="not-a-url"` yields `WorkflowInvalid` whose first problem is `{node_id:"greet", field:"config.url"}`; a dangling edge `from` yields a structured problem naming the endpoint, message no longer leading with `edge #N`. Regression guards: schema-less `output_parser` and no-config `merge` still accepted; `sub_workflow` self-ref still rejected.

## Documentation

`docs/modules/server/workflow-routes.md` documents the structured `workflow_invalid` envelope.

## Related

Part of #1016. Follow-up (deferred, blocked on graycyrus #1020 rewriting `WorkflowCreateDialog.tsx`): the frontend rename-cascade + prune-by-key + consume `problems` to highlight the node. #1016 stays open until that lands.

Note: `src/server/error.rs` here adds a `WorkflowInvalid` arm; PR #1089 (#1017) adds `DataParse`/`DataInvalid` arms to the same match — different arms, trivial rebase for whichever merges second.

Closes part of #1016 (backend).

author: echoriver89
body:
## Problem

On Windows the desktop window never appears. The app starts (processes run,
the embedded server listens, all backend services work) but no window is ever
shown, so the app looks like it silently failed.

## Root cause

Windows exports `HOSTNAME=<machine-name>` to every process. Next.js standalone
resolves its bind address from that variable:

```js
// .next/standalone/server.js
const hostname = process.env.HOSTNAME || '0.0.0.0'
```

`electron/main.js` spawns the embedded server with only `PORT` in the env, so
`HOSTNAME` leaks in from the OS. The server then binds to the machine name,
which resolves to the LAN address — and `127.0.0.1` is never bound.

The renderer loads `http://localhost:<port>`, which fails. Because the window
is created with `show: false` and only revealed on `ready-to-show`, that event
never fires and the window is never shown.

## Fix

Pin the embedded server to loopback by passing `HOSTNAME: "127.0.0.1"` in the
spawn env.

This mirrors existing practice in the repo: `scripts/dev/run-next-playwright.mjs`
already does `HOSTNAME: process.env.HOSTNAME || "127.0.0.1"` for the same
reason. The desktop spawn path was simply missing it.

## Verification

Reproduced and verified on Windows 11 with a production Electron build
(`electron-builder`, Electron 43.2.0):

**Before the fix**

| | |
|---|---|
| Server bind address | LAN address (from machine name) |
| `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` | no response |
| Window | never appears |

**After the fix** (rebuilt installer, no env overrides)

| | |
|---|---|
| Server bind address | `127.0.0.1` |
| `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` | `HTTP 307` |
| Window | appears, title `OmniRoute — AI Gateway for Multi-Provider LLMs` |

Also confirmed the bug is still present on `release/v3.8.50` — `electron/main.js`
there has no `HOSTNAME` in the spawn env.

## Scope

One line of code plus an explanatory comment. No behaviour change on platforms
that do not export `HOSTNAME`, since the server previously defaulted to
`0.0.0.0` (which already includes loopback) in that case.

author: shostako
body:
## 何が変わるか

図面から起こしたスペック JSON は public リポに置けないので、比較のたびにファイルダイアログでローカルフォルダまで潜ってアップロードし直していた。**その手間だけ**を取る。

「スペック入力」ラジオの `JSONアップロード` を **`ローカルから読込`** に置き換え、ドロップ欄はそのまま残したうえで、その上に一覧のドロップダウンを置く。

**保存するものは何も増えていない。** 置き場所を1つ指すだけで、コピーもキャッシュも一時ファイルも作らない。

## 使い方

リポ直下に `local_specs` を作る（gitignore 済み）。一度だけ:

```
ln -s /path/to/specs local_specs
```

これが無ければ一覧は現れない。**それが公開インスタンスの既定状態**。

## 設計判断

### 環境変数 `MFS_SPEC_DIR` を採らなかった

フェイルオープンだからだ。設定ミスが機能を**有効化**する側に倒れる。

Streamlit Cloud に環境変数の UI は無く、secrets が唯一の設定口。そして `streamlit/runtime/secrets.py:503` がトップレベルの `str`/`int`/`float` を `os.environ` に昇格させる。つまりローカルの `secrets.toml` を Cloud の設定欄に貼る——secrets を移す普通の手順——だけで、公開インスタンスにファイル読み取り口が生える。

gitignore されたパスは、checkout + secrets で構成される Cloud 上に**存在させる手段が無い**。有効化するには `.gitignore` を編集して commit する必要があり、それは PR で見える差分になる。

### root を1つの名前に固定した

設定可能な root だと、リポ内を指して `git add -A` するのが**顧客寸法を public リポに commit する最短経路**になる。env ゲートもパス閉じ込めもこれには一切効かない。固定すれば構造的に起きない。

### テキストのパス欄を作らなかった

ユーザー入力のパスが存在しないので、`..`・`~` 展開・prefix 一致・拡張子縛り・大小文字の問題が**書き忘れではなく発生しない**。root 外の単発ファイルは従来どおりドロップで読む。

### 一覧の既定は `— 未選択 —`

`build_geometry()` は実行ボタンの後ろではなく**毎 rerun 走る**（`app.py` の `col_left` 内）。既定で実ファイルを選ぶと、**ページを開いた瞬間に顧客形状の設計図が描画される**。

副次的に、既定選択があると「ドロップと一覧が両方生きている」が常態化して優先順位が毎回発火する。センチネルなら本来のエッジケースに戻る。

### 優先順位と、その見せ方

両方生きているときは**ドロップが勝つ**（直近の明示的な行為）。ただし:

- 勝った側を**サイドバーに**明示する。ジオメトリ構築はメインカラムなので、そこで出すと食い違っている2つのウィジェットから離れて届かない
- 負けた一覧を `disabled` にする。離れた場所の文字より、嘘をついているコントロールが無効化されている方が強い信号

## 実装中に自分のテストが釣った3件

いずれも書いたテストが落ちて発覚した、既存経路にも関わる欠陥:

1. **`Path.resolve()` は symlink ループで `OSError` でなく `RuntimeError` を投げる。** しかもその文言に絶対パスが入る。`client.showErrorDetails` の既定は `full` なので、捕捉漏れはスペックフォルダのパスを画面に描画する
2. **`Path.glob()` は権限エラーを飲み込んで空リストを返す。** 読めないフォルダが「スペック0件」と区別できない偽の緑になっていた。`os.scandir` に変更
3. **スペック読込経路が捕捉していたのは `JSONDecodeError` と `ValueError` だけ。** `PermissionError` / `FileNotFoundError` は `OSError` なので素通りし、フルパス入りトレースバックがページに出ていた。`OSError` と `UnicodeDecodeError` を追加し、**例外の文言は表示しない**

## 意図したトレードオフ

一覧はフォルダ内の**全ファイル名を画面に出す**。アップロード方式では露出が1件だったのがフォルダ内の件数になる。ファイル名は案件の識別子そのものなので、画面共有時の露出は増える。利便性の直接の対価として受け入れる（expander は既定で畳んである）。

## テスト

`tests/test_spec_source.py` 43件。全体 415 passed + 1 skipped。

純関数の単体テストと、**実 `app.py` に対する AppTest** の2層。優先順位と告知は*配線*であり、配線こそ純関数テストが通ったままアプリが別のことをする箇所だからだ。

特筆すべき2件:

- **gitignore ルールそのものをテストしている。** root を1つの gitignore 済みの名前に固定したことが境界の全てなので、ルールが消えたら他のどこも気づかない。リンク本体は実リポに問い、配下は `.gitignore` を写した使い捨てリポで判定する — 実リポに配下を問うと git が「シンボリックリンクの先」で 128 を返し、**機能を実際に使っている環境でだけ skip する**（CI では通る）テストになる。ルールが無ければ落ちることも別途 assert してある
- **IO 失敗の告知にパスが含まれないことを assert している。** フィンガープリントが避けている漏洩が、別の扉から来る経路

author: ramchandragada
body: ## Problem On Linux Mint/Cinnamon, clicking the app once showed a spinner then nothing; a second click opened the app but with **two dock icons** (pinned PDF icon + generic gear icon for the running window). ## Root causes 1. **False "window open" detection** — leftover headless Chrome processes (`pdf-sign-verifier-app --app=...`) were counted as an open window, so the first click only tried to raise a non-existent window and exited. 2. **pywebview never stamped WM_CLASS** — Chrome fallback ran `_adopt_running_window()` to set `WM_CLASS=pdf-sign-verifier`, but the native pywebview path did not, so Cinnamon showed a separate gear icon. 3. **Stale lock not cleared early enough** — zombie Flask backends from a previous session blocked the first launch attempt. ## Fix - Only treat real X11 windows (via wmctrl/xdotool) as "open", not background Chrome processes - Proactively clear stale instances before acquiring the lock (`_replace_stale_instance`, `_kill_locked_instance`) - Configure GTK program class for pywebview and adopt the window in a background thread - Shell wrapper in `/usr/bin/pdf-sign-verifier` kills zombie backends when no window is visible, before starting the app ## Testing Install the new `.deb` from GitHub Releases after merge, fully quit old processes, then verify: - Single click opens immediately - Only one dock icon (PDF icon, no gear)

author: bimvoice
body:
## Summary

`minDistanceBetweenBvhs` (`packages/clash/src/contact/min-distance.ts`), added today by #2805 (closing #2737), calls `triTriDistance` unconditionally on every candidate leaf triangle pair with no `triTriIntersect` gate. That violates `triTriDistance`'s own documented contract (`packages/clash/src/math/triangle-distance.ts:116-117`): "Intersecting triangles must be detected separately with `triTriIntersect`; this routine is only invoked for non-intersecting pairs." It also contradicts `MeshDistance.distance`'s own docstring: "0 when they touch or overlap."

The existing `'returns 0 for boxes that interpenetrate'` test in `min-distance.test.ts` did not catch this: it uses axis-aligned boxes, where overlapping-box vertices/edges happen to land exactly on the boundary features `triTriDistance` samples, so it returns 0 by accident. A tilted, non-axis-aligned triangle pierced through another triangle's face interior (no shared vertex, no edge-edge touch) has no such coincidence:

```
triTriIntersect(A,B) = true
minDistanceBetweenMeshes(A,B).distance = 1.4172159745671205   (before fix; should be 0)
```

### Fix

- Gate on `triTriIntersect` before `triTriDistance`, following the order `engine-ts/narrow.ts` already uses for its per-pair test.
- Once an intersecting pair is found, return immediately: 0 is the smallest distance this query can ever report, so nothing left in the frontier — pruned or not — can improve it. Verified this early return does not change the result on non-early-exit paths (only removes unnecessary further search).
- Symmetry (`minDistance(a,b) === minDistance(b,a)`) verified to still hold post-fix on the adversarial pair (both directions return `0`).
- **Cost**: this adds one `triTriIntersect` (SAT, up to 11 axis tests, each with early-exit on separation) call per candidate leaf triangle pair, on a traversal whose purpose is performance. Kept it simple and unconditional rather than inventing a distance-based threshold to skip the check — a hand-picked epsilon here would be a new correctness bug of exactly the kind that bit this package twice already. For the common disjoint-mesh case (this query's main purpose) every leaf pair now pays both the intersection test and the distance computation; for intersecting meshes the traversal now exits earlier than before (as soon as any intersecting leaf pair is found) rather than continuing to search.
- `bruteForceDistance`, the test file's oracle, had the identical contract violation (it also called `triTriDistance` unconditionally), so it could not have caught this bug even with a correct fixture. It now gates on `triTriIntersect` the same way, and returns `0` on an intersecting pair.

### Evidence

RED test added (`'returns 0 for a genuinely intersecting non-axis-aligned pair (not just AABB boxes)'` in `min-distance.test.ts`) using the adversarial triangle pair above, alongside — not replacing — the existing axis-aligned box test, with a comment on why the box fixture alone is insufficient.

Mutation table (one site at a time, failing test **names**):

| Mutation | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| Negate `triTriIntersect(...)` gate at `min-distance.ts:224` | `measures the gap between two separated boxes`, `returns 0 for a genuinely intersecting non-axis-aligned pair (not just AABB boxes)`, `reports witness points that are actually that far apart`, `agrees with brute force where the closest pair is NOT the first one reached`, `agrees with brute force on irregular meshes big enough to have a real tree`, `agrees with brute force across many offsets, including overlapping ones` |
| Replace the early `return` on an intersecting pair with recording into `best` + `continue` (no early exit, same final result) | none — confirms, as expected, that no test observes the early-exit optimization itself, only the final answer |
| Calibration: negate `triTriIntersect(...)` at `engine-ts/narrow.ts:97` | 11 of 16 `differential.test.ts` tests fail: `agrees on a hard clash`, `agrees on clearance (inside and outside the gap)`, `agrees on touch (suppressed and reported)`, `agrees on a self-clash`, `agrees across the full discipline matrix on a mixed model`, `agrees that skewed members sharing only a face are not a hard clash (#1362 Bug A)`, `agrees that members that interpenetrate are a hard clash (#1362 recall)`, `agrees on unequal-length aligned overlap (overlap-centre probe) (#1362)`, `agrees on transformed elements (f32-quantized world coords)`, `agrees on the mesh label for coincident-footprint BOX layers`, `agrees on the AABB-estimate fallback for a non-box contained pair (#1866)` |

Before: `packages/clash` → `npx vitest run` → 24 files passed / 1 skipped, 368 passed / 1 skipped.
After: 24 files passed / 1 skipped, **369** passed / 1 skipped.

## Note — not fixed here, maintainer's call

- The `engine-ts`/`engine-wasm` differential suite cannot catch bugs in shared code: `engine-wasm/index.ts:14` calls the same `runClash` from `engine-ts/orchestrator.ts`, so selection, severity, exclusions, dedup/sort and summary run identically for both backends. Demonstrated separately: constant-folding `inferClashSeverity` (`disciplines.ts:139`) to always return `'info'` left all 16 differential tests green.
- **Suspected, unconfirmed:** `GEO` is a fully declared discipline in `DISCIPLINES` with its own IFC-type selector, but appears in no `CLASH_RULE_PRESETS` pair, so `disciplineMatrixRules()` never generates a rule touching `IfcSite|IfcGeographicElement|IfcEarthworksElement`. `disciplines.test.ts` never references `GEO`. Declared-but-unreachable in the standard matrix; not confirmed as a functional bug, flagging for a maintainer's call.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- [x] `npx turbo run build --filter=@ifc-lite/clash^...` and `--filter=@ifc-lite/clash`
- [x] `npx vitest run` in `packages/clash`: 24 files passed / 1 skipped, 369 passed / 1 skipped
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/clash`: clean
- [x] Reproduced the bug directly against the built `dist/` before the fix, and confirmed `distance === 0` (both directions) after

author: nf-projects
body:
## Summary

A new `pentest` skill for the OrgSpace Skill Store: an authorized, quantity-over-quality security test of software the user owns or is permitted to test. The skill is written **to the coordinator** — the parent agent reasons about scope, chains, and severity, and fans the grinding out to dozens of cheap forked sub-agents, one tool against one target each.

Two hard gates frame everything. **Written authorization** is demanded before any packet leaves — exact in-scope hosts/paths, a test account, and out-of-scope items, recorded to `scope.md`; no authorization means white-box repo-only with zero network. A **prove-never-compromise stop-line** keeps it defensive: it stops at "the bug is real," never dumps data, brute-forces, or moves beyond proof.

The design decision that separates it from a noisy scanner: a finding ships **only** with an executed proof — a payload that ran in a real browser, an out-of-band callback that fired, an oracle diff, or an exact secret at `file:line` — and anything unproven is dropped. The playbook walks the kill chain (map → intercept → discover → scan → prove → verify) with copy-shaped sub-agent directives for each rung.

## Files

- `skills/pentest/skill.json` — v1 manifest, category `operations`.
- `skills/pentest/SKILL.md` — the coordinator playbook: two gates, the parent/fork split, the phased ladder with real sub-agent prompt examples, and the proof-per-class verification contract.

## Notes

- It depends on a pentest golden image (the fork tool kit — nuclei, ffuf, sqlmap, semgrep, interactsh, SecLists, HackTricks/PayloadsAllTheThings) that does not exist yet; the skill names this as a prerequisite.
- `node scripts/sync.mjs --check` → `✔ 6 manifests valid`.
- Do not merge yet.
