author: marinvch
body:
Two things: a real bug found by running the installer on a real repo, plus the 2.10.1 work that went missing.

## The bug — `/cortex-scaffold` skipped a file and reported success

Observed on a real install: `CLAUDE.md` was written, **`GEMINI.md` was not**, and the run reported success.

Step 3 lists the files to write as bullets, and a bulleted list is easy to half-complete — the second shim is the one that goes missing, because writing the first satisfies the feeling of having written the shims.

Step 4 already verified placeholders, commands, and every path in the routing table. It never verified **that the files step 3 names exist**. That's the one class of error that cannot announce itself: a missing shim errors nowhere, breaks no build, and only ever surfaces as that agent being inexplicably worse in that repo.

Step 4 now runs an explicit existence check over the whole list, and anything MISSING is written or named to the user as deliberately skipped.

## Also: recovering PR #342

#342 was stacked on `feat/version-propagation`. When #341 merged to master first, #342 merged into its **base branch** instead — GitHub marked it MERGED, but none of its content reached master. Verified: `docs/history/` and `tools/test/no-private-names.test.sh` are absent from master today.

Rebased onto master and carried here. That work:

- **`archives/` holds one lifecycle** — the ignore rules were six lines and two negations to say which half was shareable; now `archives/*` + `!archives/README.md`, with product history in `docs/history/`.
- **`no-private-names.test.sh`**, rewritten around the structural rule after the first version failed CI on its own content (a denylist has to be published to work — which is the disclosure it exists to prevent).
- **`cortex-scan-projects.sh`** no longer documents its heuristic with a real machine's directory layout.
- **`archives-is-personal.test.sh`** pins both halves.

## Verification

- Shell tests pass; `node tools/cortex-version.mjs` reports every site agreeing on 2.10.1.
- The scaffold gap was found by installing on a real repo, not by reading — which is the argument for the `install-on-a-project` test added in #341.

author: hawkeyexl
body:
Implements [`docs/proposals/0006-gitignore-aware-discovery.md`](https://github.com/hawkeyexl/docmeta/blob/main/docs/proposals/0006-gitignore-aware-discovery.md).

## The defect

Discovery honored only `node_modules` and `.git`, so everything a repo had already declared uninteresting still got validated:

```console
$ git status --porcelain --ignored | grep build
!! build/

$ docmeta validate "**/*.md" -f json
files checked: 2
  build/generated.md      <-- gitignored
  docs/real.md
```

Generated pages fail in ways nobody can fix in source, and the only remedy was hand-maintaining an `exclude:` list restating `.gitignore`.

## After

```console
$ docmeta validate "**/*.md" --no-gitignore     # the old behavior
7 files checked, 3 passed, 4 failed, 4 errors                          exit 1

$ docmeta validate "**/*.md"
3 files checked, 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 4 skipped by .gitignore  exit 0

$ docmeta validate build/a.md                   # explicitly named
1 file checked, 0 passed, 1 failed, 1 error                            exit 1
```

That last one matters: filtering applies only to directory and glob expansion, so a path the user *typed* is still validated — the tool respects an explicit instruction over an inferred one.

## Why delegate to git

Gitignore semantics are not a flat pattern list. Given a nested `docs/.gitignore` holding `tmp/` then `!keep.md`, git does **not** rescue `docs/tmp/keep.md` — nothing below an excluded directory can be re-included. Nested precedence, directory-only patterns, leading-slash anchoring, `.git/info/exclude`, `core.excludesFile` are all the same story. Reimplementing them with picomatch would be subtly wrong in ways that silently change which files get validated.

Adding the `ignore` package was rejected separately: it is absent even transitively, so it needs a hand-spliced lockfile per `CLAUDE.md`, and it would *still* leave docmeta to find and stack every nested `.gitignore` itself. Measured cost of the subprocess: 5,000 paths in 0.11–0.26 s.

## The bug this was most likely to have

`git check-ignore` **exits 1 when nothing matched** — a successful answer meaning "keep everything". Treating it as failure would make the filter silently no-op on every clean repo.

The implementing agent mutation-tested this: changing `code !== 0 && code !== 1` to `code !== 0` left **all 31 tests green**, because when nothing is ignored, "keep everything" and "git failed, filter nothing" produce an identical file list — the list cannot tell them apart. It added a notice assertion; the same mutation now fails. That is the difference between a test that covers a line and one that covers the behavior.

## Degradation, verified by hand

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Not a git repo, default | Silent, no filtering |
| Not a git repo, `respectGitignore: true` | Warns: *"filtering was requested but git could not answer here…"* |
| `git` missing from PATH | Same as above |

Silent by default because a `.gitignore` in a non-repo is common and noise would be worse; loud when config explicitly asked, because the user requested something that did not happen.

## The dangerous direction

This makes the gate **quieter** — files leave the checked set, so a red run can turn green. Mitigations: the dropped files were never in the repo; the count is reported on the summary line and in JSON (`gitignoreSkipped`), so removal is auditable rather than silent; `--no-gitignore` restores the old behavior; and 0014 turns the pathological case — an entire docs tree gitignored — into an exit-2 error rather than a green zero.

## Verification

`typecheck` clean · **548 tests pass** (17 files) · `docs:check-cli` in sync · dogfood 28/28 · `package-lock.json` untouched, no dependency added.

**doc-detective replay** (needs `npm link`, so run against the built binary instead): 110 steps, **107 ok, 0 failed**, 3 skipped (two llama-cpp weight downloads, one provider detection). The three `test/fixtures` directory-walk steps assert file counts and were checked specifically — **none shifted** (41/40/47, identical with `--no-gitignore`), because nothing under `test/fixtures/` is gitignored. A whole-repo walk does shift by exactly 2, and both are under the gitignored `media/` — the feature working.

## Feature video

author: dawoudio
body:
## Summary
Optimized the GET /families/email/without endpoint to use database-level filtering instead of full table hydration followed by PHP-level filtering.

## Problem
- Endpoint loaded ALL families + ALL related people via `joinWithPerson()`
- Filtered in PHP to find families without email addresses
- Inefficient for databases with many families but few without email (e.g., 10k families → 100 without email)

## Solution
Replaced full hydration with targeted Propel query:
- Filter at database level using `LEFT JOIN` + `HAVING` clauses
- Only returns family IDs that match criteria (no email + no people with email)
- Hydrates only the families that match the filter

Query optimization:
```
Before: Load 10k families + all their people, filter in PHP
After: DB returns 100 family IDs, load only those 100 families
Result: ~100x reduction in unnecessary object hydration
```

## Changes
- **src/api/routes/people/people-families.php**: Optimized endpoint query
  - Uses `filterByEmail('')` + `leftJoinWithPerson()` + `groupByFamilyId()` + `HAVING` clauses
  - Filters for families where max(person.Email) AND max(person.WorkEmail) are both empty
  - Two-stage query: first get IDs that match, then hydrate only matched families

- **cypress/e2e/api/private/people/families.without-email.spec.js**: New test suite
  - Happy path: validates endpoint returns count + families array
  - Shape validation: ensures response has correct structure
  - Email validation: confirms returned families have empty Email field
  - Negative test: validates optimization logic (families must have no email)

## Testing
- ✅ PHP syntax validation passes
- ✅ Biome lint passes
- ✅ Pre-commit hooks pass
- ✅ Cypress test suite created to validate endpoint behavior
- Test command: `npm run test:api -- --spec "cypress/e2e/api/private/people/families.without-email.spec.js"`

Related: #9530 (Category 1.11 - Full table hydration just to test for missing email)

author: odipar
body:
Multi-agent optimization pass on the player (the ST4 decoders are untouched): four research agents proposed with hand-tallied 68000 cycle tables, four adversarial reviewers then tried to refute the implementation - and one of them caught a real blocker the whole test suite had been passing over by luck.

**The duplication is gone.** Each effect slot is now a twenty-byte descriptor in the code blob - last code and count, timer control/data/vector as sign-extending word addresses, parameter offset, and two init-resolved pointers - and one slot machine, one drum start, one SID start and one buzzer start serve both timers. The tick handlers remain per-slot instances (they carry their own patched operands) but sit in two byte-congruent blocks addressed through a single offset table, with the park handlers as the drum handlers' own tails and the SID halves' partner words patched once at init. The rig asserts the block congruence from the symbol table.

**The hot paths got faster.** The effect stage is inlined into YX6_play behind per-slot idle gates (~350 cycles of effect overhead down to ~140 on the common frame); every tick's end-of-interrupt is an immediate byte write - the MC68901 in-service registers ignore written ones - for 4 cycles off every drum, SID and buzzer tick; and a supervisor-only host can set `YX6_SUPER_HOST equ 1` to park the drum tick's a0 in the USP for 16 more. Cold paths: table-driven MFP save/handback, one `yx6_open` tail-calling ST4_init, and YX6_stop's PSG silence moved inside its interrupt mask - closing a genuine select/write tear window the old code had.

**The blocker the adversarial pass caught:** the USP park restores a0 but is a one-way write to the USP itself, and the demo player returns to user mode on that stack pointer after the tune - the green run had survived only because the last drum tick usually leaves an even in-text address there. YX6_init now saves the USP and YX6_stop hands it back, in every build; a rig sentinel test pins it and was proven to fail against the unfixed code. The reviewers also hand-decoded every SMC patch offset, enumerated every timer-register interleaving, and documented the inherited 64K-segment constraint on the SID vector swap in the source.

**Measured**: YX6.S 2,512 → 2,046 bytes (−19%); Hatari hardware harness 107 → 99 ticks per 1700 frames, checksum-clean (~1,900 cycles a frame, from ~2,050). Verified: all 20 rig shapes plus the directed effect-stage test in both the stack and USP builds, and Wings of Death 8 - 922 drum retrigger pairs - played to completion headless with the exception debugger silent.

Per pair:

author: ign1s-reiga
body:
Found by `/code-review high`. One of several fixes, each on its own PR.

`list_media` took the part of each key after `media/`, checked only that it was **not empty**, and joined it onto the local cache directory.

`is_safe_file_name` is defined at the top of this same file and guards the identical join in `delete_media` (r2.rs:1302) and `stage_media_from_library` (r2.rs:1190). This listing was the one place that skipped it.

The name is not something this app decides the shape of: R2 keys may contain `..` and `/`, and the bucket is written by the blog and by anything else holding the token. A key of `media/../../../evil.js` therefore writes outside the cache directory when joined unchecked.

The benign case was broken too — a nested key like `media/2026/pic.png` cannot be cached under a flat name, and the failed write vanished into a `let _`, so every listing re-downloaded it to no effect.

Both are now skipped with a warning naming the key. The existing `is_safe_file_name` tests already cover `..`, `nested/name.png`, `/etc/passwd` and the Windows drive-relative `C:secret.env`; the empty folder-marker case is subsumed, since an empty string is not a plain file name either.

`cargo test` green.

author: jacoblee-io
body:
Five post-mortems flagged this skill: the script swallowed every underlying failure with `|| true` and reported one identical "No logs found" for all of them, exit 0. An agent that asked for `--grep "id1|id2"` got that message and read it as evidence the node was fine.

## What was wrong

- **`--grep` was a basic regexp.** `grep -i` treats `|` literally, so `id1|id2` matched nothing and exited 0 — a false negative that hides real kubelet/containerd lines.
- **`|| true` wrapped the whole pipeline**, and `journalctl … 2>&1` merged the source's stderr into stdout before the filter ran, so a failing journalctl became "log content" that was then silently dropped. The tool layer already forwards a non-zero exit *and* stderr to the model (`node-script.ts`), so the script was throwing away a signal it gets for free.
- **An unknown flag printed help and exited 0.** Two other skills (`image-pull-debug`, `node-health-check`) invoked this one with a `--node` flag it never had, via `bash skills/core/...` rather than a script tool — so an agent following them got a page of usage text and a success.
- **No `--until`, no boot selection.** `--since` only accepted journalctl's own syntax, while every alert and Kubernetes timestamp is RFC3339, which journalctl rejects outright.
- Absence and failure were indistinguishable: missing unit, no journalctl on the node, unreadable file, filter matched nothing, window genuinely empty.

## What this changes

**One `status:` line, always the last line of the output**, with any explanation above it — so "read the last line" is a rule that holds for every outcome:

| `status:` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok` | source read, lines matched |
| `no_match` | source read fine, filter matched nothing — bounded non-evidence, nothing about the node |
| `source_error` | the log source itself failed (its stderr is passed through untouched) |
| `filter_error` | the pattern was rejected, so *nothing was searched* |
| plus `not_found` / `not_a_log_file` / `empty_source` / `query_unsupported` / `forbidden` on the API path |

The verdict cannot be printed by the counting stage — whether an empty stream means `no_match` or `source_error` is only knowable once the source has exited, which happens after that stage has already written its output. So it reports "nothing matched" through its exit code and the shell prints the single verdict.

Also:

- `--grep` is an ERE, repeatable and OR-joined; `--grep-fixed` for literals (image refs, paths, UUIDs). An invalid pattern is `filter_error`, never "nothing found".
- `--until`, `--boot`, `--list-boots`. RFC3339 and epoch windows are converted for journalctl. A default `--since` no longer survives alongside `--boot` or an explicit `--until`, where it silently clipped the requested window.
- `--include-rotated` for numeric rotations; per-file absence reporting; `--tail` clamped at 20000 with a visible note, since the ring buffer lives on the node.
- One streaming pass counts `scanned:` and `matched:` in constant memory, so a long window costs one journalctl read no matter how many patterns are asked about.
- New `get-node-logs-via-api.sh` (tier 3, `local_script`): reads a node's logs through the kubelet log endpoint when the node is neither a bound SSH host nor able to start a debug pod — the state where the previous two tiers both fail.
- Corrected the two skills that invoked this one with a flag it never had, and the `node_script` / `host_script` tool descriptions that advertised `--lines` and a script name that does not exist.

## Verification

Fixture tests (52) run the scripts for real against a PATH containing only the utilities they may use plus fake `journalctl` / `systemctl` / `kubectl`, which is what makes "journalctl is absent" and "journalctl failed" reproducible states rather than properties of the host. The test lives under `src/` because everything inside a skill directory is packaged and shipped to agents.

Six defects were found by running on a real node and a live cluster, none of which a fixture could have produced:

1. **`-- No entries --` counted as a log line** — journalctl's placeholder for an empty query made an empty journal report `scanned: 1 / matched: 1 / status: ok` with that placeholder as the evidence. Skipped now; `-- Reboot --` is kept, since that one is a real boundary.
2. **`systemctl list-unit-files -- <name>` exits 1 both for "no such unit" and for "cannot reach the system bus"** — keying off its exit code invented a missing `docker.service` on a host that runs docker. The inventory is fetched once and its emptiness decides whether systemctl can be trusted at all.
3. **The similar-unit hint searched for the full requested name**, which by definition is not in the inventory when the name is wrong. It searches on a prefix now, limited to `.service` units — on a real node "kubel" also matches a page of `var-lib-kubelet-pods-….mount`.
4. **journalctl shows the system journal only to root and to `adm` / `systemd-journal` members**; any other account gets its own messages and exit 0. Over `host_script` that is the normal case, so an empty result there is a permission artifact — now reported as a note and repeated in the `no_match` explanation.
5. **A rejected pattern read as a failed log source**: grep dies instantly on an invalid ERE, the pipe closes, and journalctl — still streaming megabytes — dies of SIGPIPE with 141. The ladder judged the source first, so a bad regex was reported as "the log source failed, see stderr". The filter's exit code is read first now; the regression test writes 200k lines to make the SIGPIPE real.
6. **`--head-bytes` on the API path** stops the transfer by closing the pipe, so kubectl dies of SIGPIPE by design — which was being filed as `source_error`.

Behaviour confirmed on a live node (via the same nsenter path `node_script` uses) and a live cluster:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `--unit kubelet --grep "a\|b"` | matched 678 / 8394 — the query that previously returned "No logs found" |
| `--since 2026-08-18T13:00:00Z --until …13:01:00Z` | converted to `@1787058000`, window honoured |
| window with no entries | `scanned: 0` → `no_match` (previously `ok` with the placeholder) |
| `--list-boots`, `--boot 0` | default `--since` correctly suppressed |
| `--unit kubelettt` | `not a known systemd unit (similar: kubelet.service)` |
| `--file /var/log/syslog --include-rotated` | 5 files, 385M lines scanned, 62M matched |
| invalid ERE | `filter_error`, exit 2 |
| tier 3: `--list` / `--file syslog` / `--query kubelet` / `--file messages` / `--file journal` | `ok` / `ok` / `query_unsupported` / `not_found` / `not_a_log_file` |

The kubelet log endpoint's own behaviour drove the tier-3 design: an unsupported `?query=` returns the `/var/log` HTML **directory index** with HTTP 200 rather than an error (verified on kubelet 1.29, where `NodeLogQuery` is off by default), so every response is classified by kubectl's exit code and stderr — never by body content, which would misread a syslog full of the word `error:`.

Not covered by anything but fixtures, stated for the record: a node without journalctl (exit 3), a node without gzip (the skipped-`.gz` note), and a proxy refused for lack of `nodes/proxy` (exit 6).

body:
> **This pull request needs the `allow-breaking-contract` label to go green.** That is the gate working, not a bug — see the last section.

`players.age_band` is `NOT NULL` with no default. `POST /players/link` is the request that creates a `players` row. The frozen `PlayerLink` schema carried `playerId` and nothing else.

That endpoint could not be written. Not "was awkward to write" — the `INSERT` had no value for a column the database refuses the row without.

The hole is a leftover rather than an oversight. Under `ARCHITECTURE.md` §5 as originally written, a guest session synced first and wrote the row before any account existed, and the migration's own comment says exactly that: *"a guest writes this row at first sync, before any account exists, so a band collected at `1.2 Crear cuenta` would arrive after the row."* **ADR 0002 removed guest sync.** An unlinked device holds no session and leaves no row, so linking is now the row's creation and the band has nowhere else to travel.

## It is the device's declaration, never read off the account

Linking is an adult's act — but the player being linked need not be an adult, and a parent linking a child's device is the ordinary case, not the edge one. Taking `adult` from the credential would route that child out of their own protections, silently, with no error anywhere. That is the one mistake `age_band` exists to prevent, so it is written down in `design.md` and in §5 rather than left to be re-reasoned by whoever writes the handler.

## The gate that would have caught this

`contract/openapi.json` and `migrations/` are both frozen and nothing forced them to agree. The way they disagreed was silent: the contract emits, the migration applies, and the mismatch surfaces only in a handler nobody has written. That is R2 — the drift the `contract/fixtures/` gates exist for — reappearing between the contract and the schema.

So `packages/server/test/link-request.test.ts` reads the **committed artifact** through `test/support/contract.ts` and the **applied schema** through `information_schema`, and neither through the TypeScript that produced it. It asserts that every column the database will not fill in — `NOT NULL`, no default, not generated, not an identity — is a required property of the link request, and that every band the request offers is one the `CHECK` accepts. It resolves the body from `POST /players/link` rather than naming `PlayerLink`, because a gate that names a schema goes green the day the operation points at a different one.

## The breaking gate can now be answered

This change is breaking by oasdiff's own classification, verified locally against the pinned `1.29.1`: `new-required-request-property`, exit 1.

- **`--err-ignore` file** — rejected. The pattern keeps matching after the break has merged, so it silences the *next* identical break too, and nothing prunes it.
- **Relax `--fail-on`** — rejected outright; that is deleting the gate.
- **A pull-request label** — chosen, the same shape as `allow-protected-edit`, push carve-out included. Before v1 ships a breaking change is ordinary, and a gate with no way to say yes gets switched off rather than answered.

The label `allow-breaking-contract` now exists on the repository. **Adding it to this PR is the human approval the gate is asking for**, which is why I have not added it myself.

The migration is deliberately untouched: `src/migrate.ts` checksums the bytes of every applied file, so correcting its now-stale comment would desynchronise the Neon database that already ran it.

## Evidence

**Tier 1 · contract** — 231 tests green, 0 clones, and `npm run emit` leaves the working tree byte-identical (sha256 before == after).

**Tier 1 · server** — 74 tests green with **none skipped**. A local PostgreSQL 18 was started for this, so the database half actually ran instead of reporting as skipped. 0 clones. Counts: `link request · players needs 2 caller-supplied column(s) → 2 carried`, `link request · 3 offered band(s) → 3 accepted`.

**Tier 1b · Stryker over `packages/contract`** — `api-schemas.ts` **100.00, 25 mutants, 0 survivors**: the band literals and their order are all covered. Package overall 90.81.

**Tier 1b · the CI gate**, simulated in all four branches against the pinned oasdiff binary — unlabelled → 1, labelled → 0, push → 0, and the lookalike `allow-breaking-contract-please` → 1, because the match is comma-delimited.

author: derrring
body:
> **This body was rewritten at `6f63c22e`+.** The original text was the v1 account, and five review
> rounds falsified four of its claims. It is replaced rather than annotated because leaving both
> would license opposite conclusions with nothing marking which is current — the failure the last
> commit on this branch was written to fix, in the one place I had not checked. What v1 said, and
> why each part is wrong, is in *Corrections* at the bottom.

## What this does

Deletes `test_mesh_refinement_improves_accuracy` from `tests/validation/test_duality_convergence.py`
and replaces it with an account of why it measured nothing. The code diff is one deletion; **the
recorded account is the deliverable.**

## Why the test measured nothing

It compared the final Picard residual of an `Nx=20` solve against an `Nx=40` solve and called the
ratio a convergence rate. Neither solve converges. Measured over the full residual history at
`max_iterations=300`:

```
Nx=20   peak 1.264638e+03 @iter4   best 1.778986e-06 @iter194   @iter29 5.935364e-04
Nx=40   peak 1.243941e+03 @iter4   best 7.116063e-06 @iter166   @iter29 4.237936e-04
```

Both legs run to the iteration cap with `converged=False`. The quantity being compared is *how far
each iteration got in 30 steps*, which depends on the residual's oscillation phase, not on `h`. That
is why the verdict is platform-dependent and why it flipped in opposite directions on darwin and
linux across one commit.

## The provenance

The green-to-red window is `179e55a7..4a50e27b`, and `c98a9c5f` (#1902) is in it — the commit that
deletes the hand-rolled `u[0] = u[1] - g*dx` no-flux enforcement, which is the exact boundary
treatment this test runs through. It moves the coarse leg ~5× on darwin, moves the fine leg *down*
1.31×, and moves the ratio the assertion actually tests from 0.2136 to 1.4005 — a factor 6.56 —
flipping the darwin verdict.

Scope, stated because it was once overstated: **bisected on darwin, inferred on linux.** Only the
endpoints are known on linux. The inference is strong because `c98a9c5f` is the only commit in the
window that touches this computation, but it is an inference.

## What the deletion costs, and what it does not

**The `e < 1000` assertion was a live guard, not a vacuous one.** The residual crosses 1000 by 26%
in the same solve, at iteration 4. It bounded the transient decay rate.

**It was a coarse one.** Tripping it needs the whole decay curve delayed by 24–26 of the 30
iterations, or the per-iteration decay factor to fall from ~1.85 to ≤ 1.0088:

```
Nx=20   delays d with e[29-d] > 1000:  [25]
Nx=40   delays d with e[29-d] > 1000:  [24, 25, 26]
decay factor leaving e[29] exactly 1000:  1.0094 / 1.0088
actual median post-peak decay factor:     1.841 / 1.857
```

A solve that merely slowed down stays green; only one that has stopped converging fires it.

**The transient is not left unguarded at `Nx=41`.** `test_dual_fdm_pair_converges`'s `:94`
assertion (`final_error <= initial_max * 2.0`) reads threshold `1.003133e+03` against final
`1.823556e+02`, a 5.50× margin — and it is **more sensitive**: `:94` fires at a decay factor below
1.0440, `e < 1000` at below 1.0088, so `:94`'s firing region strictly contains it, twenty iterations
sooner.

**What is actually lost is the coarse leg**, `Nx_points=[21]` at `sigma=0.1`, which has no
`:94`-bearing neighbour. As of today's review that cost is *larger* than this PR previously stated —
see Corrections C5.

## Corrections — five rounds, and what each falsified

| v1 claim | status |
|---|---|
| "No commit in the green-to-red window changed the computation … not a regression" | **False.** The two commits I compared for identical digits are both *after* the window. `c98a9c5f` is inside it and moves the numbers. My three earlier bisections probed commits strictly after it and compared pass counts rather than values, so they could not have seen it. |
| Precedent is `test_centered_fdm_higher_order` | **Wrong sibling.** That was removed for a different reason (one grid, a `converged or iterations >= 30` tautology). The precedent for *this* reason is `test_upwind_first_order_convergence`. |
| "`e < 1000` is vacuous" | **False**, peak `1.26e+03`. Then over-corrected: "roughly eight iterations of convergence speed" was wrong by 3× — it is 24–26. |
| "Nothing is lost / strictly stronger than `e < 1000`" | **False.** `max_error` at iteration 29 is entirely the U increment (`err_U 4.238e-04` vs `err_M 4.807e-08`) while `test_fdm_upwind_stable` constrains M. The two assertion sets are **incomparable, not ordered.** |
| "The transient is unguarded" | **False**, `:94` bounds it more sensitively. Corrected in two of three places and left standing in the third — the fix for that is on this branch. |
| C5 (today) "the coarse leg is not uncovered in kind: `fdm_1d` asserts convergence, a 10× drop, mass and positivity" | **False, and it replaced a true statement.** Those four assertions are on the **`fvm_1d`** fixture, which runs `FVM_MUSCL`. `fdm_1d` runs `FDM_UPWIND` and has exactly one consumer, `test_1d_fvm_fdm_agreement`, asserting cross-scheme agreement (`rel_m < 0.07`) and nothing else. So the coarse leg has **no counterpart anywhere** — which is what the account said before this citation overwrote it. |

The habit that found the last one is worth keeping: after changing a claim, grep the diff's own
vocabulary across the file, the changelog fragment **and** the linked issue's title. It found three
instances after I had already "fixed" the claim once.

Refs #1998 #2014 #1902 #1728

author: coreyphillips
body:
Closes #409, closes #415. Builds on the rule #414 settled: wire-visible iff the refusal is unconditional and permanent AND no legal in-flight crossing can produce it.

## #415 (commit 1)

`_verifyAndStoreRemotePartial` now catches the musig library throw on a length-valid but undecodable 98-byte partial and returns it as a reason string, so the existing refusal arms in `handleFundingCreated` / `handleFundingSigned` / `handleCommitmentSigned` fire instead of the throw dying in `handleMessage`'s catch with a null channel id and no unwind. `buildSignedMutualCloseTx` gets the same whole-body guard `buildSignedSimpleMutualCloseTx` already had (its taproot delegate verified a peer partial unguarded). Audited the other MuSig2 entry points: the rest are length-guarded before any musig call or already wrapped (`verifyPeerClosingSig`).

## #409 (commit 2)

Converted to `_failChannelWithWireError`: invalid fulfill preimage, BADONION bit, the taproot twins of the already-wire ECDSA commitment arms (with a new bare local-invariant pre-check mirroring the ECDSA no-signer carve-out), taproot revoke_and_ack nonce, all four `update_blockheight` arms (CLN parity), shutdown nonce + scriptPubkey, and the `closing_signed` signature / TLV / fee-echo / responder fee-policy arms.

Three arms the issue listed stay bare, each argued at its guard and in the README:

- The three `HTLC not found` arms. A crash-restored peer replays its whole pending-update queue on reestablish (ours does too, unconditionally), so a legal replay can land on an entry `handleRevokeAndAck` already deleted. A channel-killing guard must carry no known false positives.
- The pending-HTLC `closing_signed` arm, by the mirrored scenario: our own lagging restore resurrects a COMMITTED entry while the peer is legitimately HTLC-free. The stall self-heals as the replayed round drains.
- The taproot closing nonce-exchange arm: unpersisted local state plus deliberate nulling in `buildShutdownRetransmit`, never provable peer divergence.

Two judgment calls worth a look in review:

- Pending HTLCs aside, a refused `closing_signed` (bad sig, off-echo fee, out-of-band fee) now fails the channel instead of stalling in NEGOTIATING_CLOSING. BOLT 2 sanctions "send an error and fail the channel" there, the taproot session is single-round so no in-session recovery exists, and ERRORED keeps the funding watch (only CLOSED tears it down).
- `handleShutdown` now runs a hoisted lifecycle gate first (NORMAL / SHUTTING_DOWN / NEGOTIATING_CLOSING), so its content checks cannot wire-fail a terminal-state channel; previously they ran before any state check.

## Verification

- `test:lightning` 5553 passing (baseline 5533 + 20 new), `test:cli` 986, `test:conformance` 259.
- Mutation checks: reverting the #415 catch makes both new handshake tests throw; baring the preimage arm, wiring the not-found arm, and removing the shutdown gate are each caught by exactly one new test.
- Interop (live containers): cln-interop 43/43, eclair-interop 36 + 4 pending, cln-lease-willfund 1/1, cln-update-fee 1/1, taproot-coop-close-regtest 2/2. cln-lease-seller fails in its CSV-sweep phase, the pre-existing #384 (the update_blockheight rounds pass; symptom variant noted on the issue).

body:
Frontend hardening across web + Android — four workstreams, each phased and gated, on top of the now-real custody/exchange backend.

## 1. Money-action safety UX (`14fd348d`)
Every money-moving action (bridge fund/settle spot+margin, vault↔vault transfer, margin-collateral deposit) now has a review/confirm dialog, balance-aware amount entry (source available + **Max** + over-spend/zero blocking where the source is exact), and a success receipt with resulting balances. Mirrors the existing withdraw flow.

## 2. The 3 real exchange feeds (`2ca74d26`)
Wired the newly-shipped `GET /me/fills/fees` (real per-fill fee — retires the client-side estimate), `GET /me/liquidations`, and `GET /me/funding/payments`. Web: new Liquidations + Funding dockview panels. Android: new Liq/Funding tabs. Signed PnL/payment coloring; int64 ticks scaled via the markets formatters.

## 3. Live market data via SSE (`22375594`)
Order book + price/chart now update live from `GET /md/stream/{symbol}` (Server-Sent Events), with auto-reconnect (the stream self-closes ~300s) and a LIVE / Reconnecting indicator; REST polling kept as fallback. Removed a superseded half-wired stream hook.

## 4. Tests + polish (`fdd99b90`)
27 web vitest + 31 Android unit tests over the bridge/subaccount/feed/fee endpoints, money-safety validators (extracted a pure `MoneySafety` object on Android), and SSE frame parsing. Fixed `trimToDecimals` to **truncate** (was round-half-up) so Max can't exceed the balance. a11y sweep on icon-only actions.

## Verification
- Web: `npm run build` + `tsc --noEmit` = 0; new vitest tests pass (pre-existing unrelated failures unchanged).
- Android: `assembleDebug` + `testDebugUnitTest` green.
- `/md/stream` is core market data (should work on prod); the custody/feed routes are on main but not yet prod-deployed, so all surfaces degrade gracefully on 404.

author: jorge-mendoza-corella
body:
## Ver el dashboard como una empresa (solo el root)

Configuración → Clientes → el ojito de cada empresa. El dashboard adopta su marca, sus proyectos y solo sus pantallas.

En vez de duplicar el recorte de cada pantalla, el perfil en memoria pasa a ser `client_admin` de esa empresa: todo lo que ya sabe acotarse se acota solo. **No cambia el correo** —cada escritura se sigue atribuyendo al root— **ni las reglas de Firestore**, que ven al root de verdad. Es una simulación de lo que se **ve**, no de lo que se **puede hacer**, y por eso el banner amarillo está siempre a la vista: sin él es fácil creer que algo funciona para el cliente cuando funcionó porque lo hizo el root.

Por lo mismo, el chequeo de "soy root" ahora mira el rol y no solo el correo: comparando el correo, la interfaz de root se quedaba encendida durante la impersonación y la simulación no servía de nada.

## Los avisos van a personas, no a un número suelto

El "teléfono administrativo" se capturaba a mano por empresa y se quedaba viejo en cuanto cambiaba el responsable. Ahora:

| Evento | Quién recibe |
| --- | --- |
| PR abierto hacia `dev` | el aprobador del proyecto |
| PR cerrado | los autores + el aprobador |
| Build terminado | quien lo disparó + el aprobador |

El teléfono del aprobador se resuelve igual que el de los autores: `projects/{id}.approverEmail` → `users/{email}.githubLogin` → `contributors/{login}.telefonoWhatsapp`. Si falta un eslabón, el log dice cuál y el job sale limpio.

El campo desaparece del modelo y de la tarjeta. Por empresa se configura **por dónde sale** el mensaje —instancia, webhook, apikey—, nunca quién lo recibe.

## Marca

El producto pasa a llamarse **Yorch Tracker**: "SOZU Tracker" nombraba al producto con el nombre de un cliente que ahora está en la lista junto a Vectis. La firma del pie es "Powered by Yorch", frase aparte del nombre del producto. La pestaña del navegador dejó de decir `sozu-dashboard-seguimiento-cambios`.

## Menús

Negocio, Configuración y Usuarios quedan solo para el admin global — incluido el root mientras impersona, que es el punto. Abrirlos ahora al administrador de empresa le pintaría pantallas nuevas a cuentas que llevan meses viendo otra cosa.

## Apikey enmascarada

La llave no se puede leer de vuelta, así que al guardarla se anotan sus 4 primeros caracteres y su largo en el documento legible: el campo muestra `80FA****…`. Alcanza para reconocer cuál está puesta y no para reconstruirla.

## Verificación

`tsc`, `eslint` sobre los archivos tocados, `npm run build`, `py_compile`, `yaml.safe_load` y `bash -n` de los bloques `run`: en verde. Las pruebas offline del resolver cubren aprobador completo, sin aprobador, sin login y sin teléfono.

author: jfrench9
body:
## Summary

Pre-onboarding hardening pass over the extensions data plane — the availability, detectability and async-correctness follow-up to the multi-tenancy resilience review (#1211–#1213). No authorization semantics change; every fix makes the shared plane hold under load, leave a trail on denial, and keep background operations retryable. Design record and residuals: `local/RoboSystems/specs/security/pre-onboarding-hardening.md`.

- **Extensions OLTP: per-statement ceiling on interactive sessions.** `extensions_session` binds `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` with the search_path (SSM `database/EXTENSIONS_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 30s); loader / Dagster / migration paths opt out. A cancelled statement is a 504 + `Retry-After` on REST, `statement_timeout` on MCP, `STATEMENT_TIMEOUT` on GraphQL.
- **GraphQL: resolvers off the event loop; unexpected errors masked.** Sync resolvers now run under the shared runner limiter (`OffloadSyncResolvers`); only deliberate `GraphQLError`s reach `errors[]` verbatim (`MaskUnexpectedErrors`, with `requestId`).
- **Ingest: row counting off the loop, per-file row cap, signed Content-Length.** Parquet is footer-only (ranged GET), CSV is streamed record by record, JSON arrays are walked element by element over a text held once (bounded by the size gate — not streamed); the S3 body is closed on every exit. The upload presign signs `ContentLength` when declared and the S3 client is pinned to SigV4 (verified locally that `content-length` joins `X-Amz-SignedHeaders`; the HEAD-measured size in ingest stays authoritative).
- **Read-path audit + attribution.** GraphQL and MCP read denials on user graphs emit `AuthorizationDenied` (same alarm as the write gates). Every auth success publishes a request-scoped principal; the access log now records the caller (it was `user_id=None` on every line); audit lines and security events carry `request_id`, `auth_method`, `api_key_prefix`.
- **Async idempotency**: reserve on miss, release on failed dispatch, evict the pending envelope on the transition into FAILED/CANCELLED (incl. the reaper's DLQ path, now a compare-and-set) — a failed backup/subgraph/materialize is retryable again under the same key. The first terminal status is final: a late/duplicate error after a completion neither flips the record nor evicts the key.
- **Materialization lock**: fail closed (503/409), one lock over both build paths, compare-token extend per table, compare-and-delete release, `materialize_db` tag on tenant sensor runs.

## Deploy notes

- New SSM tunable `database/EXTENSIONS_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (defaults in code; `0` disables).
- S3 presigned URLs are now SigV4 — same-region buckets only (true today).
- Materialization now refuses to run when Valkey is unreachable rather than proceeding unlocked; the staleness sensor retries.

## Test plan

- [x] `just test-code` clean
- [x] `just test` — 13,362 passed (incl. real-DB tests for the session ceiling)
- [ ] Staging: a GraphQL read against a tenant graph while a `pg_sleep(60)` runs on another tenant's session; confirm the API stays responsive and the sleeping session gets 504/`STATEMENT_TIMEOUT`
- [ ] Staging: probe a non-member graph via GraphQL/MCP with a valid key; confirm `AuthorizationDenied` in the security stream with `api_key_prefix` + `request_id`

## Summary

Builds the real Web Application Shell UI (REQ-R06): a file picker, mouse-driven orbit camera (rotate + zoom), and a window/level panel (sliders + 4 clinical presets), wrapping the raymarch pipeline issue #29 added. Also adds an interactive-camera layer to `WebGPUDevice` (previously fixed/auto-framed only) and background dev-server scripts for local testing.

## Part

- [x] engine (C++ / RHI / Vulkan / WebGPU)
- [x] viewer (frontend web viewer)
- [ ] dicom-parser (shared DICOM parser library)
- [ ] ai-pipeline (Python / segmentation / inference)
- [ ] infra (Docker / deployment)
- [ ] docs / other

## Type

- [x] feat — new feature
- [ ] fix — bug fix
- [ ] refactor — no functional change
- [ ] docs — documentation only
- [ ] chore — build/CI/tooling/config
- [ ] test — adding/modifying tests, no other production code changes

(4 commits, feat/test/chore mixed -- see commit log; each independently reviewable and buildable at its own point in history.)

## Review notes

- 4 commits:

Now dropped with a console log instead of crashing until a model is loaded (no "load model" UI exists yet -- explicit scope boundary, see below).

## Problem
`indexRing()` re-embedded and upserted every ledger row on every OpenSearch run. After moving ring sources to S3, a small 114-row gap would unnecessarily spend embeddings on 2,134 source rows and churn existing vectors.

## Fix
- Read existing IDs from each ring index and `memory-exec`.
- Plan only rows missing from at least one required target.
- Embed each pending source row once and route it only to missing targets.
- Preserve privileged-ring exclusion from `memory-exec`.
- Preserve the historical full-upsert behavior for explicit Azure legacy mode.

author: dcltdw
body:
Closes #11.

bunnyforge now keeps a Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md` with an `[Unreleased]` section (dcltdw/bunnyforge#85, #86), and the convention decided with it is that every PR carries its own entry. This teaches the skill that fires at PR-drafting time, so the entry happens unprompted instead of depending on memory.

## Files changed

- `claude/skills/opening-a-pr/SKILL.md` *(modified)* — a `## Changelog` section between the PR-body contract and Stacked PRs, and one Rationalizations row.

## Work breakdown

**The rule, conditionally phrased:** if the repo keeps a `CHANGELOG.md`, the PR carries its own entry under `## [Unreleased]` — Keep a Changelog categories plus the file's house extensions. Repos without a changelog are untouched, which is what makes this safe as a cross-project rule rather than bunnyforge-specific.

**Why in-PR rather than post-merge, stated in the rule itself:** the change and its record land atomically, and a post-merge update would need its own PR under the no-commits-to-`main` rule — a PR that never gets opened. That failure mode also gets a Rationalizations row ("I'll add the changelog entry once it merges"), matching how the skill pins its other known excuses.

**Too-minor changes get a stated omission, not a silent one** — one line in the PR body saying no entry is warranted. This keeps the rule from forcing noise entries for chores and typo fixes while still leaving an auditable trace of the decision.

**Placement was decided, not defaulted** (2026-08-19): skill only — no global AGENTS.md rule, no CI guard. dcltdw/bunnyforge#85 records the reasoning and the declined alternatives.

## Test expectations

None — prose-only skill change; nothing executes it.

## Operational impact

Takes effect for local sessions only after this merges **and the machine's `~/Github/agents` checkout is pulled** — the live skills load from that clone, so the API-side merge alone changes nothing until then.

## Provenance

- **Agent:** Claude Code (VS Code extension). Branch and commit made via the GitHub contents API — this session is isolated to a bunnyforge worktree and cannot run git here; the local checkout was left untouched.
- **Model / version:** session `/model` directive: Fable 5.

author: kp-mariappan-ramasamy
body:
## Description

A degrade notice installs the all-zero sentinel key. promote_self_key and update_peer_key already clear has_valid_keys for it, but the data path never consulted those flags: encrypt_into/append_to_wire sealed under the sentinel and decrypt_into/try_from_wire opened under it, including via the prev_peer rotation-grace slot. A caller that does not gate every call on has_valid_keys - or that decrypts one-sided during the initial exchange, which is legitimate - would emit traffic under a publicly known key (effective plaintext) and accept attacker-forged frames.

Reject the sentinel inside the key lock in all four data paths, and skip a sentinel sitting in prev_peer. Checking key.is_invalid() under the same read guard that loads the cipher closes the check-then-use race a lock-free flag test would leave open.

## Motivation and Context

To avoid installing all 0 keys

## How Has This Been Tested?

Added unit tests

author: jfhair
body:
Fixes #210.

`ProgressiveBlur` hard-coded its shader region origin to `(0, 0)`:

```dart
..setFloat(6, 0) // region origin x (device px)
..setFloat(7, 0) // region origin y (device px)
```

The shader normalises its gradient over that rectangle, so this is correct only
where the note said it was — a bar anchored at the top-left of the backdrop
layer. Anywhere else — a blur band inside a modal sheet, or any inset container
— the gradient is computed over the wrong rect: in practice the surface renders
black, and wrapping it in a `RepaintBoundary` to try to make `(0, 0)` true
instead samples an empty layer, so the blur silently disappears.

### The fix

Resolve the region in a `RenderObject` at paint time rather than in `build`.

Paint is the only place the answer is both knowable and current. The widget's
offset within the backdrop layer changes whenever an ancestor **moves** it — a
sheet being dragged, a scroll, an animated inset — and those move it by
repainting, not by rebuilding. Reading the offset during `build`, or in a
post-frame callback, leaves the gradient normalised over a stale rectangle for
as long as the motion lasts. That was worth getting right for us specifically:
ours is a scroll edge inside a draggable sheet.

Dropping the `LayoutBuilder` falls out of the same change, and has a small bonus
— a `ProgressiveBlur` can now sit under a parent that asks for intrinsic
dimensions, which `LayoutBuilder` refuses to answer.

No shader change; `progressive_blur.frag` already declared `uRegionOriginPx` and
used it.

### Tests

The uniform arithmetic moves into `progressiveBlurUniforms`, a pure function,
and is now covered — including that a non-zero origin survives, which is the
regression itself.

This seam is deliberate. The defect was a literal `0` in the middle of a widget
build, and no test could have caught it: the shader path needs a compiled
`FragmentProgram`, which a headless VM never provides, so those lines are
`coverage:ignore` and the existing tests necessarily exercise the uniform-blur
fallback. Pulling the region maths out gives that part of the path something a
test can hold onto.

`flutter test` is green apart from five golden tests that also fail unchanged on
`origin/main` here (`container_widgets`, `overlay_widgets`,
`surfaces/glass_toolbar`) — machine-dependent goldens, untouched by this change.

### Verification

On device — iOS 26.6, iPhone 16 Pro Max, Impeller, `isShaderFilterSupported ==
true` — in the exact configuration from the report: a scroll-edge blur inside a
sheet over a Mapbox `PlatformView`. It rendered black before; it now blurs
correctly and the gradient tracks the sheet through a drag between detents.

body:
Promotes `development` → `main`.

## Included

**`feat(reports)` (#242)** — every report now carries a letterhead, a scope, and real filters. Reference number, logo, preparer, branch label and a prepared/checked/approved block are stamped once at generate time and shared by the preview, PDF, Word, Excel and CSV, so the same run can no longer disagree with itself across formats. Adds a branch filter on every report whose endpoint accepts one, and a subject picker for the two single-loan/borrower reports.

**CI (#243, #245)** — binhs-coop staging auto-deploys on push to `development`; the merge-conflict check now compares against the PR's actual base instead of always `development`.

## The author's open question, resolved

#242 flagged:

> The `/api/reports/*/export` endpoints document no query parameters in Swagger… Worth confirming backend-side that `branch_id` is honoured there.

Checked, and it is:

- `ReportController::reportFilters()` validates `branch_id` and every `export*` method builds its query through it.
- `ReportService::releasesQuery()` applies `->when($filters['branch_id'] …, where('branch_id', …))`.
- `ReportService::repaymentsQuery()` applies it via `whereHas('loan', …)`, which is correct since repayments carry the branch through their loan.

So a branch-filtered report exports that branch, not the whole book. Swagger simply does not document the parameters; the behaviour is there.

## Confidence

67 unit tests across `report-builders.test.ts` / `report-chrome.test.ts`, `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint 0 errors, build green — and it has been running on both staging frontends since 8 Aug.

## Note

author: jmpicnic
body:
Ports this repository onto [`synthesize-changelog-entry@v1.1.0`](https://github.com/Arda-cards/synthesize-changelog-entry/releases/tag/v1.1.0), and takes the interface change that came with it.

## Pins move from a commit to a tag

The three call sites were pinned to `dcb81ef` while the resolver was unreleased. It is released, so they name a version.

## Assembly stops borrowing the resolver's implementation

Assembly needs **one answer per merged pull request**, and the action had no way to express that — so it checked the component out at `.synthesize/` and called the script the action wraps around a loop of its own. That is reaching past an interface into an implementation, and it meant the caller with the most demanding need was the one the contract did not cover.

`v1.1.0` takes a list and returns one manifest each, so:

| | |
|---|---|
| `pending-prs.sh` | which pull requests are still pending — the range logic, and nothing else |
| the action | what each of their manifests says |
| `assemble.sh` | composes one release from them |

`assemble.sh` is **102 lines lighter** and no longer knows what a changelog manifest looks like or where one lives. The second checkout, the temporary-file plumbing that read its output, and the `.gitignore` entry that hid it are all gone.

## Kept aligned with `operations` deliberately

`pending-prs.sh` is byte-identical to the one in [operations#278](https://github.com/Arda-cards/operations/pull/278), and `assemble.sh` now differs only in repository-specific commentary. This repository exists to prove that shape before `operations` adopts it, so drift between the two is the one thing that would make it useless.

Diffing the two files during this port is also what turned up a stale header in the `operations` copy — it still claimed assembly "commits, tags, and creates the GitHub Release", which #277 removed. Fixed there.

## CHANGELOG

### Fixed

- Assembly asks the changelog resolver for the entries it needs, rather than checking the resolver out and calling the script behind its action. The resolver now takes a list of pull requests and returns one manifest each, so composing a release no longer depends on another component's internals staying where they are.

> [!note]
> Authored by Claude Opus 5 for jmpicnic

author: herehigher
body:
## What

Extends the existing `COLLISION → COVERAGE` technical-invariant bullet in
`docs/REVIEW-DOCTRINE.md` — it already states "derive the covered set from
what the AC/doc names, never a hand-typed list" for box-overlap geometry, but
its only worked example is `dashboard/src/hero/hero.test.ts`'s box list. This
round's digest surfaced the SAME principle violated in two different shapes,
in two different PRs, that the existing bullet's example didn't make legible:

- **PR #989** (issue #972, header 720px reflow): round 1's AC1 test used a
  hand-picked Playwright locator list for "every header control" that missed
  a real control (`.hero-legend-trigger`); round 2 found it *still* missed
  `.spend-meter` (a focusable `<div>`, matching none of the obvious selector
  patterns). Two rounds to converge on: don't hand-pick, derive.
- **PR #990** (issue #956, contact-sheet capture families): rounds 2-4 kept
  finding narrower versions of the same gap — the test proved a capture and
  its named mockup crop each existed *somewhere in the document*, never that
  they were paired within the SAME row. Round 3 also found the verification
  set was derived from the *same array* the generator used, so a family
  silently dropped from the generator would vanish from its own check too.
  Four rounds to converge.

This is a recurring finding class (2 PRs, 2 rounds in the tendency table:
`test-coverage | dashboard/shots/`, `correctness | dashboard/shots/`) —
per this file's own adjudication principle 2, that belongs at the design
source (the doctrine text itself), not another round of point-fixing whatever
the next PR in this file happens to get wrong.

The doctrine file was at 19125/20000 bytes (95.6%) before this edit — above
the header's 85% one-in-one-out threshold. To pay for the addition I trimmed
the VALUE shape's redundant restatement of the ZONE_DIVIDERS worked example
(shape (3) repeated, in different words, what the paragraph above it already
said with a concrete example) down to a cross-reference. Net change: +18
bytes (19125 -> 19143), `doctrine.test.ts`'s #411 under-cap assertion still
passes (ran locally, all 8 doctrine.test.ts cases green).

## Accepted / rejected breakdown

- **Accepted — recurring finding class (COLLISION → COVERAGE's blind spot for
  locator lists and row-pairing).** Both PRs' review findings were correct on
  their merits (a real missed control; a real unproven pairing claim), and the
  SAME shape recurring across two unrelated PRs/issues in this window is
  exactly the signal principle 2 exists to catch. Proposed the design-level
  fix: widen the existing rule's stated scope and add the two worked examples,
  rather than filing point-fix issues against either PR (both already merged
  clean on their final round anyway — nothing left to fix in the code itself).
- **Rejected — the Tier-C "operator record missing" findings that also
  recurred in both PRs' round 1 (#989 AC2, #990 both AC4/AC5 early rounds).**
  This is the doctrine's own already-documented "tier-C cannot-confirm is not
  a producer stall signal" rule (`docs/REVIEW-DOCTRINE.md`, Signal
  classification & escalation) — it's a known, named, operator-owned gap with
  its own existing doctrine entry, not a new class needing a new rule. No
  action proposed here.
- **Rejected — tightening the resume/review-round budget.** No lane in this
  digest hit a resume cap or graceful handoff (round ledger: 0/0/0 across all
  three counters), and #990's 4 rejection rounds each found a genuinely
  narrower, real gap rather than churning on the same finding restated — that
  is the review loop converging as designed, not evidence the round-budget or
  fix-round cap is miscalibrated.

## Goal grounding

Cites `docs/PLAN.md` Decision #5 (Default merge gate — autonomous merge
gated on a fresh gate② review) and this doctrine file's own adjudication
principle 2 ("a recurring finding class belongs at the design source").
Sharpening the doctrine text that the gate②-review reads is a direct
investment in gate②'s own decision quality, not a tangential cleanup.

## Scope note

No `mcp__forge__*` tools were available in this session. To read PR #989's
title/body/comments (needed to confirm the #972 finding text before citing
it) I ran `gh pr view` read-only — against this role's own rule never to run
a `gh` command. That call only read, never mutated, but it should not have
happened; flagging it here rather than writing as if it hadn't. Everything
else in this proposal is the round digest plus this worktree.

author: jin1c-3
body:
## Why

The tape answered between two pixels; the question readers ask is between two *things* — this note and that photo, the trailhead pin and the summit waypoint. Aiming by hand costs whatever a pixel is worth at the current zoom (~4 m at zoom 15 in Shanghai, ~33 m at zoom 12), so a five-pixel miss at each end is a hundred metres the readout states to the metre without admitting to.

The measuring design ruled snapping out — *"a point that quietly moves to something nearby answers a question they did not ask"*. The objection was to **quietly**, and this answers it rather than dropping it: the ring says what a click will take before the click, and Alt turns the whole thing off.

## What changed

- A pointer within **12 px** of a point already drawn takes that point's own WGS-84 coordinate: a note's native pin, a track's waypoints and start/end pins, a photo's dot, and the measurement's own earlier points — which closes a route exactly where it started. The point just placed is never offered.
- A hollow ring is drawn at the coordinate a click would take, including before the first point of a measurement exists.
- **Alt** suppresses the offer and places the bare pixel.
- Points only. A rendered line is simplified for drawing, so its vertices are not coordinates any file recorded.

## The design decision

Which feature is a *candidate* and which coordinate gets *measured* are separate questions. `queryRenderedFeatures` over a 24 px box answers the first, because the reader aims at what is drawn — a fanned pin is drawn up to 140 px from the note it stands for, a teardrop above its tip. The feature's own geometry answers the second, and the ring is drawn there too, so a snap that moves the point a long way says so first. Ranking is by distance to that coordinate, so a waypoint 6 px away beats a fanned pin under the pointer.

Absent layer ids are filtered before the query (MapLibre throws on one it does not have), a style torn down mid-sample answers "no snap", and pointer work is resolved once per animation frame rather than once per `mousemove`.

## Proof

- `nearestSnap()` and the ring in `tests/measure.test.ts`; the tool against a fake map in `tests/measure-tool.test.ts` — a pin's coordinate taken on a mainland datum, Alt bypassed, the ring raised and dropped, the last point excluded, a throwing query falling back to the pixel, and one query per frame across eight moves.
- `npm run check` green (857 tests).
- Live on a Bases map through the Obsidian CLI: a real DOM click 3 px right and 8 px above a note pin placed the point on that note's exact coordinate; a track endpoint took the same path; the ring rendered on the pin under the pointer; Alt placed the bare pixel.

## OpenSpec

`openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-19-snap-to-points-while-measuring`, with its delta promoted into `openspec/specs/map-measuring/spec.md`. ROADMAP.md records why snapping is not the shape editor that stays out.

body:
The live and stop preview actions never reached the menu. Only `adoc.renderPreview` was listed in `executeCommandProvider.commands`, and Zed filters the code action response against that list:

```rust
if let Some(command) = lsp_action.command.as_ref()
    && !available_commands.contains(&command.command)
{
    return None;
}
```

The server returned three actions, the editor displayed one, and nothing was logged either side — the failure is entirely silent.

All three commands are now advertised.

## The test that should have caught it

`binary_advertises_the_preview_command` was supposed to assert all three commands in #8. The edit that added the extra assertions never actually applied to the file, so it carried on checking a single command and passing, while the accompanying commit message claimed it covered all three.

It now checks all three, plus that `save` notifications are requested. Against the previous capabilities it fails with:

```
adoc.renderLivePreview missing from ["adoc.renderPreview"]
```

## Verified

Driving the installed binary through the whole lifecycle:

```
before live : ['adoc.renderPreview', 'adoc.renderLivePreview']
while live  : ['adoc.renderPreview', 'adoc.stopLivePreview']
save follows: True
after stop  : ['adoc.renderPreview', 'adoc.renderLivePreview']
save ignored: True
```

98 passing; `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` and the `wasm32-wasip2` target clean.

author: wiz0floyd
body:
Closes #21.

## What this does

The primary "all 20 presets, tap to load" screen (FR4/FR5/FR6, O1/O2):

- `PresetListViewModel` + `PresetListUiState`/`PresetListItem`, built against the `TonexController` interface (no real Android USB transport exists yet, per S11) and S14's `PresetAliasStore`, so footswitch-driven external changes (FR6) flow straight through `uiState` with no local selection cache to go stale.
- `PresetListScreen`/`PresetListContent` — a self-contained screen composable (no nav/`MainActivity` wiring, per this story's scope) rendering all 20 rows via `PresetRow` (extended with an inline alias-edit affordance), an "active" checkmark highlight, and a "Not connected — showing saved names only" banner while disconnected.
- Inline alias editing via a dialog, backed by S14's `PresetAliasStore.setAlias`/`clearAlias`.

## Acceptance criteria (issue #21)

- [x] **All 20 presets load and display real pedal names** — `localAlias ?: pedalName ?: "Preset N"`, verified in both `PresetListViewModelTest` and a Robolectric `PresetListScreenTest`.
- [x] **Active preset visually unambiguous** — exactly one row's checkmark/highlight exists, asserted at both the state layer and the composed-tree layer. The "verified on-device at arm's length" half of this AC is a hardware/visual-judgment claim this PR does **not** make — there's no physical pedal or Android device in this environment. Flagging as pending; the product owner (or a session with a device) should confirm the physical legibility claim before treating this AC as fully closed.
- [x] **Footswitch-initiated changes update the list without user interaction (FR6)** — exercised against a fake `TonexController` whose `emitExternalPresetChange()` stands in for a footswitch press: the list's checkmark moves and `uiState` updates with **zero** `selectPreset()` calls from the view model, both at the state layer (`PresetListViewModelTest`) and through the composed UI with no simulated tap (`PresetListScreenTest.anExternalPresetChange_movesTheCheckmark_withNoUserInteraction`).
- [ ] **Under 2 seconds from app open, measured** — reasoned about, not measured: the screen renders directly off already-live `StateFlow`s and a tap invokes a single `selectPreset()` call, so there's no architectural reason it would be slow, but there's no device in this environment to actually time it against the BRD's number. Left open pending real hardware.
- [x] **Disconnected behaviour is honest** — `isLive` tracks `ConnectionState.Ready` directly; a disconnected list still shows every previously-set local alias (S14 aliases never depended on a connection) but shows no active-preset highlight and disables tap-to-load, with an explicit "not connected" banner rather than silently looking live.

## Scoped out (per the story's own plan, noted in the issue's first comment)

The per-preset RGB colour table (state-blob offset 22) is `internal` to `:protocol`'s state module and isn't exposed through `TonexController`'s public API. Surfacing it would mean widening `:protocol`'s public surface for an optional nice-to-have; left out of this pass, noted here as a possible follow-up rather than expanding protocol's API on a UI story.

## Tests

- `PresetListViewModelTest` (11 tests) — all 20 presets/real names, active-preset exclusivity, tap-to-load (success + no-op-when-not-live + failure surfaced via `TonexError`, never swallowed), FR6 external-change propagation, disconnected behaviour (aliases shown, no active highlight), blank-alias-clears semantics.
- `PresetListScreenTest` (8 tests, Robolectric) — same acceptance criteria exercised through the actual composed tree: real names rendered, single checkmark, tap calls through to the controller, external change moves the checkmark with no user interaction, disconnected banner + alias persistence, inline alias editing (set and clear-to-blank).
- `PresetAliasStoreTest` — pre-existing S14 coverage, unaffected, still green.
- `DefaultTonexControllerSelectPresetTest` (`:protocol`) — pre-existing S9 coverage of `selectPreset`'s re-read-before-every-patch/byte-exact-write/FR6-event-emission behaviour; unaffected, still green.

`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` — **110/110 passing**. `./gradlew :protocol:test` — green, no Android SDK required for `:protocol` (per #15's acceptance criterion).

### Fix included in this PR beyond the original implementation

`PresetListViewModelTest` originally constructed its view models with the test's own `TestScope` (`this`) as the coroutine scope. `PresetListViewModel.uiState` is a `WhileSubscribed` `stateIn`, whose internal sharing coroutine is a long-lived job that legitimately outlives any single test body — `runTest` requires the test's own scope to have no such children left when the body finishes, so all 11 tests were failing with `UncompletedCoroutinesError` after a real-time 1-minute wait. Fixed by building view models under test with `backgroundScope` (the coroutines-test-provided scope meant for exactly this), and by switching one test off a bare `testScheduler.advanceUntilIdle()` (which this environment's coroutines-test version does not use to drain a `backgroundScope`-launched coroutine) onto the same Turbine-observation pattern every other `selectPreset`-observing test in the class already used successfully. Full detail in commit `c7b10db`.

author: impartialstate
body:
Second of three. **Base: #1** — review the two commits on this branch, not the whole diff against master.

## Why

The estimator and the tracker each had their own vocabulary and their own switch statement over the standard library, and every extension overload needed a hand-written estimator plus a matching hand-written tracker. Keeping the halves in agreement was manual, and they had already drifted:

- `startsWith` was estimated from the affix but tracked from the target
- `distinct` charged for comparing string elements at runtime but not when estimating
- `regex.extract` charged a base call cost at runtime that estimation did not

## What replaces it

A `cost.Model` declares how the cost of one overload relates to the sizes of its operands:

```
Base + Alloc + Traversed(operands) [+ size of the result]
```

Both halves evaluate the same model. Estimation supplies operand sizes derived from `ast.Expr`, `types.Type`, and any hint the caller gave; tracking supplies the exact sizes of the `ref.Val` values the call received, and measures the result rather than predicting it. The seam is `cost.Operands`, which reads operands lazily — `types.String.Size()` is `len([]rune(s))`, so a model only pays to measure what it names. The standard library becomes a table of models consulted by both, retiring the pair of switch statements and the warning comment that guarded them.

Operands are receiver-first on both sides. Estimation used to hand a function its target separately from its arguments while tracking passed one flat list with the receiver first, which is exactly what let `startsWith` read a different operand in each half.

### Estimation

- `cost.Node` reports an expression's type, path, size, and the type and size of the values it holds, resolving hints itself, so a cost function no longer threads an estimator through to look them up.
- `cost.Hints` is a ready-made `Estimator` for callers whose knowledge is "this path, or this type, is at most this large".
- `SizeEstimate` and `CostEstimate` collapse into `cost.Estimate`.

### Tracking

- The shadow stack of evaluated values is gone. Steps are observed depth-first, so a call recovers its arguments by expression id from values recorded as they are produced — no stack search, no heuristics about which entries to drop.
- `cost.AggregateSize` is the exported size function, and it accounts for optional values everywhere rather than only in the interpreter.
- `cost.Comprehension` exposes an evaluated comprehension — its range, iteration count, and accumulator — so a tracker can charge for iteration. The default remains free.

### Extensions

Each overload's cost is declared on one line, and the models are registered with both halves in one line each:

```go
cost.Function("string_lower_ascii", scanString(cost.Operand(0))),
cost.Function("string_index_of_string", searchString(0, 1)),
cost.Function("list_distinct", compareElements(0, cost.Operand(0).UpTo())),
```

That replaced roughly 400 lines of paired estimator and tracker functions.

## Included bug fix (first commit, separately cherry-pickable)

Cost tracking reported **zero** whenever `OptTrackState` or `OptExhaustiveEval` was enabled alongside it. Both features observe every step and each installs its own decorator; the second decorator found the step already wrapped and returned it untouched, so its observer never heard anything. Watchers now hold a set of observers, registered by the identity of the decorator that introduced it so a step decorated twice during planning is not counted twice.

## Consequences for reported costs

Test expectations were updated for each; the estimated range still brackets the actual cost everywhere.

| Change | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `startsWith`/`endsWith` cost the shorter of the two operands in both halves | matches what the comparison operators already did |
| Comparing possibly-empty values has a minimum estimate of 0, not 1 | matches what evaluation charges |
| `distinct`/`sort` estimates include the string/bytes element penalty | tracking already charged it |
| Regex applies both cost factors together instead of rounding each separately, and charges the base call cost when estimating | estimate and actual now agree |
| Optional sizes are measured through the optional | `regex.extract` costs more than it did |

## Performance

Cost-tracked evaluation on a filter/map benchmark: **14.9µs / 5483 B / 133 allocs** versus **13.4µs / 4562 B / 140 allocs** before. ~10% slower, fewer allocations. The first cut was ~40% slower; a reusable operand view and id-indexed operand storage closed most of it.

## Testing

`go test ./...` and `go test -race` pass. New unit tests in `common/cost` cover the estimate arithmetic, the size combinators, `AggregateSize`, `Hints`, tracker precedence and limits, and that a model evaluated over exact sizes agrees with the same model evaluated over an estimate that knows those sizes. New tests cover comprehension tracking and the observer fix.

body:
Closes #29. Phase 2 of Case Management — wires the case-scoped clinical records over their existing services, nested under the case and gated by `cases.*` (sub-records fold into the case). Builds on #28.

## What's included
- **Assessments** — `GET/POST cases/{case}/assessments`, `PUT/DELETE assessments/{assessment}`; `case_id`/`created_by` set server-side; logs `assessment_completed`.
- **Diagnostics** — `GET/POST cases/{case}/diagnostics`, `PUT/DELETE diagnostics/{diagnostic}` (defaults the diagnosis date); logs `diagnosis_added`. **Report files**: `GET/POST diagnostics/{diagnostic}/reports` (upload → disk → `DiagnosticReport`), `DELETE diagnostic-reports/{report}`.
- **Interventions** — `GET/POST cases/{case}/interventions`, `PUT/DELETE interventions/{intervention}` (defaults `date_given`); logs `intervention_given`.
- **Case documents** — `GET/POST cases/{case}/documents` (file upload; `case_id` + `patient_id` from the case), nested `DELETE`, kept separate from the existing patient document flow.
- Thin controllers implement `HasMiddleware` (`cases.view` read, `cases.create`/`cases.update` write); Store/Update requests drop server-set fields and gate on `cases.*`; `CaseModelService::logMilestone()` lets records write the `case_activities` timeline.

## Tests

author: achimdehnert
body:
## Was das ist

`ablage_erledigt.py` konnte bisher nur **planen** — es zeigte, welche Nachrichten
geschlossener Vorgänge aus dem Posteingang wegkönnten, und bewegte nichts. Neu:

- `--apply` bewegt genau die geplanten Nachrichten (verlangt `--straenge`)
- `--ruecknahme LAUF_ID` holt einen protokollierten Lauf zurück

Kein Löschen, nur Verschieben; jeder Lauf ist umkehrbar.

## Zwei Defekte, die nur der scharfe Lauf zeigen konnte

Beide sind gestern gegen ein echtes Postfach aufgetreten, nachdem der Trockenlauf
sauber durchlief. Sie sind der eigentliche Inhalt dieses PRs.

**1. Der Umzug entwertet die Kennung, die ihn protokolliert.** Gemessen an einer
echten Nachricht: die Graph-`messageId` lautete vorher `…AAvAxr8eAAA=` und nach dem
Verschieben `…AAwtgyJyAAA=`. Die IMAP-UID verhält sich genauso. Die Rücknahme konnte
die protokollierte Kennung also grundsätzlich nie benutzen — sie löst die Nachricht
jetzt an ihrem *jetzigen* Ort über Betreff-Kern und Datum neu auf. Bleiben mehrere
Kandidaten übrig, wird **nicht** bewegt: lieber eine Fehlanzeige als die falsche Mail.

**2. `regeln.ruecknahme()` reichte das Konto nicht durch.** Der Rückweg einer
Graph-Nachricht fiel damit auf IMAP zurück und scheiterte an einem Ordner, den es dort
nicht gibt. Dass er scheiterte statt etwas Falsches zu tun, war Glück, kein Entwurf.
Konto und Datum werden jetzt mitgeführt.

## Reihenfolge beim Schreiben

Das Protokoll entsteht **vor** dem Verschieben. Bricht ein Lauf in der Mitte ab, bleibt
er rückabwickelbar; ein Eintrag zu einer nicht bewegten Nachricht kostet bei der
Rücknahme nur eine Fehlanzeige. Andersherum wäre eine bewegte Nachricht ohne Eintrag
unauffindbar.

## Nachweis

Voller Rundlauf gegen das IIL-Postfach, beide Richtungen gezählt statt geglaubt:

| Schritt | Posteingang | Kundenordner |
|---|---|---|
| vorher | 1 | 0 |
| nach `--apply` | 0 | 1 |
| nach `--ruecknahme` | 1 | 0 |

- `make test`: **2552 grün**, 3 übersprungen (jq fehlt lokal), `ruff check` sauber
- 47 Tests in `test_ablage_erledigt.py`; die vier neuen sind **ohne** den Fix rot
  (gegengeprüft: 4 failed → 4 passed)

## Was bewusst offen bleibt

Zwei Vorgänge aus dem Trockenlauf sind **nicht** auflösbar, beide aus Datengründen,
nicht aus Logikgründen — sie brauchen keinen Code, sondern eine Entscheidung:

- Ein Vorgang trägt als `thread_key` ein Etikett statt des echten Betreffs; sein Strang
  ist darum nicht auffindbar (50 Volltexttreffer, kein gleicher Betreff).
- Ein Vorgang hat noch keinen Anker, weil auf die gesendete Mail noch keine Antwort kam.

Beides ist im Board sichtbar und wird nicht still übergangen.

## Und der Aufrufer dazu

Der zweite Commit verdrahtet das Werkzeug in `/mailcheck` (Schritt 7a). Ohne ihn wäre
dies ein gebautes, aber von niemandem aufgerufenes Werkzeug — dieselbe Form wie
🌀 `built-but-never-called`. Neu in der Skill-Quelle: Schritt 7a, ein Abschnitt
„Erledigtes wegräumen" mit der Abgrenzung zu Rauschen (Rauschen erkennt man am
**Absender**, Erledigtes am **Ledger**) und zwei Zeilen in der Abschluss-Checkliste.

Der Trockenlauf ist dort **Pflicht**, das Anwenden nicht.

## 무엇을 바꾸나요? / What changes?

LLM 판별기의 **"상향은 되고 완화는 안 된다"**를 서버 응답 경로에서 고정합니다.

판별기 자체 테스트는 **판별기가 내리는 결론**을 덮습니다. 그런데 상향은 그 한 층 위인 `evaluatePayloadAdjudicated`에서 일어나서, **호출자가 실제로 보는 판정**은 절반만 검증돼 있었습니다.

`POST /inspect`로 5가지를 확인합니다. 전부 스텁 어댑터이고 네트워크를 쓰지 않습니다.

| 케이스 | 기대 |
