author: axelgalvez11
body:
Two shortcuts, as asked for.

## Hold space to talk

Press and hold anywhere outside a text field → the microphone opens. Let go → the transcript lands in the composer as **editable text**.

**Releasing does not submit**, deliberately. That's exactly what the ✓ control already does, and the reasoning in that file still holds: speech recognition mishears, and auto-submitting would make a transcription error indistinguishable from a wrong answer in the evidence.

Space is the most dangerous key to claim, and every guard is one way it bites:

| what space does | what stops it |
|---|---|
| types a character | refuses inside any input, textarea, select or contenteditable |
| scrolls the page | default prevented on keydown |
| clicks the focused button | …and on keyup, because browsers synthesise a button's click from keyup — and the Continue you just pressed with the mouse still has focus |
| repeats while held | `event.repeat` refuses. `startDictation` snapshots your typed text on every call, so a second one mid-hold would overwrite that snapshot with the transcript and lose what you'd typed |
| Cmd-Space is Spotlight | any modifier refuses |

Releasing is tracked by **who started it** — otherwise letting go of space would also close a microphone you'd opened with the button and were still talking into.

And keyup isn't guaranteed to arrive: hold space, press Cmd-Tab, and none is ever delivered. Blur, a hidden tab and unmount all release it the same way. That's the one failure here that costs money and privacy rather than a click.

## Command-Enter continues

Presses whatever Continue is on screen. Control-Enter too — a shortcut that only works on a Mac is broken for whoever isn't on one.

**It cannot press past a question, and it gets that for free.** `advance` is one derivation hoisted above both render sites, null exactly when `continueOwner` refused — while a demonstration is owed (its N3 guard) and while the canvas is busy. The hotkey asks whether that handler exists rather than re-deciding it, so **the keyboard cannot have a path the button doesn't**. Both Continue buttons now call the same function.

**It stands down inside the composer.** The textarea submits on `Enter && !shiftKey`, which Cmd-Enter already satisfies — so it submits there today and still does. Claiming it globally would silently change what Cmd-Enter does to a half-typed question. That asymmetry is intentional, not an oversight.

## Where things live

`lib/learn/canvas-hotkeys.ts` holds the decisions and nothing else — no `preventDefault`, no state, no listeners. Every way these fail is a *condition*, so each is a line of test rather than a browser run.

`ContinueHotkey` is a component rather than an effect in the canvas body: `continueRegion` is computed below the canvas's early return, and a hook can't sit after a conditional return. Mounting it also gives the right lifetime — no listener while a canvas is still loading.

Space lives in the composer, where dictation is. **Stated consequence:** the composer is unmounted during a recording, so hold-to-talk is inactive then — correct, since there'd be nowhere for a transcript to land.

## Proven by pressing the keys

`scripts/hotkeys-browser.ts`, real keystrokes against this commit's production build. The Web Speech engine is stubbed before the page loads — and **only** the engine: headless Chromium has no Web Speech API, so the whole path would otherwise be inert and a run would look like a pass while proving nothing.

```
PASS  C1  command-enter presses the Continue and the reading moves on
PASS  C2  command-enter inside the composer still submits
PASS  S1  holding space opens the microphone exactly once
PASS  S2  releasing closes it exactly once
PASS  S3  no microphone opens while an answer is being typed
PASS  S4  space still types a space in the composer
PASS  S5  losing the window mid-hold closes the microphone
```

**What this does not prove** is that speech recognition itself works — that's the browser's own engine, untouched here.

Six guards calibrated: dropping the typing check from either shortcut, the repeat check, the blur release, the keyup `preventDefault`, or routing the document's Continue around the shared handler each reddens exactly its own named test.

4036 tests pass.

author: mdenner1234
body:
This PR carries two tightly-coupled Fleety changes (they touch the same three chat surfaces):

## 2.2-F — member file/image uploads (ephemeral extract)
Members can attach a **PDF, image, or text/code file** in all three surfaces (ChatPage, FleetyChatWidget, GuidanceEmbed) and have Fleety read/review/analyze it.

**Key finding:** the hand-off generator has no working file→text extraction engine (ADR-0006 designed it; ADR-0007 lists it "not yet addressed"). So extraction was **built**, reusing hand-off's *discipline* (magic-byte typing, office-file refusal, FormData→edge pattern).

New edge fn **`fleety-extract`** → text → sent to `techfleet-chat` as an `attachment`, framed as **UNTRUSTED material**. By true (magic-byte) type:
- **text/code** → decoded locally (no LLM)
- **PDF (text layer)** → parsed locally via `unpdf` (no LLM); scanned PDF → friendly note
- **image** → OCR via **Gemini Flash vision** (DeepSeek is text-only); fails gracefully to "paste the text"
- **docx/xlsx** → refused (decompression-bomb/XXE not yet guarded)

**Ephemeral** (owner decision): bytes live only for the request; nothing written to Storage/DB.

Security: magic-byte typing, 10 MB cap (Content-Length + byte length), member JWT + per-user rate limit, image framed as data-to-transcribe, uploaded material bypasses caches. ADR-0014.

## 2.2-G — capture 👍/👎 on all three surfaces (feed the live learning loop)
Fleety already has a **live** learning loop: 👍'd answers become few-shot exemplars + boost canned-answer ranking at answer time; 👎'd canned answers are auto-suppressed nightly. But **only the floating widget captured feedback** — `/chat` and `/resources` (the main member widget) fed nothing back.

Now all three use a **shared** `FleetyMessageFeedback` component keyed on the `X-Fleety-Turn-Id` header, writing `fleety_message_feedback` under the member's session. The widget was refactored to use the shared component too (kept its Widget-only "Human review" + action chips). Every rating now ties to the exact turn from any surface.

## Proof
- `deno test fleety-extract/lib.test.ts` → **11 passed**
- `vitest run` fleety smoke (uploads + feedback + modes) → **30 passed**
- `deno check fleety-extract/index.ts` → clean; frontend `tsc` clean for touched files
- BDD `fleety-2.2-f-uploads.feature` (incl. `@security`/`@privacy`); ADR-0014
- `config.toml` pins `fleety-extract` `verify_jwt=false` (auth in code)

## Not in scope
Upload persistence/retention; docx/xlsx (needs decompression/XXE hardening). Image model env-overridable (`FLEETY_VISION_MODEL`).

## 摘要

使用者以實際保險業務員名冊（3,110 筆 × 87 欄）驗證後回報仍有個資遺漏。逐欄稽核找出十餘種真實資料才會出現的漏網樣態，本 PR 全數修正——修正後同一檔案補遮 **21,613 筆**，且經逐欄稽核確認個資欄位無殘留。

## 核心改變：欄位標題即強力訊號

表格／試算表中，欄位標題已明示內容性質（姓名、證號、電話、地址），整格內容應據此遮罩，不必再依賴姓氏庫或格式驗證：

| 漏網樣態 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 姓名欄的罕見姓氏（陶、葛、錢…姓氏庫列不完） | 表格欄不再要求姓氏在庫內 |

| 身分證欄的統編（法人）、舊式證號、帶狀態碼（`89731134-BD`）、檢查碼錯誤者 | 新增 `id_bare`：識別號碼欄整格遮罩 |
| 證照號碼、考試號碼、員工編號、系統帳號欄（完全未偵測） | 同上 |

author: alwick
body:
Fixes the P1 on WIC-1004: a client-side deep link or browser refresh on `app.careerpin.app` (e.g. `/dashboard`, `/applications/:id`) returned a plaintext `404 Not Found` instead of the React SPA shell.

## Root cause

`wrangler.jsonc` already carried `not_found_handling: "single-page-application"`, so the setting *looked* correct — but it was inert. When a Worker script is present, the asset router serves matching files directly and forwards everything else to `main`; `not_found_handling` is **not** applied on that forward. It only takes effect for explicit `ASSETS.fetch()` calls. `worker.ts` hands every forwarded request to `app.fetch(...)`, and `packages/api/src/app.ts` had an `onError` but **no** `notFound` handler — so Hono's default plaintext 404 was the response.

Credit to the EM correction on `3464fc98` for catching that the originally-proposed config-only fix was a no-op. All three of its claims were re-verified against `main` before this branch was written.

## The fix

- **`wrangler.jsonc`** — add `"binding": "ASSETS"` to the `assets` block. Required: without a binding the Worker has no way to reach the asset router at all. Comment rewritten to record *why* `not_found_handling` alone is insufficient, so this doesn't get "simplified" away later.
- **`packages/api/src/types/env.ts`** — declare `AssetsBinding` and add `ASSETS?` to `Env`. Optional, so unit tests and local runs without the binding still typecheck.
- **`packages/api/src/app.ts`** — add `app.notFound()`:
  1. `/api` and `/api/*` return the existing JSON `NOT_FOUND` envelope. **Checked first**, so no API path can ever receive HTML.
  2. Non-`GET`/`HEAD` methods, or a missing `ASSETS` binding, fall through to plaintext 404 — a `POST` to a bogus path should not get an HTML body.
  3. Otherwise: `ASSETS.fetch()` the original URL file-first, then explicitly retry `/index.html`. The explicit retry means the fallback keeps working even if `not_found_handling` drifts.
  4. If even `/index.html` 404s (asset dir not built), plaintext 404 rather than echoing an asset-router 404 body.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm run test -w @wic/api` — **379/379 pass**, including 21 new cases in `packages/api/test/spa-fallback.test.ts` covering: `/api/*` stays JSON, deep links get the shell, `POST` does not, file-first ordering, `index.html` retry, and the no-binding path.
- Nothing has been deployed. No migrations, no data changes, no secret changes.

## Risk / rollback

Main risk is an `/api/*` path receiving the SPA shell, which would break every client `fetch`. Mitigated by ordering the `/api` branch first and asserting it in tests. Rollback = revert the two commits and redeploy.

## Cross-PR interaction with #79 (WIC-1011) — read before the second merge

Both branches touch `packages/api/src/app.ts`, but the hunks are far apart (#79 at the imports / `app.use` block ~L16-24, this PR at `app.notFound` ~L67+), so **git auto-merges cleanly — there is no textual conflict**. The *semantic* interaction is the real risk and neither card covers it:

- #79 registers `securityHeaders()` and `httpsRedirect()` as `app.use('*', ...)`.
- This PR's `notFound` returns the `Response` from `assets.fetch(...)` **directly**.

Whoever merges second must rebase and confirm (a) the SPA shell served on a deep link still carries the full security-header set, and (b) `httpsRedirect()` does not intercept or rewrite the internal `ASSETS` sub-request. An asset `Response` whose headers are not the ones the middleware mutated is the plausible failure. Tracked on the review card for this PR.

## Governance

Per the board deployment directive: **this PR must not be merged** until board approval `34020dca` is accepted. Merging triggers `Deploy Production`.

Opening the PR triggers `Deploy Preview` only, which is `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` against `environment: dev` — it cannot reach production. This matches the established practice for #78 (WIC-1009) and #79 (WIC-1011), both opened without a separate approval. EM made the sequencing call on WIC-1016.

EM merge order once the board authorises: **#78 (credential hard-gate) → this PR (P1) → #79 (P2)**.

Closes WIC-1004 on merge.

author: sahiljagtap08
body: Fixes #10880. The OpenAPI metadata for `POST /oauth2/consent` and `POST /oauth2/continue` declared the 200 response body as `{ redirect_uri: string }` (required), but the endpoints never return that shape: every 2xx JSON response goes through `handleRedirect`, whose return type is `OAuthRedirectResult = { redirect: true; url: string }` (`src/authorize.ts`). Clients generated from or validated against the spec read `redirect_uri` and always get `undefined` — see better-auth/better-auth#10880 for the downstream misdiagnosis this caused in superset-sh/superset#6609. This PR: - Updates both metadata blocks in `src/oauth.ts` to document the implemented shape: `{ redirect: boolean, url: string }`, `required: ["redirect", "url"]`. - Adds `src/openapi-schema.test.ts`, a regression test (with `@see` link per CONTRIBUTING) asserting the declared 200 schema's `properties`/`required` match the implemented response keys for both endpoints. The runtime side is already pinned by the existing flow tests asserting `consentResult.url` contains the code redirect (`src/authorize.test.ts`), so the schema test closes the doc↔implementation loop from the other side. - Includes a `patch` changeset for `@better-auth/oauth-provider`. Tested with: - `pnpm vitest packages/oauth-provider/src/openapi-schema.test.ts --run` — fails on `main` (properties are `["redirect_uri"]`), passes with this change. - `pnpm vitest packages/oauth-provider --run` — full package suite green. - `pnpm --filter @better-auth/oauth-provider typecheck` — clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Documents the actual { redirect: boolean, url: string } JSON response for POST /oauth2/consent and POST /oauth2/continue in the OpenAPI schema, fixing a mismatch that broke generated/validated clients. The spec previously required redirect_uri, which the endpoints never returned. - Requires redirect (boolean, always true) and url (string, format: uri-reference); url may be absolute or server-relative. Updates the 200 description for /oauth2/continue. - Adds a regression test to assert the documented properties/required keys; runtime behavior is unchanged. - Publishes a patch release for `@better-auth/oauth-provider`. - Migration - Regenerate clients. Replace redirect_uri with url and handle redirect (always true). Accept relative URLs. Written for commit 4252057240bc7c443ae6408f0ac68bf9047ad505. Summary will update on new commits.

3. Do not retry URM GFNI, n26 postpone, fold-diet, dead-hook `witgen_simd`.

#141 leftover, **kept** and implemented here:

> induce `ring_switch::inner_product` AVX-512 deferred-reduction on the
> 243 L0 UDR eq-dots (SPR-only)

Call sites of `ring_switch::inner_product` on this tip, all length
`2^LOG_PACKING = 128` except the claim-check / rs_eq_ind dots which
are the same packing width, plus `direct_fold4_products` which does
256 such dots (16 banks × 16 low coords) after a bit-transpose each.
The "243 L0 UDR eq-dots" is the induce-side count on the ranked L0
shape; the function is the same.

---

## Hypothesis (one mechanism)

Replace the historical

```
let mut acc = F128::ZERO;
for (&x, &y) in a.zip(b) { acc += x * y; }
```

with **one** GHASH reduction of the XOR of unreduced 256-bit schoolbook
products, and on SPR do the unreduced accumulate 4-wide with the crate's
existing `WideGhashX4` (`vpclmulqdq` × 4 per `mul_acc`, horizontal
`fold()` to `F256Unreduced`, one `reduce()`).

This is work elimination, not a knob:

- N independent `ghash_reduce` calls become 1.
- On SPR, N scalar CLMUL schoolbooks become `ceil(N/4)` vector
  `VPCLMULQDQ` quads (4 products / 3 CLMUL-pairs worth of mid terms
  already XOR-accumulated in registers).
- No new constants, no chunk-size, no `target-cpu` fishing.

Kill: `FLOCK_NO_IP_WIDE=1` restores the portable one-reduce loop (still
not the old per-product reduce). Ranked Hilbert env is cleared, so the
wide path is the one that scores.

---

## Equivalence argument (no timed local run required)

Let `p(x) = x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1` be the GHASH irreducible.
`F128::mul` is schoolbook CLMUL + `ghash_reduce`. `F128::mul_unreduced`
is the same schoolbook **without** the fold; `F256Unreduced::reduce` is
the same fold. The crate already states the identity on
`F128::mul_unreduced`:

> Reduction commutes with XOR, so Σ (aᵢ·bᵢ) mod p = (Σ aᵢ·bᵢ) mod p.

Proof sketch: `ghash_reduce: F₂[x]/(x^256) → F₂[x]/(p)` is an F₂-linear
map (XOR of shifted copies of the high half; see `ghash_reduce` in
`field/gf2_128.rs`). Therefore

```
reduce(u) ⊕ reduce(v) = reduce(u ⊕ v)
```

and by induction `⊕_i reduce(u_i) = reduce(⊕_i u_i)`. The historical
loop is the left-hand side; `inner_product_unreduced` is the right-hand
side. Bit-identical.

`WideGhashX4::mul_acc` XOR-accumulates the four schoolbook terms
`(lo = x.lo·y.lo, hi = x.hi·y.hi, mid = x.lo·y.hi ⊕ x.hi·y.lo)` per
lane using `VPCLMULQDQ` immediates 0x00 / 0x11 / 0x01 / 0x10 — the
same four products the scalar `ghash_mul_unreduced_x86` uses.
`fold()` horizontally XORs the four lanes into one `F256Unreduced`.
Linearity of XOR gives

```
fold(Σ_lanes unreduced(x[i],y[i])) = ⊕_i unreduced(x[i],y[i])
```

so the wide path equals the portable unreduced path equals the
historical per-product path.

This is **not** the killed `WideGhashX4` package. `killed.md` entry
`b7c99465` forbids WideGhashX4 on `finish_c_banks_fold4` /
`finish_c_banks` (serial post-drain collapse, official −0.53%). This
cycle wires the same primitive into `ring_switch::inner_product` only.
Different function, different call graph, different working set
(128-wide eq-dots, not C-bank finish).

Identity test added and run as a compile/correctness smoke (not a
benchmark): `inner_product_deferred_matches_naive` compares naive
`acc += x*y`, portable unreduced, and `inner_product_wide` at
n ∈ {0,

author: pranavyadav-toptal
body:
Converts concall-alpha's presentational surface into a design system for [claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design/p/6064e2ac-c269-4a7a-aeae-5000b77ef444), so the design agent builds screens with our real components instead of generic ones.

**64 components** ship — the 24 shadcn/ui primitives, both brand marks, 7 score/read components, and 31 company-page sections — each with a hand-authored preview card. 231 preview cells were rendered headlessly and visually graded; `package-validate.mjs` exits clean with zero warnings.

## Why the bridges exist

This is a Next.js app, not a component library, so a few things had to be built:

- **`ds-entry.ts`** — a curated entry barrel, since there is no `dist/` to bundle. Excludes anything touching Supabase, server context, or `async` Server Components. It additionally exports the design-token modules (`surface-tokens`, `lib/design/shell`, `lib/score-band`, …) and model builders, so anything built with the system reaches the real class strings rather than re-deriving them.
- **`shims/`** — inert stand-ins for `next/link`, `next/image`, `next/navigation`, `next/dynamic`, plus `@/lib/utils` and `@/lib/analytics`. The last two matter most: both read `process.env` at module scope, and `process` does not exist in a browser IIFE, so every one of the 64 components threw before mounting.
- **`build-css.mjs`** — compiles the stylesheet including the Google Fonts our `next/font` setup would otherwise leave behind. Without it every design renders in a fallback face and nothing downstream catches it.
- **`build-types.mjs`** — declaration-only `tsc` output, which is what gives real prop contracts (`Button`'s `variant`/`size` unions come straight out of `cva`).

## Two portal defects this surfaced

Worked around in the **DS-only** Tailwind config so the exported system is coherent. Both are still broken in the app itself — deliberately not fixed here:

1. **`aria-invalid:*` classes never compile.** Tailwind 3.4's built-in `aria` variants omit `invalid`, but the `components/ui/` primitives are the v4-era shadcn generation and their `cva` base strings all use it. Input, Checkbox, Select, Toggle, ToggleGroup and Badge have **no field-error affordance** in the live app.
2. **`components/ui/sidebar.tsx` is a v4 file in a v3 project.** `globals.css` declares the sidebar palette in an `@theme inline` block that Tailwind 3 ignores outright, and `tailwind.config.ts` has no `sidebar` colour, so `bg-sidebar` / `border-sidebar-border` resolve to nothing. `w-(--sidebar-width)` is also unparseable v4 syntax — only a source edit fixes that one.

Smaller: `app/company/[code]/chart.tsx` never sets `isAnimationActive`, so its 1.5s draw-on is mid-flight in any screenshot. Arguably worth disabling for the product too.

## Review notes

- **Nothing here changes how the app builds or renders.** No app source is touched; the diff is `.design-sync/` plus a `.gitignore` addition.
- `.design-sync/NOTES.md` carries the full rationale and the re-sync risks.
- **The entry barrel and `componentSrcMap` are hand-maintained.** A component added to `components/ui/` or `app/company/components/` will not appear in a re-sync until it is added to both, and nothing warns you.

author: monglong0214
body:
Closes #72

## What this adds

A conformance, compatibility and digest gate over the four documents E1-001 and
E1-002 froze: `specs/aos-trace.schema.json`, `specs/events.v0.json`,
`specs/aos-result.schema.json` and `specs/opportunity-profile.schema.json`.

The failure mode the digest half exists for is a schema whose bytes move without its
recorded digest moving. `SPEC_DIGEST_MANIFEST` in `scripts/schema-conformance.mjs` is
therefore a pinned literal rather than a value recomputed from the files it gates, and
`SPEC_DIGEST_MANIFEST_SHA256` is pinned too, so forging one recorded digest breaks the
manifest digest as well. Each document carries two digests: a raw-byte one that sees a
reformat and a canonical-JSON one that sees a semantic edit a reformat would hide.

`packages/schema/src/compatibility.ts` exports `classifySchemaChange`. Anything that
can reject a document the previous schema accepted is `major`, anything that can only
widen acceptance is `minor`, and only annotation drift is `patch`. The verdict is the
maximum severity across reasons, so a breaking change hidden behind a compatible one is
still breaking, and an unrecognized keyword difference is `major` rather than silently
compatible.

The corpus is 24 fixtures: 5 positive and 19 negative across the three validatable
documents, with the negatives covering all fourteen rejection codes the frozen schemas
can raise. Every negative declares the code it must be refused for, so being rejected
for the wrong reason is a failure, not a pass.

## RED, then GREEN

The six cases the ticket's acceptance mapping names were staged first, each failing on
its pinned message with no implementation present. Full evidence is in
`OUT/red-evidence.txt`.

| Acceptance | Case | RED message |
|---|---|---|
| AC-E1-003-1 | `zero-fixture` | schema conformance rejected: zero-fixture corpus |
| AC-E1-003-2 | `valid-corpus` | schema conformance assertion failed: positive corpus must validate |
| AC-E1-003-3 | `negative-corpus` | schema conformance rejected: negative corpus must be refused |
| AC-E1-003-4 | `breaking-minor` | schema compatibility assertion failed: breaking and minor changes must be classified |
| AC-E1-003-5 | `digest-mismatch` | schema conformance rejected: digest mismatch |
| AC-E1-003-6 | `cross-node` | schema conformance assertion failed: canonical bytes and manifest digest must be runtime-independent |

All six pass at GREEN, on Node 22.23.2 and Node 24.18.0, with the same manifest digest
on both.

## Verification

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --test packages/schema/test/conformance.test.ts` | 6 tests, 6 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm test -w @aos/schema -- conformance` | 16 tests, 16 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm test` | 521 tests, 521 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm test` on Node 24.18.0 | 521 tests, 521 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm run build` | `BUILD_SCAFFOLD_PASS` |
| `npm run docs:check` | `PLANNING_CONTRACT_PASS` |
| `node scripts/validate-gate-administration.mjs` | `GATE_ADMINISTRATION_STRUCTURAL_PASS` |
| `npm run ops:check` | `OPS_CHECK_PASS mode=offline readySet=D0-002` |

Manual/live: `LIVE_NA`. This ticket owns no runtime or scenario surface.

## Paths touched

Owned by the ticket:

- `packages/schema/test/conformance.test.ts` (new, its named RED file)
- `packages/schema/src/compatibility.ts` (new, `classifySchemaChange`)
- `scripts/schema-conformance.mjs` (new)

Census pins only, because materializing those three files moves counts the repository
suite pins by exact value:

- `tests/planning-contract.test.mjs` — `ticket_owned_code_files` 37 to 40 and the three
  new paths in `ticket_owned_code_paths`, both pinned to what the validator actually
  reported
- `tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs` — each of the ten focused-lane counts
  raised by one, which is the per-file result the runner emits for the new test file

No other file changed. `scripts/resolve-execution-state.mjs` was not touched and the
ready-set derivation is unchanged; `npm run ops:check` still reports `readySet=D0-002`.
`README.md` was not touched: nothing this change materializes is named absent there.

## Two things the reviewer should look at

**`conformance/schema/**` was not materialized.** The ticket grants it, but the
repository's skeleton admission gate admits a non-source file inside the skeleton only
through a `fixtures/...` glob declared by a ticket, and admits a source-extension file
only when a ticket names that exact path. `conformance/schema/**` satisfies neither, so
a single JSON file placed there fails `root-private-scripts-and-runnable-surface` in
`tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs` — measured, not inferred. The corpus lives
in the owned script instead. Widening that admission is a control-plane change this
ticket does not own.

**Census pins are outside Exact ownership.** `tests/planning-contract.test.mjs` is
D0-004's and `tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs` is D0-002/D0-004's. Moving
their pinned numbers is the only way to satisfy this ticket's own Verification step 2
(`npm test`, zero failure), and neither edit changes an assertion or loosens a check —
only the pinned values move, to measured output. Flagging it as an ownership overlap
rather than leaving it to be found.

author: luongnv89
body:
Closes #276

## Summary

Issue #276 asked a scope-decision question: should the secret scanner's binary-file skip (files with a NUL byte in their first 8 KiB aren't content-scanned for secret values) stay, or be closed? **Decision: keep the skip.** It matches industry norm (gitleaks skips binary content in its own git-scanning mode too, and its own request to close the identical gap — gitleaks#1541 — was closed as not planned), filename/size rules still catch `.env`-style files regardless, and closing it would trade one bounded, disclosed gap for real, unmeasured cost (content-scanning every binary on every commit, a script + doc + two-test-file change, and a false-positive-cost measurement harness that doesn't exist anywhere in this repo today). This PR implements that decision's other half: `docs/pre-commit-security.md` now states the residual risk explicitly, so the skip reads as a deliberate, accepted trade-off rather than an oversight.

## Approach

Balanced approach (Option 2 of 3): append a residual-risk paragraph to the existing "Binary skip" bullet in `docs/pre-commit-security.md`'s Behavior Notes, worded as a *proxy, not exact equivalence* claim (the NUL-byte sniff `gi-secscan.py` implements approximates the documented `charset=binary` rule; a UTF-16LE-with-BOM file is one case where they diverge, verified empirically — benign here since the ASCII-anchored secret regex can't match interleaved-NUL content through either path), with a one-line cross-reference to #276 so the deliberation is discoverable directly from the doc, not only from PR/git history. No script, test, or config behavior changed.

## Decision Record

- **Root cause:** The binary-skip rule has existed since #87/#252, inherited wholesale from an external skill with zero recorded deliberation of its false-negative-vs-performance trade-off. Issue #276 is the first place in this repo's history that trade-off is decided on purpose.
- **Options considered:** Option 1 — Minimal fix (paragraph only, no in-doc pointer); Option 2 — Balanced approach (precise proxy wording + in-doc `#276` cross-reference); Option 3 — Comprehensive approach (same + a new ADR under `docs/decisions/`)
- **Options rejected:** Option 1 — satisfies AC2's wording but leaves AC1's decision undiscoverable from the doc itself, only in PR/git history; Option 3 — runs against this repo's own `docs/decisions/no-backfill-merged-decision-records.md` norm that merged PR bodies already are the decision record, and Option 2's in-doc cross-reference already satisfies discoverability without a new artifact to maintain
- **Selected option:** Option 2 — Balanced approach
- **Residual risk:** The doc's gitleaks#1541 citation and "closed as not planned" framing reflect that issue's state at time of writing; if gitleaks' behavior or that issue's status changes later, the citation would need a follow-up update. No functional or behavioral change was made in this PR, so there is no regression risk.

Analyzed at: `refactor/276-decide-whether-the-binary-file-scan @ b25f20e` (2026-08-19)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `docs/pre-commit-security.md` | Added residual-risk paragraph to the "Binary skip" bullet (~line 162); corrected a factual citation (gitleaks#1541 status) found during QA review |
| `skills/issue-resolver/references/docs/pre-commit-security.md` | Regenerated bundled copy (`./scripts/build.sh` output) |
| `skills/issue-pr-review/references/docs/pre-commit-security.md` | Regenerated bundled copy (`./scripts/build.sh` output) |

## Test Results

- Unit tests: n/a — documentation-only change (existing suites re-verified unmodified: `tests/test-pre-commit-security.sh` 23 passed, `tests/test-scripts-252.sh` 137 passed)
- Integration tests: skipped (n/a)
- E2e tests: skipped (n/a)
- Build: passed (`./scripts/build.sh` clean, no drift)
- QA cycles: 2

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| A decision is recorded (keep the skip, or close it) with its reasoning | pass | Decided: keep. Recorded in this PR's Summary/Decision Record (durable via squash-merge — this repo's `squash_merge_commit_message` is `PR_BODY`) and cross-referenced inline at `docs/pre-commit-security.md:162` |
| If kept: `docs/pre-commit-security.md` states the residual risk explicitly so it is not mistaken for an oversight | pass | `docs/pre-commit-security.md:162`, "Binary skip" bullet, residual-risk paragraph added in this PR |
| If closed: doc and script change together, with a matrix cell covering it, and the false-positive cost on large binaries is measured | unverified | Out of scope — the maintainer decided to keep the skip, not close it, so this AC branch does not apply |

author: indigo423
body:
Closes #222

## What and why

Every file attached to a release was named after `dist.zip`. For two of the five that was factually wrong: `release.yml`'s own step is called "Generate CycloneDX SBOM of the source tree", and its comment explains that syft scans `package-lock.json` rather than the bundle, because `dist/` is a single inlined `index.html` and scanning it would find nothing. So `dist.zip.cdx.json` and `dist.zip.cdx.html` asserted a subject they never described.

Nothing on the release page carried a version either, so artifacts downloaded from different releases overwrote each other.

| Current | Release (`vX.Y.Z`) | Preview (rolling, from `main`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dist.zip` | `blitsbom-<version>.zip` | `blitsbom-preview.zip` |
| `dist.zip.sha512` | `blitsbom-<version>.sha512` | `blitsbom-preview.sha512` |
| `dist.zip.sigstore` | `blitsbom-<version>.sigstore` | `blitsbom-preview.sigstore` |
| `dist.zip.cdx.json` | `blitsbom-<version>-sbom.cdx.json` | not produced |
| `dist.zip.cdx.html` | `blitsbom-<version>-sbom-report.html` | not produced |

Three decisions worth reviewing rather than skimming:

**The checksum drops `.zip` while the SBOM gains `-sbom`.** These look inconsistent. The rule is where the subject is recorded: a `sha512sum` file names its subject on the inside (`<hash>  blitsbom-0.7.1.zip`), so shortening its own name loses nothing. The SBOM records nothing internally, so its filename was carrying the whole burden.

**The preview is named, not versioned.** On `main`, `package.json` holds the *last released* version while the preview is ahead of it, so `blitsbom-0.7.1.zip` built from `main` would claim to be the 0.7.1 release. A stable `preview` name also keeps one fetchable URL for people tracking `main`, the same role `:rc` plays for images.

**`release.yml` now cross-checks the tag against `package.json`.** The build targets derive filenames from `package.json` while the release is keyed on the tag. A bump PR that moved one and not the other would previously have published a mislabelled archive; now it fails the release run.

`sbom-drift.yml` gets simpler as a side effect. It hardcoded `dist.zip.cdx.json` in five places behind an assertion reading "release.yml names this path literally" — a guard defending an implicit coupling the job never needed, since it only checks that the parser accepts `make sbom` output. It now passes an explicit `OUT`.

## Breaking change

`releases/latest/download/dist.zip` no longer resolves. GitHub's `latest/download` endpoint needs an exact filename, which no versioned artifact can provide. This is the entire cost of the change and it is not recoverable by any naming scheme that also carries a version.

The README now documents two paths instead of one:

- A versioned `curl`, guarded by a new `README_VERSION_PATTERNS` entry so a release bump cannot leave it stale. This reuses the machinery already protecting the action ref and image examples (#165).
- `gh release download --pattern 'blitsbom-*.zip'`, which resolves the current release itself. This is the honest replacement for what `latest/download` did, and where scripted consumers should be pointed.

Keeping both means the copy-paste path stays dependency-free and the automatable path stays version-free. Rejected: attaching an unversioned duplicate so the old URL survives, which would mean two names for one artifact, two things to sign and verify, and a second asset whose digest people might attest against by mistake.

Attestations are unaffected: `gh attestation verify` matches on digest, not on the subject's name. Releases published before this keep their existing names, and `RELEASING.md` records that in a blockquote, the same convention `marketplace-check` already exempts.

## Scope

Pure rename. No byte inside any artifact changes. Making the SBOM self-identifying internally (`metadata.component` is currently `{"type": "file", "name": "."}`) is deliberately out of scope and tracked as #221.

## How it was verified

Full `make ci`, green:

```
$ make ci
 Test Files  18 passed (18)
      Tests  409 passed (409)
purity-check: no forbidden runtime references.
marketplace-check: ok — description 109/124 chars, branding bar-chart-2/blue, README examples at 0.7.1.
size-check ... smoke ... e2e: OK
```

The whole release artifact chain reproduced locally with the new names:

```
$ make dist-zip
wrote blitsbom-0.7.1.zip

$ make sbom
wrote blitsbom-0.7.1-sbom.cdx.json (200 components)

$ make report SBOM=blitsbom-0.7.1-sbom.cdx.json OUT=blitsbom-0.7.1-sbom-report.html
embedded 200 components · 11 licenses · CycloneDX 1.7 · raw

$ sha512sum blitsbom-0.7.1.zip > blitsbom-0.7.1.sha512 && sha512sum -c blitsbom-0.7.1.sha512
blitsbom-0.7.1.zip: OK
```

The `OUT` footgun the Makefile documents is still contained. A bare `make report` writes to the generator's own derived name, not into the SBOM's:

```
$ make report SBOM=blitsbom-0.7.1-sbom.cdx.json
→ sbom-sbom.html
PASS: bare 'make report' did not write into the SBOM's name
```

The new version guard fires on a stale quick start and ignores the version-free `gh` glob. Verified by temporarily setting `package.json` to 0.7.2:

```
✗ README.md:20: release download URL says 0.7.1, expected 0.7.2 — "releases/download/v0.7.1/"
✗ README.md:20: release artifact says 0.7.1, expected 0.7.2 — "blitsbom-0.7.1.zip"
✗ README.md:24: release artifact says 0.7.1, expected 0.7.2 — "blitsbom-0.7.1.sha512"
```

`make clean`'s globs remove all four artifact shapes, and `actionlint` is clean on all three changed workflows.

## Not verified locally

The release and preview workflows themselves. Neither runs on a PR, so this needs a rehearsal against a throwaway prerelease tag via `release.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` before a real release depends on it. `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` is the backstop if a name disagrees.

## Checklist

- [x] `make ci` passes locally
- [x] Linked to an issue above with a closing keyword (`Closes #222`)
- [x] Commits are [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) and signed off (`git commit -s`)
- [x] AI-assisted commits carry an `Assisted-by:` trailer, and I have reviewed the output myself
- [x] No new network calls (`make purity-check` enforces this)
- [x] Docs updated if behaviour changed — including `RELEASING.md` if the pipeline changed

author: nembokid
body:
## What this is

Second attempt at #58 — the first (#63, try_join) made it worse in production: the two concurrent scans contended for the same Cloud SQL cores and `/api/agents?q=` went from answering in 8.6s to **408ing at 10s**. Measured, reverted in effect here.

## The fix

When `q` is present, ONE scan produces both the page and its total: `count(*) OVER ()` rides the paged query, and `SET LOCAL work_mem = '64MB'` (transaction-scoped, nothing else inherits it) keeps the 236k-row relevance sort in memory — it spilled to disk at the 4MB default.

Measured on the BSC run (`9516923d`, worst case: `q=agent` matches 88% of documents):

| shape | wall |
|---|---|
| two queries, serial (pre-#63) | ~8.6s |
| two queries, concurrent (#63) | 408 at 10s |
| one scan + work_mem (this PR) | **6.5s cold** |

The browse branch (no `q`) keeps its two index-served queries — a window count there would force a full-run scan on every directory page load. Past-the-end pagination (`offset` beyond the result set) falls back to the plain count so the overflow probe's `total` still holds.

Same rows, same total, same order in every case — nothing about the semantics changed.

## Verification

`cargo test` (63) / clippy / fmt clean. After deploy: worst-case timing re-measured and the full `check:api` contract run against production (it has never yet completed a clean pass — the search step always tripped it).

author: sripwoud
body:
CI and a local `mise` run now resolve the same tools from one file. Bumping a version in `mise.toml` changes what CI installs — no second edit, no silent drift.

`mise-action`'s `mise_toml` input is written *over* the checked-out `mise.toml` — its `action.yml` reads *"If present, this value will be written to the mise.toml file"*. The `check` job therefore could not see the committed tool list and restated it inline. The two had already drifted: `hk`, `pkl` and `convco` were in the repo list and absent from CI's.

Fix: move the `check` tasks into `mise.toml`, drop the input.

|                        | before  | after                    |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ------------------------ |
| tool declarations      | 2 files | `mise.toml`              |
| tools CI installs      | 4       | 7 (full repo list)       |
| `mise r check` locally | n/a     | reproduces the CI gate   |

### convco backend

Installing the full repo list means CI installs `convco`. mise's `cargo` backend shells out to `cargo install` unless `cargo-binstall` is on `PATH` — true locally, not on `ubuntu-latest`. Swapped to `github:convco/convco`, since upstream ships prebuilt musl binaries.

| backend   | cold install      | verification                                  |
| --------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `cargo:`  | Rust source build | —                                             |
| `ubi:`    | 3s                | generates a checksum                          |
| `github:` | 3s                | GitHub API digest, probes attestations + SLSA |

Timed locally against an isolated `MISE_DATA_DIR`. convco publishes neither attestations nor SLSA provenance today — both probe and skip — but `github:` picks them up if upstream ever adds them.

### `--excludes mise.toml`

Dropped from the format check. It existed only because the action clobbered `mise.toml` with unformatted heredoc content, and it left `mise.toml` unchecked in CI. dprint loads the TOML plugin and `mise r fmt` already formats the file locally, so CI now matches local.

### Test plan

- [x] `mise r check` green on a CI-equivalent tree (`dist/` moved aside) — 19 files linted, format and types clean
- [x] `actionlint .github/workflows/main.yml` clean
- [x] `mise ls --current` resolves all 7 repo tools, `github:convco/convco 0.7.1` sourced from `mise.toml`
- [x] `check:*` glob still matches the three `hide = true` subtasks (`mise r check --dry-run`)
- [ ] `check` job green here — the one criterion only CI can settle

> [!NOTE]
> Pre-existing, out of scope: biome lints gitignored `dist/` despite `vcs.useIgnoreFile: true`, so `mise r check` and `mise r fix` both fail locally in any worktree that has been built. `"root": false` with no parent config looks like the cause. Worth its own issue.

Closes #12

body:
## Summary

Continuation of the #2802 sweep (the class #2829 fixed in `useCompare`): an async job whose result is written into shared store state, with nothing verifying the job is still the one being awaited at the moment of the write.

Enumerated every hook under `apps/viewer/src/hooks/` that runs an async job and publishes to the store (`useClash`, `useIDS`, `useIfcLoader`, `useIfcFederation`, `useZoneSelection`, `useZoneWriteBack`, `useDrawingGeneration`, `useSandbox`, `useDxfUnderlay`, and others), and drove the highest blast-radius candidates by execution:

- **`useClash.ts` (`run()` / `runDuplicates()`)** — `publishClashResult`'s only guard was `clashFederationIsCurrent`, keyed on the model SET, not on which call started it. Two detection jobs issued while the federation is untouched (an "All elements" run, then a duplicate scan started while it is still going) carried the identical identity, so an older, slower run finishing after a newer one overwrote its answer. Reproduced with a real ~200-element narrow-phase run racing a real duplicate scan (`useClash.concurrent-run-supersession.test.tsx`).
- **`useIDS.ts` (`runValidation()`)** — had *no* supersession guard of any kind, not even a federation-identity check. Two validations issued back to back raced outright. Reproduced with a real 6000-entity vs 2-entity validation over two different target models (`useIDS.concurrent-run-supersession.test.tsx`).

Both now capture a per-call epoch and re-check it, synchronously, immediately before every store write that follows an `await` — publish, every error path, and the `finally` that flips the running/loading flag back off (the `finally` case is easy to miss and was real in both: a stale call's `finally` running after a newer one started would otherwise report "not running" while the newer job is genuinely still in flight). `clearAll()` (useClash) and `clearIDS()` / `clearValidation()` (useIDS) also bump the epoch so a clear mid-run cannot be resurrected by the run it cleared landing afterwards.

**Hooks checked and found already hardened, so left untouched:**
- `useIfcLoader.ts` — `loadSessionRef` epoch bumped in `loadFile`, re-checked before every downstream write (dozens of sites, e.g. finalize, streaming, cache staleness).
- `useIfcFederation.ts` — same `loadSessionRef` per-call ownership token pattern in `addModel`.

**Out of scope (no async job to supersede):** `useZoneSelection.ts` and `useZoneWriteBack.ts` are synchronous — no `await` in either, so this class of bug cannot occur there.

**Not touched:** everything on the open-PR exclusion list (`useCompare.ts`, `compareSlice.ts`, `idsSlice.ts`, etc.) per the sweep instructions — `useIDS.ts` itself is not on that list, only its slice.

## Test plan

- [x] RED: both new test files fail against the pre-fix code (pasted in commit description / available on request).
- [x] GREEN: both pass after the fix.
- [x] Mutation: forcing each hook's `stillWanted`/`stillWantedValidation` to always return `true` reproduces the RED failure in the corresponding test — confirms the guard is load-bearing, not incidental.
- [x] `useClash.*.test.tsx` full suite (57 tests) still green.
- [x] `useIDS`-adjacent suites (`idsWorkerClient`, `resolveValidationTarget`) still green.
- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` in `apps/viewer` shows no new errors attributable to `useClash.ts` / `useIDS.ts`.
- [x] Full `apps/viewer` suite run: 4816 pass / 40 fail — the 40 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (compare/layers/extensions/sources/mcp modules with build-dependency issues from other in-flight PRs); none touch `useClash*` or `useIDS*`.

References #2802.

body:
## Changes

- Pin the Playwright container image to its digest.

```diff
-      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1-noble
+      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1-noble@sha256:dcc5531e...
```

## Why

`v1.62.1-noble` is a mutable tag. Registry tags can be re-pushed to point at different content, which is the same class of exposure that SHA pinning closes for actions — and this container runs every E2E job with the repository checked out into it.

Renovate's `docker:pinDigests` (via `config:best-practices`) would do this, but it runs on Mondays, so the tag stays mutable until then. Pinning by hand now; Renovate will keep the digest current from here.

The digest comes from the `docker pull` in [the last successful run on `main`](https://github.com/corrupt952/SnackTime/actions/runs/32224651579), so it is what CI has actually been executing:

```
Digest: sha256:dcc5531e97840b9b5e794f2814476b21571c5124a3fca2267d73041f56e7580e
Status: Downloaded newer image for mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1-noble
```

This PR's own E2E run verifies it: a wrong digest fails immediately at `Initialize containers`.

Note that the digest and the `playwright` version in `package.json` must move together. Renovate handles both, but a manual bump to one needs the other.

author: jacksonfdam
body:
Closes #23.

`parsePyproject` matched one thing —

```js
content.match(/\[project\][\s\S]*?dependencies\s*=\s*\[([\s\S]*?)\]/)
```

— and then stored every entry with **`version: null`**, discarding the constraint it had just read. `django>=4.2` was filed as `django`, version unknown, while `requirements.txt` in the same parser extracted versions correctly.

Everything else in the file was invisible. Poetry below 2.0 writes no `[project]` table at all, so a Poetry project scanned as **empty**.

## What is read now

| Table | Written by |
|---|---|
| `[project] dependencies` | PEP 621, everything modern |
| `[project.optional-dependencies]` | extras |
| `[dependency-groups]` | PEP 735, what `uv` writes |
| `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` | Poetry |
| `[tool.poetry.group.*.dependencies]` | Poetry groups |
| `[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]` | Poetry 1.0 |
| `[tool.pdm.dev-dependencies]` | PDM |
| `[tool.hatch.envs.*]` `dependencies` / `extra-dependencies` | Hatch |

Which tables count is one list — `pyprojectSections.js` — so a new tool is one entry rather than a condition buried in the walker.

## Three things the real files taught

I verified against `psf/requests`, `pydantic`, `httpx`, `fastapi`, `Textualize/rich` and `python-poetry/poetry`. Each of these came out of that, and a hand-written fixture would have missed all three.

**A bracket inside a quoted string closed the array early.** `"requests[socks]"` contains `]`, so the walker stopped after the first entry of a multi-line array and `pytest>=8.0` on the next line went unread. Brackets are now looked at outside quoted strings.

**`python-poetry`'s own pyproject uses two PEP 508 forms that are not versions.** A direct reference, `poetry-core @ git+https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-core.git`, names a source — it now reports unknown rather than storing a URL as a version. And a bracketed specifier, `build (>=1.2.1,<2.0.0)`, whose brackets made the version uncomparable — they are stripped.

**`psf/requests` lists `requests[socks]` in its own test group.** A project listing itself is an editable self-install for testing extras, not a dependency to advise about, so the project's own name is excluded — read from `[project]` or `[tool.poetry]` ahead of everything else, because the table naming it does not have to come first.

## Two more things deliberately not read

`python` under a Poetry dependency table is the interpreter, and a version lookup for it would ask PyPI about the language. `[tool.poetry.extras]` references dependencies declared above rather than adding any, so reading it would count the same package twice — `rich` declares `ipywidgets` once and mentions it again there.

## Verification

On the six real files: no self-references, no duplicates, no `python` row, no bracket or URL stored as a version. Before and after on `Textualize/rich`, which is the Poetry case:

```
before   0 dependencies
after   10 dependencies   pygments^2.13.0  ipywidgets>=7.5.1,<9  markdown-it-py>=2.2.0  …
```

```
764 tests, 49 suites, all passing with TEST_DATABASE_URL
28 new tests, one fixture per tool
```

Python lockfiles — `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`, `pdm.lock`, `Pipfile.lock` — stay out of scope here and are #25.

author: toudefu
body:
## Motivation

This PR reverts several PTX-specific TensorIR (TIR) test cases back to their upstream `main` state. 

Currently, these tests heavily rely on NVIDIA-specific hardware behaviors, particularly the 32-thread warp size and specific register layouts (e.g., software fallbacks for `ldmatrix` with hardcoded 32-thread indexing). When running on architectures with a 64-thread warp/wavefront (such as Moore Threads MACA), these hardcoded memory mapping formulas cause severe data layout misalignment and precision issues. 

Instead of adding complex, architecture-specific `if/else` fallbacks that pollute the PTX test suite, we are rolling these files back to cleanly align with upstream.

## Modifications
Reverted the following files to the latest `upstream/main` state via `git checkout`:
* `tests/python/tirx-base/test_tir_ptx_cp_async.py`
* `tests/python/tirx-base/test_tir_ptx_griddepcontrol.py`
* `tests/python/tirx-base/test_tir_ptx_ldmatrix.py`
* `tests/python/tirx-base/test_tir_ptx_mma.py`
* `tests/python/tirx-base/test_tir_ptx_mma_sp.py`
* `tests/python/tirx-base/test_tir_ptx_scalar_f32_math.py`

## Target Branch
`dev`

author: sambetts
body:
# Copilot: import the three Graph Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports

Closes milestone #6.

## Why

Today 100% of our Copilot data comes from the audit log. Microsoft explicitly states audit data "is not
intended to be used as the basis for Copilot usage reporting", and that metrics like prompt count or active
user count built on it "might not be consistent" with their official reports. So our numbers can disagree
with the Microsoft 365 admin centre and we have no defence. These three reports are the numbers customers
will compare us against.

This does **not** replace the audit-log Copilot import — the two answer different questions, and having both
is the point (see *Product angle* below).

## Scope

Imports all three reports, behind a new opt-in toggle:

| Report | Grain | Table |
|---|---|---|
| `getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountSummary` | per period, per app | `copilot_user_count_log` |
| `getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountTrend` | per day, per app | `copilot_user_count_log` |
| `getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail` | per user, per date, per period | `copilot_usage_user_activity_log` |

Aggregates are imported first: they are a few thousand rows whatever the tenant size, need no per-user joins,
and are immune to the identity-concealment problem below, so they still work where the per-user report can't.

## Transport

Uses the **beta endpoints with `$format=application/json`**, over exactly the same plumbing as every other
Graph usage report here: `ManualGraphCallClient`, paged by `LoadAllPagesWithThrottleRetries`, sharing its
throttling and retry budget. No bespoke transport.

Rows are read as `JObject` rather than a fixed DTO, on purpose. The reports carry one property pair per
Copilot surface (`wordEnabledUsers` / `wordActiveUsers`) and Microsoft keeps adding surfaces — Edge,
Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat work/web all arrived in one revision. Discovering them dynamically is
what makes a new Microsoft app become new *rows* rather than a new column, a new DTO property and a schema
migration on every customer database. Unrecognised prefixes still import with a generated name; known ones map
to the names the admin centre uses, so `powerPoint` stays "PowerPoint" rather than becoming "Power Point".

## Endpoint behaviours this had to handle

Each of these fails *silently* rather than loudly if ignored:

- **`version` is optional and defaults to `v1`.** Omit it and every prompt-count and active-usage-days value
  is simply absent — no error. `CopilotReportRequest` always sends it.
- **Valid `period` values differ by version**: v1 `D7/D30/D90/D180/ALL`, v2 `D7/`**`D28`**`/D90/D180/ALL`.
  Mixing them is a plain 400, so the pairing is validated before the call.
- **The JSON nests its numbers one level down** — `adoptionByProduct`, `adoptionByDate`, and
  `copilotActivityUserDetailsByPeriod` for the per-user report. One user object therefore yields one row per
  period, which is exactly the table's `(date, user, period)` key.
- **Licensed users only, global cloud only, ~48h latency.** Reflected in the docs, log messages and cadence.

**Microsoft has not published the beta JSON schema for report version 2.** Those fields are therefore looked
up under more than one plausible name and stay null when absent. Because absence is ambiguous — it can mean
"this is a v1 response" *or* "the names differ from the ones we look for" — a response carrying no version 2
values leaves those columns **untouched** rather than writing NULL over prompt counts a previous import
captured. Blanking good data is the more damaging of the two possible mistakes. This is the one place the v1.0
CSV endpoints would have been stricter, since their column names are documented.

## Identity concealment — the important behaviour

If the tenant enables *"Display concealed user, group and site names in all reports"*, Graph still returns
`200 OK` with one row per licensed user — just with the UPN and display name replaced by hashes.

Feeding those through the usual get-or-create-user path would create **one junk user per licensed account**
(200,000 on a large tenant), permanently polluting `users` and every report built on it, and producing joins
that are *wrong* rather than missing. So:

- the per-user report is **not imported at all** in that state;
- the reason is recorded in `copilot_usage_report_import_log`;
- the Health page degrades with the admin-actionable reason (including where to turn the setting off);
- the tenant-level counts are unaffected, and the audit-log Copilot import is not affected by that setting at
  all, so Copilot reporting keeps working from the audit source.

There are two layers, because syntax alone can never prove an identity belongs to the tenant:

1. A UPN shape check (rejects a bare hash, `hash@hash`, and a 32-character all-hex local part) — defence in
   depth. The hash length is matched exactly so a genuine account spellable in hex
   (`0123456789abcdef@contoso.com`) is not rejected.
2. **The actual boundary: the loader will not invent a user on an email domain this database holds no users
   for.** Unrecognised domains are skipped and counted, with a log line pointing at the user-metadata import.
   (An empty `users` table falls back to creating, since there is nothing to validate against yet.)

## Schema

Migration `202608190725064_AddCopilotUsageReports`. Three new, empty tables — `CREATE TABLE` is metadata-only,
so this is effectively instant at any tenant size, needs no maintenance window, and rewrites no existing
table. The only lock on existing data is a brief schema lock on `dbo.users` for the foreign key.

**`copilot_user_count_log` is narrow/tall by design** — one row per (report type, period, date, app) instead
of a column per app. See *Transport* above for why that matters.

Trend rows leave `report_period_days` NULL: a daily count is the same number whichever window asked for it,
and SQL Server treats NULLs as equal in a unique index, so a D7 refresh updates the rows a D180 backfill
created rather than duplicating every day.

The per-user table follows the `*_user_activity_log` convention and is keyed
`(date, user_id, report_period_days)` — D7 and D28 describe the same user and date with *different* prompt
counts, active-day counts and last-activity values, so they're different facts, not a conflict.

Both indexes are UNIQUE and **functional, not performance-motivated**: they're the keys the importer upserts
on, which is what stops Graph's 3-day rolling gap-fill from duplicating rows on re-import. Per the repo rule
that a performance index must ship with a measured before/after benchmark, no covering index is included here
— that should be added *and measured* when a report query against these tables actually exists.

All text columns are `nvarchar`, so localised app names and non-Latin display names round-trip.

`<migrationid>.manual.sql` is included and was validated end to end: applies from the predecessor state,
stamps `__MigrationHistory` with a `Model` **byte-identical** to the `.resx` snapshot, EF then reports no
pending migrations, and a re-run is a no-op. Because this migration changes the EF model it cannot copy the
predecessor's `Model` blob (EF would then try to create the tables again), so the correct snapshot is embedded
as chunked base64; `ProductVersion` is stamped explicitly as `6.5.2` to match an installer-driven upgrade.

## Cadence

Copilot reports get their own `GraphCopilotUsageReportsIntervalHours`, defaulting to **24h on every preset**.

They deliberately do *not* reuse `GraphMetadataImportIntervalHours`: that is preset-derived and **0 (= every
cycle) on the default `High` preset**, with a 10-minute cycle pause. Reusing it would have re-downloaded and
re-processed every licensed user's Copilot row every 10 minutes against a source that only refreshes every
~48 hours. This feature has no lega

author: shiftedx
body:
Carry-forward defect from #48 (merged as `9522c3f`), found by the re-review checking the fix against
the real hermes source rather than against our stub. The finding is correct and the protection was
inert.

## The defect

`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py:1139-1156`, verbatim from the installed 0.20.4:

```python
@method("image.detach")
def _(rid, params: dict) -> dict:
    ...
    raw = str(params.get("path", "") or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return _err(rid, 4015, "path required")
    images = session.setdefault("attached_images", [])
    before = len(images)
    session["attached_images"] = [path for path in images if path != raw]
```

`path` is required, and the call removes exactly that entry. Our merged unwind sent
`{ session_id }` only, so every detach errored `4015`, `#detachQuietly` swallowed it by design, and
the stranded image still rode the user's next text turn. The I2 fix looked like protection and was
not.

## The fix

`image.attach_bytes` already answers with the absolute path it wrote (`methods_prompt.py:953-965`:
`{"attached": True, "path": str(img_path), "count": ...}`). That path is captured from the attach
result and passed to the detach.

Removing BY PATH rather than clearing the queue is also the correct scope, not just the required
shape: `attached_images` is process-global per session, so a blanket clear would throw away an image
somebody else attached in the same window.

Two smaller things on the same path:

- A detach answering `detached: false` (hermes no longer had it, most likely because the submit
  actually landed on their side) is logged rather than read as success.
- An attach that reports no `path` at all leaves nothing to unwind with, so that is logged explicitly
  instead of silently skipped. The send still fails on the submit either way; the missing path is not
  treated as a pre-submit failure, because the unwind is a contingency and not a precondition.

The path stays in memory for the length of one send: never logged, never stored, never sent to a
device. Same rule the transcript strip and the `hermesError` redaction already enforce, applied to
the one place the gateway legitimately holds one.

## On the `attached === true` question

Verified as asked. It is a strict identity test against a result first narrowed to an object, so a
non-object answer collapses to `{}` and fails the check; only a literal `true` proceeds to the
submit. It had no test for the non-object case, so there is one now.

## Why this shipped green, and what changed in the tests

The stubs were too lenient in exactly the way this repo already warns about for session ids: both the
unit stub and the fake hermes server accepted any detach and answered success, so a call hermes would
have rejected every time looked fine. Both now model the real semantics:

- `image.attach_bytes` pushes the path it returns onto a queue;
- `prompt.submit` consumes and clears the whole queue (`server.py:10495`);
- `image.detach` requires `path`, `4015` without one, and removes exactly that entry.

That lets the tests assert the property that actually matters, which is what the user's NEXT turn
picks up, instead of which RPC was called.

## Regression tests (confirmed red against merged main, then green)

Temporarily reverted the source change in place, rebuilt, re-ran. Exactly these three failed:

```
× unwinds the queued image when the attach landed and the submit did not (review I2)
× leaves nothing for the user's next turn to pick up after a failed photo send (review I2, live shape)
× leaves hermes holding nothing when the attach landed and the submit failed
```

The middle one is the user-visible defect stated directly: photo 502s, user types something
unrelated, and that turn must spend no images. The third is the same thing end to end through the
route against the fake hermes server. A fourth new test covers the no-path attach branch and a fifth
covers the non-object attach result.

## Gates

```
pnpm install                 exit 0
pnpm -r build                exit 0
pnpm test                    exit 0   gateway 784, contract 62, relay 92, conformance 29
pnpm -r typecheck            exit 0
```

author: undermybed
body:
Fixes §B and §C from the [data audit](https://github.com/UnderMyBed/TarkovGunsmith/pull/137). Two unit errors and one sign error, all pre-existing, all user-visible.

## Recoil was applied at 1/100th strength

Upstream `recoilModifier` is a **fraction** (AK-74 polymer stock reports `-0.21` for its in-game −21%). The code treated it as a percent and divided by 100.

Rather than convert at the adapter — which is what let one bug live in three copies — this **adopts upstream's unit**: `recoilModifierPercent` → `recoilModifier`, and `weaponSpec` computes `1 + sum` with no `/100` anywhere. The adapters become passthrough, and `adaptMod`/`adaptWeapon` collapse into a single shared `@tarkov/data` home next to the Zod schema that declares the unit.

The production symptom was a **blank badge**: `build-header` suppresses deltas under 0.5%, and a real −45.5% build computed −0.46%.

## `max-accuracy` was selecting for the worst accuracy

Positive `accuracyModifier` means *better* accuracy (M700 AI AT AICS chassis `+0.06`, Magpul PRS `+0.05`); negative means suppressors. `WeaponSpec.accuracy` is MOA where lower is better, so the sign was inverted — and the optimizer minimises it, picking `Math.min`. **"Maximise accuracy" returned suppressors and rejected precision stocks.**

Now `baseAccuracy * (1 - sum)`, with the bound and per-item score flipped to match.

## The clamp is provably inert

`MIN_RECOIL_MULTIPLIER = 0.01`. Measured across all 171 live weapons at the shipped recursion depth, the deepest reachable multiplier is **0.062** (Kalashnikov AKM) and it *saturates* — depth 4 and 5 give the same value. So the clamp cannot alter any number the app shows today. A floor near a "plausible" game minimum was rejected as an unevidenced modelling claim.

## Scale lockstep

`bounds.ts` had to move in the same commit. Score and bound were *consistently* wrong, which is the only reason the optimizer still picked correct mods; changing one without the other makes the bound inadmissible and prunes the true optimum. Confirmed empirically — **every attachment-choice assertion passed unchanged**.

## Also fixed

The optimizer's RCL column rendered `−0` on every changed row: `(0.23).toFixed(0)` is `"0"`.

The og fixture's four "real Tarkov item IDs" were a front sight, a receiver extension, an M-LOK rail, and **one id that doesn't exist upstream at all** — replaced with slot-legal mods and real weapon stats.

## Honest limits

- **This makes recoil ~100× less wrong, not correct.** A fully-kitted AKM resolves to 0.062 of base (vertical 145 → 9); the game lands nearer 0.4. The flat sum over every attached mod is likely not EFT's formula. The unit bug was masking that by compressing everything to nearly zero effect.
- The nested-slot bound is not admissible (covers only currently-known remaining slots). Pre-existing and scale-invariant — noted, not fixed.
- `baseAccuracy` is still the fabricated constant `3.5`, so accuracy is meaningful only as a relative comparison.

Tests were watched failing against unmodified code first: `expected 118.3574 to be close to 54.74`, and the badge test failing with *"Unable to find an element with the text: −50%"* — the blank-badge symptom reproduced.

Extends the flyer's "enter it once, reused everywhere" behavior to the **guides and co-marketing pieces** (email templates, open house kit, social kit, video scripts).

Those templates used `[YOUR NAME]` / `[BROKERAGE]` / `[PHONE]` placeholders that agents had to fill in by hand. Now the copy and print components substitute the logged-in agent's saved profile automatically.

- New `fillAgentTokens()` maps agent-identity tokens (`[YOUR NAME]`, `[BROKERAGE]`, `[PHONE]`, `[YOUR EMAIL]`, `[DRE]`, plus aliases) to the profile's values.

author: cjo2343
body:
## What

The load-rehearsal **seeder** now budgets its sign-ins against Supabase Auth's rate limit and skips workspaces a previous pass already built. Plus two harness findings from the hosted exercise-3 run (T5, T6).

### 1. Sign-in budget (finding T1)

`lib/signin-budget.mjs` — a **sliding-window budget**, default **30 grants per 300 s** (`--signin-budget N`, `--signin-window S`). When the window is empty the seeder **pauses with a visible countdown** instead of firing calls that will be refused:

```
   ⏳ sign-in budget spent (30/300 s, 30 so far) — next slot in 4 min 12s…
```

A real 429 parks **every** sign-in for the response's `Retry-After` (delta-seconds *or* HTTP-date), or a full window when the platform does not say. `httpJson`'s own 429 retry is switched off on the sign-in path so the budget owns the backoff, and `httpJson` now surfaces `retryAfterMs`.

Members are signed in **once per pass** (`SessionCache`), and the run prints its estimate up front:

```
⏳ Building workspaces… 20 to build, 0 already complete (skipped, 0 sign-ins).
   sign-in plan: ~110 sign-ins at 30/300 s ≈ 15 min (4 windows)
```

### 2. Resume skips completed workspaces (finding T3)

`lib/seed-state.mjs` — per-workspace completion markers in a small JSON file kept **outside the repo**: `--state <file>`, default `~/.vehloshare-rehearsal-seed-state.json`; a path inside the repo tree is refused. A complete workspace is skipped **before any sign-in** (zero sign-ins), so a resumed pass spends its whole budget on unbuilt work.

Markers are keyed on **project ref + `--seed` + email domain** and carry a **signature of the planned contents**, so a different project, a different seed or a changed fixture rebuilds rather than skips. A workspace that produced any warning is **not** marked, so partial work is retried. `--ignore-state` re-verifies everything the old way. The file holds no credentials and no addresses.

### 3. T5 — schema-apply names the deadlock

The first apply against a brand-new project died on **SQLSTATE 40P01** (`create trigger … on booking_handovers` vs a Supabase-side `AccessShareLock`; PostgREST re-introspects after every DDL). Reported as a generic failure it reads as *"supabase-schema.sql does not apply to a fresh project"* — which is wrong; it is a race that clears once the tenant is warm. `schema-apply.mjs` now detects it and says so, and README step 2 documents the recovery.

> ⚠️ **Deviation:** the ticket asked for an *automatic* wipe of `public` + one retry. Writing destructive DDL (dropping the `public` schema) into the toolkit was **refused by the permission classifier**, so the reset is documented as an operator step instead of performed by the tool. Say the word and I'll add the automatic version with explicit approval.

### 4. T6 — `MissingPartition` is its own refusal bucket

*"Realtime was unable to find the expected messages partition"* now buckets as **`MissingPartition`** rather than `other` — and never as `Unauthorized`, which would send the operator to RLS for a janitor race. `load.mjs`'s failure legend and the README reason table carry the explanation (fresh project: the first joins race the tenant janitor that day-partitions `realtime.messages`; production: a partition gap at a day roll-over).

## Why

Observed again 2026-08-18: `--workspaces 20` built exactly **10** workspaces, then every further sign-in got `HTTP 429`. Exercise 1 hit the same wall and plateaued at 10–12 of 20 across 13+ rounds, because each retry re-signed-in every member of every already-built workspace (T3) while the un-throttled pool burnt the window in the first two workspaces (T1). T4 — the dashboard cannot raise the limit — stands, and is why the defaults are 30/300 s.

**A full 20-workspace seed should now complete in ONE pass**, taking ~15–20 minutes of mostly waiting rather than plateauing.

## Verification

No live Supabase project was touched — everything below is `--dry-run`, unit tests, or an in-process stub on `127.0.0.1`.

- `npm run validate` → ✅ all validations passed (sibling-repo checks warn/skip as usual in a scratch worktree).
- `npm run test:load-rehearsal` → **77 passed, 0 failed** (was 64 on `main`; 13 new).
  New tests: budget timing on an **injected clock** (window spent → pause → sliding refill), the 429 backoff with and without `Retry-After`, the countdown ticks, `parseRetryAfterMs` (delta-seconds, HTTP-date, garbage), the estimate math, session reuse under concurrency, state key/signature/round-trip/corruption/`--ignore-state`, the repo-tree guard, `MissingPartition` bucketing, source scans that the seeder actually *uses* the budget and the state file (a slot taken *before* every grant; pending filtered *before* the pool), and that `--dry-run` still prints the plan and writes no state.
- `node tools/load-rehearsal/seed.mjs --dry-run --seed 42 --workspaces 20` → plan + budget + estimate + state path, no network.
- End-to-end smoke against a throwaway in-process HTTP stub (not committed): 3 workspaces seeded, 18 budgeted sign-ins with visible pauses; **re-run: `0 to build, 3 already complete (skipped, 0 sign-ins)`**; and with the stub 429ing the first six grants, all six absorbed at the stub's `Retry-After: 2` and the run still completed. That smoke also caught a real TDZ bug (`SIGNIN_ATTEMPTS` declared below `await main()`), now fixed.
- Bad input: `--signin-budget 0` and `--state <path-in-repo>` both exit 1 with a readable message.

Not touched: `supabase/`, `supabase-schema.sql`, `types/`, `tools/test-migrations.mjs`, `docs/operations/load-rehearsal-evidence.md`.

## ELI5

Signing in to the app is rate-limited: the server only lets us log people in about 30 times every 5 minutes, and that ceiling can't be raised. Our test-data builder needs to log in ~110 pretend users to build 20 pretend car-sharing groups — so it used to sprint through its allowance in the first minute and then get the door slammed on it for the remaining eighteen groups. Worse, every time we started it again it insisted on logging everybody back in from the beginning, including the groups it had already finished, so it kept re-doing the same work and never got to the end.

Now it keeps count. It logs in as fast as it's allowed, and when it's used up the allowance it simply waits — showing a countdown — until the next batch is free, and it tells you at the start roughly how long the whole thing will take ("about 15 minutes"). It also writes down which groups it finished, in a small notebook kept outside the project folder, so next time it skips those completely and spends its whole allowance on what's actually left. One run, start to finish, instead of a dozen that stall halfway.

Two smaller fixes ride along: when the very first setup of a brand-new database trips over a well-known timing clash, the tool now says "this is a timing clash, wait a moment and retry" instead of "your schema is broken"; and when the live-updates connection is refused because a piece of server housekeeping hasn't run yet on a brand-new project, that now gets its own clearly-named label instead of being lumped in with "unknown error".
