author: 0kaba0
body:
Follow-up to #1351, closing the gap the window found. appVersion 2.3.193.

## Why the previous fix was incomplete

Per-site classification is **always one site behind**. `STORE` was classified at its `UpdateFlagsMulti` call, and the failure arrived from a different call in the same handler — so a lock-service restart still reached clients as `SERVERBUG`. That is the second time a missing site was found by a rollout window rather than by a test.

## IMAP: the seam already existed

`timedSession` is the one place every command passes through on its way back to the client — it was measuring commands, and now translates the error there too.

Two properties come free with that:

- a command **added later cannot miss it**: the interface assertion in that file stops the build until the method is forwarded;
- and a structural test fails on any forwarded call that returns the store's error unclassified. Mutation-checked: un-classify `Store` and it names it.

I did not build a new decorator. Wrapping the session from scratch would have had to re-implement every optional interface the library type-asserts for (`SessionACL`, `SessionQuota`, `SessionIMAP4rev2`…), and missing one **silently removes a capability** — the exact failure mode we keep hunting. The existing wrapper already carries them all.

## JMAP: the dispatch cannot do it

`jmapcore` must stay free of yarilo imports (there is a test for it), so a wrapper around `entry.Fn` would only ever see a `MethodError` with the cause already thrown away. The seam there is **where a Go error becomes a method error**, and there is now one function that does it. The point fix in `Email/set` becomes a special case of the general rule rather than a second rule beside it.

## The marker now survives the common shape of the outage

A Service with no endpoints **blackholes rather than refusing**, so the failure arrives as a deadline, not a connection error — and an unmarked deadline is exactly what the seam would classify as SERVERBUG. Both internal wait paths mark it now.

**Deadlines only, never cancellations**, as you specified: a cancelled context is the caller giving up — a client that disconnected — and marking that would report our own callers' departures as failures of `yarilo-locks`. Four rows pin the boundary, including that the cause survives either way.

## Field check

The same experiment as before: scale `yarilo-locks` to zero, then `STORE`. Expect `NO [UNAVAILABLE]` **regardless of which call inside the handler failed** — that is the property this changes. Worth also trying `APPEND` and `EXPUNGE`, which were on the list of surfaces still answering SERVERBUG in #1339 and now go through the same seam.

author: ipv1337
body:
Groundwork for the two remaining Cloud Run integrations. Both need in-cluster workloads (Backstage, Grafana) to read GCP APIs, and both obvious routes are closed:

- **`iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` is enforced org-wide** — verified `--effective` on `prj-d-bu1-oss-floating-648a` — so no JSON key
- **Neither workload runs on GCE**, so there's no metadata server to fall back on

So this federates the cluster's own OIDC issuer instead. Nothing long-lived to leak or rotate.

## Why the JWKS is inline

The issuer is `https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local` — an in-cluster address GCP cannot resolve. Rather than expose the Kubernetes API server to the internet purely to satisfy OIDC discovery, the JWKS is supplied **statically**.

The cost is real and documented: if the cluster's signing keys rotate, the value must be re-synced or every exchange fails with an opaque `invalid_grant`.

## Why the trust is narrow

A projected ServiceAccount token is mintable by any pod that can mount one, so trusting the issuer alone would let *any* workload impersonate.

- `AttributeCondition` pins accepted subjects to an explicit list — a pod in an unrelated namespace is rejected **at the provider**, before any IAM binding is consulted
- the `workloadIdentityUser` binding names the **exact subject principal**, not an attribute `principalSet`, matching the reasoning already applied to the Pulumi ESC provider directly above it

## The injection this guards

The condition is built with `%q`, not concatenation. A subject containing a quote would otherwise close the CEL literal and have its tail parsed as an expression — turning a subject *allowlist* into a condition true for everyone:

```
subject:  a" || true || "b
%s  ->    assertion.sub == 'a" || true || "b'     ← always true
%q  ->    assertion.sub == "a\" || true || \"b"   ← never matches
```

`clusterAttributeCondition` is unit-tested on exactly that input. Verified by mutation — swapping `%q` back to `%s` fails the suite:

```
--- FAIL: TestClusterAttributeCondition/one_subject
--- FAIL: TestClusterAttributeCondition/several_subjects_are_OR-ed
```

## Scope discipline

- Setting the issuer without a JWKS, or without subjects, is a **hard error** rather than a partial build — a federation accepting every ServiceAccount in the cluster is not a useful default
- The issuer joins the existing **single** folder-scoped allowed-issuer policy as a third entry; that file exists precisely because a second policy for the same constraint fights the first rather than adding to it
- This stack creates the identity and grants it **nothing** on the app projects — the read-only roles belong to the stack that owns those projects, so the foundation doesn't quietly accumulate authority over workloads it doesn't manage
- Its own pool rather than a provider inside `foundation-pool`, so a mistake here can't reach the pool backing every foundation CI deploy
- Everything is gated on `cluster_issuer_uri`; **unset, this is a complete no-op** — which is how it will merge, since the config isn't set yet

## Verification

`go build` + `go test` clean (`GOWORK=off`), gazelle run, `//:tidy` leaves the tree clean, `license:check`/`verify` and conformance pass.

Docs: `docs/gcp-cluster-federation.md`, linked into the TechDocs nav rather than left orphaned (the mistake #1777 had to fix for the other two).

## Follow-ups

1. Set the config + grant `run.viewer`/`monitoring.viewer` in the owning stack
2. Cloud Run revision card in Backstage — certain to work; Node's google-auth-library fully supports external-account ADC
3. Grafana metrics — its plugin offers only `AuthType.GCE` and `AuthType.JWT`; I expect the GCE path honours external-account ADC via `google.DefaultTokenSource`, but that's an expectation I'll verify empirically rather than assert

author: calvinchengx
body:
Core put silver's three Spark-only constructs behind dialect macros ([contoso-data-product `bfdc9a5`](https://github.com/calvinchengx/contoso-data-product)). Its **Snowflake branch emits `DATEADD` and `table(generator(rowcount => n))` with `seq4()`** — and this emulator had neither, plus `ARRAY_GENERATE_RANGE`.

So silver-on-Snowflake would have failed at its first model. Nobody would have noticed, because nothing runs silver on Snowflake yet (G5).

## Measured before and after

The statement the calendar model actually emits now runs, and keeps its type:

```sql
SELECT DATEADD(day, seq4(), b.lo) AS rate_date
FROM b, table(generator(rowcount => 20000))
WHERE DATEADD(day, seq4(), b.lo) <= b.hi
  →  2026-01-01 .. 2026-01-05      type: date
```

Before this PR: `Catalog Error: no such function dateadd`, `Parser Error` on `generator`.

## `DATEADD` finally has an answer

The reason it can now is narrower than the one that kept it out. **`DATE + INTEGER` is a `DATE` in DuckDB**, so day and week offsets keep the type Snowflake returns. Hour, minute and second go through an interval — a timestamp either way, so also right.

`MONTH`, `QUARTER` and `YEAR` are **still refused by name**: every DuckDB spelling widens a `DATE` to a `TIMESTAMP`, and a `CASE` cannot return two types.

A `TIMESTAMP` given to the day form is an error here where Snowflake would answer — an honest error rather than a silently wrong type, recorded in `parity.md`.

## `INTEGER` and not `BIGINT`

Load-bearing rather than fussy: `DATE + BIGINT` is an error in DuckDB where `DATE + INTEGER` is a `DATE`, and offsetting a date by the row number is the entire reason the generator is here. There's a test pinning it.

**50 of 62 answered**, up from 45.

author: lewis617
body:
The ! interpolation runs under cmd.exe on Windows, so bash-only syntax
broke the context: 2>/dev/null is parsed as a redirect to a file (WinError 3
"path not found"), gh/glab never ran, and the fallback emitted a literal
'{}'. Replace with shell-neutral syntax:

- drop 2>/dev/null, use 2>&1 so failures stay visible instead of being
  silently swallowed by the fallback
- replace || true (no such command in cmd.exe) with || echo none/{}
- drop --jq '{branch: ...}' (single quotes don't group in cmd, and the
  brace expression triggers bash brace-expansion) — plain --json output

Also make the failed-log temp path Grep-tool-readable on Windows: the Bash
tool writes /tmp/gh-failed-log.txt (MSYS), but the native Grep tool can't
resolve /tmp — print the cygpath -w converted path (fallback to the MSYS
path on macOS/Linux) and have the Grep step use it.

author: bibaermek-stack
body:
The VR/AR trainer looked finished, but several parts of it did not actually work. This fixes five separate problems in `components/dashboard/VRSimulator.tsx`.

## What was broken

**One click completed every task.** Each scene had a single click handler that posted all three task ids at once, so clicking the prism marked the whole checklist done. The space and history scenes had no click handler at all — their six tasks could never be completed.

**The object info panel was dead code.** The React side listened for `VR_INTERACTION` and rendered "3D Нысанның дерегі", but nothing ever sent that message. Planet names sat in the data and never reached the screen.

**Kazakh text was mangled.** The in-scene HUD panels were missing Kazakh letters — «Толкын узындыгы», «Орталык жулдыз», «Когилдир кыш кумбез», «6-осьтик».

**The lab rendered nearly black.** Every surface used `metalness` above 0.7, and metal renders from what it reflects. With no environment map there was nothing to reflect.

**The robot arm could not bend or move anything.** Its joints were siblings rather than nested, so it stood as a straight pole. The workpiece was never picked up, despite a task asking for it.

## What changed

- Objects now carry their own label, description and task id. A click resolves the nearest tagged ancestor and closes only that task — `TASK_PROGRESS` is sent from one place instead of six. All 12 task ids across the four scenes are covered.
- `VR_INTERACTION` is wired up, so clicking a planet or artefact shows its name and a one-line description.
- HUD text corrected, including physics notation (λ, sin α / sin β, F = G·M·m / r²).
- A generated gradient panorama is set as `scene.environment`, and the light rig was rebalanced for the physically-correct renderer.
- The arm is now a real joint chain (turret → shoulder → elbow → wrist) driven by a pick-and-place cycle. The reach pose comes from a two-link inverse kinematics solution, so the gripper lands on the box rather than near it. An output tray was added; delivered boxes stay on it and a new box arrives on the conveyor, instead of one box being shuttled back and forth (which read as the box teleporting).
- The animation moved from its own `requestAnimationFrame` loop to the A-Frame component `tick`, so it stops with the scene and can be stepped deterministically.

## Verification

Driven through the browser against the running dev server:

- Clicking the laser closed only task 1; the other two stayed open (counter went 1/3, not 3/3).
- Space, history and robotics objects all resolve by name — «Юпитер — Жүйедегі ең үлкен газ алыбы», «Отырар құмырасы — XII ғасыр қыш ыдысы», «Конвейер».
- Informational objects without a task id (Меркурий, Марс, Ньютон тербелмесі) show their description without touching the counter.
- Three full robot cycles stepped frame by frame: box spawns at the far end of the belt (x = −2.95), reaches the pick point (−1.80), is carried up (y = 2.24), swung across and placed on the tray (+1.80). **Largest per-frame movement: 0.107 units** — continuous motion, no jump. Tray caps at 3 boxes as intended.
- All four scenes load with the environment map applied; `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint are clean.

## Notes for the reviewer

The animation was not verified visually — the browser pane was hidden during the session, which suspends `requestAnimationFrame` entirely (0 frames per second), so motion was measured numerically through the component's `tick` instead. Worth one look in the running app to confirm the lighting reads well on a real screen.

Controller interaction on an actual Meta Quest headset is also untested. A-Frame maps trigger and mouse to the same `click` event, so it should behave the same, but it has only been exercised with a mouse.

author: osama1998h
body:
Closes #338.

`متغير_بيئة` — `(نص) -> نص`, `getenv(3)` — is the Category 8 environment reader from the 40-name
registry in `docs/builtins-vs-stdlib.md` §1.3, and the first name outside Increments A and B. Core
tier, no import.

## The criterion, re-derived

§6.1 made re-derivation a standing rule because four §1.3 rows had criterion (a) expire under them —
`بتات_نفي` (#312), `بتات_إزاحة_يمين_منطقية` (#322), `ثنائي_إلى_نص` (#333) and `قص_حروف` (#336). This
is the first name checked whose criterion is **(b)**, and the check turns out to be a different kind
of claim:

> Criterion (a) asserts something about **the language**, which every increment edits. Criterion (b)
> asserts a capability lives in **the operating system**, which nothing in Tarqeem can move.

So a syscall claim cannot expire. What the (b) rows need checked is their *contract* instead — the
second defect class #333 identified. That check paid off without finding a defect: `trq_env_get` was
read rather than trusted, because this document's other orphan precedent is `trq_performance_now`,
which is a verbatim copy of `trq_time_now` and lies about being monotonic. This one is honest — all
five of its paths (null pointer, null data, empty name, invalid UTF-8, unset variable) already return
an empty `TrqString` rather than a null pointer, so the row's `""`-when-unset clause was satisfied by
code predating the row.

## Contract

Total — it never fails and never aborts. An absent variable, an empty name, a `لا_شيء` argument and a
name that is not valid UTF-8 all answer `""`. Two properties documented rather than fixed:

- **Set-but-empty is indistinguishable from unset.** Both answer `""`, per `getenv(3)`. Follows
  `رمز_إلى_حرف`'s `""`-as-a-value convention rather than `حرف_إلى_رمز`'s `-1` sentinel.
- **The name is not trimmed.** `trq_env_get` bypasses `string.rs`'s `as_str`, which trims — the trap
  #324 recorded. A trimming interpreter arm would answer «مرحبا» for `متغير_بيئة(" PATH ")` where
  native answers `""`, on source that reads like a typo rather than a bug.

Cross-backend agreement is structural rather than merely tested: `trq_env_get` calls `std::env::var`
and so do the interpreter arms, so both inherit the same answer for non-Unicode values.

## Eight sites — a fourth measured cost shape

Everything on the nine-site path except the `runtime-rs` function, which already existed as an orphan
with no caller anywhere.

| Shape | Cost | Example |
|---|---|---|
| IR-intercepted | 2 files | `بتات_و` (#302) |
| Symbol-mapped, new runtime function | 9 sites | `حرف_إلى_رمز` (#324) |
| Symbol-mapped, symbol already exists | **8 sites** | this one |
| Repair of a half-wired name | 6 sites | `قص_حروف` (#336) |

The discriminator is not the tier and not the return type — #330 already showed a "first" that was
only a first for its tier. It is **which half of the path already exists**. Here the runtime half did
and the codegen half did not, the mirror image of #336. `expr_builder.rs` is untouched: a core builtin
absent from `build_core_builtin_call` falls through to `Instruction::Call { func: FuncId(<arabic>) }`,
so both interpreters key on the Arabic name.

## The missing return type, predicted from the struct layout

#336 asked for this to be predicted from the return type's layout rather than sorted into loud or
quiet. Doing that in advance gave the right answer. Measured natively with the
`register_builtin_return_types` line deleted, for the value «مرحبا»:

| Assertion | Without the entry | Right |
|---|---|---|
| `اطبع(…)` | `مرحبا` | `مرحبا` — **passes either way** |
| `نوع(…)` | `مؤشر` | `نص` |
| `"X" + …` | `X4321175728` | `Xمرحبا` |
| `== "مرحبا"` | `خطأ` | `صحيح` |
| `طول(…)` | **10** | **5** |

Four of five — `قص_حروف`'s profile rather than `ثنائي_إلى_نص`'s three. `طول` catches it because the
sentinel routes `ArrayLen` to `trq_array_len`, which reads offset 0, and a `TrqString`'s field at
offset 0 is its byte length.

**The Arabic test value is load-bearing.** On an ASCII value the byte count and the character count
agree, so `طول` would pass with the entry deleted and the gate would be a three-catcher. A
`نص`-returning builtin tested only on ASCII silently gives up one of its assertions.

## Harness change: the environment cannot be set in-process

`متغير_بيئة` is the first builtin whose answer depends on the environment, and `std::env::set_var` is
unusable here — cargo runs tests as threads in one process, so it races every other test.

Every backend leg was already a child process, so the variable goes on the child. `tarqeem_with_env`,
`execute_with_env` and `assert_prints_with_env` are added and the three existing helpers become
one-line wrappers over them, so **all 147 existing call sites are untouched**. The native leg puts the
variables on the *executed binary*, not on `compile` — the compiler reads no environment on that path,
so setting them there compiles fine and then answers `""`.

Absent-variable cases need none of this. Only the exact-value, set-but-empty and no-trimming cases
inject, and set-but-empty is reachable no other way, which is why it is its own test.

## Lexer — a ninth shape, the first that would not look like a lexer failure

`متغير_بيئة` opens with `متغير` (`TokenKind::Let`). Position-wise that matches `نص_إلى_ثنائي` (#330),
but `نص` is a type name already legal as an identifier, while `متغير` opens a **statement**: a
longest-keyword-prefix scan would emit `Let` then `_بيئة` — a well-formed variable declaration — so it
would surface as a missing `=` somewhere unrelated, or not surface. Nine names, nine shapes; the check
stays per-name.

## Tests

- **Registry ratchets**: `CORE_BUILTINS` 30 → 31, grand total 193 → 194. `STDLIB_MODULE_SIZES` is
  untouched — this is an addition, not #336's promotion.
- **Sweep probe** in `test_every_core_builtin_agrees_across_backends`, chosen to be single-line
  discriminating: a stub answering `""` for everything passes every absent-variable case, so the probe
  reads a variable every process has.
- **Seven cross-backend tests**: the composition gate, the exact-value round trip with an Arabic
  value, totality for absent/empty names, set-but-empty, non-trimming, the `لا_شيء` holder in both its
  routes, and builtin shadowing.
- **Debug-interpreter arm test**, since `Backend::ALL` never reaches that interpreter — the gap that
  made `توقف` and `نم` abort under `tarqeem debug` while working everywhere else (#295).
- **CI example**: a section in `examples/مدمجات.ترقيم` printing machine-independent values only, plus
  its golden output, so both the `expected-output` golden diff and the `compare-backends` cross-backend
  diff hold. No `KNOWN_DIVERGENT` or `NATIVE_UNSUPPORTED` entry needed; both lists stay empty.

`tests/runtime_symbols_tests.rs` needs no edit — the new `declare` names a symbol `runtime-rs`
genuinely defines, so `KNOWN_UNDEFINED` stays at 11.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (exit 0), the full
suite (17 groups, 0 failures) and `cargo test -p tarqeem-runtime --lib` (176 passing). The example was
run under all three backends with `env -u TARQEEM_HOME`: byte-identical to each other and to the
committed golden.

## Downstream

`مجلد_مستخدم` and `مجلد_مؤقت` both reduce to it, so Increment G drops from 21 names to 19. Both stay
live under their own symbols until then — each is `getenv` with one key hardcoded, which is why they
collapse. `trq_env_set` and `trq_env_remove` remain orphans: neither is in the 40-name registry.

author: sheetaldharshan200
body:
When every bundled dataset is already loaded, `exakit data-load` pre-selected its **final** row:

```
    • Every bundled dataset is already loaded (reload with: exakit data-load --force).
    • Select data to load
      [ ] A local CSV / Parquet / JSON file
      [✓] Cancel (load nothing)
```

So the one screen whose only remaining purpose is to load a file of your own opened with Enter wired to a no-op, and asked you to move the cursor to reach the row you came for.

The cause was one line:

```sh
info "Every bundled dataset is already loaded (reload with: exakit data-load --force)."
_dls_defaults="$_dls_final_idx"      # the final row IS "Cancel (load nothing)"
```

It now pre-selects the local-file row, which sits one index below the final label.

Nothing else about the menu changes: Cancel is still there, still one keystroke away, and still the exclusive row that clears everything else. The **pending-datasets path is untouched** — when there is something left in the bundle, the group and its datasets stay pre-selected, which is the right default for a first run.

Mirrored in `exapump.ps1`, whose twin had the same `-Defaults @($finalIdx)`.

## Tests

Nothing covered this menu, so `tests/marketplace.sh` gains three checks. The shell assertion reads **the label the default index actually points at**, not the index itself, so renumbering the rows cannot quietly pass:

```sh
ui_checkbox_menu() {                      # $1 title, $2 defaults, $3.. labels
    _dlp_defaults="$2"; shift 2
    eval "printf '%s' \"\${$_dlp_defaults}\"" > "$_dl_probe"
}
```

- the local-file row is pre-selected → `A local CSV / Parquet / JSON file`
- Cancel is not what Enter would take
- the PowerShell twin defaults off the final row

| `marketplace` | 217 passed, 0 failed |

author: zook-bot
body:
## Summary

Found while building the su-uzy9.6 CI security gates (A3 + B5).

## What

`ios/App/Resources/capture-fixture.json` is copied into the Release bundle.
The app target's Release `EXCLUDED_SOURCE_FILE_NAMES` names four artifacts —
CaptureSeam.swift, CaptureURLProtocol.swift, CaptureAudioInjector.swift,
demo-conversation.wav — and this fifth one is absent, so the synchronized
group copies it in both configurations.

## Why it is only P3

No credential in it: 799 bytes of canned listener replies and analyst
candidates, read by `CaptureSeam.loadFixture()` — which is itself `#if DEBUG`
AND excluded, so nothing in a Release binary can read the file. It is dead
weight plus a small design-intent leak (the wording everywhere is that "the
whole capture seam" is compiled out of Release), not an exploitable seam.

## Why su-uzy9.6 did not just fix it

The gate scripts assert the plan's list of four, verbatim
(docs/plans/2026-08-02-001-...-plan.md, Gate A3). Adding a fifth name to the

EXCLUDED_SOURCE_FILE_NAMES at ios/ShutUpAndListen.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:438-443

author: aiagent2046-coder
body:
## What this reports

The tables a repository **names** that its migrations **never declare**.

Not exposure. A table created through the Supabase dashboard is invisible to every static scan in this repo, because static analysis can only judge what the schema describes — and `agent_projects`, the one table ever found genuinely exposed on the deployment we own, was exactly that. This reports the **gap**, so it is visible to the person who could close it, and so `app/proof/rls_probe.py` has names to ask about.

## Measured, 2026-08-19

n=399 repositories across two generators (Lovable, bolt). Of the 108 that use Supabase, commit a schema, and stay under the reader's cap:

| question | result |
|---|---|
| call a table no migration declares | **50% [41–59]** (54/108) |
| — Lovable | 51% [38–64] (26/51) |
| — bolt | 49% [37–62] (28/57) |
| size of the gap | median 3, p25 1, p90 13, max 67 |
| contain a `.from(variable)`, which names no table | 72% [63–80] |

An earlier n=40-per-stratum pass said **62% [46–76]**. The full corpus moved it to 50%; the intervals overlap, so the small sample was the noisier estimate, and every word of the finding is written against 50%. Record: `/home/syndiai/reality-diff-m3.json`.

**The 50% is a floor.** The measurement dropped bucket-shaped names (`documents`, `files`, `media`) *by name*; this code drops them *by call site*. Those are ordinary table names, so the detector sees a superset of what was counted. How much larger is unmeasured, and the module says so rather than quietly enjoying it.

`#296` measured the generated-types source on a different corpus (n=226): 44% [34–55] of repos with both a schema and a types file have a types file naming a table the SQL does not. **Not pooled** — different corpora, different claim strength.

## Two sources, two different claims

This separation is the design, not a detail.

| source | what it proves | wording |
|---|---|---|
| generated types | `supabase gen types typescript` reads the **live project** — the table was in the database | "these tables were in your database" |
| client code | the **application expects** it, nothing more | "what your application expects, not what your database contains" |

A `.from('x')` left behind after the table was dropped is *identical evidence* to a table created in the dashboard. The detector cannot tell them apart, so the client-code finding describes the code and never launders itself into a claim about the database. Confidence follows: **0.6** with types, **0.5** without — both at or below `app/scan/rls.py`'s read rule, which has at least been checked against a real deployment. This one never has.

Every finding discloses its own incompleteness unconditionally. The dynamic-call flag only sharpens the sentence; it never gates it, because letting a regex decide whether to admit incompleteness is how a detector ends up claiming completeness it does not have.

One finding, capped at 12 names — the gap's max is 67, and a report with 67 entries is a report nobody acts on.

## Two defects found on the way, both in shipped code

**1. Storage buckets were being probed as tables.** `supabase.storage.from('avatars')` is the identical call shape, and `find_probe_tables` was handing buckets to the live probe — sending a customer's project a request about a table name we invented. Now excluded by **call site** in the shared matcher, with a test on both readers. By call site and not by a name list, because `documents` and `files` are ordinary table names and a name list drops the real ones with the buckets.

**2. The finding was filed in an LLM-only category.** It read `Money & Data`, which is in `LLM_ONLY_CATEGORIES`. On a static-only audit `compute_scores` excludes those from the mean and `app/db.py` lists them under `unexamined` — so the finding would have moved **no score at all** and printed beneath a heading saying nobody had looked, directly above a finding proving somebody had. The free tier is static-only and is the only thing most visitors ever see. Now `Security`, held by two tests: one asserts the category is not LLM-only, the other asserts the Security subscore actually moves.

## Structure

The first commit is a **pure move**: the name matchers go to `app/scan/table_names.py` and `app/proof/supabase_tables.py` imports them back, re-exporting the two names `scripts/measure_rls_blind_spot.py` reads. `tests/test_proof_supabase_tables.py` passes unchanged, which is why it is committed on its own. The alternative — copying the matcher across the `scan`/`proof` boundary — is the failure `SUPABASE_RLS_YIELD_PLAN.md` already recorded in its own words: *"The script carried its own copy of the matcher and drifted from production within the hour."*

## Verification

- Full suite: **2202 passed, 105 skipped**
- `ruff check app tests scripts`: clean (`ruff format` not applied, per this repo's gate)
- **Replayed the shipped detector over the 108 measured repositories: 54/108 = 50.0%**, matching the measurement exactly. That replay is what caught the singular/plural defect in the customer-facing text (`queries \`todos\` ... creates them`), which fixtures written by hand could not.
- End-to-end test asserts the rule appears in `run_static_scan` output — the test that fails if a future scanner is written and never registered.

## Cost

Zero network, zero credentials, zero consent, zero LLM tokens. Runs in the free tier at no marginal cost.

## Open, and deliberately not closed here

1. **A stale call is not a live table.** Unmeasured. Handled in wording only.
2. **Generated clients.** 15% [10–21] of Supabase repos yield no literal name at all. Some is dynamic calls; the rest is uninvestigated.
3. **This is a coverage gap, not an exposure**, and must not be read as one. Its value is that it feeds names to the live probe, which *can* determine exposure — with consent, per table.

body:
PR: LeetCode Practice – String Problems

Summary
This PR includes solutions to a few basic string manipulation problems solved for practice, focused on understanding two-pointer techniques and character filtering in Python.

Problems covered:

Reverse a String
Implemented logic to reverse a given string in place using a two-pointer approach, swapping characters from both ends toward the middle.
Valid Palindrome
Solved the "Valid Palindrome" problem — checking whether a given phrase reads the same forward and backward after ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters. Used a two-pointer approach on a cleaned/filtered version of the input.
Character Filtering Utility
Added a small standalone snippet that takes user input, filters out non-alphanumeric characters, and lowercases the remaining characters into a cleaned list — used as a helper step for the palindrome check.

Learnings

Practiced two-pointer technique for in-place string operations.
Understood the difference between copying a list vs. referencing the same list in Python.
Used built-in string methods (isalnum(), lower()) for cleaning input before comparison.

author: donislawdev
body:
Eighteen commits in three batches: the Semgrep report from the local scan, three static analysers in CI, and then the supply-chain and quality work built on top of them. Every commit stands on its own.

## 1. The scanner findings (3 commits)

A local Semgrep scan produced 23 findings. **20 are fixed, 2 changed even though the rule was substantively wrong, 1 left with the reason written down.**

- **The only High**: `ci.yml` pasted `${{ github.base_ref }}` straight into a `run:` script. A `${{ }}` is expanded before any shell exists, so a branch name is not an argument there, it is source code. Both values travel through `env:` now, quoted - which the step four lines below had done since it was written.
- **17 mutable action tags** are pinned to full commit SHAs with the version in a comment. One of them was not even a tag: `actions/dependency-review-action@v5` resolved to a **branch** of that name. Immutable releases do not retire this - they lock the release tag, while the floating major is designed to move.
- **Dependabot** gains `cooldown: 7 days`, which delays version updates and not security updates.
- The crash fingerprint moves from sha1 to sha256 (a dedup key, not a signature - changed so the same false alarm stops arriving every quarter), and `tools/downloads.py` validates `--repo` before it becomes a URL path.

## 2. Three static analysers, wired as gates (5 commits)

- **ruff** with `F,B,S,ASYNC`. `F` and `B` block, `S` reports. That split is measured, not soft: `S` raises 306 findings here and 287 of them are in tests, doing on purpose what a packet-mangler's test suite does. **56 findings closed**, including two the tool earned its place with: `tests/fake_tk.py` defined `bind_class` twice, and a fixture had been feeding a nine-value row to a seventeen-column table since the columns were added.
- **mypy** over the package. Thirty findings, no `# type: ignore` needed - fifteen of them one block of attributes grown onto a class from outside its body, now a loop that also took ten lines off the largest module.
- **semgrep** with `p/default`, fetched anonymously (no account, no token). 🔴 **The gate is a script, because the flag lies:** `--severity` knows INFO/WARNING/ERROR only, while registry rules also carry HIGH and CRITICAL. Measured with a probe rule marked `severity: HIGH` - unfiltered 19 findings, with `--severity ERROR` **zero**. `tools/semgrep_gate.py` reads the JSON and blocks on ERROR/HIGH/CRITICAL, and on a scan error, because a rule that could not run is not a rule that found nothing.

Scanning the commit *before* this branch with that exact config reproduces the platform report finding for finding.

## 3. Supply chain and quality (10 commits)

**Provenance.** The release archive gains a build-provenance attestation beside the SBOM one. A signature says who signed a binary, provenance says which source and which build produced it: `gh attestation verify <zip> -R donislawdev/BeanNetworkTester`.

**Hashes.** `requirements.txt` and `requirements-build.txt` now pin artefact hashes, and the build file carries the freezer's whole seven-package closure rather than just the freezer. 🔴 Measured: corrupting **one** artefact hash does not fail an install - pip falls back to another artefact of the same version - which is why every published artefact is listed.

**Weekly audit.** `pip-audit` against the pinned set, on Windows, opening an issue on a finding. 🔴 Measured: auditing the requirement *files* covers **7 of 9** packages and still prints "No known vulnerabilities found"; auditing the installed environment covers 10. This deliberately reverses the "no automatic issues" decision for advisories only.

**Licence gate.** The official action cannot fail on a licence it could not resolve - its documentation says so. For a GPL-3.0 project shipping a binary that is the one answer nobody can act on, so `tools/dependency_gate.py` blocks on `null` exactly like a denied licence. `GPL-2.0-only` is deliberately outside the allowlist.

**Driver bytes.** The shipped WinDivert `.dll` and `.sys` are pinned by sha256, which catches a file swapped in `site-packages` after the install - something a version resource cannot notice.

**Scorecard.** OpenSSF Scorecard weekly, with the badge in both READMEs.

**Four new ratchets.** The mutation registry now *runs* in CI (per-PR on what the branch touched, weekly in full) instead of being quoted; a complexity ceiling of 29, measured; a CI job table in both READMEs with a guard comparing it to the workflow in both directions; a mypy strict-module list recorded twice so it can only grow; and diff coverage at 80% on changed lines.

## Verification

- Full suite **1195 passed**; ruff and mypy clean; GUI smoke and the real-Tk render check (EN + PL) OK.
- Mutation registry: **119 caught, 0 survived**, canary BROKEN as required.
- Every one of the 12 pinned action SHAs re-verified against the API. Every `run:` block parses under `bash -n`. All five workflows parse.
- The semgrep config, the hashed installs, the pip-audit modes and diff-cover were each run for real before being wired in.

## What still needs a human

Nothing here can block a merge until the checks are **required** in branch protection - that is a repository setting, not something a workflow can grant itself.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: hm21
body:
Closes #7864

## Description

A user reported the video player stopping mid-playback inside the video editor. The exported logs could not answer why, and that is the actual problem this PR fixes: the player logs `created` / `prepared 1 clip(s)` / `disposed` and nothing else. `play`, `pause` and every playback-state transition are invisible, so an 8-second editor session shows up as complete silence between `prepared` and the thumbnail extraction on save.

The absence was informative in one direction — the watchdogs that *do* log (`DivineVideoPlayer.Freeze` after an 8s buffering stall, `DivineVideoPlayer.Playback` on any `PlaybackException`) all stayed silent, which rules out a decoder error, a load timeout and a long stall. But it leaves no positive signal about what did happen.

Three gaps, closed:

**1. `playWhenReady` transitions, with media3's own reason** (`DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt`). This is the decisive one: media3 already knows *why* the flag flipped, and reporting it separates our own `pause()` (`user_request`) from the platform taking playback away (`audio_focus_loss`, `audio_becoming_noisy`, `remote`) and from the clip simply ending (`end_of_media_item`). Logged at info when it goes false, debug when it goes true — a stop is the interesting direction.

**2. A stall nobody asked for.** `isPlaying` going false while `playWhenReady` is still true means the player stopped on its own rather than being paused. The existing buffering watchdog only fires after 8s, so anything shorter left no trace whatsoever.

**3. The silent sibling pause.** `_pauseOtherLiveControllers()` enforces the app-wide "one video at a time" rule by pausing *every* other live controller on any `play()`, and it logged nothing on the success path — only on failure. A player stopped this way was indistinguishable in the logs from the user pressing pause, and it is a plausible mechanism here: the editor is pushed on top of a feed whose three players stay alive underneath. It now emits one line naming the initiator and every player it paused.

`debugLabel` is what makes those lines readable. Player IDs are wall-clock seeded (`665404`), identical on both sides of the channel, and otherwise untraceable back to a screen — so every one of the 11 creation sites now labels itself, and the feed labels per index (`feed[3]`).

The route naming is the same problem one layer up: all nine `PageRouteBuilder` pushes in the editor and metadata flows omitted `RouteSettings`, so `PageLoadObserver` recorded the entire cover-screen session as `unknown_route` and measured its duration against the wrong pop.

Sample of what a future export will show:

```
Player 665404 (editor_canvas): play() requested
Player 665404 (editor_canvas): exclusive playback pausing 1 sibling player(s): Player 665396 (feed[0])
Player 665396 (feed[0]) playWhenReady=false (user_request)
Player 665404 (editor_canvas) playWhenReady=false (audio_focus_loss)
```

**Related Issue:** 

## Out of Scope

- **iOS/macOS parity for the two native logs.** AVPlayer has no `playWhenReady`-with-reason; the equivalent would be KVO on `timeControlStatus` + `reasonForWaitingToPlay`, which the Swift side does not observe at all today. The reproduction is on Android, so this was not built speculatively. Everything else works on every platform: point 3 and the route names are pure Dart, and `debugLabel` is forwarded across the channel so Android and Apple both prefix their existing log lines with it.
- **A leaked native player.** In the report's logs, player `665396` is created in the home feed and never disposed — `vc_native=1` in every `MemoryTelemetry` sample for the following 2m45s confirms it outlives the screen. That is a real bug rather than a logging gap and belongs in its own PR.
- **No behaviour change.** The one non-log edit is an early `return` when `_pauseOtherLiveControllers()` finds no siblings, which skips a `Future.wait` over an empty list.

## Review Follow-up

A review pass over the first two commits found three things worth correcting, fixed in `bc2e15c`:

- The exclusive-playback rule named every sibling it paused on the success path but not on the failure path, which is the one worth reading. It now names both the initiator and the sibling that refused.
- The unrequested-stop line fired on two routine transitions — a seek drives the player through `STATE_BUFFERING` on its way to the new position, and a non-looping clip reaching its end lands in `STATE_ENDED`. Every scrub of the editor timeline therefore logged a "stall" at info. Both now log at debug, so the info line keeps meaning "stopped for no reason we asked for".
- `debugLabel` never crossed the channel, so native lines read `Player 665404` while Dart lines read `Player 665404 (editor_canvas)`. It now travels with `create`, and both native halves build the same prefix — applied to every existing native log line rather than only the new ones, since being traceable back to a screen is the whole point.

The two routes that share the name `video_metadata_cover` were deliberately left alone: `PageLoadObserver` pairs `startScreenLoad` / `endScreen` by name, so the same screen should resolve to one surface.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — no issues
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player`: 289 tests pass; coverage on the touched controller is 244/244 lines (package total unchanged at 99.50%, the four uncovered lines are pre-existing in `audio_track.dart` / `video_clip.dart`)
- `gradlew :divine_video_player:testDebugUnitTest` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (the Kotlin change compiles and the existing instance tests still pass)
- 124 tests across the 11 mirrored app test files for the touched screens and widgets
- Four new controller tests, all mutation-checked: deleting the `Log.info` reddens the sibling-naming test, deleting the empty-siblings early return reddens the solo-player test, dropping the sibling name from the failure warning reddens the third, and removing `debugLabel` from the `create` arguments reddens the fourth
- Confirmed `Log.debug` still reaches the bug-report buffer at the production log level (`warning`): `UnifiedLogger._log` captures to memory unconditionally, level filtering only gates console output


## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

author: thepig96
body:
Closes #355. Slice 4, ticket 8 of 28.

A pricing rule carries `pricing_method` — one of exactly two ratified values,
imported from the registry rather than typed anywhere — and the database refuses
a rule that carries a second component beside it. The method reaches the
published contract on both responses that carry the Pricing Receipt, marked, in
the string member of its nullable union.

### The ten acceptance criteria

| # | AC | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | two ratified values, **imported** | `PRICING_METHOD_CHOICES` derived from the registry frozenset |
| 2 | nullable; null means *not derived*, read beside the price status | the endpoint pair, and the receipt boundary that refuses a method disagreeing with its status |
| 3 | no floor, cap or additive component alongside the method — as behaviour | `ck_rate_never_composes`, INSERT plus three update doors |
| 4 | no third or fourth value anywhere | registry 2, column choices 2, published enum 2 |
| 5 | on the published contract, marker in the string member, placement named | `RecordUsageResponse` + `UsageEventDetailOut`, asserted by schema name |
| 6 | webhook section checked, result recorded either way | no payload carries a method; now a test, not a sentence |
| 7 | both method ledger entries reach 2 of 2 and are deleted | `g2-backend-pricing_method`, `g4-openapi-pricing_method` |
| 8 | value-set inventory re-taken from the census | `pricing/models.py` 3 → 4 |
| 9 | no rename, no retired term's file count moves | 40 terms in 127 sites, unchanged |
| 10 | checks, regens and suites | below |

### What review changed

Both `/code-review` axes found real defects and all are fixed in this commit.

- **The recording ack was already leaking the concept.** The first draft
  published the method on the audit lookup alone and argued the ack did not need
  it — falsified from the tree: the ack publishes the receipt too, so the method
  was already crossing there inside an `additionalProperties: true` record. The
  rule is now mechanical: the method goes wherever the receipt goes, which is
  exactly two responses, and the placement test pins that pair by name.
- **"Rules never compose" was one third true as written.** A rule may carry both
  money terms and `Rate.compute` adds them. That is the arithmetic shape's
  exclusivity rather than the method's, and refusing it here would change what an
  existing rate may be. All three parts are now named — one refused, one
  inexpressible on this table, one deliberately left legal.
- **The floor/cap guard was porous.** Keyed on `BigIntegerField`, while
  `Rate.book_version_from/_to` prove a whole-number column here need not be big —
  so `floor_micros = PositiveIntegerField()` would have sailed past the check
  whose docstring said it would be caught. Re-keyed on `IntegerField`, and proved
  by adding exactly that column and watching it go red.
- Also: an ADR-0007 §2 citation that was overreach in four places, a mechanism
  count that was short (as was the pre-existing one beside it), the write doors
  moved into the app's shared test helpers, the `pricing_method` /
  `pricing_model` near-name hazard, and one argument copied out seven times cut
  to a single statement plus pointers.

### Three pieces of existing prose were false and are corrected

No gate reads any of them.

1. `receipts.py` said "there is no price status column" — #351 landed it.
2. `test_undeclared_value_sets.py` claimed a sweep exclusion that does not exist;
   the module is swept like any other file.
3. The marker-placement test named the schemas for eight concepts out of eleven —
   `tenant_product` (#240) and the price pair (#351) had counts and no placement
   at all. All three are stated now, and the test's foot compares what it stated
   against the document so the omission cannot recur.

### Verified by mutation, five times

| Mutation | Result |

| `ck_rate_never_composes` removed | 4 tests RED, every one a refusal; the class's 3 admissions and both other classes GREEN |

## Problem

The Tags resource list gives dividers to sibling resources but not to source groups, so rows carry more visual weight than the Skills, Connectors, and Specialists hierarchy. Each row also repeats its resource type on a second line even though the group heading already provides that context.

## Proposed change

- Move the divider treatment from resource rows to resource-group boundaries.
- Add a subtle existing-token hover/focus surface to keep rows discoverable without persistent rules.
- Show each resource's existing description as secondary text; omit the line when the description is blank.
- Cover description rendering, blank-description behavior, and group/row divider structure in the Tags render tests.

## Scope and non-goals

- Renderer-only presentation change in the existing Tags settings panel.
- No changes to tag/resource data models, APIs, enums, persistence, or stored data.
- No new user-visible copy or locale catalog changes.
- No historical-data compatibility path is required; missing/blank existing descriptions simply render as a one-line row.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

- Tags resources show descriptions instead of repeated type labels.
- Blank descriptions do not reserve an empty secondary line.
- Dividers separate resource groups, not rows within a group.
- Existing row open/remove actions and group collapse behavior remain covered.

author: harvindertapper
body:
## Summary

This PR starts the billing/payment-states hardening slice for the offline-first Merchant OS.

## Changes

- Adds persisted `PaymentState` and nullable integer-paise `receivedAmount` fields to sales.
- Adds explicit Room v7-to-v8 migration with deterministic legacy backfill:
  - Cash and UPI legacy bills become `RECEIVED` with received amount equal to total.
  - Udhaar legacy bills become `NOT_REQUIRED` with zero received amount.
  - Deleted legacy sales remain unclassified (`PENDING`, null received amount).
- Enforces checkout settlement invariants:
  - Cash may record overpayment for change.
  - UPI must match the bill total exactly.
  - Udhaar cannot record a received settlement.
- Adds auditable repository payment-state reconciliation with actor authorization and no state regression.
- Adds received-amount capture to Cash/UPI payment UI and renders payment state, received amount, and change on receipts.
- Extends WhatsApp/clipboard receipts and CSV exports with payment lifecycle fields.
- Extends the explicit sale cloud allowlist with payment-state fields and safe legacy pull defaults.

## Tests

- Extends `CommerceValidationTest`.
- Extends `CheckoutInvariantsTest` for cash change, UPI mismatch rollback, and payment-state reconciliation.
- Adds `PaymentStateMigrationTest`.
- Updates existing migration tests for Room v8.
- Adds the new migration test to the required CI gate.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Local Gradle execution is blocked by the sandbox’s missing Android SDK; GitHub CI is authoritative.

## Safety / rollback

This is a versioned additive Room migration with no destructive fallback. Existing checkout, stock-underflow rejection, duplicate bill guard, udhaar credit limit, credential privacy, outbox identity, and atomic restore boundaries are preserved. Reverting the application commit is safe only together with the normal release rollback policy; the schema migration remains forward-only.

body:
## What changed or was removed
- Keep one session-scoped editable tool-feedback carrier across approval and question prompts.
- Pause animation during durable interaction suspension, then resume by editing the same Telegram message.
- Dismiss the carrier when the durable interaction reaches a terminal state, using its continuation session identity.
- Treat already-absent Telegram deletes as idempotent success and log exhausted cleanup with a hashed message identity.
- Add coordinator race, manager lifecycle, agent suspension, terminal cleanup, and Telegram regression coverage.

## Why
Approval prompts previously dismissed the active progress message and later turns created a replacement. Races between send, dismissal, and retry could also leave tool-feedback fragments in Telegram history.

## User and developer impact
Users see one stable progress message through approval cycles instead of repeated or orphaned fragments. Cleanup remains retry-owned until success or bounded exhaustion, with safe diagnostics when it cannot finish.

- make fmt

- go test ./pkg/channels ./pkg/channels/telegram ./pkg/agent -count=1
- go test -race ./pkg/channels -run TestToolFeedbackCoordinator_PauseRacingSendRetainsSingleCarrier\|TestToolFeedbackCarrierPausesAcrossApprovalAndResumesInPlace -count=1

author: longpsu-bot
body:
## Summary

This PR promotes the proven MST6 bounded-phase behavior into the production V3 runner and adds timetable-wide regularity authority instead of relying on locally uniform regimes.

### Stage 1 global regularity
- preserve no-service, critical-shortage, and planning-shortage priorities
- use passenger-proportional largest-remainder targets as a bounded +/-1 allocation envelope rather than a strict lexicographic optimum
- add cumulative Scenario-B shift envelopes at every analytical boundary so Stage 1 cannot propose a count path that one-to-one B-anchored trips cannot reach within the hard +/-30 minute shift domain
- cap and minimize per-direction service-rate change points before B-continuity and residual passenger-target error
- keep fixed total/directional trip counts, final-tail floor, protected floors, and the 16-regime hard cap unchanged
- provide Scenario B block counts only as CP-SAT hints, never as constraints

### Phase-aware regime construction (V3)
- source-trip slicing may move one trip across a 30-minute block boundary when the bounded-phase policy allows it
- per-block deviation <=1 trip, cumulative prefix deviation <=1, and zero full-direction drift remain authoritative
- regime-local construction no longer forces artificial zero phase at every regime boundary
- keep `maximum_headway_regimes_per_direction=16` as a hard cap only and continue adjacent representable merging toward a fixed point
- preserve the final service tail as a distinct anchored regime once it covers the intended tail window

### Necessary feasibility / Stage 2
- cheap necessary membership now checks Stage 2 departure domains, not one fixed Stage 1 planned witness
- if the permitted domains can still reach the bounded-phase prefix-count envelope, exact block membership is deferred to CP-SAT instead of being falsely pruned
- other necessary failures (B-shift, fleet, final-tail, regime boundary, protected constraints, etc.) are never cleared
- hard global transition authority: C transition jumps may not exceed Scenario B's observed maximum adjacent-headway change
- when final-tail demand is not rising, final-tail headway must be >= the preceding measurable regime headway
- independent validation mirrors the same production bounded-phase semantics

### Traceability / isolation
- production result JSON records `scenario_c_global_regularity_policy_v3`, phase-aware source slicing, and domain-aware necessary membership
- the production runner installs the global policy only for the duration of `main()` and restores baseline functions in `finally`
- policy and adapter fingerprints bind the installed authority stack

## Motivation from real MST 6 product review

The first feasible C candidate was internally uniform by regime but globally noisy: it used many regimes, had transition jumps worse than Scenario B, and shortened the final-tail headway even as observed late demand declined. V1 made those behaviors structurally invalid.

The first global-regularity MST6 rerun then exposed `B_SHIFT_BOUND_UNREPRESENTABLE` / `REGIME_COUNT_CAP_UNREPRESENTABLE` before Stage 2. V2 made Stage 1 count paths B-shift-aware. The next MST6 rerun reached zero regime-build rejections but both candidates were then pruned by cheap necessary feasibility before Stage 2. V3 aligns that pre-check with the same bounded-phase authority already used by Stage 2: departure-domain reachability is necessary; one fixed Stage 1 witness is not.

No solve-budget increase is part of this PR: the failing real runs consumed only ~44-46 seconds, reported `BudgetExhausted=False`, and never entered Stage 2. The blocker was semantics, not time.

## Validation

GitHub Python CI #255 passed on head `b3b7341a0616b615d5f095d213459f9e65464ada`:
- full pytest suite passed
- Ruff lint passed
- Ruff format gate passed

Focused regressions cover passenger-driven allocation, B-shift reachability, change-point control, phase-aware source slicing, domain-aware necessary membership, bounded-phase validation, transition authority, declining-tail non-densification, and reversible policy installation.

Real MST6 rerun remains local because the pilot workbook is private. The PR intentionally remains draft until that timetable is reviewed.

author: alinsran
body:
Backport of apache/apisix-ingress-controller#2693 (`b274316e`), with the minimum pinned to the value upstream carries today.

Log a warning at startup when the cluster's server version is below the minimum this controller supports. The minimum is injected at build time via ldflags (`MIN_K8S_VERSION ?= 1.31.0` in the Makefile), so it stays in sync with the docs instead of being hardcoded twice.

`checkK8sVersion` never fails startup — every step degrades to an `Info` log — so an unparsable version or a discovery error cannot block the manager.

**Also closes a gap left by #431.** apache#2693 introduced `MIN_K8S_VERSION` at `1.26.0`; apache#2804 (Gateway API 1.6.0) later raised it to `1.31.0` and updated three docs to match. #431 backported #2804 but could only take its `Makefile` hunk — the `MIN_K8S_VERSION` line and the docs sentence it edited did not exist here, because #2693 had never been backported. So this repo still advertises Kubernetes 1.26+ while shipping the Gateway API 1.6 CRDs, whose CEL validation needs 1.31. Brought in line with `apache/master`:

- `docs/en/latest/install.md` — 1.26+ → 1.31+, with upstream's current rationale
- `docs/en/latest/developer-guide.md` — test cluster 1.26+ → 1.31+
- `docs/en/latest/getting-started/get-apisix-ingress-controller.md` — 1.26+ → 1.31+

Backport notes:
- The upstream commit also dropped `github.com/panjf2000/ants/v2`, `k8s.io/code-generator` and `k8s.io/gengo/v2` from `go.mod`. That is unrelated dependency cleanup from upstream's tree, so `go.mod`/`go.sum` are left untouched here.
- `run.go` conflicted. The check is placed after `WaitForAPIServer`, which is where this repo already confirms the API server is reachable — discovery cannot fail spuriously there.

Verified: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/manager/...` clean; a build with `-ldflags "-X=.../internal/manager._minK8sVersion=1.31.0"` carries the injected value; the `Makefile` ldflags block and the `install.md` prerequisites block are now byte-identical to `apache/master`.

author: interlap01
body:
## Why

Feedback claimed a `.p12` can only be created on a Mac, making `builder signing setup` useless for the tool's main audience. That's a misconception — the only Keychain-specific step is generating the key pair and CSR, and builder can do that itself.

## What

- **`builder signing csr`** — new command that generates an RSA-2048 private key and a Keychain-style CSR (CN + IA5String `emailAddress`, verified against OpenSSL) for the Apple Developer portal. Writes `ios-signing.key` (0600) and `ios-signing.csr` to the current directory — no hidden state, the user decides where the files live — and prints a note not to commit the key plus the portal steps to follow.
- **`builder signing setup --certificate <file>.cer --key ios-signing.key`** — setup now accepts the certificate downloaded from the portal together with the private key as explicit inputs. It assembles `ios-signing.p12` protected by a password the user chooses, saves it to the working directory (it's the reusable signing identity — works with Sideloadly, a Mac, re-runs), and uploads the same three secrets as before. A mismatched certificate (key regenerated after uploading the CSR) is rejected with a clear error. Existing `.p12` files keep working unchanged.
- **README** — step-by-step no-Mac walkthrough: CSR → certificate on the portal → App ID / device UDID / provisioning profile → `signing setup`. Notes the paid-membership requirement, that the key/p12 must not be committed (gitignored files are also excluded from build snapshots), and points free-account users at MobAI re-signing.
- New `internal/signing` package with tests.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` green; new tests cover CSR structure/signature, `.p12` roundtrip, PEM certs, and key/cert mismatch.
- Generated CSR verified with `openssl req -verify`: `subject=CN=Jane Developer, emailAddress=jane@example.com` — identical shape to a Keychain CSR.
- Generated `.p12` imported into a temp keychain with the exact `security import` invocation the workflow uses.

author: spagles
body:
Eliminates redundant collections allocations, LINQ pipelines, and linear gene scans across atavism matching and weapon ability processing paths.

### Performance Optimizations:
* **Short-Circuit Xenotype Check in Atavism Matching**: Reordered `GeneticAtavismDef.Matches` conditions to validate `sourceXenotype` prior to scanning active genes. Avoids linear gene list iterations over `Pawn_GeneTracker` when evaluating non-matching xenotypes.
* **Single-Pass Gene Deduplication & LINQ Elimination**: Replaced multi-pass LINQ `Where(...).Distinct().ToList()` sequences in `AtavismUtils.Deduplicate` and helper methods with single-pass `HashSet` deduplication and index-based loops, cutting allocations and GC overhead during pawn gene generation.
* **Batched Ability Unequip & PostPostMake Optimization**: Optimized `CompAbilitiesWeapon.Notify_Unequipped` to prune weapon-granted abilities in a single pass rather than running multiple `RemoveAll` traversals, and replaced LINQ `Where` in weapon initialization with a direct loop.

author: xrequillart
body:
## Description

`/magic:pr` wrote manual test scenarios that implicitly assumed a local environment ("a service to run", "open a URL"). When the project publishes a per-PR preview deployment, the reviewer can test the code that is actually deployed for this PR instead of rebuilding it locally.

This adds a **post-creation backfill**: once the CI watcher concludes, the skill asks GitHub what was deployed for the PR's head commit and folds that URL into the testing section's prerequisites line. Nothing changes at PR-creation time, there is no new config key, and a project with no preview deployment produces exactly the PR body it produced before.

## Related Issue

Fixes #202

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] CI/CD changes
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Changes Made

- New `skills/magic-pr/references/preview-url.md`: the discovery procedure — host gate, deployment candidates via `repos/{slug}/deployments?ref=<head sha>` plus each deployment's statuses, a bot-comment fallback, a console-URL rejection filter, the fold-into-body step, a `## Usage` contract, a degradation table and a multi-repo section.
- `skills/magic-pr/SKILL.md`: new Step 7.4.2.5 running the backfill in the **main session** after every watcher conclusion; the `watchCI: false` path now states that the backfill does not run there; `watchCI` row and References index updated.
- `skills/magic-pr/references/ci-watch.md`: the watcher report gains `checks.deploy_checks`, derived from the check snapshot it already takes, so it costs no extra API call. The watcher stays a read-only observer and its contract is unchanged.
- `skills/magic-pr/references/messages.md`: `MSG_PREVIEW_URL_ADDED` and `MSG_PREVIEW_URL_MULTIPLE` (EN/FR).
- `repo.pr.watchCIHelp` extended in the four app catalogues (`desktop/src/i18n/{en,fr}.ts`, `webapp/lib/i18n/{en,fr}.ts`) and the two marketing ones, plus the `watchCI` row in `README.md`: the watch now also adds the preview URL, and without it the scenarios stay local-only.

Design notes worth reviewing:

- **Only per-PR previews are ever suggested.** A shared staging host, and the base branch's last deployment, hold code that is not this PR's — sending a reviewer there produces a confident test of the wrong thing, which is worse than testing locally. Keying on the head SHA is what makes the URL correct by construction.
- **The commit status `target_url` is explicitly forbidden.** On a real Vercel-backed PR it is `https://vercel.com/<org>/<project>/<id>` — the build-log console, not the deployed app. A filter also rejects `console.aws.amazon.com`, `app.netlify.com`, `dash.cloudflare.com` and `actions/runs/` links.
- **The user is asked when a commit has several previews** (a monorepo deploying several apps). The body is read *before* the question, so the idempotency check short-circuits runs 2-5 and nobody is asked twice per PR.

## Testing

- [ ] Tested locally with Claude Code
- [x] Ran linters (`npm run lint`)
- [ ] Tested installation script
- [ ] Tested affected slash commands

The two unchecked skill boxes are deliberate — see Additional Notes.

### Test Steps

Prerequisites: Node 20 (`.nvmrc`), `npm install`, and an authenticated `gh`. No env vars, seed data or services are needed, and this repo needs no test account.

1. **The discovery chain returns a real preview URL.** Against this repo's own PR #201:
   ```bash
   gh api "repos/Xrequillart/magic-slash/deployments?ref=7b220688a15e7d67e73852be344421596882a6bf" \
     --jq '[.[] | select(.production_environment == false)][0].id'
   gh api "repos/Xrequillart/magic-slash/deployments/5945125217/statuses" \
     --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "success" and (.environment_url // "") != "")][0].environment_url'
   ```
   Expected: deployment `5945125217`, then `https://magic-slash-85i05oyw3-xrequillarts-projects.vercel.app` — the deployed app, one candidate, so no question is asked.
2. **The console URL is rejected.** `gh api repos/Xrequillart/magic-slash/commits/7b220688a15e7d67e73852be344421596882a6bf/status --jq '.statuses[].target_url'` returns a `vercel.com/<org>/<project>/<id>` link; pipe it through the Phase 4 filter in `preview-url.md` and expect **no output** — that link must never reach a PR body.
3. **`deploy_checks` picks providers and not CI jobs.** Run the jq from `ci-watch.md` Phase 1 over `gh pr checks 201 --repo Xrequillart/magic-slash --json bucket,name,state,link,workflow,completedAt`: expect `["Vercel Preview Comments","Vercel"]` and none of Typecheck / Commitlint / Test / Lint / Validate. On a CI-only PR (e.g. #80) expect `[]`, which is what skips the bot-comment call.
4. **The settings text reads correctly.** Open the desktop app → a repository's configuration → Pull Request settings: the "Watch CI & Review" help now ends with the preview-URL sentence and the local-only caveat. Check the FR locale too, and the same row in the webapp repository form.
5. **No regression.** `npm run lint` → 0 errors (3 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings in `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Config/RepoPage.tsx`, an untouched file). `npm test` → 1184 passing, including the i18n key-parity suite that covers the strings above.

## Screenshots

Not applicable — no UI layout change. The only visual delta is the help text under the "Watch CI & Review" toggle, covered by test step 4.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code where necessary
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] I have added/updated tests if applicable
- [x] All linters pass locally
- [ ] I have updated CHANGELOG.md (if applicable)

Both unchecked boxes are intentional: no harness covers `skills/` (vitest runs over `desktop/src/**` and `webapp/lib/**` only), and `CHANGELOG.md` is generated from commit scopes at release time by `magic-release`.

## Additional Notes

**Why the two skill test boxes are unchecked.** The desktop app redistributes `skills/` at runtime, so a skill edit in this branch does not take effect in the installed `/magic:pr` until a release. The behaviour therefore could not be exercised end to end by running the command. What *was* verified directly is everything the procedure depends on: the two-call discovery chain and its real payloads, the console-URL rejection, the `deploy_checks` extraction, candidate dedup, and the shell snippets — each run in **both bash and zsh**, including empty and no-match cases, since an unmatched glob aborts a command in zsh.

**A bug found and fixed during review of the draft.** The candidate list was first shaped as `environment<TAB>url`. With `IFS=<TAB>`, a tab is IFS whitespace, so a *leading* tab is swallowed and the URL lands in the wrong variable — exactly the bot-comment case, which has no environment name. The fields are now `url<TAB>environment`: required first, optional second.

**Known limitations, stated on purpose rather than hidden.**

- The bot-comment fallback is verified against Vercel only. AWS Amplify — the provider named in the issue — publishes a commit status and may create no GitHub deployment, so it is covered by that fallback, written from documented behaviour but not measured against a live Amplify project. Worth testing first on a real Amplify repo.

author: cedricziel
body:
> **Stacked on #1351.** Base is `fix/1348-metrics-filter-union`.

Closes the coverage gap #1351 left open, and corrects a claim it made.

## What #1351 left out

Its operator coverage stopped at `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, `regex`, `exists`, and
justified skipping `between` by calling it "meaningless on a string attribute".
That was wrong. `between` lowers to `>= lo AND <= hi` — a lexicographic range,
a perfectly ordinary query — and, more to the point, it is **two comparisons
over one field expression**, a different plan shape from every single-comparison
leaf. `in` lowers to an in-list, a third shape.

Since the whole failure mode was about node arrangement around the union scan,
those are exactly the shapes that belonged inside the net, not outside it.

## The larger hole

Every case in #1351's test asserts the predicate matches **all three** fixture
rows. A predicate that plans correctly but gets dropped during the rewrite also
matches all three — so that test could not distinguish "the filter works" from
"the filter disappeared".

This adds a second test where each operator must exclude **every** row. The two
together pin both directions.

## Coverage after this

| operator | matches | excludes |
|---|---|---|
| `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, `regex` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `exists` | ✓ | — (no negative form as a leaf) |
| `in`, `between` | ✓ | ✓ |

`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` still have no leaf of their own, deliberately: `between`
exercises that exact lowering, and the test says so rather than leaving it to be
rediscovered.

## Tests

`cargo test -p querier --lib metrics_union` — 6 passed, 0 failed.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Bundles four improvements identified during the code review of the HLS detection/download pipeline and WebView fingerprint spoofing.

### 1. AES-128 HLS downloads
- `HlsPlaylistResolver` now parses `#EXT-X-KEY:METHOD=AES-128,URI=...,IV=0x...`, resolves the key URI, and attaches the correct key/IV to each segment.
- Supports both explicit IV and the implicit big-endian media-sequence IV (RFC 8216).
- New `HlsAesDecryptor` fetches the 16-byte key with the same Referer/Cookie/Origin headers, caches it, and decrypts AES/CBC/PKCS7 via the platform JCE — no native/crypto dependency.
- `SAMPLE-AES` / `SAMPLE-AES-CTR` are still explicitly rejected with a clear reason.
- Also handles `#EXT-X-BYTERANGE` (sends an HTTP `Range`) for both media and init segments.

### 2. MPEG-TS → MP4 remux
- New `HlsRemuxer` uses Android's built-in `MediaExtractor`/`MediaMuxer` (no FFmpeg, no APK size increase) for H.264 + AAC.
- Unsupported codecs (e.g. HEVC/AC-3 in TS) fall back gracefully to a concatenated `.ts` so the download is never lost.
- fMP4/CMAF playlists still concatenate directly to `.mp4`.

### 3. DASH playback actually works
- `PlayerActivity` now wires `DashMediaSource` for `StreamType.DASH`. The `media3-exoplayer-dash` dependency was already on the classpath but DASH was previously falling through to `ProgressiveMediaSource`, which cannot parse MPD manifests.

### 4. Fingerprint spoofing consistent with the active UA
- `hook.js` previously hard-coded `navigator.platform='Win32'`, 8 cores and fabricated desktop plugins even when the WebView sent an Android/Linux UA — a high-signal bot contradiction.
- It now derives platform, hardwareConcurrency, maxTouchPoints, vendor, languages and plugins from the actual User-Agent: mobile UAs keep mobile signals, only desktop Chrome gets fabricated plugins.

## Tests
- Expanded `HlsPlaylistResolverTest` to cover AES-128 with explicit IV, implicit sequence-based IV, init-map BYTERANGE normalization, KEY:NONE reset, and SAMPLE-AES rejection.
- Verified `hook.js` syntax with `node --check` and cross-checked the resolver parsing logic against a faithful port covering all new branches.
- Note: the full `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` could not be executed in this sandbox (no JDK 17 / Android SDK available); it should be run in CI / Android Studio before merge.

## Files
- `HlsPlaylistResolver.kt` — AES-128/IV/byterange parsing, `Segment`/`KeyInfo` models
- `HlsAesDecryptor.kt` (new) — key fetch + AES-CBC decrypt
- `HlsRemuxer.kt` (new) — TS→MP4 remux with .ts fallback
- `HlsDownloader.kt` — decrypted segment streaming + remux orchestration
- `PlayerActivity.kt` — DASH media source
- `hook.js` — UA-consistent fingerprint profile
- `HlsPlaylistResolverTest.kt` — expanded coverage

author: flexicon
body: ## Summary - `TestWebhooks.executeWebhook` released the expression isolate as soon as the response promise settled, but `deactivateWebhooks` (provider-side webhook teardown, e.g. GitHub `DELETE` hook, and registration deregistration) ran afterward and still needed it. - Under the vm expression engine, this raised an `IsolateError` inside the promise executor after `resolve()` had already fired, so it went unhandled and teardown silently never completed: the provider-side subscription leaked and the stale registration could interfere with the next test run. - Fix: release the isolate in a `finally` around the whole executor body, so it only happens once `deactivateWebhooks` (or the multi-main early-return) has actually completed, not when the returned promise settles. ## How to test - Added a unit test asserting `acquireIsolate` → `deactivateWebhooks` → `releaseIsolate` ordering on the successful-execution path in `test-webhooks.test.ts`. - Manual repro (vm engine default): register a webhook-trigger node whose provider `delete`/deactivation hook resolves an expression parameter, call the test webhook, then deactivate — before the fix, teardown throws `IsolateError` (swallowed) and the provider-side hook never fires; after the fix it completes normally. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-4124

## Summary

Fixes skill `!` command interpolation on Windows. Skill templates (e.g. `!`gh pr view ... 2>/dev/null || echo '{}'``) use bash-only syntax, but `executeBashCommands` ran commands through `child_process.exec`, which defaults to **cmd.exe** on Windows. Under cmd.exe:

- `/dev/null` fails with a localized "path not found" error — the skill command never executes
- The GBK-encoded Chinese error message gets mis-decoded as UTF-8 (mojibake), e.g. `ϵͳ�Ҳ���ָ����·����`

## Fix

`packages/agent-sdk/src/utils/markdownParser.ts` — `executeBashCommands` on win32 now resolves Git Bash via `resolveShellPath()` (same contract as the bash tool, /! bang command, background tasks, and hooks) and runs the command through `bash -c`; when Git Bash is unavailable it falls back to cmd with a `chcp 65001` prefix so cmd's own messages decode correctly.

## Verification

- Win32 regression test: `true 2>/dev/null || echo fallback` now exits 0 with empty output (previously cmd printed the localized path-not-found error)
- `markdownParser.test.ts` 34/34, plus skillManager/parser suites 102/102 pass; monorepo type-check green

body:
Replaces the three homepage blocks. Dan picked this set from three alternatives.

## What was wrong with the old copy

- **It led with a negative** — "Not a website that sells" opens by saying what you can't do.
- **The shop never spoke.** Written in the third person throughout, so nothing sounded like a 45-year-old family business.
- **No contractions**, which read stiff rather than quiet.

## New copy

**Ten thousand small things** — Pens, paint, paper, glue, card, ribbon — and the seasonal things Hong Kong needs when it needs them.

**Ask at the counter** — The shelves show a fraction of what's here. If you can't see it, ask — it's probably out the back.

**Call before you come** — We'll tell you in ten seconds whether it's in stock. [+852 2523 0338], [WhatsApp].

Chinese: 萬千小物 · 櫃檯問一聲 · 來之前先來電

## Two implementation notes

**The phone number and WhatsApp are real links**, not text inside the translated sentence. On a phone that makes the path from "is it in stock" to an answer a single tap, and it keeps a phone number out of a string that gets translated.

**Punctuation is locale-aware.** The separator and full stop after those links switch to full-width `，` and `。` in Chinese — an ASCII period dangling at the end of a Chinese sentence is simply wrong, and hardcoding `,` and `.` in the markup would have done exactly that.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a Python package implementing the AGEN-RS 5-block tariff system (effective 2024-01-01) for calculating and optimizing Slovenian electricity network fees.

## Package structure (`omreznicna_optimizacija/`)

- **`tarihe.py`** — Block definitions (1–5), per-block pricing (€/kW/month + €/kWh), and hour/day/season schedule lookup
- **`kalkulator.py`** — Aggregates hourly `(timestamp, energy_kWh, max_power_kW)` measurements into per-block monthly cost breakdowns
- **`optimizator.py`** — Two optimizations:
  - `optimizacija_moci` — recommends contracted power per block with configurable safety margin; computes savings against current contracted power
  - `predlog_premika_bremen` — ranks flexible-load shift opportunities (EV charging, heat pumps, etc.) by tariff price delta
- **`cli.py`** — `omreznica demo` (synthetic Jan 2024 data) or `omreznica csv <file> [--fleksibilno kWh]`

## Usage

```python
from omreznica.kalkulator import UrniVnos, izracunaj_mesec
from omreznica.optimizator import povzetek_optimizacije, predlog_premika_bremen

meseci = izracunaj_mesec(vnosi)
print(meseci[0].povzetek())
print(povzetek_optimizacije(meseci[0], dogovorjena_moc={1: 10.0, 2: 8.0, ...}))

for p in predlog_premika_bremen(vnosi, fleksibilna_energija_kwh=2.0, mesec=1)[:3]:
    print(f"{p.izvorna_ura}h → {p.ciljni_ura}h  block {p.blok_iz}→{p.blok_v}  saves {p.prihranek_eur:.4f}€")
```

CSV input format: `cas` (ISO 8601), `energija_kwh`, `max_moc_kw`.
