author: mvletter
body:
## Het gat dat dit dicht

Er waren twee losse mechanismen met een gat ertussen:

- **vertragen** — alleen bij een *herkende* 429
- **afbreken** — bij meer dan de helft mislukt

Een crawl waarin dertig procent faalt zonder herkenbare 429 viel daar precies tussendoor: vertraagde niet, brak niet af, en denderde op volle snelheid door terwijl een derde van de site niets teruggaf.

Dat is geen theoretisch geval. Vanochtend verpakte crawl4ai een 429 van intermedia.com in een ondoorzichtige 500 (`{"error":"Internal server error","correlation_id":"..."}`, geverifieerd tegen opgeslagen productiedata). We begrepen de reden dus niet en vertraagden niet. Het foutpercentage wisten we wél — honderd procent.

## Wat er nu gebeurt

Het vertragen wordt net zo reden-onafhankelijk als het afbreken al was. De stroomonderbreker telde het foutpercentage al; die geeft nu naast "doorgaan" en "afbreken" ook "vertragen" terug.

```
het gaat goed          → tempo mag omhoog
foutpercentage > 25%   → halveren, ongeacht de reden
blijft hoog na 3×      → afbreken
weigering              → meteen afbreken (langzamer lost een blokkade niet op)
```

Er komt géén tweede vertraagmechanisme naast het bestaande. Het nieuwe oordeel voedt de bestaande halveer-, afkoel- en opgeef-ladder in `crawl_site`, zodat er één plek blijft die het tempo verlaagt.

## Dubbele vertraging

Uitgesloten, en niet op hoop: één aanroep van de blokkenlus levert per definitie hooguit één stopsignaal op, dus er wordt hoogstens één keer per batch gehalveerd — of dat nu door een echte 429 kwam, door de verhouding, of door allebei tegelijk. Er is een test die beide signalen in hetzelfde blok zet en vastlegt dat het tempo van 2,0 naar 1,0 gaat en niet naar 0,5.

## Gedragsverandering om te weten

`test_majority_failure_ratio_stops_the_crawl` is hernoemd naar `test_fifty_percent_failure_ratio_triggers_slowdown_not_abort`. Vijftig procent mislukking leidt nu eerst tot vertragen in plaats van meteen afbreken — je gaat niet van volle snelheid naar stoppen zonder de tussenstap te proberen. De afbreekregels zelf zijn ongewijzigd en vangen nog steeds af wat na het vertragen niet herstelt.

## Bewijs

- 1484 tests geslaagd, 4 overgeslagen, 0 gefaald
- \`ruff check\` en \`ruff format --check\` schoon
- \`alembic heads\` toont precies één hoofd

author: zzragida
body:
## Summary

This stacked PR extends PR #11 reconciliation with durable generation leases and optimistic checkpoint concurrency so two workers cannot safely execute the same Text-to-Movie operation at the same time.

Base: `nu/add-generation-reconciliation-contract` (PR #11)

## Contract

- Add an atomic context compare-and-swap contract to SQLite and Postgres using the existing `context_messages` row; no schema migration is required.
- Session context, Text-to-Movie checkpoints, and generation leases share the same CAS boundary so a normal context save cannot erase a lease or checkpoint written by another worker.
- Text-to-Movie checkpoints carry a monotonic `revision`; a stale checkpoint object is rejected instead of overwriting newer scene/provider progress.
- Generation leases are stored under `__generation_operation_leases__` and contain an internal owner ID, random lease token, acquired/heartbeat/expiry timestamps.
- Only one unexpired lease may exist per operation. An expired lease can be taken over with a new token.
- Lease owner/token are internal and never exposed in client-facing summaries.
- Planning, each scene generation, background audio generation, and final combine use independent deterministic operation leases.
- After acquiring a lease, the worker re-reads the checkpoint revision before starting side effects. If another worker progressed the checkpoint while the lease was being acquired, execution stops with a concurrency conflict.
- Kling and Stability polling accept an optional heartbeat callback. A worker that loses/expirs its lease stops polling before subsequent persistence work.
- Video/audio paths that do not expose an in-call heartbeat are heartbeated immediately before and after the provider call; PR #11 reconciliation remains the safety boundary if a lease expires during a long call.
- Lease TTL defaults to 900 seconds and can be configured with `GENERATION_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS` (minimum 30 seconds).

## Concurrency behavior

- first planning worker acquires planning lease -> performs planning
- second planning worker -> `operation_locked`, LLM calls = 0
- first scene worker acquires scene operation lease -> may submit provider work
- second scene worker -> `operation_locked`, provider calls = 0
- lease heartbeat with wrong token / expired lease -> `operation_lease_lost`
- expired lease -> another worker may acquire a new token, then the latest checkpoint/reconciliation state is checked before side effects
- stale checkpoint revision -> `checkpoint_conflict`, no stale overwrite

## Persistence details

- SQLite CAS uses conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE context_data = expected` with first-writer `INSERT OR IGNORE` handling.
- Postgres CAS uses JSONB equality with `UPDATE ... WHERE context_data = expected::jsonb` and `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` for first-writer races.
- CAS merges retry on unrelated context changes instead of clobbering peer updates.
- `Session.save_context_messages()` preserves reserved `__...__` durable namespaces from the latest DB document.

## Regression scenarios

- two SQLite readers race to create first context -> only one CAS succeeds
- two readers race from same existing snapshot -> stale writer is rejected
- Postgres CAS query contract uses JSONB equality and conflict-safe insert
- active operation lease -> only first owner acquires
- expired lease -> takeover succeeds with a different token
- heartbeat extends current lease only
- forged/expired heartbeat -> lease lost
- CAS retry preserves unrelated peer context
- safe lease summary excludes owner/token
- checkpoint revision rejects stale overwrite
- Session normal context save preserves leases/checkpoints, including after a CAS retry
- planning lease blocks duplicate LLM planning
- scene lease blocks duplicate provider generation; after release one worker submits exactly once
- all PR #1-#11 backend contract suites remain in CI

## Scope / remaining limitation

This PR uses application wall-clock epoch values for lease expiry because the current DB abstraction does not expose database-server time. Significant worker clock skew could therefore affect expiry decisions. The 900-second default TTL, provider polling heartbeats, checkpoint revision checks, and PR #11 reconciliation reduce that risk, but a future fencing-token / DB-time lease could make the concurrency contract stronger across heavily distributed workers.

`BaseLayout.astro` hardcoded the title `Skyrule — Premium Camper Van Roof Conversions` and a matching meta description about UK elevating roofs — left over from the Webflow template this site was built from.

All seven pages using the layout inherited it, so search results and social shares for a Lagos travel agency advertised camper van conversions:

author: mboogerd
body:
Two gaps, both measured against the 2026-08-19 backlog. Rebased onto #330/#332/#334.

## 1. Filing should not claim

[#330](https://github.com/mboogerd/computenet/pull/330) repaired the friction lane's drain listing by widening it from `--status=open` to everything non-closed, because `file-friction.sh` pre-claims at filing and a claimed item is `in_progress`. That widening is right and **stays** — the assignee routing has to *see* a claimed item to skip it as theirs or steal it as stale.

But the pre-claim is the other half. Filing is not picking up: a claim belongs to the session that starts draining an item, not to the one that reported it. So:

- `--claim` dropped from `file-friction.sh`.
- The step-2 comment that justified the widening *by the pre-claim* now justifies it by the routing — which is what actually justifies it, and stays true now that filing is clean.
- `in_progress` under the SDLC epic now means a session is draining that item, which is what the routing already assumed.

## 2. Epic selection had no tiebreak, so half-built work never got finished

Step 3 picked "highest priority", full stop. A half-built feature — branch, worktree, green draft PR, merged tasks beneath it — is invisible to `bd ready`, which lists ready work rather than work already in flight. Nothing surfaces it, and its epic is one draw among every other epic at its level.

Measured: `98u.1` ([#313](https://github.com/mboogerd/computenet/pull/313), green, CLEAN) and `t6b.3.2` ([#306](https://github.com/mboogerd/computenet/pull/306), green, CLEAN) had sat 24h and 36h, each two of **twelve** P2 candidates, and both needed a hand-applied priority bump to be selected at all.

`resumable-epics.sh` resolves every `in_progress` feature to its epic through `epic-of.sh`'s walk — not the dotted prefix, since an explicit `parent` overrides it, and a feature whose epic will not resolve is skipped with a note rather than guessed. Step 3 sorts resumable-first, then priority. Finishing beats starting.

Verified against the live queue:

    true   P1  computenet-98u     BDS3
    true   P1  computenet-4ru     ORA1
    true   P2  computenet-t6b.3   KRD
    false  P1  computenet-t6b     KENA
    false  P2  computenet-6wc     BDS4
    ... ten more P2/P3

The jq carries an explicit paren: `sort_by(.resumable | not, .priority)` parses as `.resumable | (not, .priority)` and dies indexing the boolean.

## Verification

    bash .claude/skills/work/scripts/file-friction.test.sh     # 10 passed, 0 failed
    bash .claude/skills/work/scripts/resumable-epics.test.sh   #  4 passed, 0 failed
    ruby .claude/skills/remediate-friction/scripts/validate-skills.rb  # 4 checked, 0 failing

`file-friction.test.sh` case 1 now asserts the *absence* of `--claim`; the obsolete case 4 ("failed claim is a note") is replaced by one asserting the filed item is left open and unassigned.

Docs and scripts only — no Kotlin, no Gradle surface.

body:
This PR introduces the initial product requirements document for the workshop-sized Smart Parking Navigator MVP, grounded in the prepared Singapore datasets, setup guides, and existing Aspire scaffold. It captures the product scope needed for implementation planning while preserving the issue’s sequencing constraint that TRD follows PRD sign-off.

- **Scope definition**
  - Adds `PRD.md` as a standalone product spec for the MVP
  - Limits the product to Singapore destination search and nearby HDB car parks
  - Keeps deployment, databases, MCP, and agentic AI out of scope

- **User and journey framing**
  - Defines target users and the Singapore usage context
  - Documents core journeys for destination search, filtering, and stale/unavailable data handling

- **MVP requirements**
  - Covers destination search, nearby HDB car parks within 500 metres, live lot availability, basic filters, car-park details, and freshness/error states
  - Specifies supported lot types from the published data.gov.sg contract
  - Preserves frontend/backend credential boundaries in the product requirements

- **Acceptance criteria**
  - Adds measurable acceptance criteria for ranking, filtering, detail views, and freshness states
  - Makes freshness explicit with a documented threshold for fresh vs stale rendering
  - Defers TRD work until PRD review/sign-off

```md
#### UX States

- Loading
- Empty results
- Fresh data (source update time within 2 minutes of current SGT)
- Stale data (source update time older than 2 minutes, but last known data is still available)
- Live availability unavailable with last known data shown
- Error retrieving data
```

author: oct7love
body:
## Problem

P1-4: the Stop button only flipped UI state. `ai-stream-cancel` set a `cancelled` flag and destroyed the token buffer. The provider fetch/SDK stream kept running, so tokens/tools/retries still consumed quota.

## Root cause

No `AbortController` was stored per `requestId`. Preload `cleanup()` only removed IPC listeners and never sent cancel with that id.

## Change

- `ai-stream-sessions`: `requestId → AbortController`. Cancel is idempotent.
- Preload stream cleanup removes listeners, then sends `ai-stream-cancel`.
- `LLMClient.chatStream` forwards `signal`. AbortError is `cancelled` (no retry, no fallback, no circuit-breaker trip).
- OpenAI / DeepSeek / Gemini: SDK `create(..., { signal })`.
- Claude http request: `req.destroy` on abort. Codesuc: `request.abort()`. GLM: `stream.abort()`.
- `validateSender` on stream start/cancel.
- Window `before-quit` / `window-all-closed` abort all sessions.
- Conversation switch already called cleanup; new send also stops the previous stream.

Independent of M5 / CSP / docs / autoSave PRs.

## Security boundary

- Keys stay in the main process.
- Cancel does not log request bodies, keys, or Authorization.
- Unauthorized senders cannot cancel.

## Tests

**Local:**

- `npm test`: 284 passed
  - sessions: abort sets `signal.aborted`, double-cancel is safe
  - mock provider: abort listener fires, no fallback/retry
- `tsc` + `npm run build`: 0

**GitHub CI:** pending on this PR.

Did not packet-capture a live vendor stream.

## Out of scope

- Non-stream `ai-chat` abort
- Completion-stream cancel (same channel can be added later)
- Merging other PRs

## Rollback

Revert this commit. Stop returns to UI-only cancel.

author: aaylward
body:
Closes #1403. Closes #1406.

`game_features.white_title` / `black_title` were filled by fetching a chess.com profile per distinct opponent in a month. Almost nobody holds a title, so nearly every one of those round trips existed to learn that somebody is untitled — and it was the dominant I/O cost inside a run.

chess.com publishes a roster per title. Measured against the live API while writing this:

| | |
|---|---|
| requests for the entire titled population | 10 |
| players | 16,830 |
| bytes | ~230 KB |

So the whole set fits in memory for the life of the process, and per-opponent traffic goes to zero.

## The column stays

Not a candidate for deletion: `opponent.title = "GM"` is a headline example in `CHESSQL.md`, and `opponent.title` is one of the two dimensions the docs call the only correct opponent breakdown. Both workers keep writing the same values — Java per opponent, this one from the rosters — so it lands C++-only with no divergence in the data.

## Decisions the roster owns

- **Stale rosters keep answering, and say so.** A title this worker has not heard about yet is a smaller wrong than every player in the month losing the one it had. But the month that used a stale roster is not complete, because complete months are never refetched — a week-long chess.com outage would otherwise write a week of months nobody will ever correct.
- **A failed refresh backs off**, timed from when the attempt *ended*: ten calls against a chess.com that is timing out take longer than the backoff, and a backoff the attempt outlasts is no backoff at all.
- **A partial set is never kept.** Titling some players and not others reads as a title being taken away.
- **Ten empty rosters are not an answer.** Nobody on the whole site holding any title is not a state chess.com can be in; taking it would untitle everyone while reporting nothing wrong.
- **A title with no roster is a title nobody holds.** The modeled 404 stays distinct from a failure to read, so one retired abbreviation cannot stop the refresh at that title forever.
- **One player, two rosters.** Ten documents read at ten instants, so a title awarded in between lands in both. Strongest wins — ordered by the rating floor the title is awarded at, not chess.com's listing order, which pairs each women's title with its open counterpart and would answer `WGM` where the profile the Java worker reads says `IM`.
- **Case is normalised on both sides.** The rosters came back lowercase the day this was written and archives name players however they typed them, but neither is a promise.
- **A refresh checks for shutdown between titles.** Ten sequential calls noticed only at the tenth is a process the supervisor kills instead, and a killed process strands its claim until the lease expires.

## The degraded month stays, and means something narrower

The draft body said this concept would go away with the per-opponent lookups. It does not, and should not.

`indexed_periods.is_complete = false` and `index_months{result="degraded"}` used to mean *one opponent whose profile would not load*. They now mean *no roster at all, or one past its day* — which leaves every player in the month looking untitled, or titled from week-old data. That is a wider wrong than the old one, not a smaller one, and it is exactly the case worth refetching later.

## The assembly moves somewhere a test can reach it

A binary has no test target, so every wiring choice in `worker_main` was one nothing would notice changing. Building the roster inside the run lambda — ten requests to chess.com per claim instead of ten for the life of the process — failed no test. Nor did unsetting the roster, the observer or the shutdown switch, and unsetting the roster is the worst of the three: the run writes NULL titles on every row *and* marks the month complete, so the period cache carries the gap for both workers with nothing to say it happened.

`MakeRun` and `PollLoop` are that assembly, in a library with a test over it. `main` keeps the parts that need a real process: the environment, the signal handlers, the connections and the client. The seam also makes the roster mistake harder to write than to avoid — `MakeRun` takes a `TitleRoster` and has no `TitleSource` to build one from.

The loop was untested too, and three of its branches matter: a queue it cannot reach is waited out rather than exited, because the supervisor would only restart us into the same outage; an empty queue is waited on rather than spun; a claim that did work is followed straight by the next one.

## Shape

- `FetchTitled` in the smithy model and the generated client, uppercasing the title because the path spells them that way, and refusing an empty one — the generated client does not check path labels, and `/pub/titled/` 404s, which would otherwise read as "nobody holds it"
- `TitleRoster` holds the ten rosters behind a 24h TTL and a 5m failure backoff, with an injected `now` so the tests do not sleep
- `ArchiveSource::FetchTitle` is gone; `ChessComArchive` also implements `TitleSource`
- `IndexRun::Options::titles` is a `TitleRoster*`; null means no titles at all rather than a degradation, which is what the tests that do not care about titles want
- `worker.{h,cc}` holds `MakeRun` and `PollLoop`; `worker_test` covers both, and is in the sanitized set

## Review panel

Three read-only agents, three lenses. Findings acted on in `ce1c730`, `73e3d00` and `4d3d273`:

- **Five tests were deleted by the title commit that had nothing to do with titles** — three run-ceiling, two mid-month shutdown. Confirmed by mutation: deleting `index_run.cc`'s whole `stopping()` branch passed every test in the repo. All five restored, and the mutation dies now.
- **The modeled `TitleNotFound` was flattened into `Unavailable`**, so one un-fetchable title would disable titles permanently, in every process — and with no month ever written complete, no month would be a cache hit for either worker. chess.com's own validator names a title whose roster 404s today.
- **Ten empty rosters were accepted and installed**, and the backoff was timed from the start of the attempt.
- **`kTitles` was not ordered the way its comment claimed.**
- **Stale answers marked months complete.**
- **Six mutations survived the roster's own suite**: the 24h TTL was never pinned (only `t=0`, where the backoff gate covers for it, and `t=25h`, past both — so deleting the TTL left the rosters re-read every five minutes and everything still passed), a refresh replacing its map was never pinned, and all three comparisons were only tested well past their edges. All six killed.
- **Nothing covered `worker_main`.** Fixed here rather than filed — see above.

author: anantsqip
body:
The pipeline was a board that showed what somebody typed and nothing else. A deal that had sat at Proposal untouched for four months looked exactly as healthy as one that moved yesterday — same column, same colour, same size.

A pipeline's real failure mode is not *losing* deals; losing is half the job. It is **forgetting** them, and nothing in it noticed.

## What it now computes

**Four flags**, all derived from data already recorded rather than typed:

| Flag | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `STALE` | No activity for 14 days (urgent at 30) |
| `NEXT_ACTION_DUE` | The next step is due or overdue |
| `NO_NEXT_ACTION` | Nobody has said what happens next |
| `CLOSE_DATE_PASSED` | Past its own close date, still open |

Each names **one** thing. It would have been easy to reduce this to *"deal health: 72%"*, and it would be worse — a number invites comparison it cannot support and hides which of four problems a deal actually has.

**Time in stage** comes from the stage-change trail already being logged, so it works on every deal in the system today with no new data. Median rather than average: one deal that dragged for two years would otherwise make every stage look worse than it is.

> A firm losing deals at Proposal has a pricing problem; one losing them at Contacted has a qualification problem. Same board, different fix — and no individual card can tell you which.

## The join no external CRM can make

`deliveryOutlook` crosses each deal's expected close date against **the capacity board**. HubSpot knows the deal; it does not know that the people who would do the work are already committed that fortnight. Leave, holidays and committed task hours are taken out by capacity itself, not re-guessed here.

Advisory, never blocking — you do not decline work because a number looks tight, but the conversation belongs *before* the commitment rather than after.

**Testing caught a real flaw in it.** A close date in the *past* put the measured window entirely behind today, returning zero free hours and reporting "no capacity" — when the truth was a stale date and an idle team. The window is clamped to today now: work that lands late lands now.

## Also

- **Kind of work on a deal**, drawn from the same list projects are created from so the two cannot drift. This is what makes *"we win FTO and lose Invalidity"* answerable — and it is unanswerable after the fact unless captured while the deal is open.
- **Repeat-client marking** — a deal from a company we have already delivered for is flagged, matched by name even before anyone links it.
- **Win rates read "—"** until something of that type has closed. Zero would say *"we never win these"*, which is a different and much worse claim than *"we do not know yet"*.

## Testing

11 checks against a running API: each flag fires on the right deal and stays quiet on a healthy one, stage durations compute, the type breakdown returns, the delivery outlook responds, and a plain Employee still gets 403. Web production build passes.

## Deploying

author: honeybeesquad
body:
Resolves the four live-tier regions that have flagged zero-peak on every health run since the Japan allowlist (#784). Each one was verified against its upstream before touching the allowlist. Written from `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: this PR changes the health-check allowlist, adds a schema-break guard + tests to the Turkey loader, adds a WATCH comment in `entsoe.json.ts`, and updates four validation docs. No tiers change; `ci:tally-golden` passes untouched.

## Per-region evidence

| Region | Tier | Verdict | Evidence (all probes 2026-08-19) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hungary-wind` | T1a-live-tso | TRUE ZERO, structural — allowlisted | ENTSO-E A75 B19 `10YHU-MAVIR----U` live: 716/716 nonzero points 2026-08-12→19, max 225 MW. × 1% rate ⇒ ≤ 2.3 MW on the windiest hour; 30d profile peaks ~0.6 MW and flickers around the 1 MW floor (deployed record read 1.098 MW at fetch time). Fleet frozen ~330 MW by the 2016 permitting ban — does not grow out. |
| `italy-cnord-wind` | T1b-live-domestic-anchored | TRUE ZERO, structural — allowlisted | A75 B19 CNOR `10Y1001A1001A70O` live: 495/496 nonzero points, max 55 MW. × 0.4% Terna zone share ⇒ 0.22 MW peak. Clearing 1 MW needs 250 MW of CNOR wind — ~5× anything observed. Same class as already-allowlisted `italy-north-zone-wind` (0.3%). |
| `north-macedonia-wind` | T1a-live-tso | TRUE ZERO, structural — allowlisted, with a WATCH | MK wind = the single 36.8 MW Bogdanci farm; × 3% ⇒ ≤ 1.1 MW even at rated (July probe: 711 points, max 35.9 MW). Separately: MEPSO's voluntary A75 reporting **ceased 2026-08-04T22:00Z** (Acknowledgement "No matching data" for 2026-08-12→19) — the Energy Community non-reporting pattern that ended MK/RS B16 in May. The record still reads "live" because the 30d window holds pre-Aug-4 points; once it empties (~2026-09-04) the zone degrades to cached and the freshness channel catches it. WATCH comment added at the zone spec; if B19 never resumes, revert to an estimated anchor like `serbia-solar` (tier change — deliberately not done here, 15 days in). |
| `turkey-solar` | T1a-live-tso | TRUE ZERO, diurnal windowing — allowlisted + loader guard | EPIAS public dashboard endpoint carries the **current day only** (probed: 13 hourly items, `sun` = 3.4 GW at Turkish noon; the date-ranged endpoint returns HTTP 406 "TGT gerekmektedir" — needs registered credentials the repo doesn't hold). Any refresh before Turkish sunrise emits an all-zero solar profile: a true overnight reading, recurring nightly, not a break. Masking risk closed: `numberOrZero` maps a renamed `sun` field to 0, so a schema change would have emitted an all-zero "live" record forever under the allowlist — the new midday silent-zero guard throws instead, degrading to cached (freshness channel). 4 new tests. |

## Tier-honesty note (report, not change)

`north-macedonia-wind`'s T1a label is honest as a data path — it is a real ENTSO-E TSO feed and reported continuously through July — but the feed is voluntary and currently dead (15 days). If it stays dead past ~2026-09-04, the honest move is the `serbia-solar` treatment (revert to estimated in `statics.json.ts` + golden + STATUS). Flagged for a follow-up rather than done here.

## Expected effect on the health check

Simulated the workflow's exact logic against the live deployment with the new allowlist: zero-peak count drops from 5–7 (every run since 2026-08-01) to **1** right now (`alberta-solar`, a borderline ~1 MW flicker outside this PR's scope) — well under the ≥5 issue threshold. The freshness channel is untouched and remains the detector for real feed breaks, including a permanent MEPSO cessation and any EPIAS schema change.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — 192 files, 1063 tests passed (includes 4 new turkey guard tests)
- `npm run ci:gates` — all nine gates pass; tally-golden and docs-drift unchanged
- Live loader run: `tsx src/data/turkey.json.ts` ⇒ wind peak 0.0127 GW, solar peak 0.0284 GW, status live (guard does not fire on healthy data)
- Workflow YAML parses; embedded Python block compiles

## Follow-ups (not in this diff)

- EPIAS registration would unlock the TGT ranged endpoint and give `turkey`/`turkey-wind`/`turkey-solar` a real 30-day window (current `totalTWh` is computed over a partial current day and understates).
- Revisit `north-macedonia-wind` ~2026-09-04: resume, or revert to estimated.
- `alberta-solar` flickers at the 1 MW floor and will occasionally count toward the threshold; unverified, left alone.

author: rhys-smithy
body:
Fixes two Command Centre bugs found during a real production scan.

1. Elapsed timer looked frozen: the frontend re-anchored the ticking clock to the backend's elapsed_seconds on every ~1s poll, which only advances at real pipeline boundaries (can be tens of seconds to minutes apart) -- so each poll snapped the visible clock back to a stale value. Now anchored on started_at (fixed for the scan's duration) instead.
2. Results appeared then reverted ~8s after scan completion: dashboard_server.py sent no Cache-Control header, so a browser could serve a cached copy of deal_queue.html on a later fetch (second tab, back/forward nav, backgrounded-tab reload). Now every response sends Cache-Control: no-store.

Scope: telemetry/UI only, no discovery/valuation/scoring/scraper/performance logic touched.

Tests: 424 passed, 4 subtests (was 422+4; added one regression test per bug). Real browser QA performed (Playwright headless Chromium against the actual dashboard_server.py/scan_progress.py/deal_queue_report.py code) -- see commit fix/scan-timer-and-dashboard-cache for details.

author: openjiuwen-sync-bot[bot]
body:
Paired: [GitHub #3467](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/3467) ↔ [GitCode !5120](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/5120)

## 一、问题描述

用户在 08/12 17:06 使用 code 工具生成 .docx 产物文件后，jiuwenclaw sidecar 完全无响应。
17:27 用户再次发送消息【修改完善个word文档的格式排版和易懂要这么久吗】，前端报错【系统异常，请稍后重试 智能体响应超时】。

从 17:06:43 到 17:29:32，长达 23 分钟 sidecar 完全冻结，所有请求超时。

---

## 二、根因

### 2.1 冻结现场

| 本地时间     | 层         | 关键事件                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 17:06:43.117 | jiuwenclaw | `[ArtifactEmitter] 产物检测` — agent_server.log 有此条，**full.log 没有** |
| 17:07~17:29  | jiuwenclaw | **无任何日志输出**（事件循环冻结铁证）                       |
| 17:27:32     | API        | `relayclaw agent catalog sync sent` → jiuwenclaw 无响应      |
| 17:29:32     | API        | `sync_agents_configs acknowledgement timed out`（~120s）     |
| 17:29:33     | 前端       | 【智能体响应超时】                                           |

### 2.2 根因：日志 I/O 阻塞事件循环

**冻结点**：`artifact_emitter.py` 的 `emit_artifact_generated()` 函数中，`logger.info("产物检测 ...")` 这条日志。

旧版本 root logger 挂了 5 个 `RotatingFileHandler`，Python logging 是**同步串行**的 — `logger.info()` 遍历所有 handler，逐个调用 `handler.emit()`。如果某个 handler 的 `emit()` 阻塞，后面所有 handler 和 `logger.info()` 调用本身都被阻塞。

执行顺序：agent_server.log handler（写成功）→ full.log handler（**阻塞**）→ 事件循环冻结。

**full.log handler 阻塞的原因**（两个因素叠加）：

1. **`_sanitize_log_text()` 正则脱敏** — 这条日志很长（包含 artifacts 列表完整 repr），`_sanitize_log_text()` 对整条文本跑 4 组正则 + 7 条子正则 = **10 次 `.sub()`**，在事件循环线程中同步执行。

2. **RotatingFileHandler 文件 I/O** — 如果日志文件达到大小限制要 rotating（rename + 新建），文件操作在事件循环线程中同步阻塞。Windows 文件系统在 rename 时如果有其他进程持有句柄，阻塞更久。

### 2.3 为什么卡死后永久冻结

`logger.info()` 阻塞了事件循环线程 → `emit_artifact_generated()` 协程卡在 `logger.info()` 永远不返回 → 事件循环线程被占住 → 所有其他协程（WebSocket 消息处理、心跳、后续请求）无法调度 → 进程活着但什么也做不了（"活着的僵尸"）→ 后续所有请求超时。

### 2.4 边界

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "RelayClaw API 层 — 正常"
        A1[17:27:26 Created invocation]
        A2[17:27:30 session_init]
        A3[17:27:32 sync sent]
        A4[17:29:32 sync timed out]
        A5[17:29:33 error dispatched]
    end
    subgraph "jiuwenclaw sidecar — 冻结"
        J1[17:06:43 logger.info 产物检测]
        J2[full.log handler I/O 阻塞]
        J3[事件循环冻结]
        J4[17:07~17:29 无任何日志]
    end
    A3 -.->|sync 消息发出| J3
    J3 -.->|无法接收处理| A4
    J1 --> J2 --> J3 --> J4
    A4 --> A5
```

**结论：边界在 jiuwenclaw sidecar，这是 jiuwenclaw 问题。** 证据强度：confirmed。

---

## 三、排除项

| 排除项            | 依据                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 上层 API 问题     | API 链路完整：Created invocation → session binding → sync sent → 等待 → 超时报错 → error dispatched |
| MaaS/session 问题 | 无 `Huawei MaaS session not found`，session recovery 正常    |
| sidecar 退出/重启 | 进程 pid 1584 `hasExited=false`，desktop-launcher 无重启事件 |
| LLM 失败          | 无 `LLM invoke 失败`，冻结在工具执行后的产物检测阶段         |
| 普通超时终止      | 从 17:13 到 17:27 三次 sync 全部超时，说明不是偶发网络问题   |
| 前端问题          | 前端正确展示超时错误文案                                     |

---

## 四、修复方案

### 4.1 已落地修复

#### 修复 1：日志 I/O 异步化（d6393b4 已落地）

**文件**: `jiuwenclaw/utils.py`

**改动**: 把所有 `RotatingFileHandler` 替换为 `QueueHandler`，用 `QueueListener` 独立线程做文件写入和脱敏。

```python
# 事件循环线程：只做"往队列放 record"（O(1) 非阻塞）
_qh = QueueHandler(_log_queue)
root.addHandler(_qh)

# 独立线程：取 record → 脱敏 → 写文件（可能慢但不影响事件循环）
_log_listener = QueueListener(_log_queue, *_listener_targets)
_log_listener.start()
```

**效果**: `logger.info()` 不再被文件 I/O 或 `_sanitize_log_text` 阻塞，事件循环永不因日志卡死。

#### 修复 2：`normalize_python_script_file` 改用 `asyncio.to_thread`（本次提交）

**文件**: `jiuwenclaw/agentserver/code_source_unicode.py`

**改动**:

```python
# 旧代码（同步 I/O 阻塞事件循环）:
count = normalize_python_script_file(path)

# 新代码（移到线程池，不阻塞事件循环）:
count = await asyncio.to_thread(normalize_python_script_file, path)
```

**背景**: `normalize_python_script_file(path)` 内部做 `read_text` + `tokenize` + `write_text` 全是同步文件 I/O。虽然 08/12 事故的 .docx 场景因后缀检查跳过了此函数，但 `.py` 产物文件会执行完整 I/O 链路，同样会阻塞事件循环。这是与日志 I/O 同类的阻塞源，d6393b4 不会覆盖。

**效果**: `.py` 产物文件的同步 I/O 移到线程池执行，事件循环在等待期间正常调度其他协程。

### 4.2 修复覆盖矩阵

| 阻塞源               | d6393b4 (QueueHandler) | asyncio.to_thread | 本次提交 |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------- |
| 日志文件 I/O         | **直接修复**           | —                 | —        |
| 正则脱敏阻塞事件循环 | 移到独立线程           | —                 | —        |
| .py 产物同步 I/O     | —                      | **直接修复**      | 本次     |
| .docx 产物场景       | **直接修复**           | 不影响（跳过）    | —        |

### 4.3 防御层（建议后续落地）

事件循环健康看门狗 — 心跳检测任务每 5 秒推进时间戳，连续 30 秒无推进则判定冻结，自动重启 sidecar 进程，作为最后兜底。

author: johnonlee
body:
## Why

The source subsystem was ruled dropped on 2026-08-04. The ruling existed only on paper: eleven modules, a CLI command tree, four MCP tools and a dashboard tab all still shipped, and `monet source list` printed its header row and exited 0 — a dead surface answering like a working feature with an empty registry, which costs a reader a wrong inference every time. #16 originally scoped itself to *gating* that surface, deliberately leaving removal to a ruling that was not scoped to "now". That ruling was given on 2026-08-19, so this PR removes the subsystem instead of hiding it.

**Removal here means the code, not the data.** Rows a store already holds are left exactly where they are; the one thing that deletes them is a new `monet retire-source`, which takes a verified backup first and runs only when an operator asks. Nothing is destroyed by upgrading.

An earlier revision of this PR tried to make the removal safe for undisposed stores automatically — an open-time refusal, a durable marker, a dashboard guard, a migration that purged on first open. That machinery was removed after review: it existed only because a store still holding connector rows would surface them as ordinary memories, and the ruling is that this consequence is acceptable. With no root, the whole chain came out. What remains deletes far more than it adds.

## What upgrading actually does

Content that came in through the connector stops being *files* and becomes ordinary memories. Measured on a seeded store: after upgrade the rows are still present, `search` returns them alongside agent memories, and `conceptCount` / `listMemories` / `memory_fetch` all include them. For a store that ingested a vault this is a visible change — #16 recorded such content as 397 MB, 56% of that store — so most retrieval results can be document chunks until `retire-source` runs. Sync is gone, so that content is frozen at the upgrade point. The original files are untouched; they live outside the store.

## Change stratification

| | Lines | Reading contract |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Load-bearing** — `source-retirement.ts` (new, 286), `retire-source` in `repair-cli.ts`, rung 13 in `engine.ts` | ~0.5k | **Read.** Everything that can delete a row, and the one bump that records the rung. |
| **(b) Wiring** — `mcp-server.ts`, `index.ts`, `cli.ts`, `dashboard/` | ~0.9k | **Skim.** Surface deregistration; each hunk removes a call site of something deleted in (a). |
| **(c) Fallout** — 30 deleted test files, adaptations in ~12 more | ~29k | **Trust.** Most tested the deleted subsystem itself. Removed coverage is listed below. |

## Reading order

1. `packages/core/src/source-retirement.ts` — the disposal contract in one file: what counts as the connector population, what a retired table is, the purge, the residue drop.
2. `packages/cli/src/repair-cli.ts` — the `retire-source` command: backup, purge, drop, reproject, in that order.
3. `packages/core/src/engine.ts` — rung 13 (a bare version bump), then the read paths with their connector predicates removed.
4. `packages/core/src/mcp-server.ts` — four tool registrations and the source-scheduler lifecycle removed.
5. `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`, `packages/cli/src/dashboard/*` — command tree, `/api/sources`, Sources tab.
6. `packages/core/src/{retrieval,embedding-state,diagnostics,lifecycle-edges,sync-types}.ts` — remaining predicate and type removals.

## Behavior deltas

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `monet source list` | Prints a header row, exits 0 | Command does not exist |
| Agent lists MCP tools | 23, incl. `source_list` / `source_status` / `source_path` / `source_sync` | 19 |
| `memory_fetch(id, includeBody: true)` | Source concepts return `outline` / `sourcePath` / `sourceId` | No `includeBody`; none of those fields |
| Dashboard | Sources tab (shortcut 5) | No tab; shortcuts 1–5 re-map |
| `MONET_CALLER_ID` + `MONET_PROJECT_ID` | Derive the source authorization identity | Not read |
| Opening a store that holds connector rows | Served, rows hidden by predicates | Served, rows visible as ordinary memories |
| Creating a new store | 16 source tables + 2 marker columns | Neither |
| `user_version` after this build opens a store | 12 | 13 — unconditionally, on every store |
| `monet retire-source` | — | Verified backup, then purge, drop, reproject |
| `memory_store({kind: "source"})` | Refused | Refused (unchanged — nothing may mint a connector row) |

`sourceRefs` on `memory_store` is an unrelated feature that shares the word; all 25 uses stay.

Rung 13 carries no migration. What changed at it is what this build *creates*; it bumps unconditionally because a rung only some stores climb would leave rung 14 with two possible predecessors to gate on.

## Test evidence

Core 1780 passed / 10 skipped, CLI 335 passed, both typecheck clean, both build.

New:

- `source-retirement-rung.test.ts` (3) — a fresh store reaches 13 and grows none of the retired schema; an **unretired** store climbs it too while keeping every row and table it had; reopening is inert.
- `retire-source-cli.test.ts` (7) — run against a real store, not a fake port, because the property is an ordering fact: the verified backup exists and still holds the rows the store no longer does. Also covers the dry report, `--apply` without `--yes`, nothing-to-retire, a schema newer than this build supports, a native concept reprojected after owning a purged observation, and a refusal that deletes nothing when the pinned embedder cannot be loaded.

Removed coverage, in full. 30 deleted files tested the deleted subsystem and its CLI/dashboard surfaces. The ~31 cases removed from files that survive are the ones worth auditing: `embedder-pin` −10 (native/source cross-population width split, source placeholders excluded from dimension inference), `sync` −5 (export/graft refusals for source-owned rows), `gates` −5, `workstream` −4 (connector-owned slug occupancy), `migrate-embeddings` −3 (the two source phases), `non-latin-diagnostic` −2, `lifecycle-edges` −2, `recall-unit-split` −1, `write-budget` −1. Where a guard survives, its test survives with it: `lifecycle-edges`' write-time refusal keeps its coverage by minting connector rows directly in SQL.

Not covered: the purge against a large real store (the fixture's native side is one concept and one observation, so the `entities.df` recount is correct by construction rather than by measurement), and an end-to-end upgrade from a real 1.6.x store.

## Related

#42, #43, #45 and #46 describe defects in code this PR deletes, so they stop being reachable rather than being repaired — they should be dispositioned against this change rather than worked. team-monet/monet-core#99 and team-monet/monet-core#135 were already named as moot/paused by #16.

Separately noted while here: the engine constructor has no schema-version ceiling check — it imports `MONET_SCHEMA_VERSION` but never reads it, so an older build opens a newer store and fails at the first missing column rather than refusing. Latent until something removes a column; only `doctor` and `repair` check the ceiling today.

No version bump here: merge is not release.

Closes #16

- write and synchronize sensitive replacement data through the protected descriptor
- verify temporary permissions and contents before replacement

## Validation
- `swift test`
- `swiftlint lint --strict`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Hardens permissions on a short-lived staging path during config replacement; behavior is otherwise the same aside from stricter temp-file creation semantics.
> 
> **Overview**
> Config replacement no longer uses Foundation’s atomic write plus a separate chmod for staging files. **Staging now goes through `writePrivateTemporary`**, which creates each `.tmp` with `open(..., O_CREAT | O_EXCL, 0600)` and writes the payload through that descriptor so secrets are not briefly world-readable.
> 
> Import guards switch from `#if os(Linux)` to **`canImport(Darwin)` / `canImport(Glibc)`** so POSIX symbols used by the helper compile on the right platforms.
> 
> A new test hooks **`beforeReplacing`** to assert the staging file is mode **0600** and holds the replacement JSON before the live config is swapped.
>

author: tengqm
body:
Two regressions in the rebuilt sunrise wheel vs the vendor bake (PR #446), found during node A/B against the decode-hang baseline:

**1. libtriton.so RUNPATH** — upstream main dropped `INSTALL_RPATH "$ORIGIN"` (still present at fec6c8a0c CMakeLists.txt:459-461), so the rebuilt wheel's libtriton.so carries an absolute `/usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/triton/_C` RUNPATH and fails to load when installed to `/opt/flagtree` (the runtime's compiler prefix). Fix: `TRITON_APPEND_CMAKE_ARGS="-DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH=\$ORIGIN"` (setup.py:574 appends it after `-DTRITON_BUILD_UT=OFF`; shlex.split passes `$ORIGIN` through literally — locally validated).

**2. tang alias** — upstream renamed `third_party/sunrise/language/tang` → `ptpu`, but the baked runtime's flag_gems 5.3.4 imports `triton.language.extra.tang` (newer flag_gems uses ptpu). The wheel previously shipped only `ptpu`, requiring a manual `ln -sfn ptpu tang` on the node. Fix: symlink `ptpu` → `tang` before `pip wheel` — `get_package_dirs()` iterates `os.listdir(backend.language_dir)`, so both names ship as real directories.

Both are gated in the Containerfile: the wheel must contain `triton/language/extra/{ptpu,tang}` and libtriton.so's RUNPATH must contain `$ORIGIN` (no `/usr/local`).

A/B context (PR-978 rebuild fixes the sunrise flash-attn decode hang, 0.4 → 2.4 tok/s, terminates) will be recorded in report-vllm-0.24.0.md after the rebuilt wheel re-passes node E2E.

This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI.

author: chidionyema
body:
Closes #399. Founder, 2026-08-19: *"in admin ops dashboard, should be able to see last time anything deployable on the stack was deployed."*

Nothing surfaced it before. On `origin/main`, `git grep -l -i "deploy_age|buildAge|build_age|lastDeployed|last_deploy"` across `Ops.Console`, `prospector/ops` and `scripts` returned **no files**. The only deploy code in the console API drives `cutover.sh` and the launchd plists — the button, not the age.

This is the blind spot behind "reported green while the site served the old build". On 17 August production ran 17-hour-old code and every screen read green; the only way to find out was `lsof` on the pid. A workflow badge says a deploy succeeded. It does not say when, and it does not say whether main has moved since.

## What it probes

A new `deploys` read view, rendered as a **Deployed** panel at the top of the Engine page, polled every 60s.

| Deployable | Probe |
|---|---|
| Store.Web | last successful `Deploy Store.Web` run on main — its head SHA is what Fly built, its completion time is when the machines took it |
| Store.Api | same, `deploy-api.yml` |
| engine | the `prospector-live` checkout's own HEAD and that commit's date — the daemons execute that working tree |
| ops-console | the mtime of the `.next` directory `next start` serves, because it serves a build, not the source beside it |

Each row also carries **how many commits behind `origin/main`** it is, so "deployed ten minutes ago" and "running code that is not main" stop being the same answer. A deployable that cannot be probed reads `unknown`. It never reads "up to date".

## What it says about this machine right now

```
store-web    ok       age=0.0h   behind=0
store-api    behind   age=4.4h   behind=10
engine       behind   age=20.1h  behind=33   clean mirror of a commit
ops-console  unknown  age=-       no build at prospector-live/store_platform/src/Ops.Console/.next
```

The engine is 33 commits and 20 hours behind main, and the live checkout has never had a console built in it. Both were invisible before this panel.

## Three defects it produced while being written, each pinned by a test

- **It rolled its own "is the live checkout dirty" check.** An untracked `.venv` read as `LOCAL EDITS (1 paths)` while `live_checkout.py --update` — which owns that rule and ignores untracked paths — called the same tree clean. The console would have shown a wedged production checkout the updater was happy to fast-forward. It now calls `live_checkout._code_changes` instead of having an opinion.
- **The first live run printed `age=-1h`** for Store.Web, because GitHub's completion stamp was ahead of this machine's clock. A negative age sorts to the top as the freshest deploy and grades `ok` — the one answer this module exists to stop handing out for free. Ages clamp at zero and skew is named in the row.
- **`shutil.which("gh")` resolves in a terminal and returns `None` under launchd.** Every Fly row would have read `unknown` from the console while the same command worked by hand. The Homebrew prefixes are checked explicitly.

**Mutation-checked:** reverting each of those three fixes turns 5 tests red, and restoring them returns 19 passed. The gate is not vacuous.

## Verified locally

```
pytest tests/unit/test_deploys_view.py   19 passed
Ops.Console tsc --noEmit                 exit 0
Ops.Console eslint                       exit 0
Ops.Console vitest                       125 passed (14 files)
```

The panel also reuses `duration()` from `@/lib/time` rather than adding a second "how long ago" formatter, and a test asserts the view is registered on **both** sides — `READS` in python and the `VIEWS` whitelist in the Next.js route — because wiring one and not the other produces a 400 that reads like a bug in the panel.

author: mwaidh5
body:
"Draw around" dead-ended: you could draw the loop, and then nothing.

**Cause.** The loop's points live in a `useRef` (correct — they change on every pointer move and shouldn't re-render). But the **Delete inside / Keep only this** buttons were gated on `lasso.current.length > 2`, and React never re-renders when a ref changes, so the buttons never appeared.

- The loop's *presence* is now a piece of state, set when the pointer lifts, so the two choices show up immediately.
- Switching tools clears a half-drawn loop.
- Undo now steps back once per action instead of twice: the lasso only draws an outline until it's applied, so snapshotting when the drag *started* recorded an identical frame. The snapshot happens at apply time.

Verified the compositing pixel by pixel in a browser, on a known image with a known loop:

```
delete inside → inside alpha 0,   outside alpha 255
keep only     → inside alpha 255, outside alpha 0
```

author: ztjiang0123
body:
## Summary

Resolves all 5 `clone_family` (duplicate implementation) signals from Code Analyzer fix run `cifr_2bd4767d400057192226fc55` (analyzed commit `d8db837`). Each near-duplicate pair now routes through a single shared helper; intended behavior is preserved.

## Violation-by-violation

### 1. `benchmark_bitpacking.cpp:249` / `:270` — `pack_uint_odd_bit` / `unpack_uint_odd_bit`
The two forwarders shared 100% of their structure (`using fns = odd_bit_functions<nbit>; <dispatch>(triple, nbit, ...)`). Added a single `forward_uint_odd_bit<nbit>(...)` template that holds the forwarding body; pack/unpack now each just supply their nbit-specific function triple and the matching `*_values` dispatcher.

### 2. `matmul_perf_model.py:42` / `:63` — `get_tensorcore_tflops` / `get_simd_tflops`
Identical bodies differing only in the peak-tflops function. Extracted `_get_num_subcores(device)` and `_get_tflops(get_max_tflops, ...)`; the two public functions are now one-line wrappers passing `get_max_tensorcore_tflops` / `get_max_simd_tflops`.

### 3. `uintx_utils.py:120` / `affine_fake_quantized_tensor.py:213` — `_get_to_kwargs`
87% duplicate; the only difference is the QAT tensor also propagates `requires_grad`. Added `_get_to_kwargs_with_memory_format(self, *args, include_requires_grad=False, **kwargs)` in `torchao/utils.py`; both methods delegate (`include_requires_grad=True` for the fake-quant tensor).

### 4. `inference_workflow.py:87` / `quant_api.py:624` — `_..._opaque_tensor_transform` / `_int4_weight_only_transform`
90% duplicate tail: install the quantized weight as a non-grad `Parameter` and patch `module.extra_repr`. Extracted `_set_quantized_parameter(module, parameter_name, new_weight)` in `torchao/quantization/utils.py`; both transforms return `_set_quantized_parameter(...)`. Removed now-unused `types` / `partial` imports from `inference_workflow.py`.

### 5. `float8nocompile_scaling_utils.py:33` / `:183` — `forward` (the `ToFP8*` autograd Functions)
All seven `torch.autograd.Function` classes had structurally identical `forward`/`backward`, differing only by the underlying `hp_to_fp8_*` kernel. Replaced with a `_make_to_fp8_autograd_function(name, kernel, doc)` factory; each `ToFP8*` symbol is built from its kernel. Public names/docstrings and the `.apply(...)` call surface are unchanged.

## Verification

- **Behavioral equivalence (runtime):**
  - `_get_to_kwargs_with_memory_format` returns identical dicts for both delegating tensors; `UintxTensor.to()` and `_AffineFakeQuantizedTensor.to()` exercised (latter confirms `requires_grad` still propagated).
  - `_set_quantized_parameter` installs a non-grad `Parameter` and updates `extra_repr` (`weight=` appears in `repr(module)`), matching the original inline code.
  - `matmul_perf_model` `_get_num_subcores`/`_get_tflops` verified against hand-computed values (simd/tensorcore) with a mocked triton driver.
  - float8nocompile factory: forward (single- and multi-output kernels) and backward gradient pass-through verified; all six classes are `torch.autograd.Function` subclasses with docstrings.
- **C++:** the flagged file is aarch64/NEON-gated, so a standalone harness mirroring the exact trait + dispatcher + `forward_uint_odd_bit` template shape was compiled with `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra` and run — pack/unpack round-trip correct.
- **Lint/format:** `ruff check --select F,I` and `ruff check --isolated --select F821,F823,W191` pass on all changed files; `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files except a pre-existing (unrelated, unchanged) lambda in `quant_api.py` that already failed on the analyzed commit.

author: alexandrosk0
body:
## Intent

Closeout for the #2127 gate escape: the merge-snapshot ledger row, the mandatory blameless
postmortem, and the category entry it spawns.

PR #2127 (`fix(ui)` for #2110) merged `2026-08-19T10:54:57Z` with 38/38 checks green **and**
`CR findings (0 actionable)` still `pending`. `merge-gates.sh` correctly refused (`GATES_TIMEOUT`);
the orchestrator escalated under ship-loop exception 6 and the user authorised the merge. Repo
policy makes that a gate escape owing a postmortem with a named preventing gate — this is it.

## What the investigation found

Not one escape. **Seven consecutive merges** past the same permanently-`pending` context, none of
them labelled: #2127, #2130, #2122, #2121, #2119, #2118, #2117 — a window of ~18 h. Seven open PRs
(#2132, #2131, #2129, #2126, #2125, #2101, #2080) sit in the same state right now.
`postmortem-owed.sh --list`, run immediately after the merge, reported
`no gate escapes owed a postmortem (last 20 merges clean)`.

Four composing holes, each source-read rather than inferred:

1. `cr-finding-gate`'s `decide()` correctly **refuses** to score CodeRabbit's OSS-star-gate skip
   (`manual review required for this OSS repository`) as a verdict — but the refusal has no terminal
   branch. The poll exhausts `POLL_BUDGET_SECONDS=180` and posts `pending`, waiting on a repo-plan
   property that is not a race and will never resolve.
2. The action runs `set +e` and exits 0 on every terminal verdict (deliberate — it keeps the
   `if: always()` fallback poster alive through a step timeout). So the **job** is green while the
   **context it posted** is `pending`.
3. `branch_protection.required_contexts` names the job `CR finding gate`, **not** the context
   `CR findings (0 actionable)` — proven by the auto-derived 22-name `requiredContexts` array in
   #2127's own ledger row. GitHub reports mergeable; the block-on-any-red poller refuses.
4. `postmortem-owed.sh` is structurally blind to it: trigger 1 needs a *terminal* non-SUCCESS
   (`IN_PROGRESS/QUEUED/PENDING never count`), and the `required-never-terminal` column that **does**
   read `IN("PENDING","EXPECTED")` is gated on the same required set hole 3 shows this context is
   missing from. Trigger 2 needs an override label; none was used.

Underneath: `merge-gates.sh` deliberately **bounds** its CR wait (`MERGE_GATES_CR_GRACE_POLLS`,
WARN-and-pass, "so a stuck integration never wedges the ship-loop indefinitely") while the producer
posts an **unbounded** `pending`. The no-wedge hatch is defeated by the thing it hatches against.

## Preventing gate (ordered — (b) before (a) is unsafe)

**(a)** A terminal `failure` arm for the never-reviewed-by-policy input, naming the condition
(mirroring the `cr-quota-exhausted` verdict #1962 proposed for the sibling input), plus a
`tests/bats/cr_finding_gate.bats` assertion of the invariant this escape violated: the action must
never conclude its job green while the context it posted is `pending`.
**(b)** Then add `CR findings (0 actionable)` to `branch_protection.required_contexts` — which also
switches on the detector's existing never-terminal column for free — plus a parity check that every
status context a first-party workflow posts as a gate verdict appears in the required set.

(b) alone would convert today's soft repo-wide wedge into a hard BLOCK on every PR, hence the order.
Enabling CR auto-review is the real remediation but is a **human** action, named as such rather than
counted as a gate.

## Files

- `docs/self-improvement/merge-snapshots.jsonl` — #2127's row. Verdict recorded as
  `GATES_INCOMPLETE`, not `GATES_PASSED`: the poll returned `GATES_TIMEOUT` and writing a pass would
  be false. `redChecks` carries the descriptive string
  `CR findings (0 actionable) [PENDING at merge - never terminal; not red]` — tagged so no reader
  mistakes a never-terminal context for a failure (precedent: #1970's
  `"(no check runs existed at merge - 0 contexts reported)"`). Actor `orchestrator`.
- `docs/self-improvement/postmortems.md` — the entry, at the top, in the mandated shape.
- `docs/self-improvement/categories/process/2026-08-19-…` — the spawned P1 entry, with a
  `Triggered-follow-up:` re-check at 15 PRs.

Complements — does not duplicate — `2026-08-17-cr-finding-gate-accepts-a-verdict-line-without-a-review.md`:
that entry covers the review-assurance ladder failing **open** (a non-review scored as clean); this
one covers the gate mechanics failing **silent** (the correct refusal having nowhere terminal to go).
Same upstream cause, opposite direction.

## Test plan

- Pure-docs diff — build and `test-all.sh` skipped per AGENTS.md § Cadence.
- `test-markdown-links.sh --all` — **Passed: 299 Failed: 0**, 0 dangling links across 299 files. The
  single WARN is pre-existing in an unrelated 2026-08-16 entry.
- Every claim in both documents is source-read (the action's poll tail, the workflow's exit-code
  comment, the detector's jq filters, the ledger row's own `requiredContexts`) rather than reasoned
  about — the failure mode the 2026-08-17 entry records against itself.
- Diffs entirely under `docs/self-improvement/**`, so it auto-exempts CR + Bugbot with no label.

adversarial-code-review: 0 findings, inline adversarial review of the diff — docs only, no executable content; link targets verified by the checker, the ledger row re-validated against the 7-arg append contract, and the two entries cross-checked against the #1948/#1962 siblings to confirm neither already covers this input (head=978306a21c049fc58f1f25ff3062b44081a2afb3)

author: kroffske
body:
## What changes

Lands the last unpushed local commit (authored 2026-08-19) on top of today's `dev`, plus the changelog entry the pull-request policy requires. Prompt text only in the packaged `task/plan` workflow — stage count, JavaScript structure, and the standard profile are unchanged.

Five fixes, each traced to an audited plan-then-implement series:

- **Composition states the executor's reality.** Every step is later executed by one unattended CLI agent with this run's toolset. Browser play, screenshots, a stronger-model judge, and anything a person must sign now belong in a final `Operator acceptance` section of `plan.md` rather than in a step; the step-usability review checks the same rule. The audited series put exactly that work into its last step and lost ~4h to a blocked run.
- **Reviews must write `## Checks performed` and `## Findings`.** The permitted `None.` produced two six-byte review files indistinguishable from a review nobody performed.
- **Stages that write a file return a short readback instead of repeating its contents.** The repetition was ~75–82KB of ~100KB of final answers and injected a phantom "duplicate sections" claim into `plan.md`. Verification still returns its complete text, because routing and the blocker decide from that text alone.
- **Routing takes no tools and returns one quoted JSON string.** The audited run's first routing answer was rejected as invalid JSON; a second miss would have published a blocker against a ready verification.
- **Correction short-circuits with `No correction needed.`** when no review lists an actionable finding. It had spent 49m and 28 tool calls applying two wording fixes.

## Verification

`npm run check` green on this tree: 141 test files, 2489 tests. Pre-push gate passed.

## Summary

A real backtest run at `XG_BLEND_WEIGHT=0.5` came back byte-for-byte identical to the `0.0` baseline across every metric — the signature of a no-op, not "xG made no difference."

- `fixture_team_stats.xg` has been `null` for every row since it existed: migration 1701000000014 added it flagged "UNVERIFIED" whether API-Football's `/fixtures/statistics` endpoint even carries it, and that confirmation never happened — the only writer to `fixture_team_stats` is the football-data.co.uk CSV importer, which never included `xg` in its INSERT at all.
- Confirmed for real (not guessed): a live `GET /fixtures/statistics` response shows only shot/card/pass/corner counts, no expected-goals field anywhere.
- Pivoted to shots on target instead — football-data.co.uk's `HST`/`AST` CSV columns, already populated for every real Premier League and Championship match, unlike xG.
- Real wrinkle xG wouldn't have needed: shots on target isn't on the same scale as goals, so `blend_shots_on_target_into_scores` rescales it by the training set's own pooled goals-per-shot-on-target ratio (computed from the actual data passed in, not a hardcoded assumed conversion rate) before blending.
- Renamed the whole mechanism to match what it does now (`blend_xg_into_scores` → `blend_shots_on_target_into_scores`, `XG_BLEND_WEIGHT` → `SHOTS_ON_TARGET_BLEND_WEIGHT`) rather than leave xG-flavored names on a shots-on-target mechanism.

- [x] Synthetic integration check: a team with high shots-on-target but low actual goals across 10 matches gets a higher fitted Dixon-Coles attack rating under shots-on-target blending than goals-only fitting, and `predict()` reflects it

author: geiserx
body:
## The problem

Every issue `track-upstream.yml` files says this:

> Within `>=0.21.1,<1.0.0` range — Dependabot should handle this automatically.

Both halves are wrong.

1. **The range is hardcoded** and went stale two bumps ago. The real constraint
   has been `>=0.22.1`, then `>=0.23.0`, and is now `>=0.23.1`. Issue #20 was
   still quoting `0.21.1`.
2. **Dependabot cannot handle it.** The new version already satisfies our range,
   and there is no lockfile, so Dependabot has nothing to bump and opens nothing.
   That is exactly what happened: #15, #17 and #20 all needed a hand-written PR
   (#16, #18, #21). The line told me to wait for a bot that was never coming.

A third small lie in the checklist: "Update README badge (`wraps-mcp--atlassian`
version)" is unticked on every issue, but the badge reads `0.x` and only changes
on a major bump.

## The fix

- Read the constraint out of `pyproject.toml` instead of quoting one:
  `constraint=>=0.23.1,<1.0.0`.
- Say what actually happens — Dependabot will not open a PR, raising the floor is
  a manual PR, and that is what the issue is for.
- Make the badge checklist item conditional on a major bump.

## Verification

The changed step, executed verbatim as the runner will run it:

```
Current pin: 0.23.1
Current constraint: >=0.23.1,<1.0.0
```

That took two attempts and is the reason the step is tested rather than eyeballed
— the first version of the extraction matched the *description* line
("…wrapping upstream mcp-atlassian with Playwright SSO auth") and produced
`constraint=' with Playwright SSO auth'`. It is now anchored on the quoted
dependency entry.

`actionlint` reports the same two pre-existing SC2129 style hits as on `main`
(lines 35 and 88, both untouched here) and nothing new.

author: freezemanny
body:
Closes #73.

## Problem

`uv sync --locked` fails on every release PR (e.g. #70):

```
error: The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--locked` was provided.
```

uv records a `version` for the root package in `uv.lock` only when `pyproject.toml` states one statically. release-please bumps `pyproject.toml` and leaves the lock behind, so the two disagree.

The blast radius is wider than the release PR: `Test` runs on `pull_request`, so once a release PR merges, the stale lock lands on main and **every subsequent PR** fails the same way. `Docs` (`uv sync --locked --group docs`, on `release: published`) would fail on the release itself. `Publish` is unaffected — it only runs `uv build`.

## Fix

Make the version dynamic. With `dynamic = ["version"]`, uv omits the field from the lock entirely, so a release bump cannot desynchronise it and `--locked` stays strict for the dependabot PRs it was added for.

| root version | after a 0.9.1 → 0.10.0 bump | `uv lock --check` |
|---|---|---|
| static (before) | lock now stale | fails |
| dynamic (after) | lock unchanged — no version recorded | passes |

release-please now updates `src/__about__.py` through its **generic** (comment-annotation) updater instead.

## Also dropped

The `uv.lock` entry added to `release-please-config.json` in #72 was a silent no-op. Its jsonpath is evaluated by `jsonpath-plus`, which does not apply the `[?(@.name=='labops')]` filter, so it matched nothing and only logged a warning — visible in the Release Please run for #70:

```
⚠ No entries modified in $.package[?(@.name=='labops')].version
```

Non-matching paths only warn, never fail, which is why #72 looked like it worked.

## Verification

- `uv lock` → `Updated labops v0.9.1 -> (dynamic)`; the `version` field is gone from the lock
- `uv sync --locked` passes from a clean environment and installs `labops==0.9.1`
- bumping `__about__.py` to `0.10.0` leaves `uv lock --check` passing, and `uv build` produces `labops-0.10.0` artifacts
- 550 tests pass; `ruff check` clean

Not verifiable locally: that release-please actually rewrites the annotated line — that only proves out on the next Release Please run. It uses the annotation-based generic updater rather than the jsonpath path that failed before.

## After merge

release-please regenerates #70 against the new config, bumping `src/__about__.py` instead of `pyproject.toml`, and its stale-lock diff disappears.

author: drtamirlan911-cell
body:
Фаза 3 плана Treatment Concierge. Презентацию можно было читать, но не слышать.

## Что сделано

**Озвучка на сервере, кэш по содержимому.** Ключ кэша — `sha256(provider|model|voice|locale|нормализованный текст)`: не бит, не план, не пациент. «Здравствуйте, я расскажу о вашем плане лечения» синтезируется **один раз на всю платформу**, повторный просмотр бесплатен по построению, а перегенерация сценария пересинтезирует только те реплики, которые действительно изменились.

**Синтез ленивый, по акту.** Большинство пациентов открывает первый акт; синтезировать шесть вперёд — платить за то, чего никто не услышит. Плюс лимит символов на запрос, чтобы «убежавший» сценарий не выставил счёт одним вызовом.

**Тишина — не ошибка, а штатный исход.** Хранилище не настроено, провайдер лёг, бюджет исчерпан, браузер отказал в автовоспроизведении, файл не загрузился — каждый из этих путей приводит к воспроизведению реплики по расчётному времени чтения. Пациент не видит ошибки никогда.

| Файл | Роль |
|---|---|
| `patient-presentation/voice.service.ts` | OpenAI TTS (`gpt-4o-mini-tts`, голос `sage`), кэш, деградация |
| `voice.service.test.ts` | 15 тестов |
| `schema.prisma` + `migrations/20260819_voice_assets/` + блок в `src/index.ts` | `VoiceAsset` установленной парой |
| `patientPresentation.routes.ts` | `GET /:releaseId/voice` + общий `buildScriptForRelease` |
| `src/lib/presentation/audioPersona.ts` + `.test.ts` | `AudioPersona`, 13 тестов |
| `src/utils/api.ts`, `TreatmentPresentation.tsx` | клиент и подключение с предзагрузкой |

## Два дефекта, найденные у себя и починенные до отгрузки

1. **Маршрут голоса собирал сценарий без имён пациента, клиники и врача**, а маршрут сценария — с ними. Пациент бы *слышал* одну фразу и *читал* другую, причём id битов совпадали бы — ровно то, из-за чего это было бы трудно заметить. Оба маршрута теперь идут через один `buildScriptForRelease`.
2. **Первая реплика молчала бы всегда.** Голос грузился при *входе* в акт, а режиссёр начинает говорить сразу — то есть молчала бы единственная реплика, ради которой экран существует. Теперь акт 1 ждёт озвучку до `play()`, а акт N+1 подгружается, пока играет N.

## Просьба к следующему, кто будет это читать

Озвучка генерируется нами, **не является документом пациента**, не должна появляться во вкладке «Документы» и не должна удаляться через файловый UI. Поэтому она идёт через `lib/storage.ts` напрямую и **намеренно** не трогает аллоулист расширений в `files.routes.ts` и enum `ImageType`. Это не недосмотр — пожалуйста, не «чините».

## Проверено

`tsc` 0 в обоих проектах · 904/904 теста · обе сборки · eslint в потолках CI (13 фронтенд, 70 бэкенд) при **0 ошибках**, ни одного предупреждения из новых файлов.

**На живом Postgres 16, не на моках — 19/19:**

- миграция идемпотентна (два прогона), `prisma db push` после неё говорит «already in sync» — **дрейфа нет**;
- две «разные клиники» с одинаковой фразой → **один** объект и **одна** строка;
- отличие только в пробелах попадает в ту же запись; другая локаль синтезируется отдельно; дубль внутри одного запроса стоит одного синтеза;
- **гонка двух одновременных запросов на новую фразу оставляет ровно одну строку** — уникальный индекс держит, а `upsert` делает проигравшего no-op, а не падением;
- таймаут провайдера → `audioUrl: null` и **строка не пишется**;
- пустая реплика ничего не стоит;
- выданный браузеру URL — подписанный `http` с `X-Amz-Expires=900`, а не `s3://`.

Отдельно: при `storageConfigured() === false` все реплики молчат по порядку, **провайдер не вызывается вообще**, ни одной ошибки.

## Что осталось вне этого PR

Фаза 4 — акты 3, 5, 6: библиотека последствий, Essential/Optimal/Premium, интерактивная стоимость, цифра рассрочки, следующий шаг.

author: szabosteve
body:
## What this PR does

Related to https://github.com/qdrant/landing_page/pull/2621

/md/ requests for documentation paths that `qdrant.tech` has since moved currently 404, because the redirect rules live in Netlify config on the landing page and the mirror never sees them.

This PR adds a build step that fetches the merged table published at `qdrant.tech/redirects.txt` and writes it into `public/_redirects` with a `/md` prefix on both sides, so moved paths answer with a 301 at the edge before the `/md/*` proxy forwards to `search.qdrant.tech`.

The landing_page repo stays the single owner of these rules; nothing here is hand-maintained, and a failed fetch warns and deploys without them rather than failing the build.

author: erikdarlingdata
body:
Closes #2348.

`\\?\UNC\server\share` is the extended-length spelling of a **real share** and `\\?\C:\Users\bob` of a **real profile**, but both guards excluded `\\?\` wholesale, so each was waved through with no diagnosis. Skipping a check is not the same as passing it.

## Why a normalization and not just deleting the exclusion

The exclusion was right about one case: `\\?\C:\PerformanceMonitorDarling` is an ordinary local root written the long way, and refusing it would strand an install that works. Deleting the carve-out would have called it a share.

So the prefix is stripped at the **single entry point**, and every existing rule then runs against the ordinary spelling. One place knows the prefix exists; the profile test, the UNC test and the drive-qualifier test are all written against real paths and needed no changes at all. The old `&& !StartsWith(@"\\?\")` is simply gone.

Two details that are easy to get wrong and are pinned:

- **UNC is matched first**, because it is the longer prefix. Stripping `\\?\` first leaves `UNC\server\share`, which is neither a share nor a local path and would classify as neither.
- **`UNC` is matched case-insensitively**, because Windows accepts `\\?\unc\`. An ordinal match would leave that spelling looking like a local path — re-opening this exact hole for the operator least likely to be checked on.

## Both halves, together

`install-darling.ps1` gets `Convert-ExtendedLengthPath`, applied to a separate `$classifyRoot`. The installer still writes to `$root` **exactly as given** — the prefix instructs the path parser and is not part of where the install lives, so normalizing for the decision changes which rules see the path and nothing about where files land.

## Tests

- The three rows that pinned this as a known residual (verdict `None`) now assert the fix — `UserProfile`, `UncPath`, `UncPath` — joined by lowercase `\\?\unc\`, an extended-length share **root**, and an extended-length **mapped drive**.
- `GetNetworkPathKind_...` now composes `Convert-ExtendedLengthPath` ahead of `Get-NetworkPathKind`, because that is what the script does. Calling the kind function on a raw path would test a contract the installer no longer uses.
- New `ConvertExtendedLengthPath_RewritesBothSpellings_AsShipped` executes the normalization itself.
- The cross-language parity test lifts the **normalization line** out of the shipped script alongside the two rule lines. Lifting only the rule lines would quietly test a composition the installer does not perform.

## Verification

Both projects build clean (0 warnings, 0 errors). The suites target `net10.0-windows` and cannot run on macOS, so the classification logic was exercised in a throwaway `net10.0` harness over all 16 cases first — including the load-bearing `\\?\C:\PerformanceMonitorDarling → None` — all passing. CI is the first place the PowerShell half actually executes.

author: klausaschenbrenner
body:
## Summary

`do_transfer` in `kernel/src/drivers/ahci.rs` used to hold `AHCI_LOCK` (which
disables interrupts on this single-core kernel) for the *entire* function,
including both busy-poll loops (up to 1,000,000 iterations waiting for a free
command slot, and up to 5,000,000 iterations waiting for completion). That
meant every AHCI transfer — any FAT32 file read/write on the UEFI boot path —
blocked the timer tick and all other interrupt-driven I/O for as long as the
underlying disk command took.

- `AHCI_LOCK` is now held only for the brief register snapshot/write
  sections (port lookup, per-iteration `ci`/`sact`/`is` reads, and the
  bounded command-programming sequence), not across either busy-poll loop.
- Since this driver only ever uses command slot 0, simply narrowing the lock
  would let a second task race a still-in-flight transfer (e.g. reprogram
  slot 0's command header while the first transfer's command is still
  outstanding) now that interrupts are no longer disabled for the whole
  call. A new `AHCI_REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT` atomic + `AHCI_REQUEST_WAITQUEUE`
  (mirroring `ata.rs`'s existing `REQUEST_IN_FLIGHT`/`acquire_request_slot`
  pattern) restores "only one transfer in flight at a time" without
  disabling interrupts while a task waits its turn.
- Timeout/error semantics (`AhciError::Timeout`, `AhciError::PortError`) are
  unchanged; iteration counts and returned errors match the original code
  exactly.
- Deliberately did **not** add `core::hint::spin_loop()`/`PAUSE` to the
  poll loops: this file already documents (see `delay_ms`) that
  PAUSE-loop-exiting under KVM turns a tight PAUSE loop into a storm of VM
  exits, which previously made an unrelated bring-up delay appear to hang
  for minutes. Adding it to these 1M/5M-iteration loops risked reproducing
  that exact hazard.
- Added SAFETY comments for the newly-restructured locking (a full SAFETY
  audit of the whole unsafe block, including the DMA/FIS/PRDT pointer
  derivations, is tracked separately in issue #49).

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_ahci_request_slot_enforces_mutual_exclusion` and
      `test_ahci_request_slot_does_not_leak_across_repeated_calls` to
      `kernel/tests/block_test.rs`, exercising the new request-slot
      primitive via a test-only seam (`try_acquire_transfer_slot_for_test`
      / `release_transfer_slot_for_test`), since `do_transfer`'s hardware
      path cannot be driven end-to-end without a mapped AHCI port (not
      present in the default QEMU test environment, same limitation
      already documented for `max_prdt_entries_for`).
- [x] `cargo test` (all 47 QEMU integration test binaries / 465 test cases)
      passes, including the two new cases.
- [x] `cargo clippy` — zero warnings/errors.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean.

Fixes #48

author: kazakovak2001-lgtm
body:
## Summary
- The canonical `goal -> blueprint -> lua -> assets -> validate -> export` pipeline (`POST /api/generate/game`, `POST /api/generate/export` in `server/src/routes/generation-v2.ts`) ran `GameValidationEngine` but ignored the result: both routes built and returned an export package even when validation reported errors, so a structurally valid but Roblox-invalid generation could still reach a "deliverable" package.
- `LuaGenerator` interpolated blueprint text (title, genre, currency, mechanic/biome/stage names — planner/AI output this generator does not control the shape of) directly into Lua string literals, and in one case into a bare table-key identifier, with no escaping. A value containing a quote, backslash, or space produced Luau that fails to parse.

## Fixes
- `generation-v2.ts`: both `/game` and `/export` now refuse (422, no package returned) when `GameValidationEngine.validate()` reports any error. `/export` previously ran no validation at all on caller-supplied blueprint/lua/assets; it now reuses the same validator.
- `LuaGenerator.ts`: added a `luaString()` escape helper and applied it to every interpolated blueprint field embedded in a Lua string literal; replaced the bare-identifier `currency` table key (`${currency} = 0`, invalid Luau for any non-identifier currency name) with a computed string key (`["${currency}"] = 0`).
- Added `server/src/generation/__tests__/genviability1.minimal-package.test.ts` proving:
  1. a minimal generated game (empty plan output) passes validation end-to-end and produces a well-formed, importable Rojo export (server + client scripts, a spawn point, `default.project.json` with correct paths, every script under `src/`);
  2. quote/backslash-bearing blueprint text no longer breaks generated Lua (no unterminated string literals, balanced function/do/then/end);
  3. both routes contain the fail-closed gate ahead of the export call.

## Scope
Confined to `server/src/routes/generation-v2.ts` and `server/src/generation/{blueprint,lua,assets,validation,export}` — the exact `goal → blueprint → lua → assets → validation → export` pipeline this router's own docstring describes. No changes to the agent/plan-executor-based `GameGenerationService` pipeline, Studio integration, security/governance, or docs. No parallel validator/pipeline was introduced — `GameValidationEngine` (already the validator/tester stage) is reused, just enforced.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (server) — clean, aside from a pre-existing unrelated `wasmoon` module-resolution error in test support code.
- [x] Targeted vitest run: `genviability1.minimal-package.test.ts`, `security2gE.generation-v2-scope.test.ts`, `secauthz1.cross-tenant-harness.test.ts`, `security2gE.api-key-small-routes-enforcement.test.ts`, `firstplayable1.luaTokenBudget.test.ts` — all pass (38 tests).
- [x] `npm run validate` (pre-commit hook) — all checks pass; tracked inventories regenerated via `scripts/cleanup/generate-tracked-inventories.mjs`.

## Summary

This PR refactors the original one-file Dev Confessions Express API into a focused MVC structure while preserving the existing endpoint paths and documented response behavior.

### Refactoring decisions

- Added `AUDIT.md` with the complete pre-refactor problem inventory.
- Renamed vague variables and recorded every rename in [`CHANGES.md`](https://github.com/roshantejas121/dev-confessions-refactor/blob/refactor/clean-up/CHANGES.md).
