author: 0feklevy
body:
The same fabrication as #39, **one layer earlier and far more durable** — because this one persists to the database.

## What happens today

The config `PUT` runs the character through `projectCharacterId`, which returns the **default** when handed nothing:

```ts
const characterId = projectCharacterId({ characterId: incoming.characterId ?? existing.characterId });
```

The settings modal only sets `characterId` when the owner actually touches the picker. So saving the form **at all** — changing only the greeting — writes `characterId: 'einstein'` into `avatar_config`. From that moment the project is indistinguishable from one whose owner deliberately chose Einstein.

**This matters more after #39, not less.** #39 taught the client to name a character only when someone genuinely chose it — and this write was quietly manufacturing exactly that evidence. Any project whose owner had ever opened avatar settings would still show "Ask Albert Einstein", and #39 would have looked ineffective for the most common case.

## The fix

A character is stored only when someone actually sent one. An unrecognized id is **dropped**, not rewritten to the default — rewriting is the same fabrication in a different disguise.

## The invariant is intact

The old normalization existed so the stored config and the persona fingerprint could not disagree. They still can't: there is exactly **one** stored value and **one** normalizer. `bakedCharacterId()` already maps an absent or unrecognized id to the default on *read*, and the bake call now uses it explicitly rather than the stored value — which is legitimately absent when nobody chose.

All three direct readers of `cfg.characterId` already tolerated `undefined`:

| reader | behaviour on unset |
|---|---|
| `resolveCharacter` | → `source: 'default'` ✓ |
| `bakedCharacterId` | → `'einstein'` for the bake ✓ |
| `transcriptPropagation` | `?? DEFAULT_CHARACTER_ID` ✓ |

## Verification

5 new cases pinning the write. **Mutation-checked** — restoring the old normalization turns two red.

body:
## Problem
`controller/agenticrun/templates/escalation_request.tmpl` references `{{.Success}}` on the items of `.AnalysisResults` / `.ExecutionResults` / `.VerificationResults`, but those are `[]v1alpha1.StepResultRef` — whose only fields are `Name` and `Outcome`. There is no `Success` field.

Go's `text/template` errors at execution (`can't evaluate field Success in type v1alpha1.StepResultRef`). `renderTemplate` swallows the error and returns `(template "escalation_request.tmpl" error: ...)` as the escalation request body, which is then sent to the escalation agent. The resulting escalation summary describes the template bug instead of the actual remediation failure.

## Fix
Use `{{.Outcome}}` (the `Succeeded`/`Failed` enum) on the three lines.

## Impact
Escalation still completed before this fix (the run reached the Escalated state), so this restores escalation **quality** — the escalation agent now receives the real step outcomes instead of a template error string.

## How it was found
Surfaced during the first end-to-end cluster test of the escalate-on-verification-failure flow (epic [OLS-3816](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OLS-3816)). Confirmed pre-existing on `main` — not introduced by that epic.

author: cristim
body:
## Problem

`scripts/check-azure-role-parity.sh` constrains **which** role is granted and **where**, but never **who**. A fourth `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments` resource binding the allowed custom purchaser role, at the correctly inherited subscription scope, to a hardcoded foreign `principalId` passes the guard cleanly. That role carries `Microsoft.Capacity/reservationOrders/purchase/action`, which spends the customer's money.

Verified against `origin/main` before changing anything: the bypass exits 0.

**The repository's own test data asserted the bypass passes.** `uppercase-allowed-roledefinitionid-arm.json` was an exit-0 fixture whose only role assignment binds an allowed role, at inherited scope, to the literal GUID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000aa`. Every fixture carrying a `principalId` used a hardcoded GUID; none used the parameter. Corrected here.

## Finding 2 is worse than filed

The issue describes a success line that asserts a check happened when little was examined. Measured against `origin/main`, all four of these exit 0:

| scenario | pre-fix |
|---|---|
| a `Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities` resource added | exit 0, `OK: all 4` |
| the Reader grant duplicated | exit 0, `OK: all 5` |
| the Cost Management Reader grant **deleted** | exit 0, `OK: all 3` |
| a role assignment with `principalId` deleted entirely | exit 0, `OK: all 4` |

Removing a grant also passes. The template can be silently weakened, not only extended, and the only trace is a count inside a line that reads as success.

## Change

**Principal axis.** `principalId` is collected and compared against the sanctioned `parameters('servicePrincipalObjectId')` reference. A `roleAssignments` resource with no `principalId` emits `<absent>` and fails the comparison rather than being skipped.

**Grant-set axis.** The template's expected set of grants is asserted, so the guard is no longer a growing list of shapes it happens to refuse. An empty expected set is itself refused, since every template satisfies "grants nothing beyond nothing".

## Three further escalations, found by adversarial review of the first commit

All one class: the check compares the **text** of an ARM expression, so it asserts a name, while the binding between that name and its target lives elsewhere in the template, unasserted.

| # | escalation | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `variables.roles.reader` repointed at built-in **Owner**. Every compared string stays byte-identical and `[variables('roles').reader]` remains on the #1658 allowlist | exit 0 | exit 1, grant-set diff |
| 2 | a `defaultValue` on `parameters.servicePrincipalObjectId`. Every `principalId` still reads the sanctioned parameter; the portal form and `az deployment sub create` prefill the attacker's object ID | exit 0 | exit 1 |
| 3 | `$schema` set to the management-group template with `#subscriptionDeploymentTemplate` appended as a URL **fragment**. ARM reads the path; the pin was an unanchored `test()` reading the fragment | exit 0 | exit 1 |

Escalation 1 is a privilege escalation to Owner that passes a guard built specifically to constrain which role may be granted.

Fixes: `roleDefinitionId` resolves through the template's own `variables` table before being recorded, so the expected set names the built-in role GUIDs the grants resolve to rather than the variables pointing at them; an unresolvable form records as `unresolved:<text>`, which is in no expected set and therefore fails closed. The principal parameter is asserted to carry no `defaultValue` and no `allowedValues`, gated on having **seen** the parameter referenced rather than on the declaration existing, so deleting the declaration is not the way out. The `$schema` test is anchored on the URL's file name.

## Verification

Every new assertion is mutation-proven against a copy of the tree, each mutation required to produce its specific FAIL line since a syntax error also exits non-zero. The `arm/` sweep asserts a non-empty discovery, so "no violations" cannot mean "inspected nothing".

Closes #1681

author: picchu-ai
body:
## Problem

`timeoutSeconds` on a standalone (non-workflow) approval request was documentation only:

- `src/be/db.ts` — `getExpiredPendingApprovals` existed with a `TODO: wire into a periodic sweep` and **no production consumer**.
- `src/http/approval-requests.ts` — the respond route resolved any `pending` request without ever consulting `expiresAt`.
- `src/workflows/recovery.ts` already auto-timeouts expired workflow-linked approvals → the two paths were asymmetric.

Net effect: a standalone request could sit `pending` forever, and an answer arriving long after the deadline was still accepted as an approval.

## Fix

**1. Deadline enforced inside the CAS, not before it.** `resolveApprovalRequest`'s single atomic `UPDATE` now carries the `expiresAt` guard alongside `status = 'pending'`. A read-then-write check in the caller would leave the read→UPDATE window open for a late response to race the sweep; putting it in the transition closes it. `timeout` is exempt from the guard — it is the one transition the deadline itself authorizes, which is also what keeps `src/workflows/recovery.ts` working unchanged.

**2. Idempotent periodic sweep on the existing tick.** `sweepExpiredApprovalRequests()` rides the existing `startWaitPoller` tick (`src/workflows/wait-poller.ts`, 5s) rather than adding a timer — it is the same job, pending rows whose deadline has passed, on the same cadence. Idempotency comes from the CAS: a row already swept is no longer `pending`, so a second pass is a no-op and returns 0.

**3. Workflow behavior preserved.** The sweep queries `getExpiredPendingApprovals({ standaloneOnly: true })`, so workflow-linked approvals are untouched and stay owned by the workflow engine — otherwise the sweep would flip the row terminal without resuming the run, stranding it until the next boot recovery.

**4. One terminal transition, one effect.** The transition and its side effects (workflow `approval.resolved` emit, standalone follow-up task) are funnelled through `finalizeApprovalRequest`. Only the caller whose CAS returned a row fires the effects, so a responder colliding with the sweep produces exactly one transition and exactly one follow-up task.

A late response now gets `409` and the request is driven to `timeout` rather than left pending. The follow-up task uses a new `hitl.timeout` prompt template (registered in the prompt-template registry, per the repo invariant) — the existing `hitl.follow_up` text says "Human responded", which is false for an expiry.

## Why a new module (commit 2)

The lifecycle logic lives in **`src/be/approval-lifecycle.ts`**, not in the route module. The poller importing `src/http/approval-requests.ts` pulled route registration into its import chain, changing module evaluation order and reordering every path in the generated `openapi.json` — a ~2900-line diff for a backend-only fix, and an `OpenAPI Spec Freshness Check` failure. Inverting the dependency keeps `openapi.json` byte-identical.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/be/db.ts` | `expiresAt` guard in `resolveApprovalRequest`'s CAS; `getExpiredPendingApprovals({ standaloneOnly })`; TODO removed |
| `src/be/approval-lifecycle.ts` | **new** — `finalizeApprovalRequest` (transition + effects) and `sweepExpiredApprovalRequests` |
| `src/http/approval-requests.ts` | respond route delegates to `finalizeApprovalRequest`; expiry-aware `409` |
| `src/workflows/wait-poller.ts` | sweep call on the existing tick |
| `src/tools/templates.ts` | `hitl.timeout` template |
| `src/tools/request-human-input.ts` + `MCP.md` | `timeoutSeconds` description now matches the real behavior |
| `src/tests/approval-expiry.test.ts` | **new** |

No migration, no route-shape change, no API break.

## Tests

`src/tests/approval-expiry.test.ts` — 6 tests, driving the respond route through the real production pipeline (`handleCore` auth → `handleApprovalRequests`):

1. response before the deadline → accepted (`200`, `approved`, one follow-up)
2. response after the deadline → refused (`409`), request ends `timeout`, late answer not recorded, exactly one follow-up
3. the CAS itself rejects a post-deadline approve/reject, while `timeout` still passes
4. sweep idempotent — 2 passes, 1 transition, 1 follow-up, `resolvedAt` unchanged
5. response racing the sweep — 4 interleaved contenders, exactly 1 wins, 1 follow-up
6. workflow non-regression — workflow-linked expired approvals excluded from the sweep, still `pending` after it, and `recovery.ts`'s `timeout` transition still succeeds

```
$ bun test src/tests/approval-expiry.test.ts src/tests/approval-requests.test.ts \
    src/tests/workflow-hitl-routing.test.ts src/tests/workflow-wait-*.test.ts \
    src/tests/prompt-template*.test.ts
 262 pass  0 fail  919 expect() calls
```

Full local suite: **no new failures.** This checkout's suite is flaky (scripts-runtime sandbox / apps-sync / heartbeat suites fail non-deterministically here: `main` gave 166 fails, this branch 115 then 40 across runs). Comparing failure *sets* rather than counts, `comm -23 branch-fails baseline-fails` is empty — every failure on this branch also fails on `main`, and no approval/HITL test fails on either. CI's `Run Tests (1-4/4)` are green.

Also green: `bun run lint`, `bun run tsc:check`, `check-db-boundary.sh`, `check-api-key-boundary.sh`, `check-audit-columns.sh`, `check:rbac-coverage`, `check:openapi-response-coverage`, `check:dep-graph` (12 warnings / 0 errors, identical to `main`).

Backend-only — no `apps/ui/` changes, so the UI lint / `qa-use` gates don't apply (`apps/ui` diff vs `main` is empty; that job's 79 Biome errors reproduce unchanged on `main`).

author: amerissa
body:
Makes a single `kyuubi-base` able to serve both NX1 Spark flavours.

### Background

`nx1-spark` now publishes two images — `spark3` (Scala 2.12 / Spark 3.5.6) and `spark4` (Scala 2.13 / Spark 4.2.0) — and `nx1-kyuubi` layers a server image on each.

Kyuubi already handles this well: `build/dist` ships **both** the 2.12 and 2.13 Spark engine jars, and the server picks one at runtime from the Scala version of the Spark it finds in `SPARK_HOME` (`SparkProcessBuilder.extractSparkCoreScalaVersion`).

### The gap

The extra-engine build inherits the main build's profiles. With the default Spark 3.5, that produces a Scala 2.13 engine **compiled against Spark 3.5** — which won't run on Spark 4.2.

### The change

`EXTRA_SCALA_213_SPARK_PROFILE` applies a profile to just that extra engine build. It is **empty by default**, so upstream behaviour is unchanged; `nx1-release.yml` sets it to `spark-4.2`.

Result — one dist, both engines, each matched to the Spark it will actually run on:

| Engine jar | Built against | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| `kyuubi-spark-sql-engine_2.12` | Spark 3.5 | `spark3` image |
| `kyuubi-spark-sql-engine_2.13` | Spark 4.2 | `spark4` image |

### Why not just `-Pspark-4.2 -Pscala-2.13` on the whole dist

That is upstream's intended way to build a Spark 4 dist, and it would work — but it also moves the **server** to Scala 2.13. `nx1-kyuubi`'s `kyuubi-keycloak-authentication` extension is Scala, compiled against `kyuubi-common_2.12`, and would break. Keeping the server on 2.12 leaves it binary-compatible.

### Verification

```
mvn install -DskipTests -Pspark-4.2 -Pscala-2.13 -pl :kyuubi-spark-sql-engine_2.13 -am
```

produces a 40MB shaded jar with Java 17 bytecode. `bash -n build/dist` passes and the workflow YAML parses.

Once merged, this needs a tag cut so `kyuubi-base` is republished before `nx1-kyuubi` can build its Spark 4 flavour.

author: merefield
body:
## Why

Codexometer's version was resolved and displayed differently across the CLI, dashboard, and app-server clients. Development pseudo-versions were suppressed, while one app-server path advertised the literal value `monitor`. This made builds harder to identify and did not follow Go's normal version metadata conventions.

## What changed

- use one build-aware version resolver for the CLI, dashboard, and all app-server client metadata
- prefer an injected release version, then Go module/build information, then VCS development metadata
- distinguish Go pseudo-versions from Codexometer's explicit VCS fallback when `Main.Version` is `(devel)`
- display the resolved version in the dashboard masthead
- make `-v` and `--version` report the same canonical value without an extra `v`
- bump the maintained source version to `0.7.8`
- add a small Makefile that injects the nearest Git tag when available
- document tagged, direct, and development-build version behavior
- cover the resolver and its consumers with tests

## Impact

Release builds report `0.7.8`. Go-provided module versions remain authoritative and are displayed without a leading `v`. When Go reports `Main.Version` as `(devel)`, the resolver instead uses the documented `0.7.8-dev+<commit>[.dirty]` VCS fallback. Existing quota, monitor, and benchmark behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race -cover ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `git diff --check`
- local and six distribution binaries rebuilt for macOS, Linux, and Windows on amd64/arm64
- verified an injected build reports `codexometer 0.7.8`
- verified a direct development build reports Go's embedded pseudo-version

## Release follow-up

After this PR is merged, create and push the repository's first semantic release tag, `v0.7.8`, on the resulting `main` commit. Tagging after merge ensures the release tag identifies the code actually shipped and seeds Go's future pseudo-version calculation.

body:
## What

A small, docs-only addition to Session 3 (Testing with `ansible-test`): a gotcha slide + a matching GLOSSARY one-liner explaining that **`ansible-test sanity` runs pylint over your `tests/` directory too**, not just the module.

## Why

This is a genuine beginner stumble that fits Session 3 exactly: you write a passing module, add a test, run sanity, and get failures on your *test* code. The two most common surprises:
- an **unused import** (e.g. `import pytest` you never reference)
- **`_`** as a throwaway loop variable → pylint `disallowed-name` (`for _ in range(2):` fails; use `for attempt in range(2):`)

Both came up while building a real collection with this same harness pattern, so it's a real-world callout rather than a hypothetical.

## Scope

Docs only — one slide in `slides/session-3.md` and one row in `GLOSSARY.md`. No code, no toolchain changes.

> Note: intentionally *not* including the `ansible.module_utils.six` / `ansible-bad-import-from` gotcha — it only fires on the devel pylint and presumes a py2/3-compat import a beginner won't reach for, so it'd be noise for this audience.

author: michaellubega
body: ## Problem The dashboard stats (present today, absent today, active lists, live sessions, etc.) were inaccurate and kept changing visibly, making the app look unready. ## Root Causes Identified | Cause | Effect | |---|---| | `unawaited(bootstrapLoadIfNeeded())` fires after dashboard already painted from local cache | Numbers jump 1–3 seconds after opening | | 45-second periodic full re-fetch (`syncStaffAttendanceForeground`) | Numbers briefly drop/change every 45 s while store is repopulated | | `prefetchActiveListDetails` lazy-loads per-list records in background | Present/absent counts grow incrementally as each list loads | | Live Firestore listeners flush into same store | Each new check-in triggers a full repaint from partially-loaded store | | `warmFromLocalSnapshot` (disk) runs concurrently with Firestore fetch | Disk data can land after Firestore data and overwrite fresher values | ## Fixes ### 1. Stable metrics cache (`_stableMetrics`) Both `DashboardScreen` and `LecturerDashboardScreen` now maintain a `_stableMetrics` field that latches the last *meaningful* computed value. The displayed numbers are only replaced when: - The new computation has non-empty lists (store is populated), **or** - A foreground refresh just completed (not a background poll) This prevents the UI from showing zeros or decremented counts while the store is mid-repopulation. ### 2. Background poll interval 45 s → 3 minutes The `_staffAttendanceRefreshInterval` was 45 seconds. Firestore **realtime listeners** already push record changes immediately — the periodic poll only catches structural list changes (new list published, etc.) which don't need sub-minute latency. Raising to 3 minutes eliminates most of the churn with no functional regression. ### 3. Comments clarify unawaited intent Added inline comments explaining why the unawaited bootstrap path exists — to avoid blocking the UI — so future developers don't accidentally await it and introduce a loading spinner.

author: artokun
body:
Found while driving #1783 to a terminal state.

**The gap.** `release/0.52.7` was cut at `aa3efcb` (11:04Z), before #1784 merged
to main at 11:27Z. GitHub squash-merged the version bump *on top of* #1784, so
the tag `v0.52.7` (`9d8827a`) does contain the fix — confirmed in the published
artifact, where `package/dist/orchestrator/panel-tools.js:7077` carries the
discriminator form:

```js
(isFencedActiveWorkflowMutator(cmd) &&
    !isCapabilityRefusal(err) &&
    !isNoTrustedIdentityRefusal(err))
```

The changelog entry could not have known: `gen-changelog` ran during `npm version`
on a branch where `4037ad6` did not yet exist.

**Why it will not self-correct.** `describe --tags` makes the next release's range
`v0.52.7..HEAD`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4037ad6 v0.52.7` is true — so
`4037ad6` is excluded from that range and from every later one. The fix would stay
absent from the record permanently.

Docs only. No source or test change.

author: shaft3796
body:
Bumps the fork iteration so the operator has a named, buildable version carrying tonight's work.

`.conv/fork-release`: `5` → `6`. `.conv/upstream-base` is untouched (`v1.18.4`), so the composed
version becomes **`1.18.4-conv.6`** — confirmed by running `script/conv-version.sh` in this branch,
which prints exactly `1.18.4-conv.6`.

## What `conv.6` contains that `conv.5` did not

| PR | Change |
|---|---|
| #35 | `docs/BUILDING.md` — the verified one-command build recipe for this fork |
| #36 | provider and model shown on every subagent title line and footer, so cross-provider delegation is visible |
| #37 | `providers list` reconciles stored credentials against the live registry and names any credential that produced no provider, with the reason |
| #38 | a background subagent's result is rendered in the parent transcript, and a failed background child no longer renders as a success |
| #39 | the task-management tools are scoped to the caller's own subtree and then offered at any depth, so a middle subagent can see and stop its own children |
| #40 | subagents dispatched from a **root** session run in the background by default; transitive subtree tracking; a `subagent_background` policy knob; a background child can no longer hang on a permission prompt |

## The one behaviour change an operator will notice immediately

Delegating from a top-level conversation now returns the prompt in about a second with a
"background task started" acknowledgement, instead of blocking on a spinner until the child
finishes. The conversation resumes on its own when the child's result arrives.

Nothing changes for nested dispatches — the flip is root-scoped by a predicate that structurally
cannot be true for a subagent session.

**To turn it all off, no rebuild required:** set `"subagent_background": "caller"` in the config.

## Verification

- `script/conv-version.sh` in this branch prints `1.18.4-conv.6`.
- The `P0: binary self-reports the fork version SSOT` conformance job builds with `OPENCODE_VERSION`
  deliberately unset and asserts the built binary reports the composed string, so this bump is
  checked against a real binary rather than against the file it edits.
- Single-file, single-character change; revert is one commit.

## Summary

Add missing `@is_admin_or_owner_required` and `@rbac_permission_required(RBACResourceScope.WORKSPACE, RBACPermission.CREDENTIAL_MANAGE, resource_required=False)` decorators to the GET endpoint:

The `POST` and `DELETE` handlers of `ToolOAuthCustomClient` already enforce that only workspace admins/owners or members with the `CREDENTIAL_MANAGE` RBAC permission can manage OAuth custom clients. author: konard
body:
Closes #227. Advances #228 (see the scope note — it is **not** closed by this PR).

## #227 — `with gemini` failed every run

The issue reports that `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` is not read by the client. **Measuring it directly says otherwise**, and the real cause is narrower: the CLI resolves settings as `<home>/.gemini/settings.json`, where `<home>` is `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` if set and `$HOME` otherwise. The router pointed the variable at the `.gemini` directory itself, so the CLI searched `<root>/.gemini/.gemini/`, found nothing, and fell back to the user's personal settings.

Isolating the two cases settles it — same file, same flags, only the variable differs:

```
GEMINI_CLI_HOME=$D          → runs (fails later on the stub endpoint)
GEMINI_CLI_HOME=$D/.gemini  → Invalid auth method selected.
```

That distinction matters for the fix: had I taken the issue's diagnosis at face value and only overridden `HOME` while leaving `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` pointing at `.gemini`, the bug would have survived — which is exactly what happened on my first attempt. **Verified end to end against the real binary**, which is how I caught it:

```
$ router with gemini --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --non-interactive "Ответь ровно одним словом: тест"
тест
```

Two smaller fixes in the same path, both from the issue:

- the settings write no longer uses `create_new`, which silently deferred to a pre-existing file — with the home fix that becomes load-bearing, since an inherited `oauth-personal` would otherwise survive into the isolated run;
- `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE` is set, because with auth fixed the next wall is the trusted-directory prompt, which a `--non-interactive` run cannot answer.

Tests: the environment names the root for both variables; a conflicting pre-existing file is replaced; the selected auth type is pinned; and an end-to-end preparation test asserts the file exists *at the path the CLI reads*. Verified to fail on the old behaviour.

## #228 — Cursor: documented, not implemented

**I am not closing this issue, and I did not ship a partial adapter.** Two findings from measuring the installed `cursor-agent 2025.08.27-24c29c1`:

**The issue's premise is wrong, in a way that helps.** It attributes the zero-requests symptom to HTTP/2 ignoring proxy variables, and prescribes a `NODE_OPTIONS` shim. In fact `CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT` *is* read — and then overridden, because an undocumented `-e, --endpoint <url>` option carries a default that is always present. Passing that flag captures plaintext Connect-RPC directly, no shim involved. That removes the first wall the issue warns about, rather than working around it.

**But there is a prerequisite outside the code.** This machine's Cursor credential is expired: `cursor-agent status` drops into an interactive login, and a `--print` run issues no requests at all. I could not capture the chat protobuf, so I could not write — let alone exercise — an adapter. Shipping one that cannot be run would be worse than shipping none.

So `cli-cursor.md` now records what was measured: the flags (`--endpoint`, `--repo-endpoint`, `--insecure`, `--http-version`), the bootstrap RPCs a capture reveals, that the chat turn needs an **h2c** server rather than a TLS proxy or a CA, that `/auth/exchange_user_api_key` is itself redirected so a local adapter can mint the token it accepts, and the login prerequisite. The second prior-art project from the issue is cited with a note on why its approach targets a different build.

That is the honest state: the checklist is unchanged, the first wall is gone, and the remaining unknown — the chat message schema — is named rather than estimated.

## Verification
901 tests pass, exit code 0. `cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, CI's exact rustdoc command, and the file-size check are clean.

## Was
Bei „Google Ads Landingpage" stand am Mengen-Stepper und im Vertrag „monatlich" — das ist der **Einheiten-Label-Wert** (`unit_label`) dieses Moduls im Katalog, kein Code-Text. Es geht dort um die einmalige **Anzahl** gebauter Landingpages, nichts Monatliches.

Der Code erzwang bei leerem Label bisher „Einheiten" bzw. zeigte das (falsche) Label. Jetzt:
- `rowToModuleDef`: leeres/kein `unit_label` bleibt leer (kein erzwungenes „Einheiten").
- Baukasten-Stepper: ohne Label → **„Anzahl:"** statt eines leeren Labels.
- Vertrag: ohne Label → **„Anzahl: N"** statt „N <label>".

So lässt sich das irreführende „monatlich" entfernen und nur die reine Anzahl anzeigen.

## Datenpflege nötig
Das „monatlich" steht als `unit_label` beim Modul in der DB. Nach diesem Deploy einmal leeren (oder auf „Landingpages" setzen) – SQL wird separat geliefert.

## Test
- `tsc --noEmit` sauber · Modul-Tests grün · `next build` erfolgreich

## Summary
- Steepened the level ramp so level 10 lands around where level 60 used to sit (board size and trail length), and growth keeps climbing past that instead of plateauing (up to ~86×109 by level 120).
- Fixed a class of "obviously easy" arrows: exit direction is now chosen from a shuffled order instead of always the nearest wall, and trail growth is now a backtracking walk (tracks the longest path found) instead of a plain greedy walk that gave up at the first dead end — that greedy behavior was quietly flooding boards with short, trivial 2-cell arrows. A level-scaling minimum trail length further reduces short arrows.
- Fixed incomplete board coverage: a fill pass now places single-cell arrows in leftover empty cells after the main placement loop, closing most previous gaps (boards now hit ~80-98% coverage instead of leaving visible holes).

author: zbindendaniel
body:
## Summary

When search is skipped (via reviewer request), the extraction pipeline now presents stored search results as authoritative evidence rather than rendering them as an empty context. Previously, the reuse path collapsed to "Current search context: None." when persisted sources lacked descriptions, even though real evidence existed.

## Changes

- **`item-flow-search.ts`**: When `shouldSearch` is false and stored sources exist, format them using the shared `formatSourcesForRetry` utility (numbered Title/URL/Description blocks) instead of joining only descriptions/content. This ensures sources without descriptions still contribute their title and URL, and the context block is never empty when sources exist.

- **`item-flow-extraction.ts`**: When search is skipped and the search context is non-empty, relabel the context block from "Current search context:" to "Previously collected search results (search skipped — extract from these; do not assume no evidence):" so the model treats reused sources as authoritative rather than assuming no evidence exists.

- **`item-flow-search.test.ts`**: Added test case verifying that skip-search with stored sources (including description-less ones) produces a single non-empty context containing titles, URLs, and descriptions.

- **Documentation**: Updated `docs/detailed/item-flow.md` and `docs/changelogs/agentic.md` to explain the skip-search behavior and the reuse of collected results.

## Implementation Details

- Reused the existing `formatSourcesForRetry` formatter (already used by the in-cycle retry path) to maintain a single attribution format for "here are the sources" whether fresh-retry or reused-skip.
- No schema or flow-shape change: still one `SearchContext` pushed with the same `sources` array; only its `text` rendering and extraction label changed.
- The label switch is guarded on `singleContextText` being non-empty, so genuinely empty contexts still render "Current search context: None."
- The persisted `LastSearchLinksJson` shape (`{url, title?, description?}`) frequently carries no description (Tavily returned title+url without a snippet); the formatter now handles this gracefully by always emitting title + URL and "Description: (none)" when absent.

author: savvaniss
body:
Wave 2 of the apex consolidation. `exchange` moves to `subdomain: ''` +
`basePath: '/exchange'`, keeping `devPort` 5194 and `viewsAnyNetwork`.

**Stacked on micro-ui#25** (wave 1) — that PR merges first.

### Wave 2 is `exchange` alone, and the plan said otherwise

It was paired with `developers` on the test "no `/v1` router of its own —
developers is docs". `developers` is not docs: `cf-api-developers` routes `/v1`
to `cf-svc-devplatform`, 35 handlers.

Counting APIs by the router's **upstream** instead, twelve of the fourteen moving
surfaces have one on their own hostname; only `exchange` joins `journal`. And
`foresight` — which answers `/me`, `/markets`, `/ideas` and three more
**unversioned at the root** — is read as having *no* API by a `/v1` test, when it
is the hardest surface in the estate to move.

### A switcher home is an address, not a subdomain

`surfaces.test.ts` asserted `s.subdomain.length > 0` under the name "holds no
surface that is in the switcher and has no home". The switcher navigates to
`cloudsforgeHosts()[key]`, which is origin + `basePath ?? ''` — so **either half
answers the question**. The subdomain form was an exact proxy while every
switcher entry owned a hostname.

Same shape as wave 1's `viewsAnyNetwork` reversal, on a different invariant.
Wave 1 missed it only because `journal` is `inSwitcher: false`.

The replacement checks both halves, and the second could not have been written
before: **two switcher entries resolving to one address** strands a reader who
picks Forge Exchange on the marketing site, and that becomes possible for the
first time now that more than one surface can live on the apex. Both halves
negative-tested.

430 pass, 0 fail. Not merged, not deployed.

author: ahilles107
body:
## Summary

Consolidating instructions is a migration, not a copy. The wizard used to offer a "keep originals"
choice, so a run could end with the same guidance in two places and nothing saying which one wins.
Consolidation now always archives the sources it absorbed, and `undo` restores them.

### Wizard

- Drop `archiveOriginals` from `InstructionScopeSelection` (`packages/cli/src/setup/types.ts`) and
  the question that set it, along with its stage in the Instructions chain.
- The chain sub-row loses the now-empty `Files` tab, and back-navigation lands on the last
  *applicable* form instead — Project Duplicates when a duplicate review applies, otherwise Project
  Sources, otherwise the Global action.

### Planner split

`instruction-planner.ts` was doing three jobs; it now delegates two:

- `instruction-merge.ts` — composes the consolidated target. Convergent by construction: the
  existing target is carried through verbatim as the base, and a source whose provenance heading is
  already in that base is skipped, so a source restored from an archive is not appended twice.
- `instruction-links.ts` — wires managed applications to the scope targets that survived planning.

### Divergence is not archived

A source whose heading is already in the target but whose content has since changed contributed
nothing to this merge, so archiving it would destroy the only copy of what it now says. It stays on
disk and the run names it under _Steps to take yourself_.

### Copy

The consolidate option description, the `setup --help` footer, `README.md`, and `docs/cli-ux.md`
all state that consolidating moves files and that `undo` restores them — `--yes` can take the
consolidate default on a machine with no shared file yet, so the screens have to say it up front.

## Linear

USE-1396

## Test plan

- [x] All CI checks pass (`pnpm verify`: build, lint, typecheck, format:check, knip, fallow, 1668 tests)
- [ ] `aura setup` on a machine with scattered instruction files: confirm the plan lists every move, then `aura undo` restores them
- [ ] Re-run `aura setup` after an `undo` and confirm sources are not appended twice
- [ ] Edit an already-merged source, re-run setup, and confirm it is listed under _Steps to take yourself_ rather than archived
- [ ] Back-navigate out of Snippets and confirm it lands on Project Duplicates / Sources, not a Files stage

## Summary

- compose application components as native Cordis/DSH plugin registrations
- add a native DSH entry point for Python using `defineTool()` and canonical structured output
- keep the Python executor and formatter independent from both the legacy and DSH tool surfaces
- project DSH tool presentation metadata into the current timeline summary and workspace-change fields

- web and native workers do not switch their default session runtime in this PR

author: hollujay
body:
## Summary

Closes #931.

Implements a consistent shutdown/drain protocol for queue workers, per
the issue's implementation requirements, and applies it to every worker
named in the issue: the webhook dispatcher, digest queue, indexer, and
recurring keeper.

## What changed

**`backend/src/services/workerLifecycle.js`** — new `createDrainController(name, { gracePeriodMs })`:
- States: `running -> draining -> drained`.
- `trackJob(fn)` wraps a unit of work so the controller knows the
  current in-flight count.
- `beginDrain()` stops treating the worker as running, waits up to
  `gracePeriodMs` (default 30s, `WORKER_DRAIN_GRACE_MS`) for in-flight
  work to finish, then marks the worker drained — even if a job never
  finishes, so a stuck job can't block shutdown forever. The pod-level
  termination grace / `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` must stay ≥ this value,
  same coupling the existing readiness doc already calls out for other
  timeouts.
- `getWorkerDrainStates()` — a snapshot of every registered worker's
  state + in-flight count, now surfaced on `GET /api/readyz` as
  `checks.workers` for operators watching a rolling deploy.

**`backend/src/services/metrics.js`** — new `worker_draining{worker}`
Prometheus gauge (1 while draining, 0 otherwise).

**Applied to each worker:**
- `recurringKeeper.js` — **fixes a real bug**: `stop()` previously
  cleared the interval and returned immediately, even while a keeper
  cycle triggered by that interval (or the initial on-start cycle) was
  still mid-flight submitting an on-chain transaction. `stop()` now
  waits for that cycle to finish (bounded by the grace period).
- `webhookQueue.js` / `digestQueue.js` — wrap the pg-boss job handler
  with `trackJob()` and mark drain state around pg-boss's own
  `graceful: true` stop (which already stops claiming and waits for
  active handlers), so their state is visible through the same
  mechanism as every other worker rather than being pg-boss-internal
  and opaque.
- `indexerService.js` — wraps per-operation processing so `stop()`
  closes the SSE stream (stops claiming new operations) and then waits
  for an in-flight donation write to finish before flushing the
  donation batcher.

**`backend/src/routes/readiness.js`** — surfaces `checks.workers` from
`getWorkerDrainStates()`. Informational: the existing `isShuttingDown()`
check already fails readiness for the whole process during shutdown;
this adds per-worker visibility on top of that for operators.

## What I did not do

This is a single Node process running HTTP + all workers together —
there's no separate per-worker process to give its own readiness
*endpoint* to (the issue's "readiness probe endpoint per worker" reads
as written for a multi-process deployment). I surfaced per-worker drain
state on the existing shared `/api/readyz` instead, which is the
closest equivalent in this codebase's actual topology; happy to split
this differently if the maintainers deploy workers as separate
processes elsewhere.

I didn't touch `PDB`/`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` orchestration config — no
Kubernetes manifests or PDB definitions exist in this repo tree.

No "outbox dispatcher" exists in this codebase under that or any
similar name, so there was nothing to wire up there.

## Test plan

- [x] `workerLifecycle.test.js` — unit tests for the drain state
      machine: idle vs. in-flight `beginDrain()`, `trackJob` accounting
      (including on job failure), grace-period force-drain via fake
      timers, and `getWorkerDrainStates()`.
- [x] `recurringKeeper.test.js` (new) — SIGTERM-mid-job simulation:
      `stop()` blocks while a cycle is in flight and only resolves once
      it finishes; a second test confirms the grace-period force-drain
      path when a cycle never finishes; a third covers the no-op case
      (`stop()` with nothing in flight).
- [x] `webhookQueue.test.js`, `digestQueue.test.js` — unaffected,
      still passing.
- [x] `readiness.test.js`, `metrics.test.js` — unaffected, still
      passing; confirmed `checks.workers` appears correctly in a live
      readiness response.
- [x] Full backend suite: `109` suites, `1175` tests — same 6 failures
      before and after this change, all pre-existing `testcontainers`
      integration tests that need a real Docker/Postgres container
      unavailable in this environment (confirmed via `beforeAll`
      timeout on container startup, unrelated to any file this PR
      touches).

## Compatibility

No job semantics change for queued items. `webhookQueue` / `digestQueue`
retry, DLQ, and dedup behavior is untouched — this PR only adds
observability and waits around the *existing* stop paths. The one
behavioral change is `recurringKeeper.stop()` now actually waiting
(bounded) instead of returning early, which is the bug fix.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added graceful shutdown tracking for background workers, including in-flight jobs and configurable grace periods.
  - Readiness reporting now includes each worker’s drain state.
  - Added worker-draining metrics for monitoring shutdown progress.
  - Recurring tasks now use locking to prevent overlapping cycles.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved shutdown handling for digest, webhook, indexing, and recurring workers.
  - Ensured active processing completes before associated resources close.

author: sunholo-voight-kampff
body:
Consumes Mark's directive on #745 (`D-19 : B`, 2026-08-19T10:58:40Z), which outranks the queue.
**D-19 → RESOLVED; the decision ledger now has zero OPEN rows.**

The ruling's own words set the deliverable — *"a much larger sprint needing decomposition first"* —
so this is a roadmap, not an implementation (Gate 3's multi-week rule).

## Deliverable
`design_docs/planned/m-list-cons-cells-decomposition.md` — 505 lines, 20 first-party verification
rows, **8 sprint-sized pieces / 15.5–21.5 person-days**, queued individually. `LC-1` (representation
spike) runs first and carries an explicit **kill criterion**.

⚠ **Letter collision:** the superseded `m-list-cons-quadratic.md` labels its own options A–D, and
its **Option A** is what this ruling's **B** selects, while its **Option B** (the arena) is declined.

## Key find — a count I certified was right about the repo, wrong about the question
I handed the designer `902` `.Elements` refs / `386` `ListValue{` constructions under a
VERIFIED-BY-ME label. Both reproduce exactly at HEAD. The **sentence** was false: `Elements` is a
field name owned by **22 struct types** across `internal/{ast,core,eval,typedast,types}`, so those
are contaminated upper bounds, not a `ListValue` blast radius. Rule 3b(ix) — a count is only true
inside the scope it was taken in, and re-deriving it *reproduces the number and confirms the error*.
Consequence: LC-2's first deliverable is a `go/analysis` census, and every migration AC is
denominated in the analyzer's count, not grep's.

## Quorum round 1 — BLOCKED, 2-of-2, $0.0884
`absent_reviewers` **empty**, both `present=true` — a genuine block, not an N−1 degrade.
- **`gpt5-6-sol`** (correct, not disputable): deleting `ListValue.Elements` does **not** give
  compiler-enforced immutability — Go has no immutable fields, and the owning package is
  `internal/eval`, which is also the evaluator. The `listrep` analyzer is **retained, not retired**.
- **`gemini-3-1-pro`**: `LC-3c` was assigned escape sites owned by `LC-3a`/`LC-3b`, guaranteeing
  merge conflicts across the parallel lanes.

Both carry verbatim reviewer-authored fixes; **neither disputes the design direction**. Quoted in
full in the doc, because the artifacts are untracked (`.gitignore:82`).

## Gate 5 — one skill edit: Standing rule 8, `PARKED-ON-LANE`
Two consecutive first-party frictions (228, 229). The loop had **one** park state for two different
blockers: judgment and capacity. They have opposite resume conditions, and filing a capacity park as
`needs-human-review` manufactures a decision the human does not have. The new state must name the
role, the lane's refusal **with its rc**, and when the lane returns — a predicate the next iteration
*runs* rather than a narrative it reconstructs.

The owed revision is parked exactly that way: `codex:gpt-5.6-sol` probed **rc=1** (quota, resets
**2026-08-20 05:34**), gemini/managed_agents is read-only under `CapRemoteSandbox`, and Fable's
one-run diet was spent on the create. **No human judgment is owed.**

## Gates
Docs-only change. Charter rotation asserted: `after == before + 2 − 2×moved` held exactly
(2383 → 2383), stamp count 3, and the rotated-out iteration-226 stamp was confirmed **present in the
archive** with its control firing. Ledger re-validated by `scripts/mission_decisions.sh --check`
(21 rows, 0 OPEN). Green on darwin/arm64; CI legs unrun locally.

author: zuizui0223
body:
## Purpose
Correct the Tier-B1 topology validation from PR #186 before drawing a scientific conclusion from its failure.

## Problem found
PR #186 reused the richness sampling-design layer for topology. Doré's published source code uses different mandatory controls for each topology response:
- Connectance: `ln_sptot + ln_SE + ln_ATS + Sampling_type`
- Li: `ln_pl + ln_SE + ln_ATS + Sampling_type`
- Lp: `ln_ins + ln_SE + ln_ATS + Sampling_type`

Doré also runs the topology models on `aggreg.webs_full_str_no_polar.RData`, not the unfiltered aggregate table.

## Correction
- read the source-native structure-filtered non-polar RDS;
- require and preserve source-native `ln_sptot`, `ln_pl`, `ln_ins`, `ln_SE`, `ln_ATS` rather than reconstructing them;
- use the response-specific source controls above in all sampling-only/geography/ABM held-out comparisons;
- retain the exact same frozen systems, GIFT geography, distance-ECDF primary mapping, geography-PC1 sensitivity and saturation envelope.

## Boundary
This correction supersedes the *measurement-layer interpretation* of PR #186. The old result remains in history but must not be used as evidence that isolation alone fails for topology until this corrected run is evaluated. No system or model setting is changed based on the old failure.

author: hegelstad
body:
## Problem

The Grok Build harness (and any harness using the shared PTY idle detector) periodically crash-looped: it would ack a task then spam `state_change: active` ~4×/sec for hours, ballooning `sessions/<agent>/events.jsonl` to ~100MB until the process was OOM-killed and auto-restarted straight back into the same loop, producing zero useful work.

## Root cause

`internal/session/agent/shared/ptycollector` called `send(StateActive)` on **every** output signal, with no dedup. A streaming CLI child writes output many times a second, so each write became another `active` state update → another `EventStateChange` appended to the event log.

## Fix

- Track the last emitted state in the collector's run loop; emit only on genuine `idle<->active` transitions. Repeated output while already active just defers the idle timer.
- Route `SignalInterrupt` through the run loop (new `interruptCh`) so its forced-idle stays consistent with the tracked state and is a no-op when already idle (previously it wrote to the state channel from the caller goroutine, bypassing tracking).

## Tests

`go test -race ./internal/session/agent/shared/ptycollector/` passes. Added:
- `TestCollector_NoDuplicateActiveOnBurst` — a 50-output burst yields exactly one `active` transition then the `idle` edge (the regression test).
- `TestCollector_InterruptForcesIdle` — interrupt forces `active->idle` once, redundant interrupt is a no-op.
- Rewrote `TestCollector_ResetTimerOnOutput`, which previously asserted the buggy re-emit-on-every-output behavior.

author: degrassiaaron
body:
Due fette di **#314** (CP 14.7): il Reaction Profile smette di essere un dato senza lettori e diventa una
scelta che si gioca. La issue **resta aperta** — vedi *Cosa NON chiude*.

## Fetta 3 — il profilo decide in partita (D-047)

`BraceAllowedResponses` aveva **zero** chiamanti fuori dai test e `ARTUnit::ReactionProfileId` era
trasportato e mai letto: un dato con produttore e senza consumatore, che è la forma esatta del difetto che
[#583](https://github.com/DegrassiAaron/refactor-tactics-main/issues/583) chiama per nome. Ora il ramo
`Status.Braced` di `RTTurnManager_Blast.cpp` costruisce l'opportunity dal profilo dell'unità e chiede la
decisione con la **stessa** `AskReactionDecision` dell'Overwatch, non con una macchina parallela.

Col profilo base non cambia niente, ed è una proprietà e non una fortuna: una sola risposta,
`RequiresDecisionBoundary` falso, `HoldImmediate` senza interrogare nessuno. La voce di DoD «col profilo base
nessun boundary si apre» è vera **per costruzione**, non per un `if` che la protegge.

### `SIDESTEP` = `SelfReposition(1)` — `D-176`

Non è una primitiva nuova: è quella che D-093 ha creato perché nessun effetto sapeva spostare *chi reagisce*,
e che `Reaction.EmergencyDash` e `Reaction.HazardEscape` già portano. Vincolata da `BAS-4`, che dichiara
questo profilo «risponde al **Forced Movement**» nella forma `Reposition 1`.

⚠️ **Conseguenza dichiarata invece che scoperta**: la direzione non è un parametro, quindi contro una spinta
di **1** l'esito coincide con il subirla; la scelta vera esiste contro le spinte di **2** (`Weapon.Impact`,
loadout di default di Phase). L'alternativa perpendicolare è stata **scartata**: avrebbe aperto due
sotto-decisioni — quale perpendicolare, e cosa vale se sono entrambe illegali — per chiuderne una.

⚠️ **La voce canonica di `D-176` non è nel Decision Log**, che è `integration_only` in questo batch. L'ID è
riservato con `scripts/rt_shared_id.py`; il contenuto autorevole è `spec-reaction-clash-e14.md` §2.5-bis, e
**nessun link `D-176` punta al Decision Log** — sarebbe un rinvio a vuoto che non fa cadere nessun gate.

### Due profili su tre restano dichiarati e non eseguibili

`Profile.Grounding` e `Profile.Glance` sono contenuto **deciso** da D-132 e non hanno effetti, perché «Charge
del `Grounding`» e «ampiezza della deviazione» sono dichiarate **aperte** dalla spec §2.5. Il catalogo
continua a dichiarare `2/2/3` (D-132 non si muove); il resolver interroga `BraceExecutableResponses`, che dà
**1/2/1**. La distanza è misurata da `Reactions.Brace.DeclaredIsNotYetExecutable`, scritto per **diventare
rosso** quando una delle due voci si chiude.

### La scelta sicura non è la stringa `HOLD`

`Timeout → HOLD` di ADR-0004 §3 è una regola sul *comportamento*, non sul token: il `Brace` chiama la propria
`Hold Ground`, e per lui `HOLD` non è nemmeno legale. Con la vecchia costante ognuno dei **sei** ripieghi di
`AskReactionDecision` avrebbe applicato una risposta che il resolver stesso considera illegale.
`SafeResponse` la deriva dall'opportunity, e **l'ordine dei due rami è la regola**: nell'Overwatch `HOLD` sta
in *coda*, quindi «prendi la prima» farebbe **sparare** una finestra scaduta. Per l'Overwatch nessun esito
cambia.

## Fetta 4 — lo scenario di D-047 diventa verde

`Spec.Brace.ProfileChangesResponse` passa da `BLOCKED` a **PASS (7/7)**, e `ReactionProfile` scende fra le
capability disponibili. Le tre condizioni che la sua riga prescriveva sono soddisfatte **tutte e tre e nello
stesso commit** — separarle sarebbe stato il «rosso a giorni alterni» che la fase A registra: runtime, dati
per rispondere, T2 pieno.

### Formato scenario **v3**, e il bump è argomentato

Il cambiamento è solo **espansivo**: nessun file `version: 2` valido oggi cambia significato. Si bumpa lo
stesso per il verso che conta — un file con `respond: "SIDESTEP"` dichiarato `version: 2` verrebbe
**accettato** da una build a `SupportedVersion = 2` e poi rifiutato con «risposta sconosciuta», un messaggio
che accusa il *file* mentre il difetto è la *build*. Il test della versione tiene ora il caso negativo a
`SupportedVersion + 1`, così non invecchia al prossimo bump.

Il vocabolario si **chiede al catalogo** (`AllReactionProfileResponses`), non si riscrive nel loader: una
seconda lista divergerebbe al primo profilo aggiunto, e a divergere sarebbe il *gate*.

### Tre cose corrette dal rosso, non dalla lettura

| Scoperta | Come |
|---|---|
| `decisions` era validata in **due** posti | Ne ho aggiornato uno; il corpus è diventato rosso col messaggio della copia vecchia. Estratta in `ValidateDecisionForm`, chiamata da entrambi |
| `Action.Push` **non è nel kit di nessun eroe** | «'V1' non possiede l'abilità». Sostituita con `Hero.Phase.PressureJet`, la fixture del gemello `GuardAndBraceOnMixedHit` |
| Due turni erano **impossibili** | `Action.Brace` dura 1 turno e ha cooldown 1: al T2 lo stato è scaduto e l'azione non è ridichiarabile. Turno unico |

## Verifica

**Suite completa: 1062 avviati · 1062 `Success` · 0 falliti**, `EXIT CODE: 0`. Non un filtro.

**Sei mutazioni**, una per volta, ognuna caduta sul test atteso e ripristinate byte per byte (`diff` contro
un backup preso prima):

| # | Mutazione | Cade |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `BraceExecutableResponses` → `BraceAllowedResponses` nel resolver | «nessuna finestra per un profilo senza effetti dichiarati» |
| 2 | ramo `HOLD` rimosso da `SafeResponse` | un test **preesistente**: «lo scadere risponde HOLD, ma era `FIRE:3`» |
| 3 | `EscapeSteps = 0` | «con `SIDESTEP` il difensore lascia la cella» |
| 4 | `Phase->ReactionProfileId = NAME_None` | «decisione dichiarata per 'R1' e mai consumata» |
| 5 | ramo delle risposte di profilo spento nella session | il bersaglio vuoto non si risolve |
| 6 | atteso di R1 uguale a quello di B1 | `FAIL (difetto del GIOCO) — atteso (0,3), ottenuto (1,3)` |

⚠️ La **6** è stata rieseguita: la prima volta girava ancora il binario della 5, perché avevo ripristinato il
sorgente senza ricompilare. Un ripristino non è un rebuild.

**Gate**: naming ✅ · tables ✅ · symbols ✅ · capability-owners ✅ · `rt_shared_id check` ✅ (170 ID) ·
`audit-refs` ✅ (28 ref, nessuna collisione).

⚠️ **`check-docs-links.py` è ROSSO (exit 1) e NON per causa di questo lavoro**: i quattro findings sono in
`docs/archive/src/*` e `docs/roadmap/roadmap-post-v0.1.md`, nessuno nel write-set di questo branch
(`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`). È una regressione già presente su `main`, verosimilmente dello
svuotamento di `docs/src`. Registrata, non riparata: quei file sono di altri.

## Due sessioni in parallelo su #314, e i due merge che ne sono usciti

Mentre queste fette giravano, `feat/314-reaction-profile-e-clash` ha mergiato **tre** PR (#1210, #1211,
#1216) implementando il Clash runtime — la fetta che questo lavoro aveva **scartato dichiarandolo nel batch
prima di cominciare**. Non è una duplicazione: le due metà sono complementari (qui il cablaggio di D-047, là
la macchina di D-048). Ma i file coincidevano.

Il **primo** merge ha avuto un conflitto su `RTReactionOpportunityTypes.cpp`, puramente posizionale: entrambe
le sessioni avevano inserito codice dopo `CompareGrammarIntents`. ⚠️ Il merge automatico aveva accoppiato la
**loro** firma di `DecisionOnTimeout` col **mio** corpo di `SafeResponse` — avrebbe compilato e significato
un'altra cosa. Ricostruito a mano leggendo le due versioni, niente scartato. Misurato invece che assunto: su
`main` `SafeResponse` non esisteva.

Il **secondo** merge è stato pulito, ma «pulito» non è «valido»: verificato ricompilando e rigirando la suite
intera, non ispezionando i conflitti.

## Cosa questa PR NON chiude — #314 resta OPEN

- **`ReactionClash` è tuttora indisponibile.** Le sue funzioni pure esistono — `ResolveContestedBoundary`,
  `MakeClashLogEntries`, arrivate dalle PR sopra — e **nessun punto del resolver le chiama**: un turno che la
  chiedesse non troverebbe niente da eseguire. Gli otto `Spec.Clash.*` restano `BLOCKED`.

author: ahmadalikaram89-pixel
body:
Screenshots from an installed iOS PWA showed the app scaled and shifted sideways, with the header cut off at both edges. Two separate causes:

**Pinch and double-tap zoom.** There's nothing here for zoom to reveal — one column, no maps or diagrams — but it does leave the layout offset, and squaring it back up by hand is fiddly. `maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no` turns it off; `touch-action: manipulation` on `body` covers double-tap, which the viewport meta doesn't.

**iOS auto-zoom on focus** — the bigger of the two. iOS zooms the page in whenever a focused field's text is under 16px, and leaves it zoomed afterwards. Fields ranged from 14px to 15px, so simply tapping a field shifted the app. Every text field is now at least 16px:

- one rule in `theme.css` (`input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]), textarea, select`), whose specificity clears the component-level declarations — those are removed rather than left contradicting it;
- the two inline-styled fields (the auth inputs and the rating textarea) carry the same number themselves, since inline styles outrank any stylesheet.

That second half also holds in Safari-the-browser, which ignores `user-scalable=no` — only the installed PWA honours it.

**Trade-off:** manual pinch-zoom is gone. OS-level zoom (iOS Display Zoom / text size) is unaffected, and the fields read slightly larger than before.

**Verification**

`tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean. Driven in Chromium at 390×844 @2x across the auth, calendar (form open), search, todo and settings screens: no field computes under 16px, `document.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth === 0` on every screen, `getComputedStyle(body).touchAction === 'manipulation'`, viewport meta as intended in `dist/index.html`, no console or page errors.

author: ptz000
body:
…eration

nextjs:create mixed path.posix.* with the platform separator, which breaks factory generation on Windows.

 componentDir is built with path.join (platform separator) but is passed to
   path.posix.relative against the POSIX factoryKey. On Windows
   path.posix.relative('component', 'component\block') treats the backslash
   path as a single segment and returns '../component\block', so the emitted
   import is:

     import BlockComponent from './../component\block';

   '\b' is a backspace escape, so the specifier resolves to
   './../componen<U+0008>lock' and the bundler reports
   "Can't resolve './../componenlock'".

author: ranjith36963
body:
## ⚠️ RED IS THE INTENDED RESULT OF THIS PR. Do not "fix" the red.

`python scripts/lane.py --drill` went from **64/64, exit 0** to **47/66, exit 1**.
That is the point. It is the first time this drill has told the truth. It goes green
again only after `path_matches` is fixed (next PR) — not before.

**Nothing in CI runs `lane.py` today**, so no existing job turns red because of this.
Measured: the whole tree holds exactly one non-self reference to it —
`.github/merge-policy.yml:211`, which merely lists it as owner-owned.

```
$ grep -rn "lane\.py" --include=*.yml --include=*.py --include=*.sh --include=*.md . | grep -v "^./scripts/lane.py"
./.github/merge-policy.yml:211:      - "scripts/lane.py"
```

---

## What was wrong

`scripts/lane.py:364-365` asserted this is False:

```python
pattern.startswith("*.") and "/" not in pattern
```

That is the shape of **the one pattern somebody happened to find** (`*.md`), not the
class the bug belongs to. Plain `README.md` does not start with `*.`, so the drill
printed this line and counted it as a pass:

```
ok   fast lane `harness` has no depth-crossing glob: README.md
```

The sentence is false. `README.md` in the fast lane *does* reach
`docs/product/pillars/README.md`. A guard reporting success about a question it is not
asking is this repo's signature failure — and it had got into the guard built to catch it.

## The mechanism the old comment named — and got wrong

The comment at `:355-361` said *"this repo's matcher lets `*` cross `/`"*. **It does not.**
I compiled it rather than trusting it:

```
$ python -c "from merge_cage import _glob_to_re; rx=_glob_to_re('*.md'); print(rx.pattern, rx.match('docs/a.md'))"
[^/]*\.md\Z None
```

`*` compiles to `[^/]*` and stops at `/`. The real leak is one function lower —
`path_matches` (`scripts/merge_cage.py:195-196`):

```python
if "/" not in pattern:  # a bare name is a basename rule, at any depth
    return bool(rx.match(path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]))
```

After the full-path match fails, **any pattern containing no `/` is re-matched against the
basename, at every depth**. No star is required. So the correct condition is
`"/" not in pattern` — slash-free, star or no star — and the comment now points at
`merge_cage.py:195` instead of at an innocent line.

## The consequence, asserted on behaviour not on a string (rule #21)

Pattern-shape checks are schema-presence. This is the value-presence version — two
documents in the **same directory**, opposite verdicts, decided purely by filename:

| file | lane | auto_merge |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/product/PRD.md` | `product_owner` | `False` ✅ |
| `docs/product/pillars/README.md` | **`harness`** | **`True`** ❌ |

Ten tracked files reach a fast lane *only* through that fallback:
`backend/README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/archive/README.md`,
`docs/harness/fable/README.md`, `docs/product/pillars/README.md`,
`frontend/README.md`, `test-artifacts/README.md`, `frontend/.gitignore`,
`backend/.dockerignore`, `frontend/.dockerignore` — every one `auto_merge=True`.

The new check compares the pair rather than hardcoding a lane, so it stays honest if
`docs/product/**` is later given a lane of its own.

## The 17 patterns the drill now names

All in the `harness` fast lane (the `product` lane has zero slash-free patterns):

`README.md` · `ARCHITECTURE.md` · `CONTRIBUTING.md` · `SECURITY.md` · `STATUS.md` ·
`ENGINES_KANBAN.md` · `LAUNCH_PLAN.md` · `2030.md` · `PLAN-?-*.md` ·
`anthropic-patterns-upgrade.md` · `fable-harness-plan.md` · `scrapingdesccion.md` ·
`.gitignore` · `.gitattributes` · `.dockerignore` · `.coderabbit.yaml` ·
`pyrightconfig.json`

## Base branch — why this is not `--base main`

`scripts/lane.py` **does not exist on `main`** (`git cat-file -e origin/main:scripts/lane.py`
→ *does not exist*). It arrives with #348. A PR based on `main` would therefore show
**192 files changed** and duplicate the whole of #348; based on the cage branch it shows
**1 file changed**. A 192-file diff whose stated purpose is "change one condition in one
drill" is misinformation by construction.

**Cost of that choice, stated plainly: CodeRabbit is disabled for non-`main` base
branches, so this PR gets no automated review.** It is 46 added lines in one function,
most of them comment. Land it with or immediately after #348.

## Verification

- `python scripts/lane.py --drill` → **exit 1**, `47/66`, 19 red lines (17 patterns + 2 behavioural)
- `python -m ruff check scripts/lane.py` → **exit 0**, all checks passed
- `python scripts/lane.py scripts/lane.py` → this PR classifies `harness_owner`, `auto_merge: false` — **you merge it by hand**, which is correct for a change to the classifier itself
- Nothing in `backend/tests/` or `frontend/` imports `lane` or `merge_cage` (grep, no hits)

**Not checked:** I did not run the backend suite (this file is not imported by it), did not
touch `merge_cage.py`, and did not change `.github/merge-policy.yml`. Pre-existing and
unrelated: `scripts/stale_path_check.py` already exits 1 on `feat/two-lane-cage` —
`merge-policy.yml:93` still names `docs/product_design_rules.md` in a comment, which wave 1
moved to `docs/product/product_design_rules.md`. That is a wave-1 loose end in a file I did
not touch, not a regression from this PR.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds client-side heartbeat and bounded reconnect to the ink TUI's gateway client. The client periodically sends `gateway.ping` and, if it stops seeing acks past a deadline, treats the socket as silently dropped and reconnects with bounded exponential backoff. It's the client half of the `gateway.ping` wire contract in #89958 — it only starts the heartbeat when the server advertises `heartbeat` in `gateway.ready`, so against an older backend it's a no-op and behaves exactly as today.

## Related Issue

Client half of #89958 (heartbeat wire contract); part of #83166.

Also addresses **#32997**, which names `ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts` and `handleTransportExit()` — the exact file and function this changes — and whose suggested fixes 1 and 2 (a WebSocket ping/pong, and exponential-backoff reconnect at 1s/2s/4s/8s capped at 30s) are what this implements. It does **not** cover that issue's suggested fix 3 (buffering unsent composer text across a reconnect); this only touches the client transport, so typed text is still lost on reconnect. #60727 is an earlier open PR over the same files — this is that work re-split against current main, not a claim over it.

Related: #53374 reports the same keepalive gap on Windows sleep/resume, and #89083 the macOS Desktop version.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts` — heartbeat interval/deadline + bounded-backoff reconnect; a `disposed` flag so `kill()` stops reconnecting; a heartbeat-ack short-circuit; all gated on the server's advertised `heartbeat` capability.
- `ui-tui/src/gatewayTypes.ts` — `heartbeat?` on `gateway.ready`, a `gateway.reconnecting` event.
- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/gatewayClient.test.ts` — heartbeat/reconnect coverage.

Constants: `WS_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS=15000`, `WS_HEARTBEAT_DEAD_MS=45000`, `RECONNECT_BASE_MS=1000`, `RECONNECT_MAX_MS=30000`.

## How to Test

```text
cd ui-tui && npx vitest run src/__tests__/gatewayClient.test.ts   → 18 passed
tsc --noEmit                                                       → clean
```
Covers: healthy-idle-with-acks, auto-reconnect-on-missing-ack, older-backend-omits-capability (graceful no-op), no-double-reconnect, no-reconnect-after-`kill()`.

author: narseh-ir
body:
Stacked on #97 — the store tests there assert a guarantee this restores. Merge #97 first; the base retargets to `master` automatically.

`setTokens(tokens, remember)` decides whether a session lands in `localStorage` (survives a browser restart) or `sessionStorage` (does not). Both refresh paths omitted the second argument, and it defaults to `true`:

| Caller | When it runs |
|---|---|
| `api.ts` `doRefresh` | every 401 retry |
| `auth.store.ts` `initialize` | every page load with a valid refresh cookie |

So the first token refresh moved any session-only login into `localStorage`.

`routes/auth.verify.tsx:153` omits the argument too. That one is deliberately left alone: a sign-in completing email verification is a real login, so remembering it matches the other login paths. Worth knowing that a user holding an ephemeral session who opens a verification link is promoted to `localStorage` — by intent rather than by omission.

## Why it matters

Ephemeral sessions are not hypothetical — `'ephemeral'` is passed at `routes/auth.index.tsx:62`, `routes/index.tsx:73`, and `routes/m.$meetId.tsx:570`. That last one is a guest joining a meeting, which is exactly the case where the machine is likely to be shared.

Such a session then survived a browser restart for as long as the access token stayed valid, because `initialize`'s fallback re-authenticates the persisted token against `/api/auth/me`.

## The fix

`currentRememberMode()` reads the mode from whichever storage holds `REMEMBER_KEY`, and both refresh paths pass it. With no session on record it returns `true`, so a first login is still remembered — no change to the normal sign-in flow.

## A second layer, found in review

`setTokens` wrote its chosen storage but left the other one's keys in place, while `currentRememberMode()` reads `localStorage` first. So keys from an earlier remembered login made a later ephemeral session read back as remembered, and its first refresh wrote the guest token to `localStorage` again — the same bug one level up.

Reachable without contrivance: none of the three ephemeral call sites clears first, and `handleJoin` in `routes/index.tsx` gates on the in-memory `tokens`, so entering a meeting code before `initialize()` finishes leaves the stale keys in place while guest-logging in as `'ephemeral'`.

`setTokens` now clears the other storage in both branches, making ownership single rather than implied.

**This is a behaviour change beyond the PR title.** Any ephemeral login now wipes the `localStorage` keys, so a remembered session in another tab loses its persistence. That is intended: a guest login replaces the server-side cookies anyway, so the other session is already over — its keys were only going to mislead `currentRememberMode()`. Calling it out so nobody later reads it as a regression.

## Why nothing caught it

Each module is correct in isolation. The store honours the flag exactly as its tests in #97 assert; the caller simply never passed one. Only a test crossing both modules can see it, which is what `session-persistence.test.ts` does:

- ephemeral, session-only and remembered sessions each staying put across a 401 refresh
- a session not being fooled by keys left behind from an earlier remembered login
- `initialize`'s four branches — cookie refresh, persisted-token fallback via `/api/auth/me`, the clear path, and the concurrent-caller dedupe — which had no tests at all

The single-owner contract is also tested directly in `auth.store.test.ts`, in both directions. The existing "does not leave a stale token in localStorage" test used to call `clear()` in between, so it passed for the wrong reason; that `clear()` is gone.

## Verification

`bun run test` — 52 files, 251 tests, 0 failures. `tsc --noEmit` and `biome check` clean for the changed files.

Mutation-checked in three places:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove the `currentRememberMode()` argument | 2 crossing tests fail |
| Remove the two `removeItem` calls | the crossing test plus both direct contract tests fail |

## Two related notes

- **`updateAccessToken` has no callers** outside the store. Had `doRefresh` used it, there would have been no bug — it already writes to the correct storage. Worth either adopting or deleting, but that is a separate decision. Not changed here.
- **`initialize`'s dedupe promise** is now released through `finally` rather than only on the failure path. It was benign — the `initialized` guard stops a second run — but it made resetting `initialized` without `clear()` a silent no-op, which cost time in these tests and would have cost it again. It also closes a window in the old code, where the failure path nulled `_init.promise` *before* settling, so a caller arriving in between would start a second `initialize()`.

author: os-elon
body:
Fixes #9925

**Clause-② notice: this PR changes contract acceptance on the type axis of a published surface** — `InlineLocaleMap`'s emitted key type narrows so the retired `{ key, defaultValue }` key-reference form becomes a compile error on every `I18nLabel` surface. Runtime acceptance is unchanged in both directions (the schema always refused that shape at parse time). Draft by dispatch contract — the PM reviews and lands it.

## Ruling implemented

Maintainer ruling of 2026-08-19 on #9925 (comment 5339545579, Option B): narrow `InlineLocaleMap`'s key type in `@objectstack/spec` so the retired form is a compile error on every `I18nLabel` surface in both repos at once, instead of a publish-time-only refusal. The BCP-47 key regex is a Zod runtime refinement erased from the emitted type — `I18nLabel`'s object half read as a plain string record, so the retired form structurally type-checked everywhere (objectui#5264 shipped a full release rendering a raw dotted i18n key as the visible KPI label because the wrong shape compiled).

**Both attached conditions are honored, and both turn out moot on the measured shape:**

1. **Escape hatch (single named export, never a loosened record key):** no hatch is needed at all. Computed-key sites (`{ [locale]: text }`) and plain string-to-string `Record` sources still assign under the chosen shape — an index signature declares no `key`/`defaultValue` property, so the `never` limbs never fire on them (measured, pinned as positive probes). The record key type is nowhere loosened; no hatch export exists.
2. **Fallback A, never C:** not taken. The measurement found zero broken computed-key call sites (see triage), so Option B lands as ruled. No grep gate anywhere.

## Shape measurements and pick

Both ruling-offered shapes probed with real tsc (strict, isolated probe files; logs in the session record):

| Probe | `Record(string -> string) & { key?: never; defaultValue?: never }` (angle-bracket generics spelled arrow-style here — the platform sanitizer eats short angle fragments) | Template-literal locale-tag key (letter-union approximation, a `Partial` record over the tag union) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Valid inline maps (`{ en, 'zh-CN' }`, `zh-Hans-CN`, `default`) assign | pass | pass |
| `{ key, defaultValue }` refuses (both property orders) | pass | pass |
| Lone `key` refuses | **pass** | **FAIL — compiles** (`key` is three lowercase letters, matches the `${L}${L}${L}` arm; same boundary the schema doc records for the runtime regex) |
| Lone `defaultValue` refuses | pass | pass |
| Computed-key `{ [locale]: text }` assigns | pass | pass |
| Plain string-to-string `Record` assigns | pass | pass |
| tsc wall time (isolated probe) | **1.8 s** | 16.3 s at a 12-letter scale; the honest 26-letter version (18,252-key mapped type) **did not complete in ~7 minutes** and was killed |

A branded-tag key was ruled out without a full probe: object literals cannot supply branded keys, so every one of the repo's 31 authored inline maps would stop compiling. **Pick: the never-intersection** — strictly wider refusal coverage, negligible compile cost, zero escape-hatch need, and it is the shape the ruling itself offered. The narrowing is deliberately exactly the measured harm class, not BCP-47 fidelity; the full key grammar remains the runtime refinement's job.

## Implementation

- `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n.zod.ts` — `InlineLocaleMap` is now hand-tied (`Record(string -> string) & { key?: never; defaultValue?: never }`, arrow-style spelling again) and carried into every `z.input`/`z.infer` derivation by an explicit `z.ZodType` annotation with both the output and input halves set to `InlineLocaleMap` on `InlineLocaleMapSchema` (the `QuerySchema`/`FormFieldSchema` annotation pattern; no cast needed — verified the built `.d.ts` carries the intersection through `I18nLabelSchema`'s union and `AriaProps.ariaLabel`).
- `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n.label-type-assertions.ts` — new compile-level pin file (the `app.nav-type-assertions.ts` pattern: plain src module, no barrel export, checked by the required `tsc --noEmit` program). Positive half: literal maps, qualified tags, plain string, computed-key and widened-record sources. Negative half (`@ts-expect-error`): the retired pair in both orders, lone `key`, lone `defaultValue`, direct against `InlineLocaleMap`, and embedded on two real surfaces — `AriaProps.ariaLabel` and `DashboardWidgetSchema.title` (this repo's closest analogue of objectui#5264's metric-widget title).
- `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n.test.ts` — property-order twin added to the existing runtime refusal pin (`{ defaultValue, key }` also refused, `invalid_key`). Runtime behavior untouched.
- `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.test.ts` — fixture triage, one hit: the `{ constructor: 'Ctor' }` parity vector was never schema-legal (11-letter key fails the regex) and compiled only through the erased type; it now declares itself out-of-contract with the same `as unknown as I18nLabel` its neighboring out-of-contract vectors already use. Disposition: declare, not delete — the vector pins the resolver's defensive own-property behavior, which is exactly its job.
- `packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` — the ADR-0122 gate itself ordered the `Iso759` isomorphism pin deleted (no bare `z.input` alias relies on the exemption any more); pin count 840 → 839 with receipt, both prose statements recomputed per the file's own convention.

## Consumer triage (type-axis accept change — real readings)

| Surface | Reading | Disposition |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `packages/spec` src (all `I18nLabelSchema` embeds: view/app/component/chart/dashboard/report/action/page/settings-manifest/translation) | `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; full suite 414 files / 11,019 tests green | No change needed beyond the two test files above |
| `packages/platform-objects` (the repo's 31 authored inline maps, three pages) | `typecheck` green in the 57-task turbo sweep | Literal BCP-47 keys assign unchanged |
| `packages/lint` (`validate-component-props`, showcase-shape fixtures authoring labels) | `typecheck` green in the same sweep | No change |
| `packages/cli` (i18n tab-coverage test) | `typecheck` green in the same sweep | No change |
| `packages/services/service-analytics` (`resolveI18nLabel` consumer, dataset-compiler) | no typecheck script (ledger-covered); full suite 77 files / 1,722 tests green; builds clean | No change |
| Dependency closures of all four | `turbo run build` 55 tasks green; `turbo run typecheck` 57 tasks green (pnpm-style `--filter` with the trailing three-dot suffix — each named package plus everything it depends on; the typecheck sweep direction is the named packages themselves, whose programs compile the label-typed call sites) | No change |
| `service-messaging` / `service-realtime` / `service-storage` `i18n-extract.config.ts` | `zh-CN` hits are translation-bundle locale keys (`TranslationData` surface), not `I18nLabel` inline maps | Out of reach, no change |
| objectui (out of scope per dispatch) | Call sites get caught when the spec pin bumps; the known breakage class is exactly the already-filed #5264. No foreseeable breakage beyond it: `pickLocalized` consumes maps read-only (reads survive the intersection), and computed-key construction survives by the same measurement | Nothing filed beyond the existing #5264 |

## Reverse verification (from the committed state)

Fix committed first; then `git restore --source=origin/main -- packages/spec/src/ui/i18n.zod.ts` (tree-only, unstaged) and `tsc --noEmit` re-run: **exactly the 7 negative pins flipped to `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`** (5 direct + 2 embedded-surface), positives stayed green — the pins are live and the annotation is the single load-bearing carrier. Restored via `git restore --source=HEAD`, working tree clean against HEAD, green leg re-run exit 0. No `dist` in this measurement loop on either leg — `tsc --noEmit` compiles `src` directly, so no rebuild was required
