author: tecpey
body:
## Summary

W4 from the QA register — the last item. **Corrects the register's framing:** investigating the theme setup showed the issue is not an OS-preference asymmetry. TecPey ships **dark-mode-first** — `next-themes` with `attribute="class"`, `defaultTheme="dark"`, `enableSystem={false}`, and Tailwind's `dark:` variant wired to that class (`@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))`), consistent with the `--tp-bg`/`--tp-text` token system.

Against that dark default, the English free-course pillar page styled its answer/module/route cards **light-only** (`bg-white`, `text-slate-950`, no `dark:`), so they rendered as stark white blocks in the default theme — while the Farsi twin adapted via `dark:` variants.

## Change (fix + enforce)

- Bring the English cards to parity with the Farsi dark treatment (matching `dark:` variants); the two pages now share an identical **14-token** `dark:` set.
- Document the theming convention in `docs/ui/THEME_AND_DARK_MODE.md` (dark-first, class-based, `dark:` wired to `.dark`; content must be theme-aware; bilingual twins must match).
- Add `src/tests/ui/content-theme-parity.test.ts` asserting bilingual page pairs carry identical `dark:` treatment, so the two editions can't drift apart.

## Verification

- UI test suite 8/8 (`src/tests/ui/*.test.ts`). **Load-bearing:** removing a `dark:` variant from either locale fails the parity test with a precise diff.

author: benyblack
body:
## What this changes

The last shape `NativeSshCapability` refused. The native backend now requests a `tcpip-forward` listener on the server per remote-forward rule and serves the connections that arrive on it, so `-R`-style forwards work without the OpenSSH backend — and the capability gate refuses nothing.

Fixes no tracked issue; this completes the native-SSH gap plan (after #325, #328, #330, #331, #332).

Details:

- **rusty_ssh**: a `RequestRemoteForward` worker command awaits `session.tcpip_forward` and replies with the bound port through the existing reply pattern, exposed as `nova_ssh_request_remote_forward`. A server refusal maps to a new `NOVA_SSH_RESULT_REMOTE_FORWARD_FAILED` code — distinct from `CHANNEL_OPEN_FAILED` because nothing channel-shaped exists to retry. Incoming `forwarded-tcpip` channels land in a new `server_channel_open_forwarded_tcpip` handler on the **target session's handler only**; jump hops carry no channels map and close unsolicited opens outright. The channel-wiring body of `open_direct_tcpip_channel` is extracted as `register_forward_channel` — the machinery is direction-agnostic once the channel exists — with a `before_reader` hook that queues the `ForwardChannelIncoming` announcement after the map entry exists but before the reader task can deliver a byte, so data can neither race ahead of the announcement nor address an id the managed side cannot close.
- **Managed**: `NativePortForwardSession` requests listeners on a background task (the worker only answers once the session is established, and a refusal is loud but not fatal, matching `ssh -R`'s warning), registers incoming channel state synchronously on the poll loop — the ordered outbound queue holds any data while the local destination is being dialled — then connects and starts the same pumps, budgets, and backpressure the outgoing kinds use. A connection announcing a port no rule asked for is refused rather than dialled anywhere.
- **Capability**: `NativeSshCapability.Evaluate` now refuses nothing. The gate and all its call sites (editor at save time, factory and session at connect time) stay wired, so the next unsupported shape gets one refusal reaching all of them at once.

Explicitly NOT claimed by this PR: parity with OpenSSH for a default flip. The native backend still lacks ssh-agent auth (the connection editor's recommended method) and silently ignores `MuxOptions`/`ExtraSshArgs`; those are the remaining blockers for changing the default backend, discussed with the owner.

## Invariant and ownership

- **What invariant does this change affect?** No-silent-degradation, in both directions: a refused `tcpip-forward` request is logged loudly by name (session survives, like `ssh -R`), an unsolicited incoming channel is refused rather than dialled anywhere, and the announcement-before-first-byte ordering guarantees no forwarded bytes are dropped while the destination dial is in flight.
- **Which module owns that invariant?** NovaTerminal.Platform (`Ssh/Native`), with the FFI contract shared with `src/NovaTerminal.App/native/rusty_ssh`.

## Tests

- **What tests cover this change?**
  - Rust (`cargo test`, 91 passing locally): 3 new FFI-contract tests for `nova_ssh_request_remote_forward` — argument validation, the round trip through the worker command with the bound port, and the refusal mapping to its own result code.
  - `NativePortForwardSessionTests` (4 new): the listener request is made with OpenSSH's `-R` bind default; an incoming channel dials the destination and carries bytes both ways **including data queued behind the announcement before the dial completes** (the ordering the `before_reader` hook exists for); an incoming channel matching no rule is refused; an unreachable destination closes the channel.
  - Existing tests that pinned the remote-forward refusal flip to pinning acceptance (`NativeSshCapabilityTests`, `SshSessionFactoryTests`, `NewSshConnectionViewModelTests`).
  - **Docker E2E** (`NativeSshDockerRemoteForwardE2eTests`, runs in the blocking `Native SSH Docker E2E` job): socat inside the fixture container dials the remote listener the session requested; a local destination answers with a *transformed* reply, so the assertion cannot match the echo of the typed command — only bytes that actually crossed the tunnel both ways.

- **Which categories did you run locally?**
  - [ ] full unfiltered run (`scripts/build.sh test`)
  - [ ] `Category=Replay`
  - [ ] `Category=RenderMetrics`
  - [ ] `Category=PtySmoke`
  - [ ] `tests/NovaTerminal.App.Tests` (non-blocking in CI — check it yourself)
  - [ ] full local CI rehearsal (`ci/run.sh` / `ci/run.ps1`)

  Rust tests, clippy, and rustfmt ran locally (clippy/rustfmt byte-identical to main's baseline). The .NET categories did not: no .NET SDK is reachable from the authoring container (same as every PR on this branch); CI is the compile and the test run, and the Docker E2E job is the real exercise for the new tunnel path. `NovaTerminal.App.Tests` changes are the view-model test flips, which CI runs even though that job is non-blocking.

## Impact

- **Does this affect cross-platform behavior?** The tunnel logic is platform-neutral (managed + Rust, same code paths everywhere); Docker E2E exercises it on Linux, Rust FFI tests run on both CI OSes.
- **Does this change renderer metrics?** Not applicable — no renderer code touched.
- **Does this change VT coverage?** Not applicable — no VT sequences touched.

author: pyup-bot
body:
### Update [asgiref](https://pypi.org/project/asgiref) from **3.8.1** to **3.12.1**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.12.1
   ```
   -------------------

* Restored the previous SyncToAsync.__call__ internal code shape, which was
  relied on by some APM services. (572)

  Note, this change was available whilst maintaining the underlying fix (from
  564). It does not constitute an API stability promise. Ideally APMs are
  *not* monkey patching internal APIs, and future changes will be made here if
  needed.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.12.0
   ```
   -------------------

* ``AsyncToSync`` no longer captures the running event loop on
  instantiation. (562)

  This resolves a series of deadlocks that users experienced after asgiref 3.9.0,
  particularly with pytest-asyncio. pytest-asyncio stops the event loop between
  tests, and long-running unawaited futures could find themselves trying to
  schedule work onto a stopped loop, and so would never complete. Ideally, code
  should be structured to await long-running futures before returning, but this
  change should help users experiencing issues here.

  The loop is now resolved when the callable is invoked rather than when it is
  created. If ``async_to_sync`` is called from within ``sync_to_async``, the
  parent event loop is still used, as before.

  The possibility of deadlock therefore remains in some nested patterns. For
  example, an async function may call a long-running ``sync_to_async`` function
  that itself uses ``async_to_sync``; if the outer function returns before the
  sync future completes, the parent event loop may already be stopped, and the
  nested calls cannot be driven to completion.

  This is not a bug in asgiref — the same patterns deadlock in plain asyncio. As
  above, restructure your code to await the ``sync_to_async`` future before
  exiting the driving coroutine.

* Fixed an event loop deadlock when exiting ``ThreadSensitiveContext``
  while its executor thread was still blocked waiting on the event loop.
  (535)

* Dropped support for EOL Python 3.9.

* Fixed ``StatelessServer.run()`` failing on Python 3.14, where
  ``asyncio.get_event_loop()`` no longer creates an event loop if none
  exists. It now uses ``asyncio.run()``. (559)

* Fixed ``Local`` leaking data between unrelated sync threads when
  ``sys.flags.thread_inherit_context`` is enabled (Python 3.14+), so a newly
  started thread inherits a copy of the spawning thread's context. This flag is
  on by default on free-threaded builds and opt-in on the regular GIL build.
  ``Local`` storage is now tagged with its owning thread and re-homed only when
  asgiref intentionally moves work across threads (in ``async_to_sync`` /
  ``sync_to_async``), restoring the documented thread-local behaviour in sync
  threads.

* asgiref is now tested against the free-threaded builds of Python 3.13 and
  3.14 in CI.

  available for type-checking the codebase.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.11.1
   ```
   -------------------

* SECURITY FIX CVE-2025-14550: There was a potential DoS vector for users of
  the ``asgiref.wsgi.WsgiToAsgi`` adapter. Malicious requests, including an unreasonably
  large number of values for the same header, could lead to resource exhaustion
  when building the WSGI environment.

  To mitigate this, the algorithm is changed to be more efficient, and
  ``WsgiToAsgi`` gains a new optional ``duplicate_header_limit`` parameter,
  which defaults to 100. This specifies the number of times a single header may
  be repeated before the request is rejected as malformed.

  You may override ``duplicate_header_limit`` when configuring your application::

      application = WsgiToAsgi(wsgi_app, duplicate_header_limit=200)

  Set ``duplicate_header_limit=None`` if you wish to disable this check.

  with an attribute named ``context``. (537)

   ```

* ``sync_to_async`` gains a ``context`` parameter, similar to those for
  ``asyncio.create_task``, ``TaskGroup`` &co, that can be used on Python 3.11+ to
  control the context used by the underlying task.

What's new in Django 6.1
========================

Model field fetch modes
-----------------------

The on-demand fetching behavior of model fields is now configurable with
:doc:`fetch modes </topics/db/fetch-modes>`. These modes allow you to control
how Django fetches data from the database when an unfetched field is accessed.

Django provides three fetch modes:

1. ``FETCH_ONE``, the default, fetches the missing field for the current
   instance only. This mode represents Django's existing behavior.

2. ``FETCH_PEERS`` fetches a missing field for all instances that came from
   the same :class:`~django.db.models.query.QuerySet`.

   cases of the "N+1 queries problem" to two queries without any work to

   exception.

author: timothystl
body:
## Summary
Final two items from the CR7 review findings, closing out CR7 entirely.

**(a) Constant-time shared-secret comparison.** The `X-Intake-Key` header check in `api-intake.js`, and an identical second copy in `api-scheduler.js`'s Christmas Market summary route, both used a plain `!==` string compare against a high-entropy shared secret — theoretically a timing-attack surface. New `timingSafeEqual()` in `auth.js`: hashes both sides with SHA-256 first (so both are a fixed-length digest regardless of input length — no Node-only `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, which Workers doesn't guarantee), then XOR-accumulates every byte with no early exit. Removes both the length signal and the byte-position signal a bare `!==` leaks. Both call sites updated.

**(b) Narrowed the CORS preflight handler.** `tlc-volunteer-worker.js`'s `OPTIONS` handler answered preflight for *every path in the app* with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` — including `/admin/api/*`, login, everything. Narrowed to `isSchedCorsPath()`, an explicit allowlist matching the exact set of paths whose real (non-`OPTIONS`) handlers actually emit `SCHED_CORS` (`schedJson()`/`schedHtmlPage()` in `api-scheduler.js`).

A first attempt at the allowlist over-matched: it excluded only `/api/events` from the generic `/api/*` breeze-proxy catch-all, but three more `/api/*` sub-routes (`/api/ministry-roles`, the Christmas Market summary route, everything under `/api/intake/`) are matched *above* that catch-all in the real routing order and never reach it — so they never emit `SCHED_CORS` either. A verification harness caught `/api/intake/funds` being wrongly included before anything shipped; fixed with an explicit exclusion list mirroring the real routing precedence.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 1601/1601 passing
- [x] `node --check` on all 4 touched files
- [x] A standalone harness asserting `isSchedCorsPath()` matches every real CORS-emitting route and correctly excludes every non-CORS route, including the three easy-to-miss `/api/*` exclusions
- [ ] Live cross-origin caller verification — not possible in this session (standing limitation for all frontend/network work in this repo, per `CLAUDE.md`)

With `header.mobileMenuStyle = "dropdown"`, the panel only closes through its own X button. `setupMobileMenuEscape()` already dismisses it with the keyboard, so the missing pointer equivalent leaves the panel sitting over the page after a stray tap.

body:
## Description

`read_hex_file` builds its DataFrame one value at a time. This changes it to read the file in a single pass and fill preallocated arrays, constructing the DataFrame at the end. Same inputs, same outputs.

Measured on `tests/resources/test-data/19plus_V2.hex` (3,069 scans, 7 sensors), best of five runs:

The test suite goes from **~12.0 s to ~7.0 s** (min of three), since several tests read `.hex` files.  It noticeably speeds things up when loading a full cruise's dataset.

### What changed

Two things, in one function:

1. **The file is read once instead of twice.** The row count was obtained by iterating the whole file, then the file was re-read to parse it. The data lines are now collected on the first pass and the count taken from that list.

2. **Values are written into arrays rather than into the DataFrame.** Each field of each scan was assigned with `DataFrame.loc[row, column]`. The first scan is now parsed to establish the column names and their types, values are written into preallocated per-column arrays, and the DataFrame is built once at the end.

`preallocate_dataframe` was only ever called from `read_hex_file`, so it is removed. 

### Behaviour

No change. A file whose header is not followed by any scans returns an empty DataFrame, as before.

### Test added

`tests/test_instrument_data.py` gains `TestReadHexNoDataRows`, covering the header-only case. It passes against the unmodified code as well, so it records existing behaviour rather than introducing any. The rest of the rewritten code is exercised by the existing per-instrument hex-reading tests.

author: sanlee-ys
body:
## What

Fixes a verified bypass in `security/credential-guard.py` (v2.12 → v2.13) and refreshes the stale derived copy at `vendors/claude/plugin/hooks/credential-guard.py` (was v2.11).

## The bypass (MEDIUM)

`cp --target-directory=/tmp ~/.env` was ALLOWED. In `_copy_operands`, a `_DEST_FLAGS`/`_SRC_FLAGS` token that carries its value attached with `=` still consumed the NEXT token as the flag's value. The credential source became the destination value, the operand list held no source, and the launder rule saw nothing to judge. `mv --target-directory=/tmp ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` had the same hole. Reproduced against v2.12 before the fix: both commands returned exit 0.

## The fix

When a dest/src flag token contains `=`, the parser now takes the text after the first `=` as the value and does not consume the next token. The plain two-token form (`cp -t /tmp SRC`) is unchanged.

Regression tests added to `tests/test_credential_guard.py`:

- `cp --target-directory=/tmp ~/.env` → blocked
- `mv --target-directory=/tmp ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` → blocked
- `cp --target-directory=/tmp README.md` → allowed

## Stale plugin copy (HIGH, cross-consistency)

`vendors/claude/plugin/hooks/credential-guard.py` sat at v2.11 while canon was v2.12. Re-copied canon over it byte-for-byte after the fix (`cmp` verified identical, now v2.13), per the plugin README's "edit canon, then re-copy" rule.

**Drift-check pair NOT added, deliberately.** `scripts/check-generated-drift.py` declares no pairs itself — pairs live in a per-repo `.generated-drift.toml`, which this repo does not have, and this repo's `ci.yml` only py-compiles the script and never runs it. Wiring the pair means a new config file plus a new workflow job, and the plugin README explicitly defers that wiring to the cutover session ("The mechanical fix at cutover is to wire these paths into scripts/check-generated-drift.py" / "Cutover (a future session's job — do NOT do it as a side effect)"). So this PR does the re-copy only.

## Verification

- Full suite the way CI runs it (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"`, Python 3.11): 672 tests, OK.
- All eight `py_compile` targets from `ci.yml`: pass.
- Note: the suite on the local default Python 3.7 shows 11 unrelated failures (`tomllib` is 3.11+); CI pins 3.11, where everything is green.

author: magnew
body:
## Problem

Creating a preview project with content copying fails entirely — zero spaces, charts, or dashboards copied — when any chart in the source project has an ad-hoc `sum_distinct` / `average_distinct` custom metric (which always carries a deduplication key).

`ProjectModel.duplicateContent` re-inserts rows read via `select *`. node-postgres serializes a raw JS array as a Postgres array literal (`{"a","b"}`) instead of JSON, so the jsonb `distinct_keys` column (`string[]`) fails with `invalid input syntax for type json`. The column was added in Feb 2026 but never added to the copy path's `fieldPreprocess` map (the same map already stringifies the other array-shaped jsonb columns: `filters`, `custom_range`, `custom_groups`, `pivot_values`). The copy runs in one transaction, so a single such metric aborts the whole copy.

Audited every jsonb column across all tables the copy path touches — `distinct_keys` was the only array-shaped one missing preprocessing.

## Fix

Add `distinct_keys` to the `fieldPreprocess` map, guarding `null` so rows without keys keep SQL `NULL` (matching the write path, which omits the column when absent).

## Verification

Reproduced end-to-end locally: saved a chart version with a `sum_distinct` metric (`distinct_keys: ["id_status.order_id"]`), `POST /createPreview` with `copyContent: true` → 500, Postgres log shows `invalid input syntax for type json ... {"id_status.order_id"}`. After the fix, the same call copies 26 spaces / 79 charts / 10 dashboards, the metric row arrives as proper jsonb, and null `distinct_keys` remain SQL NULL.

Closes: PROD-10277
Closes: #27570

author: teamleaderleo
nightshaddow13
body:
## Summary

Turns `Event` into a JsonApiDotNetCore resource at `/api/events`, with Admin/Director authorization enforced from the internal JWT's role claims (ADR-0007, ADR-0017) — no per-request database scoping query.

- **Admin**: full CRUD over every Event.
- **Director**: read/update on only the Events they're assigned to; never create or delete.
- An unassigned Director's single-resource request gets **403**; a collection request is silently filtered to only visible Events instead — a deliberate asymmetry, recorded in ADR-0031.
- `Slug`/`Passcode` are server-generated on create (not client-creatable over the wire) and remain editable via PATCH — matches P2-6's "starting value, editable afterward" and CONTEXT.md's Passcode entry ("auto-generated the moment an Event is created").
- `Name`/`Slug` uniqueness collisions map to **409** (case-insensitive, matching SQL Server's real default collation) instead of the raw 500 an unhandled unique-index violation would otherwise produce.

## Design notes

- Authorization lives in `EventResourceDefinition` (a JsonApiDotNetCore extension point), not a hand-written controller or middleware — ADR-0031 records why that still satisfies ADR-0004's "zero hand-written controllers" framing, per the ticket's explicit ask to confirm this.
- `EventAccessPolicy` is a small pure type parsing `ClaimTypes.Role` claims via the existing `RoleClaimValue`/`RoleNames` contracts — unit-tested independently of any host.
- `Slug`/`Passcode` are typed `string?` rather than non-nullable, because ASP.NET Core's implicit-required-for-non-nullable-reference-types validation otherwise rejects a `POST` body that correctly omits them (JsonApiDotNetCore validates this before `OnWritingAsync` ever runs). The `NOT NULL` database contract is preserved explicitly via `IsRequired()` in `VirtualLeadersGuideDbContext` rather than relying on the C# type convention. Verified no EF model drift (`dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes` reports none).

## Testing

- 23 new integration tests (`EventsResourceShould`) covering Admin CRUD, Director scoping (assigned/unassigned, read/update/create/delete), collection filtering for zero-role callers, and Name/Slug conflict-to-409 mapping (including both colliding at once).
- 6 new unit tests (`EventAccessPolicyShould`) for claim parsing edge cases (malformed scope, no scope, multiple grants).
- `DomainAuthorizationEntitiesAreNotJsonApiResourcesShould` updated — `/api/events` moves from the negative case to `EventsResourceShould`'s positive coverage.
- Full solution builds clean (0 warnings). All 99 `Api.Tests` and 45 `Web.Tests` pass. `AppHost.Tests` fails locally only because Docker Desktop isn't running in this environment (pre-existing, unrelated to this change — that test starts the full Aspire-orchestrated stack with containerized SQL Server/Azurite).

Closes #16

## Summary
- `CheckpointCallback.on_step_end` triggered on `step % save_interval == 0`
  (exact equality). PPO's `step` only advances in increments of
  `n_steps*n_envs` (98304 for this project's real config), and
  `gcd(98304, 100_000) == 32`, so the first step that's ALSO an exact
  multiple of the default `save_interval=100_000` is
  `lcm(98304, 100_000) == 307,200,000` — past the end of every real run
  this project has actually done (max so far: 120M steps). Found while
  investigating why zero periodic checkpoints were ever written across
  several real, multi-hour PPO verification runs — only `best_*.pt`
  (score-gated) and `final_*.pt` ever appeared.
- Fixed to trigger on CROSSING a multiple of `save_interval`
  (`step >= next_save_step`) instead of landing exactly on one, correctly
  handling a call that jumps past more than one interval at once (saves
  once, reschedules the next real boundary — doesn't double-save or skip).

- [x] 5 new tests (`tests/test_checkpoint_callback_interval.py`),
      including one reproducing the exact 98304/100_000 arithmetic that
      motivated this

author: markgov
body:
Encrypt iam-credential-exposed-alert SNS topic with a customer-managed KMS key
Summary
Adds server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) to the iam-credential-exposed-alert SNS topic in the iam-credential-response module, backed by a customer-managed KMS key created in the same module. Also grants the responder Lambda the KMS permissions it needs to publish to the now-encrypted topic, and removes an out-of-date checkov skip.

Why
The iam-credential-exposed-alert topic carries data derived from IAM security incidents (exposed credentials). It should not be transmitted or stored unencrypted at the topic level.
Encrypting with a CMK satisfies CKV_AWS_26 (SNS topics should use KMS encryption) properly, so we can remove the previous checkov:skip and tfsec:ignore that were papering over the missing encryption.
A prior comment claimed "encrypted topics do not work with PagerDuty subscription". This is not correct: SNS SSE-KMS is transparent to HTTPS subscribers — SNS decrypts messages before delivery — so the existing PagerDuty integration is unaffected. Confirmed against the AWS SNS SSE docs ("The messages are stored in encrypted form, and only decrypted when they are sent") and the current PagerDuty CloudWatch integration guide, which uses a plain HTTPS subscription with no KMS considerations.
What changed
main.tf

Added data "aws_caller_identity" "current".
Added two aws_iam_policy_document data sources (iam_credential_response_kms, iam_credential_response_multi_region_kms) providing a root-delegated key policy — permissions to use the key are granted via IAM to the responder Lambda role.
Added a new customer-managed KMS key aws_kms_key.iam_credential_response with:
enable_key_rotation = true
deletion_window_in_days = 7
Descriptive description
Tagged via var.tags
Added a matching aws_kms_alias.iam_credential_response.
Added an equivalent multi-region key + alias (aws_kms_key.iam_credential_response_multi_region, aws_kms_alias.iam_credential_response_multi_region) to allow cross-region use of the same key material if required in future.
Set kms_master_key_id on aws_sns_topic.iam_credential_alert to the new CMK ARN.
Removed the # tfsec:ignore:aws-sns-enable-topic-encryption marker and the #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_26 line — both are satisfied by the encryption being in place.
Added a UseSNSKMSKey statement to aws_iam_role_policy.credential_responder granting kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt on the CMK ARN, so the Lambda can publish to the encrypted topic without hitting KMSAccessDeniedException.
variables.tf

Added iam_credential_response_kms_name (default alias/iam-credential-response).
Added iam_credential_response_multi_region_kms_name (default alias/iam-credential-response-multi-region).
Security considerations
Key policy is intentionally minimal: only the account root, with permissions delegated via IAM to the Lambda role that needs to publish. No AWS service principals are granted kms:* on the key.
Key rotation is enabled.
No subscriber-side changes are required for PagerDuty: SNS decrypts at delivery time; the HTTPS endpoint receives plaintext messages exactly as before.
CKV_AWS_26 is now satisfied by real encryption rather than by a suppression.
Testing
terraform init -backend=false && terraform validate passes on iam-credential-response.
No changes to module inputs required by consumers: both new variables have sensible defaults, and no existing variables were renamed or removed.
Out of scope / follow-ups
The multi-region KMS key is provisioned but not yet consumed. If it isn't needed for a planned cross-region use case, we can drop it (and its alias, data source, and variable) in a follow-up.
The KMS key policy currently grants no AWS service principals. If another AWS service later needs to publish directly to this topic, extend the policy at that point.

author: saddamr3e
body:
The debug and local-variable section readers in the .mrb loader take a 16- or 32-bit length or count field from the section and use it before checking the bytes are still inside the buffer. read_section_debug reads filenames_len and then each entry's f_len, and read_section_lv reads syms_len and each name's str_len, in every case advancing bin first and only testing it against end afterward. A crafted .mrb whose debug or lv section ends right where one of those fields begins makes bin_to_uint16/bin_to_uint32 read a couple of bytes past the declared binary. I ran into it feeding a truncated section to mruby -b, where ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow read in read_section_debug (load.c:538) and read_section_lv (load.c:628). The existing symbol-length check here guards the bytes a length points at, not the read of the length field itself, so this adds the missing check right before each field read, using the same form read_debug_record already applies. Valid .mrb files are unaffected because a real section always carries these fields.

author: gfeitel1-maker
body:
## What this is

Reimagines the reconciliation screen as a **root map**: a warm root illustration with **data-bound, stateful nodes sitting on the actual roots**. Each of the five domains (Structure, Scheduling, Time, Resources, Context) and its children is a real node coloured by its ingested state. The roots *are* the interface — not a decorative backdrop.

Clicking a node populates the attention panel with that item's **real reconciliation decisions** and an **"Open in {screen} →"** action that navigates to where the director actually edits that part of their camp. Tiles filter by state; hover reveals a node's label.

## How it works

- **`src/ingest/rootMapModel.js`** — pure, tested projection of `buildReconciliationReport` output → the node model. Reuses `reportToLanes`/`domainOf`/`childOf`; honest state space (`absent` only for the unattributed Context domain, never fabricated).
- **`domainRollup`** widened 4→5 (+Context) with presentation-only `DOMAIN_LABELS` (Facility→"Resources"); the only other consumer updated. Blast radius verified.
- **`rootMapNav`** — domain/child → edit-screen map, **completeness-tested** so a click can never dead-end.
- **`rootMapLayout`** — node coordinates snapped onto the illustration's real root pixels.
- **Keyed illustration** bundled at `src/assets/reconciliation/root-map.png` (background removed so it sits on the app's own paper).
- **Design-audit (impeccable) + Emil polish**: visible hover label, node press feedback, dot-fill + panel crossfade transitions, tile selected-state tint, connectors that encode absence — all on `index.css` motion tokens, reduced-motion gated.
- Shared `reconciliationCards` so old/new render paths agree. Gated first-import `ReconstructionMoment` scaffolding retained.

## Decisions / notes for review

- **Filter behavior narrows** from multi-select domain chips to single-select state tiles + node selection (per the accepted interaction-model spec). Pre-production, no live users.
- **v1 state fidelity is honest, not full**: per-child dots reflect real decisions (understood/attention/changed); richer per-entity "absent" state is a flagged follow-up rather than faked.
- Node coordinates are hand-tuned onto the art (verified on-root programmatically); tightening the illustration crop so branches read bigger is a possible follow-up.

## ADRs

- `docs/adr/2026-08-18-rootmap-screen-port.md` (accepted) — the shipped Approach A.
- `docs/adr/2026-08-18-reconciliation-rootmap-screen.md` — marked **superseded** (the abandoned Blender-parts-kit exploration), retained for history.
- `docs/adr/2026-08-18-roots-reconstruction-moment-gating.md` — the retained first-import moment.

## Verification

Full gate green: **209 files / 3215 tests, 0 introduced failures**, build (asset bundled), governance clean, integration **25/25**.

author: samdefmacro
body:
First of three steps for G7-23. **The dependency lands and is proven before any
node code depends on it.**

## What changed

- `libzmq3-dev` in the runtime apt line, beside `libleveldb-dev` — same stated
  reason: the `-dev` package carries the plain `.so` name the CFFI probe looks
  for.
- `python3-zmq` in a trailing layer beside `nodejs`, for the reason that file
  already gives for nodejs: it is a test dependency and nothing the node ships
  uses it.
- The three live pins moved to `2.6.5-3` (`scripts/dev.sh` ×2,
  `scripts/docker-sbcl.sh`, `CLAUDE.md`). `docs/gap-analysis-8-plan.md` keeps
  its `2.6.5-2` deliberately — it documents a past wave's procedure.

## Why pyzmq is the point

A Lisp publisher checked only by a Lisp subscriber proves that our code agrees
with itself, which is exactly the failure mode a wire protocol has. This was my
stated reason for not hand-writing ZMTP; with pyzmq in the image the publishers
get verified against an **independent** ZeroMQ implementation.

## Verified in the built image

- SBCL loads **libzmq 4.3.5** through CFFI.
- A Lisp `PUB` socket's multipart message — topic, 32-byte body, little-endian
  sequence — arrives intact at a `pyzmq` `SUB` socket:
  `OK hashblock 0102…20 7`.

## Two things reviewers should know

**`ZMQ_LINGER` defaults to `-1`.** `zmq_close` then blocks *forever* on queued
messages — it hung my first round-trip attempt for the full timeout. The
publisher implementation must set it. Recorded here so it is not rediscovered.

**Build path.** `docker.io` is unreachable from this machine, so the canonical
Dockerfile (`FROM debian:trixie-slim`) could not resolve its base image here.
The local `2.6.5-3` was built by adding the same two apt lines on top of the
local `2.6.5-2`; the package set is identical, the layer arrangement is not. The
**committed Dockerfile is the canonical one** and should be rebuilt from it
wherever registry access exists, to confirm the two agree.

No node code depends on libzmq yet — that is step 2, and it will load the
library **lazily**, so a host without libzmq keeps running fine as long as ZMQ
is off.

author: drawmeanelephant
body:
## What

Second slice of **M15 — GitHub source** (#179), the "Add GitHub
Account…" settings sheet per `docs/GITHUB-OAUTH-DESIGN.md`. The OAuth
seam (#180) was the state machine; this is the flow that drives it.

- **`Sources/App/Settings/AddGithubAccountSheet.swift`** — the sheet:
  choose browser sign-in or token; device flow shows the `user_code`
  with an "Open GitHub" button and a cancellable poll spinner; token
  mode is a `SecureField`; repo step shows the signed-in identity +
  granted scopes, owner/repo fields with a Check that fetches the
  default branch, and Clone & Add.
- **`AddGithubFlowModel.swift`** (`@MainActor @Observable`, app-side
  glue like `PreviewWebModel`) — runs the device-code request, opens
  the browser, polls in a cancellable `Task` (cancel wipes the token),
  verifies via `GET /user`, resolves the repo, then clone → Keychain →
  `WorkspaceStore.addGithub`. The token lives in a `SecureBuffer`,
  wiped on cancel / dismiss / finish.
- **`GithubAPIClient.swift`** — `GET /user` + `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`
  (default branch from the remote, never guessed). Tokens ride the new
  transport `get(_:bearer:)` seam as `SecureBuffer`; non-2xx bodies
  surface as `GithubOAuthError.httpStatus(status, message)` — never
  swallowed (D11).
- **`GithubTokenStore.swift`** (`Sources/Security/`) — Keychain-only
  lifecycle, account `github:<owner>/<repo>` (matches
  `GithubSource.tokenAccount`); the token never touches UserDefaults /
  plists / argv / env / logs.
- **`WorkspaceStore`** — `addGithub` (bookmark + beginAccess + select +
  persist), github-aware `beginAccess`/`resolvedURL`/`relocate`, and
  `PersistedWorkspace.github` load/persist so the source survives
  relaunch.
- **`GitClone.clone`** — new `environment:` param; the default sets
  `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so a private repo without credentials fails
  fast with git's own error instead of hanging on a hidden prompt
  (the credential-helper slice makes private clones work).
- **`Project.yml`** — `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` build setting →
  `GithubOAuthClientID` Info.plist key (operator step, public by
  design; empty = sheet offers the token path only, flow never dead).

## Tests (10 new, no network)

`GithubAPIClientTests` — user decode (with/without name), repo decode
(public/private, default branch), 404 message surfaced, malformed body
→ invalidResponse, bearer rides the GET. `GithubTokenStoreTests` —
save/load/delete isolation, overwrite, Keychain account parity with
`GithubSource.tokenAccount`. Shared doubles moved to
`GithubTestSupport.swift` (transport gained `get`; `form` optional in
recorded calls).

## Notable decisions

- Token is persisted **before** the clone (design §3 step 5): a save
  failure aborts cleanly with nothing on disk; a clone failure leaves
  the token in the Keychain — accepted, same posture as any OAuth app.
- The flow model is app-side (not unit-tested) matching the codebase's
  view-model pattern; the logic it calls (OAuth state machine, API
  client, token store, clone) is all tested.

## Gates

`SKIP_EMBED_BORIS=1 make build` ✅ · `make test` 305 tests, 0 failures
✅ · `make lint` 0 violations (SwiftFormat + SwiftLint --strict) ✅ ·
spike scheme ✅.

author: ssdavidai
body:
## What changed

- gives every active sprint one durable remote branch and Superset integration worktree
- pins planning and worker branches to the exact sprint checkout
- automatically squash-merges only CI-green, exact-SHA-reviewed lane PRs into that sprint branch
- opens one final sprint delivery PR to `main`, runs full CI and a read-only exact-SHA retrospective, and merges only after both pass
- keeps issues open as `integrated` until final delivery, then closes issues and the sprint
- exposes the integration branch, worktree, PR, retro state, and failures on the local dashboard
- adds schema-v9 migration, guarded merge/base validation, configuration gates, documentation, and regression coverage

## Why

The existing controller stopped each lane at `ready_merge`, targeted `main`, and could close a sprint without a combined integration boundary. That required repeated manual merges and provided no final whole-sprint verification.

## Safety

Agents still cannot commit, push, merge, or access GitHub. The trusted controller binds every merge to the reviewed head SHA, validates the expected base branch, respects branch protection, and never uses `--admin`, force-push, reset, or branch deletion. The feature is config-gated.

## Validation

- `python3 -m compileall -q src tests`
- `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q` — 241 passed, 7 subtests passed
- `git diff --check`

## โจทย์

> "อยากปรับ สเตจ RD รับเรื่อง ยังไม่ต้องใส่วันกำหนดส่ง แต่ให้ยืนยัน เพื่อเข้าสถานะ รอกำหนดส่ง แล้วเพิ่มการกด แจ้งกำหนดส่งเป็นอีกสเตป เพื่อให้การรับเรื่องเป็นเหมือนการตัดรอบ และ บางที รับเรื่องแล้วแต่ยังไม่สามารถแจ้งกำหนดได้เพราะรอส่วนอื่นๆ"

ทับมติ 2026-08-08 ที่บังคับวันกำหนดส่งตอนกดรับเรื่องทุกหัวข้อ — เหตุผลที่มติเดิมพัง: ฝ่ายรับเรื่องบ่อยครั้งยังตอบวันไม่ได้จริงตอนกดรับ ⇒ เหลือทางเลือกที่แย่ทั้งคู่ (เดาวันไปก่อนแล้วเลื่อนทีหลัง หรือไม่กดรับเลย แล้วใบค้างที่ "รอรับเรื่อง" ทั้งที่ฝ่ายดูอยู่)

## สามก้าว สามความหมาย

| ก้าว | action | ความหมาย | เธรด |
|---|---|---|---|
| รับเรื่อง | `acknowledge` | ตัดรอบเข้าฝ่าย (โมดัลยืนยัน ไม่ถามวัน) | `acknowledge` |
| แจ้งกำหนดส่ง | `commit-due` | รับปากวันครั้งแรก | `commitDue` (ใหม่) |
| เลื่อนวันกำหนดส่ง | `reschedule` | แก้คำสัญญาที่ให้ไปแล้ว (ต้องมีวันเดิมก่อน) | `reschedule` |

- **"รอกำหนดส่ง" เป็นสถานะที่ derive** (`acknowledged` + ยังไม่มี `committedDueDate` — `requestAwaitingDue`) **ไม่เพิ่มค่าลง `REQUEST_STATUSES`** ⇒ ไม่มี migration และไม่ต้องไล่แก้ทุกด่าน/ตัวกรอง/trigger
- ป้ายบนคิวทับได้ **เฉพาะก้าวที่เป็นของฝ่าย** — เวอร์ชันแรกทับทุกก้าว ทำให้ใบที่ฝ่ายส่งครบแล้วรอผู้ขอปิดกลายเป็นงานค้างของฝ่าย
- ก้าว `ack` **รายแถว** ไม่เขียน `committedDueDate` ของใบอีกแล้ว — วันของใบมาจาก `commit-due` ทางเดียวที่ลงเธรดเสมอ

## ราง

- ตารางรายการ (`queueTrack`) 4 → 5 ขั้น: ส่ง · รับเรื่อง · **กำหนดส่ง** · ตอบ · ปิด
- หน้ารายละเอียด (`requestRail`) 5 → 6 ขั้น — ขั้น `commitDue` แทรกที่ตำแหน่ง 2
- `index` ของรางหน้ารายละเอียด **เลิกเท่ากับลำดับสถานะ** (`acknowledged` หยุดที่ 2 จนกว่าจะแจ้งวัน) — จุดที่เคยเกิดบั๊ก "ไฮไลต์ชี้ผิดช่อง" จึงมีเทสต์คุมทั้งจำนวนขั้นและตำแหน่งไฮไลต์
- ใบเก่าที่จบไปแล้วโดยไม่เคยแจ้งวัน = `skip` (หมุดกลวง) ไม่ใช่ `now` ค้างตลอดกาล

## คำที่เปลี่ยน

| เดิม | ใหม่ |
|---|---|
| `อยากได้คำตอบภายใน` / `วันที่ต้องการคำตอบ` / `ผู้ขอต้องการคำตอบ` | **วันที่ต้องการรับงาน** |
| เธรด `ฝ่าย RD รับเรื่องแล้ว — กำลังหาราคา` | `ฝ่าย RD รับเรื่องแล้ว — รอแจ้งกำหนดส่ง` |
| ราง `กำลังหาราคา` | `กำลังดำเนินการ` |

"คำตอบ"/"หาราคา" เหลือมาจากตอนที่คำร้องมีแต่สายขอราคาวัสดุ · แถวเธรดเก่าไม่ backfill (เป็นประวัติ)

## ตรวจแล้ว

- `npm test` 3397 ผ่าน · `eslint` 0 error · `audit:ui` ผ่าน · `check:migrations` ผ่าน · `build` ผ่าน
- เดินกับ dev server จริง: ราง 5 ขั้นบนคิว RD · ราง 6 ขั้นบนหน้าใบ FD-26080007 · ป้าย "ผู้ขอต้องการรับงาน"
- ยิง API จริง: `commit-due` ซ้ำ → 409 "ใบนี้แจ้งกำหนดส่งไปแล้ว" · `acknowledge` ซ้ำ → 409 · ไม่ส่งวัน → 409 (ไม่มีการเขียนข้อมูล)
- ใบเดิมในระบบทั้ง 51 ใบมีวันกำหนดส่งครบ ⇒ ไม่มีใบไหนตกไปอยู่ "รอกำหนดส่ง" ย้อนหลัง
- **ยังไม่ได้เดิน happy path จริง** (รับเรื่อง → แจ้งกำหนดส่ง) เพราะต้องแตะข้อมูลจริง — ขอ UAT ตรงนี้

author: folpe
body:
## Pourquoi

Une Cartographie n'a pas la forme d'un prompt. Un prompt est un gabarit à trou, rempli en une fois. Une Cartographie est un entretien de plusieurs tours qui produit **deux artefacts distincts** — une Carte partageable et un Dossier développé — ce qui demande trois appels au modèle : conduire l'entretien, rendre la Carte, développer le Dossier.

Étendre le schéma `prompts` aurait produit un schéma à moitié vide dans les deux cas.

## Ce que ça ajoute

```
content/cartographies/raison-detre/
├── meta.json          id, catégorie, labels, axes, tours {min, max}
├── entretien.{fr,en}.md    frontmatter + gabarit de conduite
├── carte.{fr,en}.md        consignes de la Carte
└── dossier.{fr,en}.md      consignes du Dossier
```

Trois documents par locale plutôt qu'un seul : les fusionner aurait obligé le site à découper un markdown à l'exécution, avec un format implicite que rien ne validerait.

Nouveaux artefacts : `cartographies.{fr,en}.json`.

## Les garanties ajoutées au validateur

| Garantie | Ce qu'elle empêche |
| --- | --- |
| Vocabulaire fermé des jetons d'exécution | Un `{{CARTE_PRECEDANTE}}` mal orthographié serait lu comme une consigne par le modèle, et l'entretien dériverait sans que rien ne le signale |
| `{{TOURS_MAX}}`, `{{TOUR_COURANT}}`, `{{CARTE_PRECEDENTE}}` exigés | Un gabarit sans bornes ni état : coût non maîtrisé et carte amnésique |
| Axes déclarés une fois, seuls les libellés traduits | Une carte dont la structure change selon la langue |
| Parité stricte des jetons FR/EN | La même classe de défaut que celle déjà couverte pour les variables |
| `promesse` d'au moins 80 caractères | Une promesse creuse. Ce n'est pas cosmétique : c'est le point de conversion, et une promesse faible ne se rattrape pas par un bon entretien puisque l'entretien n'aura pas lieu |

Chacune a été vérifiée en cassant volontairement la source avant d'ouvrir cette PR.

## Le renommage

Première Cartographie : **Raison d'Être**, l'ex-« Ikigai ».

Le diagramme à quatre cercles est celui d'Andrés Zuzunaga, publié en 2012 sous le titre « Propósito ». Il est appelé « ikigai » depuis un billet de blog de Marc Winn en 2014, mais il n'est ni japonais ni l'ikigai. Le terme est rendu à l'échelle Ikigai-9, qui mesure réellement ce concept. Un champ `attribution` porte cette précision dans le contenu, pour qu'elle soit affichable et pas seulement documentée.

## Ce que cette PR ne fait pas

Le prompt `ikigai-archeologie` est **délibérément conservé**. Le site ne sait pas encore servir une Cartographie ; le retirer maintenant supprimerait sa page la plus consultée sans remplacement. La suppression et la redirection permanente viendront avec la mise en service.

## Vérification

`npm run check` vert : validation, build, artefacts à jour.

author: marwin11golz
body:
Handy und iPad teilen sich denselben Kartenstapel. Fünf getrennte Commits, damit nachvollziehbar bleibt, was wozu gehört.

## P0 — Zugangsdaten absichern
`.gitignore` ignoriert `.env`-Dateien (Vorlage `.env.example` ausgenommen), **bevor** der erste Schlüssel ins Spiel kommt. Die Warnung bei fehlgeschlagenem Speichern wurde bisher gesetzt, aber nirgends angezeigt.

## P1 — Code in Bausteine aufteilen
`App.jsx` enthielt alles in einer Datei. Lernlogik → `src/lib/srs.js`, Farbwelt → `src/lib/theme.js`. Reines Verschieben, kein Verhaltensunterschied.

## P2 — Kartenschema für den Abgleich
Jede Karte bekommt `updatedAt` und `deleted`. Löschen **markiert** die Karte, statt sie zu entfernen — sonst lässt das andere Gerät gelöschte Karten wieder auferstehen. Zustand und Speicherung liegen in `useVocabStore`, das nach außen nur Absichten anbietet, damit keine Änderung den Zeitstempel vergessen kann.

**Kritischer Punkt:** Der Zeitstempel für Altkarten wird aus `lastReviewed`/`createdAt` **abgeleitet**, nicht auf „jetzt" gesetzt. Beide Geräte tragen dieselben Altkarten; bei „jetzt" würde das Gerät, das die App als zweites öffnet, jede Karte gewinnen und den Lernfortschritt des anderen still überschreiben. Abgeleitet entsteht ein Gleichstand, den `pickWinner()` zugunsten des höheren `totalReviews` auflöst.

Nebenbei behoben: Der Import aktualisierte bestehende Karten nie und überschrieb Lerntage. `rateCard` bewertet die gespeicherte Karte statt einer Momentaufnahme aus der Warteschlange.

## P3 — Echte App statt Lesezeichen
`vite-plugin-pwa` mit `autoUpdate`. iOS wertet das Manifest nicht aus, deshalb zusätzlich die `apple-*`-Angaben — erst `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` entfernt die Safari-Leiste. Abstand zum Notch über `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Bewusst **kein** `runtimeCaching`: Datenbankantworten dürfen nie aus dem Zwischenspeicher kommen.

## P4 — Abgleich über Supabase
Die App bleibt local-first: ohne Konto und ohne Netz funktioniert alles wie bisher, der Abgleich liegt als Schicht darüber.

Entscheidungen, die konkrete Fehler verhindern:
- **Zeitstempel werden normalisiert.** Postgres liefert `…762+00:00`, lokal entsteht `…762Z`. Als Zeichenkette verglichen wäre ein Gleichstand fälschlich ein Unterschied (`+` sortiert vor `Z`) — die Geräte würden sich endlos gegenseitig überschreiben.
- **`updated_at` kommt vom Client, nicht von `now()`.** Sonst käme jede hochgeladene Karte mit neuerem Zeitstempel zurück und sähe wieder geändert aus.
- **Die Hochlade-Menge wird aus dem Zusammenführen abgeleitet**, nicht über eine Merkliste. Offline Geändertes ist automatisch neuer; ein abgebrochener Upload heilt sich selbst.
- **Lernaktivität pro Gerät.** Jedes Gerät schreibt nur seine eigene Zeile — würde der zusammengerechnete Anzeigewert hochgeladen, würden sich die Zahlen bei jedem Abgleich aufschaukeln.
- **`revision` steigt nur bei echten Nutzeränderungen**, damit ein Abruf nie ein Hochladen auslöst.
- Während einer Lernsitzung wird nicht abgeglichen.
- Vor dem ersten Abgleich eines Kontos wird der lokale Stand gesichert; meldet sich ein anderes Konto an, wird gefragt statt hochzuladen.

Kein Realtime-Websocket: Für zwei Geräte, die nie gleichzeitig laufen, ist ein Abruf beim Wechsel in den Vordergrund praktisch nicht unterscheidbar — aber deutlich einfacher.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` ohne Fehler
- [x] 16 Zusammenführ-Tests
- [x] 38 Tests der Abgleich-Logik gegen eine nachgebaute Datenbank: Vorrang des jüngeren Standes, Löschung setzt sich durch, Gleichstand nach Migration lädt Fortschritt hoch, **kein Dauer-Hochladen bei identischem Stand**, Aktivität pro Gerät, Fehlerfall lässt lokalen Stand unberührt, Postgres-Zeitstempel kollidiert nicht
- [x] 21 Browser-Prüfungen: Migration von Altdaten, Sicherungskopie, Löschung als Grabstein, Bewerten, Export
- [x] 19 PWA-Prüfungen gegen den Produktionsbuild inkl. Offline-Start
- [x] Browser-Läufe **mit** und **ohne** hinterlegte Zugangsdaten — ohne Zugangsdaten zeigt die App einen Hinweis statt abzustürzen; ein fehlgeschlagener Anmeldeversuch liefert eine deutsche Meldung und lässt die Vokabeln unangetastet
- [x] Zugriffsschutz in der Datenbank geprüft: RLS auf allen drei Tabellen aktiv, je eine Richtlinie auf `authenticated`, ohne Anmeldung liefert `auth.uid()` NULL und damit keine Zeile; Supabase-Sicherheitsprüfung ohne Beanstandung
- [ ] **Offen:** der Lauf über zwei echte Geräte — diese Arbeitsumgebung darf `supabase.co` nicht erreichen

## Nach dem Merge
1. **Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables:** `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` und `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` eintragen (Production, Preview, Development), dann **Redeploy** — die Werte werden beim Bauen eingesetzt
2. Auf beiden Geräten das Symbol vom Startbildschirm löschen und neu hinzufügen (iOS übernimmt Symbol und Name nur beim Installieren)
3. Auf beiden Geräten mit **derselben** E-Mail anmelden — ein zweites Konto wäre ein zweiter, getrennter Kartenstapel

body:
Robust authentication layer for device-to-backend communication, fulfilling the P0-02 audit requirement for security.

* Database: Added `token_hash` column to `device_settings` table to store non-reversible device credentials.
* API Security:
    * Implemented SHA-256 hash validation across `POST /trash-events`, `POST /device/sync`, and `PATCH /device/commands`.
    * Added input sanitization (`.trim()`) to `deviceToken` to prevent cross-platform (Windows/Linux) newline character mismatches.
    * Integrated `Bypass-Tunnel-Reminder` header handling to support LocalTunnel/Ngrok proxy environments.
* Edge/Python:
    * Updated `main.py` to use secure `.env` token injection with whitespace stripping.
    * Added support for the required proxy bypass header to prevent request timeouts.
* Middleware: Restricted dashboard data access (`GET` endpoints for telemetry and configs) to users with `read:dashboard` permissions.

This change ensures that only devices with a matching token-hash can interact with the API, preventing unauthorized data injection.

PR Checklist:

[ ] Run npm run migrate:up to add the token_hash column.

[ ] Generate a new hash from the test token using node -e "...".

[ ] Update the device_settings record with the new hash.

[ ] Update the .env on the test edge device with the raw token.

author: meawoppl
body:
Matt's ask: the published crate version should **link to the tested CLI version**. It did — but only via README prose, and the one programmatic pin that existed had silently drifted: codex's private `TESTED_VERSION` const still said **0.146.0** while its README said 0.147.0, so the runtime newer-version warning was keyed off a stale baseline.

Now the link is machine-readable from every published artifact and cannot drift:

- **`version::tested_cli_version()`** in all four crates (muse gains it as a uniform alias over its existing `TESTED_MUSE_VERSION`/`TESTED_MUSE_BUILD` pins — nearly clobbered those before noticing muse had solved this first)
- **CI lockstep clauses**: the consistency check now compares each const against its README `Tested against:` line — the codex-style silent drift fails the build from here on
- **opencode's live watchdog** asserts the server against `tested_cli_version()` instead of `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` — the correct semantic under version-means-tested, and crate-side patch offsets no longer trip it
- Trains: claude → **2.1.234**, opencode → **1.18.19** (published numbers were taken; offsets noted in README bullets); codex/muse absorb into unpublished 0.147.0/0.1.8

All suites green, workspace clippy clean, consistency clauses verified locally.

O conflito textual foi pequeno (2 arquivos, 3 hunks). O caro foi o que o git **não** marca.

## 1. Assinatura mudou

`providerForFallbackCandidate` passou a receber o `FallbackCandidate` inteiro em vez de provider+model. Três chamadas nossas, todas em código do fork: `llm_media.go` (delegação de visão e de cron) e `llm_media_delegate.go`.

## 2. Provider primário — este quebrava produção

O upstream passou a devolver um `unavailableLLMProvider` (um provider que falha em **toda** chamada, com mensagem amigável) quando o provider do modelo não sobe. Aqui isso transforma *"um modelo com problema"* em *"assistente mudo"* — o modo de falha que já nos custou caro em conversa morta e resposta vazia.

Mantida a escolha deste fork: **cai no provider injetado**, que é construído da mesma configuração e funciona. O `unavailableLLMProvider` continua valendo para os **candidatos de fallback**, onde não existe injetado para onde voltar e a mensagem amigável é melhor que um erro cru.

## 3. Configuração sintetizada

O `resolvedRuntimeModelConfig` novo monta uma configuração a partir dos defaults quando o modelo não é entrada do `model_list` **nem** casa com template de provider: sai um `api_base` padrão e **nenhuma chave**. O provider que nasce daí responde 401 em tudo — e substituía o injetado, derrubando 4 suítes.

Agora só assume quando há entrada explícita ou credencial para herdar. O casamento por template do upstream (modelo cru sob provider configurado) continua valendo — o teste deles cobre e passa.

## Por que isso virou teste

Os itens 2 e 3 foram **regressões silenciosas**: o merge não marcou conflito em nenhum dos dois. `TestResolvePrimaryProviderForAgent_MantemProviderInjetado` trava os três casos (provider não sobe / sem credencial para herdar / entrada explícita sem chave ainda resolve), para a próxima sincronização não desfazer de novo sem ninguém ver.

## Tiers e cron

Continuam populando providers **por nome**, ao lado da herança por candidato que o upstream trouxe: o caminho novo só cobre quem virou candidato, e fallback declarado por nome ficaria sem provider.

## Verificação

- `pkg/agent`: **0 falhas** (eram 34 no meio do caminho, 28 delas com a mesma causa — o item 2).
- `golangci-lint run`: 0 issues.
- As 3 falhas de `pkg/tools` na minha máquina são as conhecidas de macOS (diretório temporário com symlink).
- Validação ponta a ponta no kind com o control plane real vai no comentário abaixo.

body:
Closes #12

## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (runs on `windows-latest`, on pull requests targeting
`main` and on pushes to `main`) plus `PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` at the repo root.
No changes to `dev_drive.ps1` or `README.md`.

### What each step does

1. **Parse dev_drive.ps1 syntax** - `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile`
   against `dev_drive.ps1`; fails the job on any parse error.
2. **Install / Run PSScriptAnalyzer** - installs PSScriptAnalyzer pinned to `1.25.0`, then
   runs `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`
   and fails the job on any finding the settings file does not exclude.
3. **Run Pester tests** - only if at least one `*.Tests.ps1` file exists in the repo (after
   excluding `.claude` - see below). Today there are none, so the step emits a `::notice::`
   and exits 0 without failing the build. The check is data-driven, not a manual flag: the
   moment a `*.Tests.ps1` file lands, this same step installs Pester (pinned to `6.1.0`),
   runs it, and enforces pass/fail via `Run.Exit = $true` - no further workflow change
   needed, and it cannot silently stay a no-op forever. Verified locally that a failing test
   makes the step's PowerShell process exit 1, and a passing one exits 0.

Both PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester versions are pinned via workflow `env:` so a PowerShell
Gallery release cannot turn the build red on its own. Pester is pinned to `6.1.0` rather
than an older `5.x` release specifically to match what contributors run locally, so a suite
that passes on a dev machine can't fail here (or vice versa) purely from a Pester
major-version difference.

**`.claude` worktree trap.** This repo keeps git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. On
Windows only `.git` carries the Hidden attribute here - `.claude` does not - so a plain
`Get-ChildItem -Recurse` (the detection gate) already walks into it, and Pester 6 changed
its own discovery to use `Get-ChildItem -Force` (which finds anything under a dot-prefixed
folder except `.git`/`.svn`/`.hg`). Left unpruned, a local run from the repo root would
also pick up and run every other worktree's copy of the suite, each checked out at a
possibly different commit. Both the detection gate and `$config.Run.ExcludePath` now prune
`.claude` explicitly (resolved to an absolute path at run time, so it works regardless of
checkout location); commented in the workflow. Verified locally with a decoy test file
under a fake `.claude/worktrees/...` path plus a real one at the repo root: without the
exclusion Pester (6.1.0) ran both; with it, only the root one.

**`-SkipPublisherCheck` asymmetry.** Present on the Pester install only, because Windows
ships an in-box Pester module signed by Microsoft while the PSGallery build is signed by
the Pester team - the flag suppresses that specific publisher mismatch. PSScriptAnalyzer
has no in-box copy on Windows, so there's no mismatch to suppress there, and adding the
flag would only weaken verification for no reason. Both install steps now carry a comment
saying so, so the asymmetry reads as deliberate. (Raised by a review bot on this PR; replied
in the discussion thread with the same reasoning.)

**Safety:** no step executes `dev_drive.ps1`, `diskpart`, `Format-Volume`, `New-Partition`,
or anything else touching storage - the workflow only parses, lints, and (now) unit-tests
the script from the outside.

### Analyzer rules excluded, and why

Three of the four exclusions are tracked by an issue that will let the rule be
re-enabled once fixed; the fourth is a deliberate, permanent choice.

- `PSUseApprovedVerbs` - `Prompt-BitLockerChoice` / `Prompt-DeduplicationChoice` /
  `Prompt-CompressionFormat` / `Prompt-CompressionLevel` use the unapproved verb `Prompt`.
  Renaming them is tracked in #11.
- `PSAvoidUsingEmptyCatchBlock` - the empty `catch` around line 662 that lets configuring
  one scheduled dedup task fail without aborting the others. Tracked in #16.
- `PSUseDeclaredVarsMoreThanAssignments` - `$creationMethod`, `$bitLockerChoice`,
  `$deduplicationChoice` are built but never printed. Tracked in #17.
- `PSAvoidUsingWriteHost` (permanent) - `dev_drive.ps1` is an interactive console script run
  directly at a terminal (`#Requires -RunAsAdministrator`, `Read-Host` prompts throughout).
  Its colored `Write-Host` output is the intended UI, not diagnostic noise competing with a
  caller's own output stream, so the rule's rationale doesn't apply. Judgment call, open to
  disagreement.

### Local verification

- PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 and Pester 6.1.0 installed from PSGallery locally (matching the
  versions pinned in the workflow) to test all steps before pushing.
- Syntax parse step: ran locally against `dev_drive.ps1` - 0 parse errors.
- PSScriptAnalyzer step: ran locally with `-Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` over
  the repo - 0 findings outside the excluded rules.
- Pester step, no-tests branch: ran locally with no `*.Tests.ps1` files present in the repo -
  emits the `::notice::` and exits 0, as intended.
- Pester step, tests-exist branch: ran the exact step script in a fresh `pwsh` process
  against a temporary `dev_drive.Tests.ps1` at the repo root (removed afterward, not
  committed) under both Pester 5.9.1 and 6.1.0 - a failing test exits 1, a passing test
  exits 0.
- `.claude` exclusion: reproduced the worktree trap with a decoy `*.Tests.ps1` under a fake
  `.claude/worktrees/...` path - confirmed both the detection gate and Pester 6.1.0's own
  discovery pick it up without the exclusion, and skip it with `ExcludePath` set.
- Workflow YAML: parsed with `ConvertFrom-Yaml` (via the `powershell-yaml` module) after
  every change to confirm it stays structurally valid.
- Confirmed on the actual GitHub Actions run for this PR (initial version, before the Pester
  6 / `.claude` update): `validate` passed, all three steps green, Pester correctly no-op'd
  with the notice.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

`klt lvs --check <report> --rerun` reconstructed the compare it re-runs from
the committed report's own echoed fields, but those fields were lossy: the
report recorded a single `top` and no `options` block. Full mode therefore
applied that one top to **both** sides and dropped every compare-shaping
option, so:

- a report from an **LVS negative control** (a `<cell>_shorted` layout
  compared against the intact `<cell>`'s reference netlist — two different
  tops by construction) exited `1` with `top cell/subcircuit '<x>' not found
  in reference netlist`; and
- a clean `status: "match"` report from a `combine_devices: true` request
  re-ran **un-folded** and reported the resulting fresh mismatch list as
  `status: "drifted"` — a spurious "your evidence drifted" verdict about a
  compare the consumer never asked for.

Fixed by direction 1 of the issue ("record enough to reconstruct"), which the
Curator recommended: the report now echoes the reference-side top and the
`options` block as used, and the reconstruction consumes both.

## Changes

- `src/klayout_tools/lvs.py`
  - `run_lvs()` response gains two **additive** fields: `reference_top` (the
    reference side's own resolved top circuit) and `options`
    (`combine_devices`, `flatten_layout`, `flatten_reference`,
    `netgen_setup`, `parameter_tolerance` — every key always present with its
    effective value). `top` and the top-level `parameter_tolerance` are
    unchanged. `options.keep_extracted` and `options.netgen_timeout_s` are
    deliberately not echoed (neither can change a verdict; the first is
    already visible as `environment.extracted_netlist`).
  - `_reconstruct_lvs_request()` applies each side's own top and rebuilds the
    full `options` block, instead of reusing the one `top` for both sides and
    rebuilding `options` from `parameter_tolerance` alone. Reports predating
    the new fields fall back to the previous behavior exactly.
  - `rerun_lvs_report()` excludes `reference_top`/`options` from the drift
    diff when the **committed** report predates them — a field a report never
    carried cannot itself have drifted, so an older committed report re-runs
    exactly as accurately (and exactly as best-effort) as it did before.
- `src/klayout_tools/cli/lvs_cmd.py` — text output prints a `reference top:`
  line only when the two sides resolved to different circuits, so ordinary
  human output is unchanged. No new `status` value and no new exit code.
- `docs/cli/lvs.md` — response example + field-table rows for the two new
  fields; the `--rerun` "Known limitations" paragraph no longer lists
  `reference.top`/`options.*` as unreconstructable, and gains an explicit
  paragraph on pre-#1205 committed reports.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `Unreleased` → `Fixed since release` entry.

### Schema-version decision

**No `schema_version` bump** (`klt lvs` stays at `1`). Per
[`docs/json-contract.md`](docs/json-contract.md) ("additive envelope, not a
wrapping envelope"): a command bumps its own `schema_version` only for a
non-additive (breaking) change; *adding* fields is explicitly not one. No
existing field is renamed, removed, or retyped — verified by re-reading the
policy and by `test_run_lvs_echoes_reference_top_and_options`, which asserts
`schema_version == 1` alongside the untouched `top`/`parameter_tolerance`.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

- [x] **`--rerun` on a report with `reference.top` != layout top no longer
      raises** — `test_rerun_lvs_report_reconstructs_asymmetric_reference_top`
      re-runs a negative-control report (`INV_SHORTED` vs. `INV`) with
      `status: "match"`, `drift: []`, fresh verdict `mismatch` (the committed
      one). Manually confirmed via the CLI (below): exit `1` before, exit `0`
      after.
- [x] **`--rerun` on an `options.combine_devices` report no longer reports
      spurious drift** — `test_rerun_lvs_report_preserves_combine_devices_option`.
      Manually confirmed: exit `3` / `status: drifted` before, exit `0` /
      `status: match` after.
- [x] **Applied consistently** — the report grew the fields needed to
      round-trip both, rather than half-guessing; the remaining documented
      gaps (`reference.form`, `device_map`/`device_bulk`,
      `top_cell_pins`/`declared_pins`, and the `layout.netlist`+`layout.deck`
      shape ambiguity) are unchanged in behavior and still documented as
      "use cheap mode".
- [x] **`docs/cli/lvs.md`'s `--rerun` "Known limitations" updated** — the two
      fixed items are removed from the list, and the pre-#1205-report case is
      described explicitly.
- [x] **`SCHEMA_VERSION` checked against `docs/json-contract.md`** — see
      "Schema-version decision" above: additive, no bump.
- [x] **Cheap `--check` unaffected** —
      `test_check_lvs_report_cheap_mode_unaffected_by_asymmetric_top`, plus
      the four pre-existing `check_lvs_report` tests, unmodified.

## Test Plan

**TDD:** the two reproduction tests
(`test_rerun_lvs_report_reconstructs_asymmetric_reference_top`,
`test_rerun_lvs_report_preserves_combine_devices_option`) encode the issue's
own two reproductions; both were confirmed failing against `main` (`dc3bb0e`)
by running the identical scenarios through the pre-fix build — the first
exits `1` (`klt lvs: top cell/subcircuit 'INV_SHORTED' not found in reference
netlist`), the second exits `3` with `status: drifted` and a fresh
`device.property`/`device.unmatched` mismatch list — before the fix was
written.

New tests in `tests/test_lvs.py`:

- `test_run_lvs_echoes_reference_top_and_options` — the new report fields and
  the unchanged pre-existing ones.
- `test_rerun_lvs_report_reconstructs_asymmetric_reference_top` — (a) the
  negative-control round-trip.
- `test_rerun_lvs_report_preserves_combine_devices_option` — (b) the folded
  `combine_devices` round-trip, no spurious drift.
- `test_rerun_lvs_report_without_combine_devices_still_drifts_on_real_change`
  — the round-trip does not paper over a *real* input change.
- `test_rerun_lvs_report_preserves_parameter_tolerance_in_options_block` —
  the doubly-echoed tolerance resolves to one value.
- `test_rerun_lvs_report_legacy_report_without_request_echo_fields` — a
  report with the new fields stripped re-runs with no drift (back-compat).
- `test_check_lvs_report_cheap_mode_unaffected_by_asymmetric_top` — (c) cheap
  mode still works on exactly the reports full mode used to choke on.

Runs:

- `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_lvs.py tests/test_cli.py
  tests/test_drc.py tests/test_signoff.py` — all pass.
- Full suite (`npm run test`): 45 failures, **all pre-existing and unrelated**
  — `test_equiv`/`test_synthesize*`/`test_techmap*`/`test_place_and_route`/
  `test_gallery_signals`, i.e. the external-toolchain tests (yosys cannot open
  its own `.klt/equiv/equiv.ys`, OpenROAD, icarus). Verified pre-existing by
  reproducing `tests/test_equiv.py::test_cli_equivalent_exits_zero` against an
  unmodified `main` checkout at `dc3bb0e`. Nothing under `tests/test_lvs.py`
  fails.
- `npm run lint` (`ruff format --check .` + `ruff check .`) — clean.
- Manual CLI verification of the issue's own reproduction, before vs. after,
  on the pre-extracted-netlist form of the negative control and the folded
  `combine_devices` case:

  | scenario | before (`dc3bb0e`) | after |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `klt lvs --check neg.report.json --rerun` | exit `1`, `top cell/subcircuit 'INV_SHORTED' not found in reference netlist` | exit `0`, `status: match` |
  | `klt lvs --check fold.report.json --rerun` | exit `3`, `status: drifted` (fresh `device.property` + `device.unmatched`) | exit `0`, `status: match` |
  | `klt lvs --check neg.report.json` (cheap) | exit `0`, `status: match` | exit `0`, `status: match` (unchanged) |

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Lease fence + push credential.** `./.loom/scripts/sweep-lease-fence.sh
  check 1205` returned `3` (`ABORT: EXPIRED`) — the lease comment is this
  sweep's **own** (`host=host-d0749b00`, not superseded by

body:
Closes #264.

The counts in the issue are from before the screen splits: what was left is 60 emoji in the tournament admin, 12 on the registration form and a handful of `⏳` standing in for a spinner. The public tournament page and the leaderboard are already clean.

Those are now `Icon` and `IconLabel`, so they take the colour of the text around them instead of dropping a coloured glyph onto a tinted background. The five `⏳` become `PageLoading`, which is the spinner the rest of the app uses and carries a screen reader label the emoji never had.

What stays, and why, is now a list in `eslint.config.mjs` rather than something to rediscover: the yellow and red cards and the Mauritanian flag, where the colour is the whole message, and three push notification bodies, which are plain text and cannot carry an SVG. A lint rule holds the line — an emoji anywhere else in `src` now fails the build.

author: fw-bot
body:
Some generic validation errors raised by core account models lack enough context to identify which record caused the issue, making FEC imports harder to troubleshoot.

This commit improves the two error cases identified for this use case:
- `account.account._check_account_code` now includes the invalid account code in the error message.
- `account.move.write` now includes the move name/reference and displays human-readable field labels instead of technical field names when attempting to modify read-only fields on posted entries.

Although motivated by FEC import, these are generic core validations, so the improvements are implemented at the source to benefit all callers rather than only the FEC import flow.

Enrichment is scoped to the two cases above, other constraints/errors across these models are intentionally left unchanged for now, since editing core error messages more broadly should be done deliberately and on a case-by-case basis, not as a blanket rewrite

author: abibifogh
body:
Four changes, all from reading the live guide. Merging deploys them.

## Tapping a pin no longer moves you down the page

It used to scroll the reader to that place's card, which lost their position in the list. Now it fills the panel beside the map and does nothing else.

On a phone that panel would sit below the fold, so it opens as a sheet over the map instead, with a close button, a scrim you can tap, and an Escape handler. The "Full entry" link is still there for anyone who does want the card.

## The maps zoom and pan

Buttons, scroll wheel, double-click, double-tap and pinch, with the current level shown and a reset.

Three things that had to be right for it to feel like a map rather than a scaled image:

- **Labels, pin radii and stroke widths are divided by the zoom**, so they hold their size on screen instead of ballooning as you go in.
- **Panning rewrites the viewBox rather than re-rendering.** Re-rendering mid-drag replaced the pins under the pointer and made the drag stutter.
- **A drag's window listeners are added on mousedown and removed on mouseup.** They were being attached inside the render, so every redraw added another set. Playwright caught this as "element is not stable".

On touch, the map only claims the gesture once you have zoomed in, so at rest a thumb on the map still scrolls the page.

## Beds and food are out of the trip tally

Guests are sleeping in our beds, so quoting them accommodation on top read badly. The total is entry fees plus travel now, and the panel says so.

## The calendar moves above the map

When you are here decides where you can go, so it belongs before the choosing rather than after it. The numbered steps follow it: interests, timing, map, places.

## The copy has been rewritten

Em dashes are gone from every line of guest-facing text, about a hundred and thirty of them. They were not swapped one for one; each sentence got the mark it actually wanted, which in most cases meant becoming two sentences. Appositive piles like *"Ahanta Waves — the first Ghanaian-owned surf school, started by a Busua local — will get you..."* have been unpacked, and the intensifiers that were doing no work went with them.

Only code comments and the clock placeholder still contain the character.

## Checks

Run in Chromium at 1360px and 390px:

- pin click leaves `scrollY` unchanged (was the bug)
- viewBox changes on zoom, level readout tracks it, reset returns to 1×
- close button and scrim both clear the selection
- mobile sheet and scrim appear and dismiss
- tally shows fees + transport only, with no beds row
- no JS errors

Ports the three features the MBF companions gained since `aj.js` was cut, keeping the sibling discipline (own copies, no shared imports from `mbf.js`):

- **Speaking**: Speak button + `POST /api/aj/transcribe`, an exact mirror of MBF's OpenAI transcription. Gated by the AJ access code, 503 without `OPENAI_API_KEY`, 25MB cap, transcript goes into the textarea for review and is never auto-submitted.
- **Send to Chad**: buttons in the top bar and the closing panel, backed by `POST /api/aj/send` via Resend. Fires only when the person presses it. author: dorokuma
body:
## What

Adds an AgentHistoryReader for Antigravity CLI (agy), so Shepherd can surface the last assistant message for agy agents managed through Herdr (agent_session refs with source herdr:antigravity_cli previously resolved to unknown, leaving wake summaries empty).

## How

- New AgyHistoryReader parses ${HOME}/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<sessionId>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl. Line mapping: USER_INPUT -> user; PLANNER_RESPONSE with text content -> assistant; PLANNER_RESPONSE with only tool_calls -> tool_result (tool name from the first call). Malformed lines are skipped, matching the existing readers.
- historySourceFromSessionRef maps agent agy / antigravity* refs to the new agy-jsonl source. Discovery resolves kind: id refs to the transcript path and scans the brain directory (most recently modified transcript first).
- Directory auto-discovery filters candidate transcripts by the agent's cwd using conversation_summaries.db (workspace_uris), so concurrently running agy agents do not pick up each other's transcripts. When no conversation matches the cwd, discovery returns no history instead of an unrelated one. If the summaries database is missing or unreadable, discovery falls back to the newest transcript.
- The agy-jsonl source type is appended to the AgentHistoryRef union; AgyHistoryReader is appended to the default reader list. No existing reader is touched.

## Testing

- 12 new unit tests: multi-turn parsing, tool-only responses, empty file, malformed JSON lines, missing file, session-id path resolution, default service registration, source mapping, brain directory discovery, mtime ordering across multiple sessions, cwd filtering via conversation summaries, no-cwd-match returning no history.
- Full suite: 239 tests passing. tsc --noEmit, biome check, and build are clean.

Note: agy transcripts do not embed a cwd; directory auto-discovery matches the agent's cwd against conversation_summaries.db when available and falls back to the newest transcript otherwise.

author: izzywdev
body:
Two things: unblocks Kafka UI, and documents the one manual dependency in the SSO chain.

## Kafka UI — why it alone stayed broken

After the IdP was fixed to advertise `https://` issuers, **Grafana recovered immediately but Kafka UI kept failing with "Invalid credentials".**

The difference is discovery. Grafana is configured with explicit URLs. Kafka UI is Spring Security, which fetches the issuer's discovery document **once at startup** and caches it for the life of the process. Its pod booted while the IdP was still advertising `http://` endpoints and has been holding them ever since — and nothing in its Deployment changed, so Argo had no reason to restart it.

Adds a `checksum/oidc` pod annotation hashing the `kafkaUi.oidc` block, so any future change to the issuer, client id or secret reference forces a fresh discovery fetch. Same pattern as `checksum/blueprints` on the Authentik deployments, which exists for exactly this class of bug — config changed, pod never rolled, change appears not to have applied.

Gated on `oidc.enabled`; nothing changes for overlays that do not use it.

## The runbook

`docs/runbooks/google-oauth-manual-dependency.md`.

The original requirement for this work was *"script gitops not clickops, so re-installation will install that too."* Everything honours that **except the Google OAuth client**, and it cannot: Google exposes no API and no Terraform provider for Web-application client IDs or their redirect URIs, and `gcloud alpha iap oauth-clients` covers IAP brands only.

Losing it breaks every admin login **and** every product login simultaneously, with a `redirect_uri_mismatch` that points at the application rather than at a missing Console entry.

The runbook records:

- All three redirect URIs on the `FuzeOne` client and **what each one breaks** — entry 2 carries every customer login, so it matters that an edit does not clobber it
- The separate Cloudflare Access client, and its count-gate hazard: an empty client id/secret makes the Terraform plan a **DESTROY** of the IdP and its policies rather than a no-op
- That the consent screen is in **Testing** mode — a useful second allowlist for admins, but project-wide, so product sign-in is limited to test users too
- An **unauthenticated curl** that reports whether a given redirect URI is registered, so a Console edit can be verified without logging in
- Why this cannot be automated, so nobody re-investigates it

## Verified

`helm lint` clean; the annotation renders under `values-contabo.yaml` and is absent when OIDC is disabled.

**Not verified:** that the rolled pod actually fixes the Kafka UI login. Checking against prod after Argo syncs.

author: atm-jonathan
body:
# FIX Skip usergroup query when no group is selected

`htdocs/holiday/card_group.php` resolves the members of the selected user groups with an unconditional query:

```php
$sql .= ' WHERE  fk_usergroup in (' .$db->sanitize(implode(',', $groups)) . ')';
```

When a group leave request is submitted with **users only**, `$groups` is empty, `implode()` returns an empty string and the query becomes `WHERE fk_usergroup in ()`, which the database rejects:

```
DB_ERROR_SYNTAX You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds
to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near ')'
```

Selecting users without any group is a valid input: the form validation raises an error only when **both** `$groups` and `$users` are empty. The group query must therefore not run in that case.

The leave request is still created, because the failed query returns `false` and the selected users are added right after. The only effect is an SQL error logged on every such submission.

**Fix:** run the group query only when at least one group is selected, consistent with the `/** USERS */` block right below it.

**To reproduce:** Leave requests > New group request, leave *Groups* empty, select one or more users, fill type, dates and approver, then submit. The error above is written to the log.
