author: slin1237
body:
## Description
### Problem
cache_aware matches the full wire `input_ids`, but on multimodal lanes an engine can only share prefix cache across conversations up to the first media placeholder (engine cache keys incorporate media content). Match ratios computed over the full sequence therefore shrink as conversations grow: on a production multimodal video lane, a conversation follow-up (~17k wire tokens containing its ~3k first-turn text) scores matched/raw ~= 0.17 and never returns to the engine holding its conversation state — measured at under 0.1% deep-prefix conversion for the ~37% of traffic that is follow-ups, while an automated fan-out cohort with near-identical prefixes (matched/raw >= 0.92) converts at 78%. No fixed threshold fixes this: third turns score lower still.
### Solution
`--routing-token-boundaries <ids>`: truncate extracted routing tokens at the first occurrence of any configured boundary id (e.g. media placeholder ids) before worker selection, on all three selection paths (HTTP regular, HTTP PD, gRPC pipeline). Matching then covers exactly the engine-shareable, conversation-invariant prefix: a follow-up scores ~1.0 against its own conversation at any length, unrelated requests score near zero. Empty config is byte-identical to today. A boundary in first position yields an empty prefix (match rate 0 → least-loaded), avoiding full-text fallback into the string tree. Truncations are observable via `smg_routing_tokens_truncated_total{router_type}`.

## Changes
- `routers/common/routing_tokens.rs`: shared truncation (borrowed-slice and in-place-owned variants) + metric
- `routers/http/router.rs`: truncation at both token-extraction sites before `SelectWorkerInfo`
- `routers/http/pd_router.rs`: `/generate` routing-input extraction factored into `generate_routing_inputs` with truncation
- gRPC: truncation at the `WorkerSelectionStage` choke point; boundaries plumbed through `PipelineDeps`
- Config: `routing_token_boundaries: Vec<u32>` (types/builder/CLI space-separated list, serde default) + flow test
- Python bindings: field appended at the positional tail (lib.rs x5, `router_args.py`, frozen-sequence tests)

## Composition
The obligation from #2202 is discharged in this PR: `route_streaming_request` truncates hinted tokens at the configured boundaries, and a boundary-emptied hint falls back to buffered routing (body unconsumed). No coordination needed with open PR #2206 (rid-based sticky): rid keys are not token sequences and are unaffected by token truncation.

## Test Plan
- Router (all three paths): follow-up pins to first-turn worker at threshold 0.5 with boundaries (repeat-selection hardened); the same follow-up provably lands elsewhere without boundaries; distinct conversations don't pin; boundary-first and no-boundary edge cases; empty-config identity
- Config: serde default/roundtrip; CLI list flow into `RouterConfig`
- `cargo +nightly fmt --all --check`; targeted module tests green (router 25, PD 12, gRPC selection 5, shared helper 3, config 38, CLI flow 1, pipeline 7); full clippy + suite in CI

<details><summary>Checklist</summary>

- [x] Format clean; lint self-audited (`#[expect]` with reason, no `unwrap` in prod paths)
- [x] Tests added and passing
- [x] Bindings updated (Python); Go unaffected
- [x] DCO sign-off, conventional commit
</details>

author: fiorelorenzo
body:
Issue #278 filed three bounding constants nobody had measured, plus a fourth found while reading. Two of them, `DEFAULT_TOP_K` and `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`, had a blocker written into the issue: no universe of realistic size existed, so issue #168's own sweep ran on 32 chunks and its conclusion about top-k was explicitly conditional on that. Issue #257 landed a real community world in the import formats, which removes the blocker. This is the re-run, plus the audit-cap census and the keyword boost in the same pass.

One number moves. Three stay, and two of the three stay for a different reason than before.

## The corpus, and how it was built

The measurement needed a universe carrying both retrieval layers, which no previous sweep had:

- **Own canon**: the 32-entity bilingual Valdoria Reach, seeded and indexed through `indexEntity` exactly as before. 32 chunks.
- **An imported source**: Valdris, the 78-note CC BY-SA 4.0 community vault issue #257 already renders into the import formats (`offendingcommit/valdris`), read off disk by a new `WikiClient` (`packages/bench/src/corpus/vault.ts`) and indexed as a real `data_source` through `indexDataSource`, into the same per-universe collection. 2293 chunks.

**2325 chunks at 2560 dimensions**, 72 times issue #168's corpus and past `SPEC.md` §11.4's own 2044-chunk reference point.

Two choices worth defending. The vault goes in through the crawl pipeline rather than the LLM import loop because that is the layer this sweep measures (chunk, extract metadata, embed, upsert), and because the loop costs about six credits a note by `docs/demo.md`'s own measurement, which is five hundred credits for this vault and produces extracted proposals rather than indexed prose. And the eighteen `ASK_QUESTIONS` and their gold are unchanged, so every added chunk is pure competition: the question is what 2293 more candidates do to the same retrieval, not whether a new gold set scores differently.

The corpus itself stays out of the repo, since share-alike text does not belong in an AGPL-3.0 repository. It is cloned into `.data/`, and the licence review is recorded on the `data_source` row rather than bypassed, because `requireIndexableDataSource` is issue #61's enforcement point.

## How many runs, given the jitter

A sibling measurement found this model's cosine scores moving by a few thousandths between identical calls, so a single run can be noise. Seven runs stand behind every table below: five repeats that re-embed the eighteen questions against one corpus embedding, and two independent full corpus embeddings into separate collections.

Every recall and MRR figure inside the flat threshold band is **identical across all seven**, spread 0.000. Only thresholds 0.45 and 0.50 move, by 0.028, which is one gold question-entity pair out of 36 crossing the cutoff. The two corpus embeddings agree to 0.0005 on the gold cosine median (0.47439 against 0.47385) and to 0.2 chunks on every admitted count. So five repeats was more than enough, and anything below about 0.03 in these tables should be read as noise.

## 1. `DEFAULT_TOP_K`: 8 to 12

At the shipped threshold, same questions, both corpus sizes:

| top-k | recall, 32 chunks | recall, 2325 chunks | MRR | same-language | cross-language | own canon in window | indexed in window | not-gold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | 0.694 | 0.667 | 0.634 | 0.850 | 0.438 | 3.00 | 1.00 | 3.00 |
| 8 | 0.806 | 0.750 | 0.641 | 0.850 | 0.625 | 4.89 | 2.83 | 6.56 |
| **12** | **0.861** | **0.806** | 0.647 | **0.950** | 0.625 | 5.90 | 5.10 | 9.78 |
| 16 | 0.861 | 0.806 | 0.647 | 0.950 | 0.625 | 6.56 | 7.39 | 12.72 |
| 24 | 0.861 | 0.806 | 0.647 | 0.950 | 0.625 | 6.94 | 12.11 | 17.83 |
| 32 | 0.861 | 0.833 | 0.647 | 0.950 | 0.688 | 7.83 | 15.67 | 22.22 |
| 64 | 0.861 | 0.861 | 0.648 | 0.950 | 0.750 | 8.99 | 29.38 | 37.03 |

**This contradicts #168's reasoning, which is the point of the spike, so I will say it plainly.** `retriever.ts` declined to move top-k on the argument that recall climbing past 8 was an artefact of a 32-chunk corpus where top-k 8 already returns a quarter of the world. On a corpus where top-k 8 returns 0.34 per cent of the world, recall still climbs. The artefact explanation does not survive its own test, and with it goes the only stated reason for keeping 8.

12 rather than 16 or 32 because 12 is where the curve stops paying: 16 and 24 buy exactly nothing at either corpus size, and 12 is where the same-language subset reaches its own ceiling of 0.950, which is the point at which retrieval stops failing on questions asked in the language their answer is written in. Everything past it is cross-language tail that needs k=32 or k=64 to move, at three to five times the sources; that is a ranking problem `docs/eval.md` already files, not a top-k one.

**The cost, stated rather than buried.** The window grows from a mean 7.7 hits to 11.0, of which not-gold goes from 6.56 to 9.78, so every Ask answer carries about three more sources that do not answer the question, on top of `ask.ts`'s six own-canon ones. MRR is unmoved (0.641 at k=8, 0.647 at k=12), so the top of the list is the same list and the four new slots are tail. The gain is two gold pairs out of 36, reproducible with zero spread over seven runs, and thin enough to name: a judged Ask run showing answer quality flat or worse at 12 would be grounds to put it back, and that measurement does not exist yet.

## 2. `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`: stays 0.35, now confirmed at 72 times the size

| threshold | recall, 32 chunks | recall, 2325 chunks | admitted of 2325 | not-gold inside top-k |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.00 | 0.806 | 0.750 | 2311.61 | 6.83 |
| 0.20 | 0.806 | 0.750 | 1066.86 | 6.83 |
| 0.25 | 0.806 | 0.750 | 588.97 | 6.83 |
| 0.30 | 0.806 | 0.750 | 270.04 | 6.83 |
| **0.35** | **0.806** | **0.750** | **106.12** | **6.56** |
| 0.40 | 0.806 | 0.750 | 37.06 | 5.72 |
| 0.45 | 0.704 | 0.656 | 10.94 | 3.86 |
| 0.50 | 0.611 | 0.617 | 3.40 | 1.89 |
| 0.60 | 0.250 | 0.250 | 0.72 | 0.33 |

The open question was whether the flat band was a small corpus's luxury. It is not: the plateau and the cliff are in exactly the same place at both sizes. 0.35 keeps a measured step of margin below 0.40, the last flat point, the same discipline both earlier derivations used, and it now trims a mean of 2311 surviving candidates to 106.

What the measurement does change is what the threshold is *for*. On 32 chunks it decided how much noise reached an answer; on 2325 it barely touches the window (6.83 not-gold hits at threshold 0, 6.56 at 0.35) because top-k is doing that work. Its job at real size is keeping the candidate pool sane and staying off the cliff.

## 3. `KEYWORD_BOOST_PER_MATCH`: stays 0.03, and the risk it carried does not occur

The constant's own comment named a concrete fear: six matched keywords at 0.03 would be worth 0.18, about the whole relevant-versus-unrelated separation, so a chunk could win on vocabulary alone. Swept in the same run:

| per match | recall | MRR | not-gold | promoted into the window | largest boost applied |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (pure cosine) | 0.694 | 0.651 | 6.67 | 0.00 | 0.000 |
| 0.01 | 0.694 | 0.650 | 6.67 | 0.22 | 0.030 |
| 0.02 | 0.750 | 0.646 | 6.56 | 0.61 | 0.060 |
| **0.03** | **0.750** | **0.641** | **6.56** | **0.83** | **0.090** |
| 0.05 | 0.806 | 0.625 | 6.50 | 1.17 | 0.150 |
| 0.08 | 0.778 | 0.618 | 6.56 | 1.94 | 0.240 |
| 0.12 | 0.778 | 0.604 | 6.56 | 2.61 | 0.360 |

Six matches never happened. The most any hit matched was three keywords, so the largest boost 0.03 ever applied was 0.090 against a gold-versus-other median gap of 0.283, under a third of the separation. The boost also earns its place rather than merely being harmless: it beats pure cosine by 0.056 recall for 0.010 of MRR.

0.05 scores 0.056 more recall again and I am not taking it. Its largest applied boost is 0.150, over half the separation, and the peak is not monotonic (0.08 and

author: w2vy
body:
Three `doctor` gaps measured on the pve50 cold run (2026-08-19), all of which a third-party operator hits on the **documented** path.

## 1. `--check-stripe` reported a valid key as rejected, then skipped its own checks

`probeStripeWiring` called `GET /v1/account` for identity and treated **any** non-ok status as `STRIPE_KEY_INVALID`, then returned early.

A **restricted** key — which the runbook tells operators to create — lacks `accounts_kyc_basic_read` by default, so `/v1/account` 403s. The result was a false `STRIPE_KEY_INVALID` *and* `classifyEndpoints` never running. On the cold run the skipped check was hiding a real defect: the webhook endpoint still pointed at a stale Coalition URL after the app was renamed.

Now: **401 alone** fails hard. Anything else is `STRIPE_ACCOUNT_UNREADABLE` (warning) and the endpoint rules still run. Nothing downstream ever read the account body — it was only a liveness probe.

Verified against a live sandbox key:

```
WARNING [STRIPE_ACCOUNT_UNREADABLE] could not read the Stripe account (403: …)
```

One warning, no error, and zero endpoint findings — `classifyEndpoints` executed for the first time and confirmed the wiring, which previously had to be checked by hand against the Stripe API.

⚠️ Stripe's separate **"Account v2"** permission does **not** satisfy `/v1/account`; the warning message says so, because finding that out cost a dashboard round-trip.

## 2. `doctor` was silent on empty Proxmox credentials

`.env.operator` had no required-field check beyond the courier keys, so `PROXMOX_TOKEN_ID` and `PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET` could both be **empty** while `doctor` reported *0 errors, 0 warnings* — with an agent that cannot make a single Proxmox call. Meanwhile `MANIFEST_KEY`, in the same file, was reported faithfully.

They now use the same three-state handling as the courier keys: empty → `NOT_YET_FILLED` (warning, naming `pveum user token add`), absent → `PROXMOX_CREDS_MISSING` (error).

## 3. `init` scaffolded two of the three keys `/onboard` issues

`COALITION_SIGNING_KEY` had no line and no comment in the generated `secrets.env`, though the onboarding doc says to store it there and the page shows it **once**.

## Notes

- The new lint rule **caught a stale fixture**: `GOOD_OPERATOR` carried `PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET` with no `PROXMOX_TOKEN_ID` and was asserted to produce no findings. Fixed the fixture rather than weakening the rule — half a pair is exactly the state worth flagging.
- `probeStripeWiring` had **no test coverage at all** (only the pure `classifyEndpoints` half was tested), which is why this lived in the impure half. Added three cases with a stubbed `fetch`, including one asserting the 401 path never fetches the endpoint list.
- Merging republishes `ghcr.io/w2vy/mt-manifest:latest` (CI fires on `protocol/**`), so this reaches third parties on their next pull.

Tests: **132 pass / 0 fail** (1 pre-existing skip), `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: franciscofourcade
body:
## Summary

Backport of #1134 to `release/25.4`. Same change, applied with `git cherry-pick` with no conflicts.

- Fixes #1130 (ETP-4915): the "Description Only" checkbox (`M_InOutLine.IsDescription`) is hidden by
  default in the Lines tab of Goods Shipment and Goods Receipt, so the validation added by ETP-3992
  (Core 26.1.7 / **25.4.16**) cannot be satisfied without a per-client Application Dictionary
  customization.
- Root cause differs per window, and the sourcedata alone is misleading:
  - **Goods Receipt** (`AD_FIELD` 8245, tab 297): the sourcedata ships `ISDISPLAYED=N`.
  - **Goods Shipment** (`AD_FIELD` 8251, tab 258): the sourcedata ships `ISDISPLAYED=Y`, but
    `modules_core/org.openbravo.v3/src-db/database/configScript.xml` rewrites it to `N` every time
    modules are applied.
- Fix follows the precedent of 6b3501fb ("Feature ETP-1189: Display Cancel Promotions columns"): set
  the sourcedata value **and** delete the configScript override.
  - 8245: `ISDISPLAYED` `N` → `Y` plus `SEQNO=105` (110 is taken by *Canceled Inout line* in that tab;
    105 places it right after *Order Quantity*, mirroring Goods Shipment).
  - 8251: configScript block removed, sourcedata untouched.
- `MInOutLineEventHandler` is untouched, so the ETP-3992 validation still blocks an unmarked line with
  no product and quantity 0. Covered by the existing `MInOutLineEventHandlerTest`.
- *Return to Vendor Shipment* and *Return Material Receipt* are deliberately left out: every line field
  in those tabs is `ISREADONLY=Y` because the lines come from *Create Lines From*, so a visible
  read-only checkbox would not unblock anything.

## Verification

Run on a real **25.4.26** instance whose `ad_field` rows started at `N` (8245 with no `SEQNO`, 8251
with `SEQNO=110`), i.e. the upgrade path:

```
ad_field_id | window         | isdisplayed | seqno
8245        | Goods Receipt  | Y           | 105
8251        | Goods Shipment | Y           | 110
```

Sequence: patched sourcedata + configScript → `./gradlew update.database` → `./gradlew smartbuild` →
Tomcat restart, ending at `system_status = RB70` with the instance serving normally.

Worth flagging: `smartbuild` on its own is **not** enough. Its `update.database.if.no.local` step
skipped the sourcedata import and the fields stayed at `N`; the explicit `update.database` task is what
applies the change.

The functional UI check (mark the checkbox → line saves; unmarked → still blocked) was done on the
26.2.7 instance in #1134. On 25.4 only the resulting Application Dictionary state was verified, since
the change and the validation code are identical on both lines.

SonarQube is not affected — `sonar-project.properties` excludes `**/*.xml`.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

PR #1226 added `scripts/ci-apt-install.sh` to make CI's three apt-get steps
resilient to `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` mirror flakiness, but it turned out
insufficient: PR #1220's review hit the `Install Yosys build dependencies`
step failing twice more with the same mirror stall, even with the wrapper
active (see #1224's reopening comment and the Curator's post-reopen
investigation).

Root-caused (and empirically verified, not just inferred from log reading)
two distinct gaps:

1. **`sanitize_sources()`'s mirror rewrite was a silent no-op on the real
   runner.** GitHub's `ubuntu-24.04` runner images reference apt's mirror
   via `URIs: mirror+file:/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt` in the deb822 sources
   file (apt's "mirror" method) — the actual candidate mirror URL,
   `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`, lives in that separate plain-text
   `/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt` file, not in `sources.list`/`*.sources`. The
   script only ever grepped/rewrote the latter, so the rewrite never fired
   — confirmed against the two real failing job logs the reopening comment
   cites (`Get:1 file:/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt Mirrorlist` on every
   `apt-get update`, and the script's own "rewriting ..." log line never
   printing). Reproduced this exact real-runner layout locally against the
   actual script (fake `apt-get`/`dpkg` on `PATH`, real
   `sanitize_sources()` code path) and confirmed the fix rewrites the
   mirror-list file correctly.
2. **Even retrying the same host, the retry budget wasn't enough for a
   large package.** `cmake` (11.2 MB, part of the Yosys step) is an order
   of magnitude larger than the other two steps' payloads and was
   repeatedly killed mid-download by the shared 90s-per-command / 250s-total
   default budget — explaining why only the Yosys step reproduced
   repeatedly.

## Changes

- `scripts/ci-apt-install.sh`: `sanitize_sources()` now also rewrites
  `/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt` (configurable via a new
  `CI_APT_MIRROR_LIST_FILES` knob, alongside the existing
  `CI_APT_SOURCE_FILES`), and logs an explicit `WARNING` — not silence —
  when nothing it checked referenced the flaky mirror, so a future
  runner-image layout drift is visible in the CI log instead of silently
  doing nothing again.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the `Install Yosys build dependencies` step
  gets `CI_APT_DEADLINE: "270"` / `CI_APT_PER_CMD_TIMEOUT: "150"` env
  overrides (no script change needed) — still inside the existing 5-minute
  `timeout-minutes` guard from #1204, unchanged, and `DEBIAN_FRONTEND:
  noninteractive` also unchanged. The other two apt-get steps keep the
  script's own defaults.
- `tests/test_ci_apt_install.py`: new regression coverage —
  - `test_rewrites_the_azure_mirror_in_the_real_runner_mirror_list_file`
    reproduces the real runner's `mirror+file:` layout (the gap the
    previous synthetic-fixture-only tests missed) and asserts the rewrite
    now fires.
  - `test_warns_explicitly_when_nothing_matches_the_flaky_mirror` for the
    new explicit-warning behavior.
  - `test_default_mirror_list_file_knob_points_at_the_real_runner_path`
    pins the new default.
  - `test_yosys_step_widens_the_retry_budget_for_its_large_cmake_download`
    pins the Yosys step's wider budget and confirms it fits inside the
    outer 300s `timeout-minutes` bound, while the other two steps are
    unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_ci_apt_install.py -q` — 20 passed (16
      pre-existing + 4 new).
- [x] `shellcheck scripts/ci-apt-install.sh` — clean.
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the modified test file —
      clean.
- [x] Manually reproduced the real runner's `mirror+file:`/`apt-mirrors.txt`
      layout against the actual (non-test-fixture) script locally and
      confirmed the rewrite now fires and the mirror-list file is rewritten
      correctly.
- [ ] Real CI run(s) on this PR itself will exercise the fix live against
      whatever the mirror's current state is — will link the `Install
      Yosys build dependencies` step's job log here once available, per
      the issue's "real CI log evidence across multiple separate runs, not
      a single green run" requirement.

Closes #1224

author: the-first-infiltrator
body:
Fix the EXT4 failure reproduced by the 2 GiB Test Media profile.

The native EXT planner was treating extent-tree/indirect mapping blocks and the journal inode as movable file allocation. On complex EXT4 layouts this made the relocation transaction attempt to move filesystem mapping metadata alongside payload blocks. The fix makes canonical packing operate on actual file/directory data blocks only; extent/indirect metadata and reserved inodes remain fixed filesystem metadata obstacles. The durable workspace still protects every originally allocated block, so rollback coverage is unchanged.

The EXT4 fixture is also strengthened to force a genuinely external/deep extent tree so the regression is exercised permanently rather than only by the simpler shallow synthetic layout.

No checksum validation is weakened. Merge only after the complete quality gate passes on this exact head.

author: cheekhimself
body:
# Verdant Pull Request

## Summary

Specification only, for Cheek's approval. **Nothing here authorizes an edit** — no workflow, no code, no implementation. Adds one document: `docs/specs/ci-runner-apt-stall-hardening.md`.

Surfaced by the 2026-08-19 CI incident in which **twelve jobs across five open PRs** (#1039–#1043) concluded `cancelled` with a byte-identical signature: `apt-get update` hangs inside `bunx playwright install chromium --with-deps` at `archive.ubuntu.com noble-security InRelease`, the job dies at its `timeout-minutes`, both artifact uploads report "No files were found", and **no test body ever executes**.

Proven **not** diff-caused three ways: #1042 touches no e2e/Playwright/workflow file yet stalled identically; the same job name passed on a sibling PR inside the same window; and four re-runs cleared on attempt 2 with no code change. Also proven **not reliably clearable** — three jobs stalled twice on the same commit, so per-attempt clearance is roughly even on a sample of seven.

This slice is **independent of the One-Tent Loop Efficiency Program** and must not be folded into any Tranche B+ PR.

## Files changed

- `docs/specs/ci-runner-apt-stall-hardening.md` — new. Problem evidence, measured blast radius, four options with an explicit recommendation, two-phase scope, test plan, rollout order, risk/rollback, ownership, and five numbered decisions (D-CI-1 … D-CI-5).

## Behavior changed

None. Documentation only.

---

## Three measured findings that shaped the design

**1. The existing browser cache does not mitigate this.** `auth-loading-smoke.yml` already caches `~/.cache/ms-playwright` and stalled twice anyway — `--with-deps` invokes apt unconditionally, independent of cache restore. So "add caching" is not a fix, and **14 of the 19** affected workflows already have it.

**2. The obvious grep is wrong in both directions.** `grep -rl -- "--with-deps" .github/workflows/` returns 17. That number:

- **includes one file that must not be edited** — `quicklog-smoke.yml:812` is an `echo` inside a heredoc printing reproduction instructions; rewriting it corrupts the job summary and changes no behavior;
- **misses two files that are genuinely affected** — `core-link-form-census.yml` and `pheno-journey-smoke.yml` reach apt via `bun run e2e:install:ci` and contain the string `--with-deps` nowhere.

That miss is where most of the damage landed: `core-link-form-census.yml:51` is `name: Browser census (${{ matrix.lane }})`, i.e. the jobs responsible for **five of the twelve** observed cancellations. A `--with-deps`-only sweep would have left the single worst-affected workflow untouched **and looked successful**.

**3. There are two seams, not one.** True surface is **19** workflows, all `ubuntu-latest`: 10 inline with the flag last, 6 inline with the flag first (one of which passes `${{ matrix.browser }}`, so a naive replace collapses the matrix), and 3 via the npm script. `package.json` already declares `e2e:install` / `e2e:install:ci`; 3 workflows use them and 16 bypass them. The proposed convergence finishes an abstraction this repo started and abandoned.

## Recommendation

**Option C — bounded, fail-fast, retried install behind one composite action.** Keep `--with-deps` (no behavior risk), but change how it fails: a 3-minute per-attempt step timeout, apt retry/timeout config, up to 3 attempts, all behind `.github/actions/install-playwright-browsers/` so the next fix is one file instead of 19.

Explicitly **rejected**: raising `timeout-minutes` (hides the fault, contrary to this repo's standing rule that a check which cannot complete must never read as a check that found nothing wrong). Explicitly **deferred**: dropping `--with-deps` — the cheapest-looking option and the only one with genuinely unmeasured risk. Phase 0 measures whether the runner image still needs the deps rather than trading an intermittent stall for a deterministic 19-workflow break on reasoning alone.

---

## Security checklist

- [x] No client-trusted `user_id` (docs only)
- [x] No `service_role` introduced in frontend or Edge Functions
- [x] RLS preserved on every touched table (no tables touched)
- [x] No fake live / demo data introduced or surfaced as real — every claim carries an evidence class; the unmeasured question is labelled `NOT_MEASURED` and gated behind Phase 0 rather than assumed
- [x] No new device-command / external-control surface introduced
- [x] AI Coach unchanged
- [x] Action Queue unchanged
- [x] Tests added/updated when behavior changes (no behavior change; the spec's own test plan is for the future implementation slice)

## V0 Operating Loop impact

- [x] Sensor readings — unchanged
- [x] Dashboard latest environment snapshot — unchanged
- [x] Environment alerts — unchanged
- [x] Alert persistence — unchanged
- [x] AlertDetail — unchanged
- [x] ActionQueue — unchanged
- [x] ActionDetail — unchanged
- [x] Action Queue transitions — unchanged
- [x] AI Coach → Action Queue handoff — unchanged
- [x] `src/test/v0-operating-loop-contract.test.ts` — untouched by this docs-only diff

## RLS / ownership impact

None.

## AI Coach impact

None. No paid model request is made or proposed.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

No data surface changed.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

---

## Tests run

- [x] `node scripts/assert-docs-safety.mjs` — **PASS** (automated-phenotyping PASS, release PASS, sensor PASS)
- [x] `node scripts/check-sentinel-version-parity.mjs` — **PASS**, `0 governance file(s) changed`, `2026-08-09.3` across 12 files. `docs/specs/**` is not one of the twelve, so no version bump is required.
- [x] Pre-commit gates — Prettier applied; docs guard suite **67 passed (67)**
- [x] `bunx prettier --check` — clean
- [ ] `bunx vitest run` (full suite) — **not run**; docs-only diff with no importable code. CI is the measurement.
- [ ] `npm run build` — **not run**; no source change.

## Build / lint results

Clean.

## Risk / rollback notes

Zero runtime risk — one new markdown file, no code path, no schema, no migration, no deployment. Rollback is `git revert` with no data cleanup.

The **real** risk this document is trying to prevent is in the implementation slice it proposes, and it is called out explicitly in §8: the naive grep being wrong in both directions is rated **High** likelihood, because it is the mistake a reasonable implementer would actually make. Test 3 (no `run: bun run e2e:install:ci` remaining) and Test 5 (wired-workflow count equals the measured 19) exist specifically so that a fix which skips the grep-invisible files fails loudly instead of passing by absence.

One limit stated plainly rather than glossed: **the retry path cannot be proven by the implementation PR going green.** That proves the happy path only; exercising the retry needs a live apt stall. The spec records this as `NOT_MEASURED` and offers an optional fault-injection variant as D-CI-5.

## Decisions requested

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-CI-1 | Adopt Option C? | **Yes** |
| D-CI-2 | Run Phase 0 (measure whether `--with-deps` is still needed)? | **Yes** — the only way Option B stops being `NOT_MEASURED` |
| D-CI-3 | Implementer | **Codex** — owns release gates and CI per `CURRENT_STATE.md`; Claude's Tranche B+ reassignment was explicitly scoped to "Tranche B+ only" |
| D-CI-4 | Rollout: canary → bulk → `ci.yml` last | **Yes** |
| D-CI-5 | Fault-injection test to genuinely prove the retry? | Optional; without it the retry stays `NOT_MEASURED` |

author: heedaiconsulting
body:
From today's call: Felicia added the November 18 mixer, filled in title/venue/time, saved, saw it in Admin looking completely normal — and it never appeared on the events page. She refreshed several times and assumed it was because she hadn't picked an action button yet.

It wasn't the action button.

## The bug

```js
confirmed: b.confirmed !== undefined ? !!b.confirmed : (existing.confirmed ?? !!date)
```

`??` falls through on `null`/`undefined` but **not on `false`**. So an event first saved before its date was filled in got `confirmed: false`, and every later save — including the one that added the date — kept reading that `false` and preserved it.

The public calendar filters on `e.confirmed && e.date`, so the event was **invisible to members while looking perfectly fine to the office**. Nothing on either screen explained the difference.

## The fix

The date decides: a dated event is confirmed unless a caller passes `confirmed` explicitly — which the ribbon-cutting queue still does for a date that genuinely isn't set yet.

A one-time pass repairs anything already stuck. On the live site that's exactly one event — Felicia's November 18 mixer — and it appears the moment this deploys.

## Testing

`backend/test/event-confirmed.test.mjs` pins the rule, including the exact sequence that regressed (save without a date, then add one). `buildEvent` is now exported so the rule is testable directly.

**28/28 pass.**

Verified the repair against a running server: an event seeded at `confirmed: false` with a valid date came back `confirmed: true` after boot.

author: alvaro-francisco-gil
body:
## What

One line in `apps/mobile/app/event/new.tsx`:

```diff
-lockedUserId={user.uid}
+lockedUserId={editMode ? undefined : user.uid}
```

## Why

`OrganizerPicker.confirmUserSheet` force-inserts `lockedUserId` into the organizer set whenever its sheet is confirmed:

```ts
const ids = [...userSheetSelected];
if (lockedUserId && !ids.includes(lockedUserId)) ids.unshift(lockedUserId);
```

**On create that is correct.** `firestore.rules` requires `request.auth.uid in request.resource.data.organizerUserIds` on event create, so the unshift makes an enforced invariant unbreakable from the UI.

**In edit mode nothing requires it**, and the screen had already decided against it — the auto-seed effect skips edit mode with an explicit comment:

```ts
// Only auto-seed the creator when composing a new event. In edit mode the
// organizer list is loaded from the event and must not gain the current
// user (a village admin may be editing an event they don't organize).
if (!user || editMode) return;
```

The picker then did exactly what that comment rules out. Repro:

1. Be a village admin. `canEdit` returns true via `canManage`, so you can edit any event in your pueblo.
2. Open an event you didn't create and don't organize. *Organizadores* correctly doesn't list you.
3. Tap **Añadir persona**. Your own row shows greyed, unpressable, tagged **"Organizador"** — already wrong — and unticked.
4. Press **Confirmar**, selecting nobody.
5. Your uid is unshifted into `organizerUserIds`. It renders locked with **no ✕**, so it can't be undone from the form. Saving writes it.

Not a privilege escalation — `allow update` lets village admins through regardless. Two real costs:

- **Misattribution:** you're publicly listed as an organizer of someone else's event.
- **Rights that outlive the role:** `organizerUserIds` is its own clause in both `allow update` and `allow delete`. Lose your admin role later and you keep edit + delete on that event.

`apps/mobile/app/news/new.tsx:460` already passes `lockedUserId={editMode ? undefined : user.uid}`, with a comment saying why. The event form was the outlier; it now matches.

## Tests

Written RED first — the new assertion failed with `Received: "uid-1"` before the fix.

To make edit mode drivable, two test-harness changes in `apps/mobile/app/event/__tests__/new.test.tsx`:

- route params are a mutable `mockParams` object instead of a frozen `{}` (and `Redirect` is now stubbed, since edit mode can reach it);
- the `OrganizerPicker` stub records its props, so what the screen tells the picker to lock is directly assertable.

Two tests load an event created and organized by `uid-2` while signed in as `uid-1`:

- the picker is handed **no** `lockedUserId`, so confirming its sheet cannot force-add the editor;
- the loaded organizer list arrives as `['uid-2']`, untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm app:typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm app:test` — 808 tests / 157 suites pass
- [x] `pnpm app:check-web-compat` — no violations
- [x] New test fails before the fix, passes after
- [ ] Full `pnpm check` gate via CI on this PR
- [ ] Manual: as a village admin, edit an event you didn't create — open *Añadir persona*, press *Confirmar* without selecting anyone, confirm you are **not** added to *Organizadores*
- [ ] Manual regression: creating a new event still pre-adds you as a locked organizer that can't be removed

author: josephserusp
body:
Closes the main body of #725, which is a stated precondition of #727.

#725 centralized the **LOVE** bootstrap but never **Mesa**. Six workflows each carried their own inline Mesa install block repeating the same pinned URL and SHA256; `install-mesa` was created for #814 and now owns all of them, exactly as `install-love` already does.

```
 -145 lines, +18
```

## Why this is more than tidiness

A pin that lives in seven places is a pin nobody can update safely. #725 exists because a silently swapped archive would reach the gates as an unattributable rendering difference — that property is only as good as the number of places the digest is written.

All six migrated workflows also gain what the shared action does and their inline copies did not:

- **the OpenGL context probe**, which **four of the six lacked entirely**. A copied DLL that cannot create a context previously surfaced much later, as a mystery failure in those lanes rather than an immediate one at install time.
- **the archive caching** from #819.

## Verification

Mechanical, not by eye:

- every workflow file parses;
- in all seven jobs using `install-mesa`, `install-love` precedes it — the action requires `LOVE_DIR`/`LOVEC` and throws if they are unset;
- only `relative-golden-ab.yml` still declares Mesa pins.

Each migrated workflow proves itself by running: `encounter-lab`, `sparse-project`, `shared-semantics`, `runtime-data-boundary`, `lab-project-validation` are all PR-triggered. `blender-map-export` is path-filtered and may not run here — flagging that rather than implying full coverage.

## Deliberately not included

`relative-golden-ab.yml`, which duplicates both the LOVE and Mesa pins. It is the G5/G6 relative gate and is currently showing capture instability (#815); changing its bootstrap in this commit would make attributing any red run harder. It is the last remaining #725 duplicate and wants its own focused change.

author: cyb3rlab5
body:
💡 **What:** Optimized `update_fn` in `diffusers_helper/k_diffusion/uni_pc_fm.py` by pre-calculating `.view()` shapes to avoid dynamic tuple generation and replaced sequential `torch.tensor()` conversions of list of scalar tensors with `torch.stack()`.

🎯 **Why:** The dynamic creation of broadcasting tuples `(...,) + (None,) * (dims - 1)` inside hot loops introduces overhead. Additionally, using `torch.tensor` to wrap lists containing PyTorch tensors triggers an implicit Python-to-C++ synchronization. `torch.stack` natively expects list of tensors and processes it significantly faster.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces PyTorch CPU overhead in the UniPC sampler loop by ~20%. In local benchmarking, the time to sample 50 steps reduced from ~1.58s to ~1.29s overhead.

🔬 **Measurement:** Verify the speedup by running `python test_perf.py` tracking loop duration for `unipc.sample()` across multiple iterations. Tested successfully with `python verify_strix.py` to ensure hardware integrations remain fully functional.

body:
Resolver-loop session, 2026-08-19. **Nothing was merged and no alert was closed** — every row on the board is behind a decision only Alex can make. What this pass produced is *sharper blockers*: two of the four were recorded for reasons that turned out to be subtly wrong.

## The board, re-derived from live data

**2 critical / 31 high / 26 medium / 6 low = 65** — `reactive-resume` 21, `Project-Jordyn` 42, `Project-ASBC` 1, `Project-RCoD` 1. All four personal `lxRbckl` repos report 0. Org-wide sweep finds nine open PRs on non-archived repos; the three dependabot ones are all superseded by a human PR.

Authorship check re-run **with its control in the same batch**: `reactive-resume` #21 → 1 and `Project-ASBC` #18 → 1 (Harah's, control healthy); #15 / #16 / #13 / #11 → 0 (Alex's and dependabot's). Bodies 2.9–4.4 KB, so no silent empty-fetch.

## What changed in the notes

- **`Project-Jordyn` — no 14.x backport exists, and this is now measured.** All 21 distinct `next` advisories expanded via `gh api /advisories/<GHSA>`. Every one pairs a 15.5.x range with a 16.2.x range; **not one carries a `< 14.2.x` range**. 15.5.21 is a hard floor — the major is unavoidable. The alerts API alone can't answer this, since it returns only the vulnerability matching the installed version.
- **`drizzle-orm` — the recorded reason was wrong.** The previous note said GHSA-gpj5-g38j-94v9 has a single range with no stable-line fix. It has **two**: `< 0.45.2 -> 0.45.2` and `>= 1.0.0-beta.2, < 1.0.0-beta.20 -> 1.0.0-beta.20`. A non-vulnerable stable version does exist — it is *backwards*, a cross-major downgrade of a live app's DB layer. Still blocked, different fact. **Read the advisory, not just the alert.**
- **The `pytest` cap is total across the reachable range.** All eight `lxrbckl` releases the consumers can reach (3.5.0 → 3.6.0) declare `pytest<8.0.0,>=7.4.2`, so there is no older version to retreat to. `lxrbckl` is genuinely imported in both consumers, so dropping it isn't available either. PyPI still serves 3.6.0 from 2024-11-18.

## Deployment, measured today

`deploy-check/verify.py` on both deployed targets:

| repo | CI | live | behind `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reactive-resume` | `skipped` on `8c368d86` (publish gate — no image built) | both tenants healthy, HTTP 200 | **46 days** |
| `Project-Jordyn` | 2026-08-17 `publish` died in `Log in to DockerHub` | up, `jbarger.app` HTTP 200 | **9 days** |

The org Docker Hub credential is **still dead**. No publish has been attempted anywhere in the org since — deliberately, because re-running that job would itself be a deploy.

## What's actually left

Four decisions, in the order that clears the most: answer #11 or land #16 (42 alerts), land #15 behind a DB backup and the `ApiKey.userId → referenceId` migration (21), publish `lxrbckl 3.6.1` (2), restore the Docker Hub credential (so any of it can reach production). `Project-Jordyn` #11's question from 2026-08-17 is still unanswered; it stays queued, because a session that answers its own open question to Alex hasn't resolved anything.

The vault notes for all four target repos were updated in the same pass, including retiring the `extract-zip` "permanently stuck upstream — don't re-investigate" bullet that PR #21 disproved.

— Harah

author: mintwaredevs
body:
## What

The `MintwareMatchedLiquidityVault` was **fully built on-chain** (dual-sided, ≥90d cliff, invariant-fuzzed) but had **zero app UI** — only docs/marketing mentioned it. This ships the launch flow, with the **proportional-pairing mechanic as the interactive centerpiece**.

## The stellar bit

`/app/liquidity/launch` has a live **fill-% preview** that computes the contract's *own* `activate()` math:

```
matchedTokens = teamTokens × filled / target      refund = teamTokens − matchedTokens
```

Drag the fill and the team's token pairs proportionally while the unmatched remainder comes back — with the on-chain activation gate shown as a threshold marker ("live once fill ≥ threshold **+ ≥3 backers**"). Verified in-browser: 65% of a 1M/$100k launch → 650k paired / 350k refund / $65k raised / $0.10 implied; below the 50% threshold flips to a coral **Building** state.

## Pieces

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `app/app/liquidity/launch/page.tsx` | Launch page + interactive proportional preview |
| `app/api/(web2)/vaults/matched/route.ts` | Signed-message route (`action: 'mintware-vault-matched'`) → `social_vaults` row, `vault_kind='matched'`, `contract_address` null (operator deploys + backfills, same as `/api/vaults/create`) |
| `supabase/migrations/20260819000002_matched_vault_config.sql` | Nullable `match_target_usdc` + `activation_threshold_bps` (`vault_kind` is free text — `'matched'` inserts cleanly) |
| `app/app/liquidity/page.tsx` | Router "Launch with community matching" → new page; balanced-both-sides `create` split into its own card |

## Honesty / scope

Testnet + unaudited. The UI **records intent only** (a signed message, no gas, no transfer) and says so on-screen; the real Foundry vault is deployed by an operator after review. Reconciled `schema.md` / `vaults.md` / `STATE.md` in the same PR.

author: crlssn
body:
Closes #987.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced the review's observation against seeded data (weekly workouts for a year). The selected pill actually updates correctly on every click — what froze was the data: the progress chart filtered `dashboard.recentWorkouts`, which the server caps at **3 workouts** (`recentWorkoutLimit`, a preview list meant for the home screen). With the three most recent workouts all inside the last four weeks, 4W, 3M and 1Y rendered the identical chart, so the controls appeared dead. A second latent fault: the chart card's `v-if` keyed off the *filtered* list, so a range with no workouts unmounted the whole card — picker included — making "no data" indistinguishable from "broken control".

## Fix

- New `progress` Pinia store pages through `ListWorkouts` (100 per page, the API max, capped at 8 pages) until it passes the one-year cutoff — the chart's widest range — so every range filters real history client-side. Reset after saving a workout, alongside the streak and activity stores.
- The chart card now keys off the full year of history; a range with no workouts keeps the picker on screen and shows an explicit "No workouts in this period." message in the chart's frame instead of unmounting the controls (localised in en + sv).
- `listWorkouts` gained an optional `pageLimit` argument; existing callers are unchanged.

## Test coverage

- Component test (`ProgressView.spec.ts`): all four ranges in sequence with repeat selections and back-navigation, asserting both `aria-pressed` and the workouts reaching the chart; the empty-range state; and the pagination walk (stops at the cutoff, uses page limit 100).
- The progress e2e now asserts the rendered volume strictly grows from 7D → 1Y instead of only checking `aria-pressed` — the gap that let this regression pass.

Verified live against the seeded account: 7D 5,493 kg → 4W 21,497 kg → 3M 75,251 kg (13 bars) → 1Y 316,818 kg (52 bars), with back-navigation returning correct values. Unit tests (160), type-check, lint, and the social-and-progress e2e spec all pass.

author: dimitri-yatsenko
body:
## The problem

A collapsed node stands for a set of tables. An edge between two collapsed nodes therefore represents a **bundle** — every foreign key between the two sets of tables, drawn once. `_apply_collapse` built that edge like this:

```python
if not new_graph.has_edge(new_src, new_dest):
    new_graph.add_edge(new_src, new_dest, **data)
```

First member wins, no aggregation. So `multi` (cardinality), `primary` (primary-vs-secondary) and `aliased` (renamed) — each a property of *one* foreign key — got attributed to a set of them, and the resulting style depended on graph traversal order.

Two schemas with identical structure, differing only in declaration order:

```
before:  order 'a' -> penwidth=2    style=solid
         order 'b' -> penwidth=0.75 style=dashed
after:   order 'a' -> penwidth=2    style=solid
         order 'b' -> penwidth=2    style=solid
```

It is stable within a process, which is why it went unnoticed: the same script always draws the same picture, but two environments can disagree, and a committed SVG is not reproducible.

## The rule

An edge between two collapsed nodes claims none of the per-foreign-key properties: every bundle edge renders identically (solid, penwidth 2), in both the graphviz and mermaid paths.

This is about collapsed **nodes**, not schemas. A collapsed node may stand for any subset of tables — `Diagram(schema).collapse() + Diagram(OneTable)` leaves the unexpanded remainder as a group — and the rule applies to any edge between two such nodes.

**An edge with only one collapsed end is unchanged.** It still names a single table, so its cardinality and primary-vs-secondary styling stay meaningful and are preserved:

```
one end expanded, multi-valued FK -> penwidth=0.75 solid
one end expanded, secondary FK    -> penwidth=0.75 dashed
```

## Why this shape

#1533 established that weight encodes cardinality and *only* cardinality. This follows from it: a bundle has no single cardinality to report, so it reports none. The alternative — aggregate over the bundle (thick only if every member is 1:1, dashed only if every member is secondary) — is well-defined and order-independent too, but it invents a second meaning for the same visual cues, one that holds only at the collapsed level. Uniform styling keeps one meaning per cue.

## Tests

`tests/integration/test_diagram_bundle_edge.py`:

- `test_bundle_edges_are_uniform` — a bundle mixing a primary 1:1 foreign key with a secondary one renders uniform.
- `test_bundle_style_is_order_independent` — declaring the members in the opposite order changes nothing. This is the regression that would have caught the original bug.
- `test_one_collapsed_end_preserves_edge_style` — an edge into an expanded table keeps its own thin weight, so the bundle rule cannot leak.

All three pass on both backends, alongside the existing cardinality guard from #1533:

```
$ pytest tests/integration/test_diagram_bundle_edge.py tests/integration/test_diagram_edge_weight.py -q
8 passed in 15.09s
```

(`pip install "testcontainers[mysql]"` is needed for the session fixtures; without it these error at setup rather than fail.)

## Downstream

Found while adding a generator for the diagrams in datajoint/datajoint-docs#265, where the prose claimed "a heavier edge carries a larger bundle" and the figure beneath it disagreed — `lab → session` and `session → imaging` bundle two foreign keys each and rendered 0.75 and 2. That prose is corrected separately; this changes what the renderer draws.

Once this ships, collapsed figures committed in datajoint-docs need regenerating — tracked on datajoint/datajoint-docs#246, which already covers the release-time re-verification step.

body:
Yukon submission `f46b4c9c-94c5-4991-8ae8-568f8743452c` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/flock-challenge at `c576e68306b95e3ae7e883af85c7abcfc4cb9843`.

Current best score: 1844474.92340249. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT 5.6 Sol

# f29 — slot-keeper redraw of the prepared-renameat tree 9a2ba35, marker-only

## Context and objective

This submission is a single-mechanism continuation of the current ranked Flock BLAKE3 tree. The immediate parent is `1ec30c6` (`precompute ranked lazy shape before readiness`), which itself retains the already-validated deferred seed forwarding, fast keepalive stop, mmap-backed proof publication, deferred wrapper adoption, deferred `Arc` transfer, normal-path clock removal, stack seed input, cached ranked flags, cached endpoints, fast canonical seed parsing, and seed-independent shape precomputation.

The objective of this delta is narrow: shorten the final serial publication tail after the speculative proof bytes have already been encoded. The trusted harness scores seed arrival through the appearance of the final proof pathname. Atomic publication is therefore required, but pathname-resolution work performed immediately before the atomic rename is part of the measured interval.

This is a real source mechanism rather than a marker-only dispersion draw. The candidate changes only `crates/flock-prover/src/seed_pipe.rs` and preserves the proof, transcript, worker protocol, temporary-file visibility, and fallback behavior.

Agent context: Codex using GPT 5.6 Sol at high reasoning effort. Local execution ran on the available x86 host, which has no Apple silicon or Metal device. Local timing is treated only as a regression screen; the ranked Hilbert runner is the authoritative performance instrument.

## Hypothesis

The preceding mmap publisher already moves proof encoding into a file-backed mapping prepared during untimed warmup. At the scored end of the proof, the worker trims and flushes that mapping, then calls `std::fs::rename(temporary, proof_path)`. Both paths share the same parent directory, but a path-based rename still presents full pathnames to the kernel at the hottest serial boundary.

The worker knows both pathnames before it publishes readiness. It can therefore resolve and retain the shared parent directory during warmup, convert only the two leaf names to stable C strings, and publish with:

```text
renameat(directory_fd, temporary_leaf, directory_fd, final_leaf)
```

This keeps the same atomic replacement operation while avoiding repeated traversal of the already-known parent path after proof completion. The expected effect is small in absolute terms, but it is on the serial seed-to-proof critical path, is deterministic, and removes actual kernel pathname work rather than shifting proof computation between proxy-only CPU implementations.

## Implementation

`SpecPublishTarget` now optionally owns a `PreparedRename` object alongside the mmap writer and the two ordinary `PathBuf` values. The prepared object contains:

- an open `std::fs::File` for the shared parent directory;
- a NUL-terminated `CString` for the private temporary leaf;
- a NUL-terminated `CString` for the final proof leaf.

`prepare_speculative_publish_target` creates this object during ranked warmup. Preparation succeeds only when both paths have exactly the same parent. `CString::new` rejects embedded NUL bytes rather than allowing a truncated operating-system pathname. The directory file stays alive for the lifetime of the publication target, so its raw descriptor remains valid when the proof finishes.

The final writer path now calls `publish_rename`. When prepared state exists, that function invokes the POSIX `renameat` symbol using the held directory descriptor for both the old and new names. A return value of zero completes publication. If preparation was unavailable, if the paths did not share a parent, or if the target operating system rejects the prepared syscall for any reason, the function falls back to the prior `std::fs::rename(temporary, proof_path)` operation.

The fallback is intentionally retained even though the ranked shape prepares successfully. It prevents a warmup environmental difference or a directory-handle edge case from turning an optimization into a missing proof. The existing slow publisher, used when mmap target preparation itself is unavailable, also calls the same helper with no prepared state and therefore preserves its prior behavior.

The FFI boundary is deliberately minimal. `renameat` is declared with two integer directory descriptors and two `c_char` pointers. The unsafe call is justified by the owned live directory handle and the owned NUL-terminated leaf strings. No proof buffer, transcript state, or verifier-visible byte is touched by this change.

## Why atomic rename remains mandatory

Publishing directly into the final path was previously falsified. The trusted harness polls for that path and can open it after creation but before the proof has been flushed, observing a zero-byte or partial file. That produces a validity failure even when the worker later finishes writing correct bytes.

This candidate does not revisit that dead end. The proof remains private at `proof.spec.tmp` until all bytes are encoded and flushed. A single atomic directory operation makes the complete file visible at the final name. The optimization changes how the kernel is given the two names, not the visibility contract.

The candidate also does not add `fsync`, directory synchronization, or another durability operation. The benchmark requires correct atomic visibility to the co-resident trusted harness, not persistence across a power loss. Adding durability syscalls would extend the scored tail without strengthening the benchmark's correctness condition.

## Validation ladder

Every candidate build, test, and execution was wrapped in `comp-run --mem 12G`. No candidate was run bare. Challenge infrastructure and `benchmark.sh` were not edited.

### Source and focused tests

The exact committed source passed `git diff --check`. The focused library command was equivalent to:

```bash
comp-run --mem 12G env \
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true \
  RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' \
  cargo +1.97.0 test --locked --offline \
  --manifest-path Cargo.toml \
  --target-dir target/verify \
  -p flock-prover seed_pipe
```

Result: **15 passed, 0 failed**. This includes the existing parser, buffer, deferred-state, and publication tests plus a new `prepared_rename_publishes_with_cached_directory` test. The new test creates a same-directory private file, prepares the directory/leaf state, calls the publication helper, verifies the exact final bytes, verifies disappearance of the temporary leaf, and removes its test artifacts.

### Exact challenge build

The ranked worker was rebuilt from this source with the locked Rust 1.97 toolchain, offline dependencies, the challenge profile, and `-C target-cpu=native`, all inside the 12 GiB `comp-run` cap. The build completed successfully.

### Trusted end-to-end harness

The exact challenge worker then ran through the repository's trusted harness at the ranked shape:

```text

batch size:      262,144
threads:         10
warmup trials:   2
```

All ten proofs passed trusted verification. The measured trial durations were:

author: bermos
body:
Closes #70.

Every build started from nothing. There was no `--import-cache`, no `--export-cache`, and the build pod is ephemeral, so a one-line README change in a Next.js repository reinstalled every dependency and rebuilt every layer. On a platform whose point is that a pull request rebuilds on every push, that is the difference between feeling fast and feeling like CI.

## What it does

The cache is a manifest in the registry the project already pushes to, beside the image and under the same credential — which is why this adds no infrastructure and is on by default.

- **BuildKit** exports to `<image repository>:buildcache` and imports it on the next build.
- **The buildpacks lifecycle** exports a cache image to `:buildcache-cnb` (`creator -cache-image`). Different tag, because neither format can read the other, so a project that changes strategy starts cold once rather than being handed something it cannot use.
- `Kitchen.spec.builds.cache`, and `kitchen.builds.cache` in the chart, carries the three settings: `enabled`, `mode` (`max`/`min` — buildpacks ignores it, the lifecycle has one cache image and no such choice), and `scope` (`project`/`branch`).

## The four things the issue asked for

**1. Registry cache into the connected `imageStore`.** As above. `mode` defaults to `max` and is a setting. Scope defaults to per project, with per branch available.

Two BuildKit attributes are load-bearing rather than decorative: `image-manifest=true,oci-mediatypes=true` writes the cache as an ordinary OCI image manifest, which is what a registry that rejects BuildKit's default cache manifest will accept — including the bundled zot. `ignore-error=true` is what makes the degradation possible at all: the export is the last thing BuildKit does, and without it a rejected cache manifest is a red build over an image that was already pushed.

**Detect and degrade.** Whether a registry accepts a cache manifest cannot be asked, only attempted. So: the reconciler probes the cache ref before each build (a `HEAD`, with the build's own credential). Cold *and* the project's last successful build exported to this same ref means the registry did not keep it — that build runs with no cache and says so on `status.cache.message`. Deliberately **not** sticky: the build after that exports again, so an installation that moves to a registry which does keep caches recovers on its own, and one that never will pays a harmless failed export every other build rather than a failed build ever.

**3. Report it.** Every build carries `status.cache` — `enabled`, `warm`, `ref`, `mode`, `message` — surfaced in the API's build view, next to the duration on the build page, in `kitchen deploy`'s result line, and on the commit status: *"image built and pushed in 4m12s, cache cold"*.

There is deliberately no hit rate and no "time saved". Neither BuildKit nor the lifecycle reports how many layers it reused, and the counterfactual is not measurable, so claiming a number would be inventing one. What a cold build actually needs is to say it had nothing to reuse, so that a slow first build does not read as a regression — that is what warm/cold does.

**4. Bound it.** The default scope is bounded without anything having to prune it: one tag per project, overwritten in place, so what grows is the unreferenced blobs underneath, which the bundled registry (zot) reclaims while running. `scope: branch` is explicitly not bounded — one tag per branch that ever built, which nothing removes — and is documented as the setting to weigh against the registry's own retention.

## The decision the issue left open

**Point 2, a persistent BuildKit `StatefulSet` with a PVC: not taken.** It would be faster still, and `docs/SCOPE.md` does remove the isolation objection. But it makes the platform stateful, needs a garbage-collection policy of its own, and pins builds to whichever node holds the volume. The registry cache needs none of that and is the option `SCOPE.md` names. Written down in `SCOPE.md` as a decision rather than left as an assumption, so it can be revisited with the reason in view.

## Interface surfaces

Per `CLAUDE.md`, no route was added, renamed, or had its requirement changed — the build view gained a field. The CLI mirrors it in its `build` type so `--json` stays complete, and `kitchen deploy` prints warm/cold on the result line. The dashboard shows it under the build's duration. The three settings are platform-wide alongside `defaultStrategy` and `concurrency`, so they are chart values, deliberately and documented.

## Checks

`make test` (including new envtest cases and unit tests for the ref, the slug, and both builders' flags), `make lint`, `helm lint` and a full `helm template` with the CI value sets, `npm run build` and `npm test` for the dashboard. Generated CRDs and chart templates regenerated with `make manifests helm-manifests`.

author: lost-conn
body:
Fixes edits silently not persisting on any book that is **not** cut over, when sync is on. Regression from #22.

## What broke

#22 enforced the single-writer rule on the client alone: a body that was syncing got no REST write. That is correct for a cut-over book — the canonical document is the truth there and the REST snapshot is a stale duplicate that reinstates deleted text.

It is wrong for every other book, and every other book is the default:

- sync pushes the edit into the canonical store
- the REST write that would have put it in git is suppressed
- nothing mirrors canonical → git (mirroring is cut-over only)
- the read comes from git, which never got it

The writing goes somewhere real and the reading looks somewhere else. Reported as *"my edits aren't sticking."*

## Why it isn't just a missing `if`

Neither side of the wire knows enough to decide alone:

- **The client** knows whether it is syncing a given document. It does *not* know whether the book is cut over — that's server env config, and anything it cached could be stale by a restart.
- **The server** knows whether the book is cut over. It does *not* reliably know whether this client syncs — keying off the stored `synced_at` would drop writes from a client that has since turned sync off, because that flag never clears.

Deciding with the client's half alone is the bug above. Deciding with the server's half alone is a worse one: silent loss with no way for the user to turn it off.

So **the client declares and the server decides.** `sync_owned` rides on the update request as a statement of fact — "sync is carrying this body" — and the server honours it only where the book is cut over, evaluating that at request time. The authoritative bit is checked where it is authoritative; a stale client cannot cause loss, and a client that stops syncing resumes writing immediately.

Titles and note colours are never covered: they are structure, and sync does not carry them.

Also picked up a third body-write site (a flush path) that the original fix had missed entirely.

## Tests

**Server** (`tests/cutover.rs`):
- `sync_owned` is honoured for a cut-over book — the stale snapshot reaches neither git nor the canonical copy, *and the two still agree*, since writing one alone locks the document on the next read
- `sync_owned` is ignored for a book that isn't cut over — the regression, directly
- it never covers a title or a note colour

**e2e** (`sync-single-writer.spec.ts`, rewritten):
- sync on, book not cut over → the edit survives a reload (this is today's bug, and the e2e server cuts nothing over, so it's exactly that configuration)
- sync on → the body write still carries `sync_owned: true`, so the server has something to decide with (guards the original #22 bug from coming back)
- sync off → the write is sent and explicitly does not claim ownership

Full e2e **34/34**. `cargo test --workspace` green across 27 binaries. Both frontend targets build.

author: kunboruto20
body:
Adds the three things a library needs before anyone will build on it: published types, a test suite, and CI. No runtime file is touched — `lib/`, `index.js` and `cli.js` are byte-identical to `main`.

## 1. TypeScript declarations (`index.d.ts`)

Derived from `lib/`, not from the README.

- **All 82 runtime exports are declared.** Verified by diffing the declared names against `Object.keys(require('./index.js'))` in *both* directions, so there are no phantom declarations promising something the runtime lacks — the kind that type-checks and then throws.
- **~110 client methods** carry real parameter and return types: `send*` resolve to `{ id, status }`, `sendPoll` adds `encKey`, the app-state calls (`pinChat`, `archiveChat`, `muteChat`, `starMessage`, `markChatRead`) return the boolean saying whether the change reached app state, and the group calls return `GroupParticipantResult[]` with its `ok` / `needsInvite` getters.
- **Events are a typed map**, so `client.on('conected', …)` is a compile error and each payload has its real shape.
- **`package.json` gains `"types"` and lists `index.d.ts` under `"files"`** — without the second, the file sits in git and never reaches the published tarball.

Things the audit turned up in the code itself:

- The `message` event is emitted in **three different shapes**. The plaintext-body variant carries `text` and no `decoded`; the group variant adds `isGroup`. `decoded` is therefore optional, not assumed present — code doing `msg.decoded.type` without a guard can crash on the first variant.
- Four methods were initially typed as always returning a value when they can resolve `null`: `changeProfilePicture`, `changeGroupPicture`, `getGroupMetadata`, `queryGroupInviteInfo`. `const id: string = await client.changeProfilePicture(buf)` used to compile and hand back `null`.
- The binary store fields (`deviceId`, `identityId`, `backupToken`, `advIdentity`) were declared `string`. They are `Buffer`s in memory; the base64 strings in the README's example JSON are the *serialized* form that `saveStore` writes. `loadStore` restores Buffers, so the in-memory interface says Buffer and a doc comment spells out the difference.
- `encryptMedia` was declared with two parameters. It takes `(plaintext, mediaKey, keyName)` and returns `{ encrypted, sha256Plain, sha256Enc, mediaKey }`, now typed as `EncryptedMedia`.

Signal, WAM and protobuf internals are typed `any` on purpose. Their surfaces are large and internal, and a plausible-looking wrong signature is worse than no type; the reason is written into the file.

## 2. Test suite — 119 tests

Built on `node:test`, so the suite **adds no dependency of its own** and `npm test` runs with only the runtime deps installed. This is verified in CI by installing with `--omit=dev`.

| File | Tests | What it pins down |
|---|---|---|
| `reachout-timelock` | 11 | `"0"` as an expiry means "not reported", not 1970; hours are not wrapped at 24; unknown enforcement types fall back to `DEFAULT` |
| `group-participant` | 16 | `error="0"` is a success; a 403 with an `add_request` is invitable; LID and phone addressing both resolve; results still stringify to a bare JID |
| `session-paths` | 15 | Both on-disk layouts against a real temp dir; an existing loose session is never implicitly relocated; `migrateSession` moves pre-keys, never overwrites, and is safe to re-run |
| `store` | 18 | Display-name rules (trim, collapse, 25-char cap, `"User"` is a placeholder); a disk round-trip proving keys return as `Buffer`s byte for byte |
| `media-crypto` | 14 | Encrypt/decrypt round-trip; tamper and truncation both rejected; the key-name mapping — a sticker is keyed as an image, a voice note as audio |
| `auth-utils` | 21 | Cache semantics including that a miss is deliberately **not** cached; records returned by reference so a `SessionRecord` keeps its methods; transactions buffer, see their own writes, roll back on throw, and nest without committing early |
| `jid-and-pairing` | 14 | JID normalisation leaves group/LID/newsletter addresses untouched; the pairing code is 8 chars from a 32-symbol alphabet with the confusables removed |
| `public-api` | 10 | The guard tying `index.d.ts` to `index.js` in both directions |

The tests check documented behaviour, not that functions exist. Example: a GIF encrypted with the image info string downloads fine and decrypts to garbage — there is a test for exactly that.

The drift guard was **verified to be able to fail**, by breaking it deliberately in both directions (a phantom declaration, and an export with its declaration renamed) and confirming each is caught.

## 3. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

| Job | Does |
|---|---|
| `test` | Node 18 / 20 / 22, installed `--omit=dev` to prove the suite needs no devDeps |
| `types` | `tsc --strict` over `index.d.ts` |
| `package` | Unpacks the tarball and fails if `index.d.ts` is missing or if test files leaked in |

All three were simulated locally before pushing. `npm install` rather than `npm ci`, since no lockfile is committed. `actions/checkout` runs with `persist-credentials: false` — no job pushes.

## 4. README / Brasil.md

The `[!CAUTION]` block saying the library "needs to be rewritten" and "is in testing" is replaced by a `[!NOTE]` framed as active development. The facts are kept — the mobile protocol changed, pull requests are accepted — without reading as a warning against using the library. Applied to both files so they stay in sync; CI and types badges added to both.

Checked after the edit: 322 headings and 568 code fences in each, **zero broken internal links**.

## CI status on this PR

The workflow itself is valid — GitHub created all five jobs and expanded the matrix correctly — but no runner was ever assigned: `runner_id: 0`, no logs, and `total_ms: 0` billable on every job across two separate runs. That is an account-level Actions block, not a defect in this diff. The suite passes locally on every commit here.

## Known issues this surfaces (not fixed here)

- **`engines: ">=14.0.0"` is not accurate.** `@cacheable/node-cache` declares `>=22` and uses `structuredClone`, which lands in Node 17. Node 14 and 16 cannot run this package regardless of what the field says. Bumping it changes who npm lets install, so it is left as a decision — `>=18` matches this code, `>=22` matches the dependency.
- **Two README examples are wrong.** The media-retry snippet reads `msg.key.id`, but the emitted message object has no `key` — the fields are `id`, `from`, `participant`. And `saveStore(result.store, …)` assumes `.store` is always present; `cli.js` itself uses `r.store || store`.
- `Brasil.md` is not in the npm tarball. The link from the README is an absolute GitHub URL so it works from npm either way; including it would add ~209 KB to every install.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 119/119 pass, ~0.6 s
- `npm run test:types` — clean under `--strict`
- Realistic consumer file compiles; a file of deliberate mistakes is rejected on every line
- Works for both `import` and `require` consumers
- `npm pack` carries `index.d.ts` and excludes `test/`
- `require('./index.js')` still loads, 82 exports

author: scottrbk
body:
## Sample-Site Process Activation

Turns the dormant sample-site scripts into a registered Dark Orchestrator
**Process** that an operator runs on demand — without changing the existing
atomic claim, BuildFailed, idempotency, one-correction, or privacy contracts.

### Reference docs
- Requirements: [`docs/requirements/sample_site_process_activation.md`](docs/requirements/sample_site_process_activation.md)
- ADR-006: [`docs/architecture/adr/adr6_sample_site_process_activation.md`](docs/architecture/adr/adr6_sample_site_process_activation.md)
- Architecture: [`docs/architecture/architecture.md`](docs/architecture/architecture.md)
- Active plan: [`docs/plans/active/sample-site-process-activation.md`](docs/plans/active/sample-site-process-activation.md)
- Related: ADR-004 (CRM claim), ADR-005 (static website generation)

### What changed
- **Explicit model CLI (Slice A).** `processes/run_sample_site_builder.py`
  now *requires* `--model` and *accepts* optional `--effort` (default
  `high`). It builds one `GenerationAgents` profile with `AgentType.PI` for
  the designer, builder, reviewer, and QA roles from that single model +
  effort (the model is data, never a shell command). No repository-selected
  model/profile is hardcoded. Missing `--model` still fails closed before any
  CRM read, workspace creation, or agent effect.
- **`build_next` Process (Slice B).** New `processes/build_next_sample_site.py`
  is the operator-facing Python Host-file Process. It validates `--config`,
  `--workspace-root`, `--model`, optional `--effort` (default `high`), and
  optional `--builder-timeout` (default **10,500**) *before* any effect, then
  builds a trusted argv **list**
  `[sys.executable, sibling run_sample_site_builder.py, "--config", ..., "--workspace-root", ..., "--model", ..., "--effort", ...]`
  and calls the existing `claim_new_lead.run(...)`. No `shlex`, no
  `shell=True`, no command string, no duplicated claim logic. Claims the
  oldest eligible New + SalesBrief Lead, builds one site, exits. Unchanged
  failure semantics: adapter-primary BuildFailed + claim safety-net replay,
  idempotent duplicates, one bounded correction, non-secret output.
- **10,500 / 10,800 decision.** The process default inner builder timeout is
  **10,500s**, strictly below the intended Orchestrator outer timeout of
  **10,800s** (`DARK_ORCH_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10800`, set by the operator
  before server start; stock default 900s). The 300s margin lets a timed-out
  builder be terminated and reported truthfully before the outer kill. These
  limits must never be set equal; CRM config does not set the server timeout.
- **Safe workspace / config boundaries.** `--workspace-root` must be an
  absolute path resolved outside this checkout (empty, relative, in-repo, and
  in-repo-symlink paths fail closed with `workspace root is invalid`). The
  private CRM config path stays outside Git; `ClaimProcessError` is mapped to
  one generic `claim process failed` outcome so private config paths cannot
  leak. Loopback `base_url` enforcement and no-redirect / no-proxy behaviour
  are unchanged.

### QA / gates
- **Isolated browser QA: PASS** (not the live CRM/model gate). Enabled Python
  Host-file Process created; one future-scheduled 8-token Job produced zero
  runs before Run now; Run now once produced exactly one completed
  no-candidate run; fake CRM issued exactly one bounded `GET
  /api/leads/byStatus` (no claim/failure, no workspace/builder/model);
  captured output safe/non-secret; outer 10,800 / inner default 10,500; no
  recurrence, deploy, preview, ReadyForEmail, or email.
- **No automatic registration / schedule / deploy / email.** This change
  registers no Process, Job, or schedule and does not deploy, persist a URL,
  or set ReadyForEmail. The operator creates the Process and Job in the UI.
- **Real CRM/model invocation deferred by user choice.** Per the active plan,
  the user chose to perform the one real CRM/model operator E2E invocation
  **post-merge** (explicit go-ahead gate). It has **not** been run here; the
  isolated QA above is the only QA evidence in this PR.

### Test evidence
- **Focused process suite: 379 passed** (verified locally via
  `pytest tests/processes`; the Slice B checkpoint recorded 377, Slice C
  added the final 2 before this PR).
- **Broad suite: 412 collected/passed excluding the known env-only failure
  `tests/test_frontend_serving.py`** (absent generated `web/dist`). Full broad
  = 412 + exactly that one environment-only failure.
- **Isolated UI QA: PASS** (Playwright-style operator journey recorded in the
  plan; fake CRM, patched agents, no live tokens).

### Out of scope / unchanged
No package, dependency, or schema changes. No direct database access from the
process. Private CRM config and retained workspace remain outside Git.

### Notes
Branch `feature/sample-site-process-activation` at `90a8fba`, clean, all
commits authored/committed by Scott (no co-author). Ahead of `origin/main` by
4 commits, zero behind, no divergence. Plan is intentionally left **open**
(active) — real CRM/model E2E remains an explicit post-merge operator gate;
this PR is not merged.

body:
## Summary
- Fixes #685: \`_update_shadow_engine_diagnostic()\` logged a WARNING the instant any of 6 comparison axes disagreed, even when the mismatch was a momentary artifact of a real multi-step production transition. Confirmed via live log evidence: a single real cascade hit 4 axes and resolved within 11.71s, with duplicate log lines firing 1-2ms apart. This noise erodes trust in the signal epic #594 Phase R depends on to gate any future switchover to authoritative FSM control.
- Adds a **wall-clock time-based** debounce (proven necessary over a naive count-based approach — the 1-2ms duplicate timing would trip a snapshot counter before a cascade even finishes): a WARNING now only fires once a disagreement has persisted 60+ continuous seconds, applied uniformly to all 6 comparison axes.
- Threshold justified with real margin on both sides: 5x above the largest observed cascade (11.71s), 9-20x below both a confirmed real sustained mismatch (522s) and the historical #676 case (1200s+) — genuinely stuck cases still surface within ~1 minute of onset, not masked.
- Purely additive to \`_shadow_engine_diagnostic\`'s schema (new \`debounce\` sub-dict + \`cumulative_reset_date\` key) — no existing key changed, so \`sensor.py\`'s only consumer needs zero changes to keep working.
- Diagnostic-only. No production HVAC/fan/grace/override logic touched.
- Part of epic #594 Phase R (Phase 0d in the consolidated plan).

## Test plan
- [x] 4 pre-existing "disagreement logs warning" tests updated to seed a past-threshold disagreement streak, preserving original intent (persistent divergence still logs)
- [x] 4 new regression tests proving a *fresh* single-tick disagreement does NOT log, independently revert-verified by a separate Verification agent (reverting the gate condition made the new tests fail with the exact WARNING leaking through)
