author: m-jerez
body:
## What broke

The [website deploy](https://github.com/MionKit/ts-run-types/actions/runs/32305306661) failed in the `Build binary + benchmarks + static site` step:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
    at readLane (scripts/website/bench-data/gen-docs.mjs:363)
```

`rtx website build` runs the cross-library alignment audit (`cmdAudit`) immediately before `gen-docs`, and that audit writes `results/<competitor>.alignment.json` next to the per-competitor timing results. `buildValidationBench` filtered those out by name; the strict bench's `readLane` (added in 31f88d0b with the bun lane) carried its OWN copy of that blocklist and never learned about `.alignment.json`. It parsed `ajv.alignment.json` as a timing result, found no `cases` array, and died — a red deploy after ~30 minutes of build work.

## What changed

- **`scripts/website/bench-data/gen-docs.mjs`** — both readers now go through one `readCompetitorResults(dir)` that filters on SHAPE (`competitor` string + `cases` array), the same approach `container/benchmarks/aggregate.mjs` already took after the same class of bug, and names what it skipped so a genuinely malformed competitor file surfaces instead of vanishing. The one artifact shape cannot rule out is `<competitor>.spec.json` (removed spec-conformance lane: it carries both fields and would overwrite a real timing row), so that stays an explicit name exclusion.
- **`container/benchmarks/aggregate.mjs`** — same `.spec.json` exclusion, closing the identical latent hole there.
- **`packages/ts-runtypes-devtools/test/bench-lane-contracts.test.ts`** — contract tests for the new reader: it keeps only the competitor results out of a dir holding `env.json` / `.alignment.json` / `alignment-misalignments.json` / `.typecost.json` / `.compiletime.json` / `transform-wire.json` / `.spec.json` / malformed JSON; it returns nothing for an absent lane dir (the bun subdir under `RT_BENCH_BUN=0`); and there is exactly ONE results-directory reader in the file, so a second blocklist cannot drift back in.
- **`container/website/app/data/test-counts.json`** — regenerated by the build (the committed copy had drifted behind main).

## Verification

Every step of `website-deploy.yml` was run locally on macOS/arm64, except the Cloudflare deploy itself (production secrets) and the GitHub-only artifact upload:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `release verify-live` | PASS (all 3 packages live at v0.12.0) |
| pull shared image | local image matches the published digest |
| `pnpm rtx website build --quick` | **PASS** — the audit wrote its `.alignment.json` files and gen-docs skipped all 7 non-competitor artifacts |
| `pnpm rtx website check --static` | PASS, 9/9 benchmark pages render (`/benchmarks/strict` included) |
| `pnpm rtx bench engine-check` | OK, counter inversion holds on node + bun |

Repo gates: `pnpm test` 9338 passed / 8 skipped, `pnpm run lint` clean, `pnpm run format` clean.

Note: the local benchmark run used `--quick` (short timing windows, typia skipped), so the measured numbers are noisy — that affects values only, not the code path that failed.

author: fdsimms
body:
Photograph a store receipt and it checks the matching rows off your list, records what each cost, and files the trip against the store.

All three of those were already recordable by hand in the finish sheet, and in practice the prices never were — a per-row price for a forty-row shop is more typing than anyone does while unpacking bags. The receipt already has all of it.

**No schema change.** `finishShopping(shopId, priceById)` already took a price map, so this needed no column, no migration and no new store action.

## How it's split

`extractReceipt` reads the paper — store name, the line exactly as printed, a plain-English reading of it, quantity, price — and decides nothing. `receiptMatch.ts` is offline, pure and tested, and owns every judgement that decides what gets written.

Asking the model for the plain-English name rather than expanding abbreviations offline is the load-bearing choice: a receipt's shorthand is store-specific, unbounded and drifts, so a lexicon of it would be a guess-machine we'd maintain forever. A vision model is already reading the page and is good at exactly this. Prices go through `parsePriceInput`, the same reader a hand-typed price uses, so a discount line's negative and a garbled amount are refusals here for the reasons they're refusals there.

## What keeps it safe

Three confidence tiers, and what separates them is what arrives **pre-checked**:

| Tier | Example | Arrives |
|---|---|---|
| `exact` | list "Milk" ← `GV MLK 2% GAL` | checked |
| `likely` | list "Chicken" ← `chicken breast` | checked |
| `weak` | list "Chicken thighs" ← `chicken breast` | shown, flagged, **unchecked** |

An unchecked row saying "Not sure this is the same thing" is a question; a pre-checked one is an assertion. Getting that backwards is how someone ends up having marked chicken thighs bought because the receipt said breast — and the thing on the other side of the confirm is `finishShopping`, which takes the whole list off in one pass.

**A receipt is evidence of a purchase, never of an absence.** Nothing here ever writes an `unavailableAt`, and list rows the receipt never named are left exactly where they are. Same call the finish sheet already makes about an unticked leftover: the usual reason something is missing is that you didn't get to it.

Two lines reading as the same row are surfaced rather than summed — two "MILK 3.48" lines is someone who bought two, and adding them into one 6.96 puts a number on the row that no line of the receipt says and that `lastPriceQuantity` has no way to qualify.

## The price check is really a matching check

A line four times off what the item last cost is almost never inflation or a sale — it's the line having been read onto the wrong row. That makes price the one piece of evidence available from a completely different direction than name similarity, so it catches the failure the tiers structurally cannot: a wrong match whose *name* reads perfectly.

It's only trustworthy because it refuses so much. Prices are compared **per unit** whenever both sides name a measurable amount, and refused outright when they can't be reconciled — one side qualified and the other bare, or two different dimensions. Same all-or-nothing rule `unitPricesFor` follows: a comparison that quietly drops the part it couldn't read is worse than no comparison. An item nobody has priced says nothing at all.

The 4x threshold is deliberately blunt. Sales take a third off, a year of inflation adds a fifth, and the big pack doubles the line outright — anything tight enough to catch those would fire on most of a normal receipt, and a check that cries wolf gets tapped past.

A **quantity** mismatch is shown too but deliberately does *not* demote the row: coming home with 1 lb when the list asked for 3 lb is an ordinary thing that happened, and the row is still the right row. The two treatments differ visually to match — the price caution is orange and takes the tick away, the quantity note is quiet and keeps it.

A **live tally** states what the checked rows come to against the receipt's printed total. Nothing reconciles the two and nothing should — tax, deposits and everything not on the list are real parts of that number — but stating the gap makes a large one visible to the only reader who can judge it.

## It fills the finish sheet in; it doesn't replace it

The confirm ticks the rows and opens `FinishShoppingSheet` with the store and prices already filled, so the trip still ends where it always has. A receipt can't answer which of the leftovers the store didn't have, and that question is that sheet's whole second half — ending the trip from here would either skip it or duplicate it.

## Notable decisions

- **`acceptedByDefault` owns "what arrives checked"**, rather than a field on the match result. That was fine while the answer depended only on the name; the price check depends on which store you say you were at, so it changes under a store picked after the fact, and two places computing it is how the checkbox and the caption would come to disagree about one row.
- **Receipt scanning defaults to Sonnet**, not the app-wide default. It's the hardest read in the app — faded thermal print in store shorthand that has to be *understood* rather than transcribed — and the most expensive to get wrong, against a couple of cents a trip. Still per-feature switchable.
- **Store matching compares on a space-closed key**, so the user's "Trader Joe's" meets a receipt's "TRADER JOES" — `groceryNameKey` turns an apostrophe into a space, and possessive store names are the normal case rather than an edge one. It refuses an unrecognized name rather than picking the nearest: a wrong store files a whole trip's prices against somewhere you never went, and `ItemShopLink` is exactly the record with no way to notice that later.
- The recipe photo pipeline is reused as-is (no base64 out of the picker, unconditional JPEG re-encode for HEIC).

## Merge with main

Main's recipe-from-a-link work landed on the same three files. `RecipeSourcePicker` gained a Link tab while this branch gave it a photo-only mode — they layer, but `photoOnly` now suppresses two text modes instead of one, so both are read through locals that account for it. And `useRecipePhotoSource` was **deleted** on main in favor of `useRecipeImportSource`; this branch's only change to it (parameterizing the camera-denial copy) moved across.

Also fixes a duplicate `extraTaskDraft` key in `dayLoad.test.ts`'s fixture that **arrived from main**, not from this branch. CI runs `npm test` and `expo export` but not `tsc`, and Jest is happy with a duplicate object key (last wins, both values `null`) — so it merged green while `npx tsc --noEmit` was red. One line, and it blocks this branch's typecheck.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit && npm test` — **152 suites, 6141 tests green.** 41 tests in `receiptMatch.test.ts` cover the tiers, claim/duplicate resolution, tie-break stability, store matching, every caution refusal, and the store-dependent re-decision.

No component tests exist (Jest runs in `node` with no renderer), so the review sheet was checked against a 390pt HTML mock built from the real `src/theme/index.ts` values, in both themes. That proves the layout numbers and the visual hierarchy and nothing else — no Yoga, no gestures, no `SwipeableRow`.

No demo seed row: the feature adds no new persisted shape, and `demoSeed.ts` already seeds priced trips through `finishShopping` — the exact shape a scan produces.

## Scope decisions, filed rather than described

- #1805 — off-list receipt lines are ignored, so an impulse buy's price is read and thrown away
- #1806 — the trip is stamped now rather than the receipt's own date, which matters most for shelf-life days
- #1810 — receipts are downscaled to a ceiling chosen for cookbook pages, which is a harsher cut for something long and thin

author: stxkxs
body:
`npm run schemas:freshness` exits 2 to mean "the pin is behind" — a verdict the
steps below turn into a filed drift issue carrying the report and the re-vendor
command. That verdict never reached them.

GitHub invokes a `run:` block as `bash -e {0}`, so errexit is already on when
the script starts, and `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it. A bare invocation
exiting 2 terminated the step at that line, before `code=$?` executed. With the
output unset, every `if: steps.freshness.outputs.code == ...` step below was
skipped — no issue filed, no report, no remediation text, only a red run whose
log ends at the command that produced the answer. A check that reports "behind"
and nothing else is the one a reader consults instead of checking whether the
mechanism works.

Initialising `code=0` and capturing through `|| code=$?` puts the command on the
left of a `||` list, which errexit exempts, so a 2 is captured rather than
fatal. The job still fails while the pin is behind; the drift issue is filed
alongside it.

author: molinajonyy-hub
body:
Follow-up de UX del bloque W1, salido del smoke owner en producción. Dos ajustes acotados. **Sin migraciones, sin tocar RLS, sin tocar Cloud API backend, sin tocar plantillas.**

---

## 1 · Fuera el módulo Cloud API del sidebar

El item **WhatsApp** llevaba a `/whatsapp`, que es la pantalla del módulo Cloud API (conexión con Meta, API oficial no conectada, automatizaciones). En el flujo Standard no se usa y confunde.

Se retira **sólo el item de navegación**. Quedan intactos: la ruta, la pantalla, los componentes, los servicios, las Edge Functions y las tablas.

Único efecto colateral: `WhatsAppIcon` queda sin usar y `noUnusedLocals` lo rechazaría, así que se va con el item. Se conservan el flag `isWhatsApp` del tipo `NavItem` y su CSS — si el módulo Cloud API vuelve a ofrecerse, el estilo sigue ahí.

**Las plantillas Standard se siguen editando en Configuración → WhatsApp**, que no depende del sidebar. Un E2E lo fija, y de paso comprueba que `/whatsapp` sigue respondiendo.

## 2 · Una sola pestaña, reutilizada

**Síntoma en producción:** “Abrir WhatsApp” terminaba en `api.whatsapp.com/send` — la pantalla intermedia (“Abrir aplicación” / “Continuar en WhatsApp Web”). Ese paso extra era el que estrenaba pestañas: al elegir “Continuar en WhatsApp Web” el navegador abría una nueva, fuera del nombre de ventana que fija el módulo.

**Causa:** en desktop se usaba `wa.me`, que **redirige** a esa intermedia.

**Arreglo — handoff por plataforma:**

| | URL | por qué |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | `https://web.whatsapp.com/send?phone=<dígitos>&text=<encoded>` | directo, sin intermedia; navega **dentro** de la pestaña ya abierta |
| Móvil | `https://wa.me/<dígitos>?text=<encoded>` | es el que deja al sistema abrir la **app nativa**; forzar WhatsApp Web en un teléfono sería peor |

La detección de plataforma **no es nueva**: se reutiliza `isMobileDevice()` de `whatsappFormat`, y se hace inyectable para testear ambas ramas sin tocar el user-agent. Sin UA hacks.

**Target estable:** `techrepair_whatsapp`, sin `noopener` (con él el navegador ignora el nombre y estrena pestaña).

- 1er handoff → crea la pestaña.
- 2º y siguientes → el navegador la encuentra **por nombre** y navega esa misma, aunque cambien cliente, teléfono y mensaje.
- Si el usuario la cerró → `window.open` la vuelve a crear, sin ruido.

**`focus()` best-effort:** si el navegador devuelve una referencia cross-origin donde `focus` no existe o lanza, la apertura sigue siendo válida. Sin polling, sin referencias globales.

**Límite honesto, documentado en el código:** no se promete adoptar una pestaña de WhatsApp Web que el usuario haya abierto por su cuenta. El navegador no deja enumerar pestañas ajenas; sólo responde al nombre que fijó esta app.

## Lo que NO cambia

- **Un solo `encodeURIComponent`**: `preview === decodeURIComponent(text)`. Sin `%250A`.
- El click sigue registrando **`opened`**. Reutilizar pestaña no es enviar. Nunca `sent`/`delivered`/`read`.
- **Cero Cloud API** en el camino Standard.

## Tests

- **+11 unitarios**: las dos ramas, ausencia de `api.whatsapp.com`, encoding sin doblar, **tres handoffs seguidos con el mismo target y URLs distintas**, `focus` tolerante a null y a excepción.
- **+1 de componentes**: dos mensajes consecutivos reutilizan la pestaña.
- **E2E**: caso nuevo de sidebar; y el vertical ahora verifica hostname `web.whatsapp.com`, target estable, **segundo handoff sobre la misma pestaña**, y ausencia de `api.whatsapp.com` y de `_blank`.
- **Guard**: checks nuevos de `web.whatsapp.com` y de `api.whatsapp.com`.

**Verificado que no es vacuo**: al volver desktop a `wa.me` fallan las **tres capas** (2 unitarios, 2 de componentes, 1 E2E).

## Validación

| Gate | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 |
| `lint:errors` | 0 |
| `build` | OK |
| `test:unit` | **928/928** (+11) |
| `test:components` | **308/308** (+1) |
| `guards` (agregado) | OK |
| `guard:whatsapp-w1 --self-test` | **59/59** |
| E2E `m7-local` | **69/69** (+1) |

## Nota sobre la evidencia visual

Correr los specs `@visual` regeneró los PNG de `tests/e2e/evidencia/`, y varios incluyen el sidebar — o sea que la evidencia trackeada todavía muestra el item “WhatsApp” que este PR retira. **No se commitean**: `guard:visual-evidence` existe justamente para que la evidencia no se regrabe sola, y regrabarla es una acción deliberada (`npm run e2e:m7:evidencia`). Queda como decisión aparte.

body:
Telegram: N/A | Nickname: N/A
Powered by LingTai AI: https://github.com/Lingtai-AI/lingtai

## Problem

Every registered tool's canonical prose is rendered onto **two** model-facing surfaces in the same turn, from the same source string:

1. the resident `## tools` section of the composed system prompt — `_refresh_tool_inventory_section()` (`src/lingtai/kernel/base_agent/tools.py`), called on every `_build_system_prompt` / `_build_system_prompt_batches` (`base_agent/prompt.py:30`, `:49`);
2. the tool-calling schema's top-level `description` — `_build_tool_schemas()` reads the *same* `module.get_description()` (`base_agent/tools.py:101-107`).

`WIRE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION` already deduplicated this for the API adapters by replacing their wire description with a pointer at the section. But `claude_code` and `kimi_code` have no wire tools array and were deliberately excluded (`src/lingtai/llm/ANATOMY.md:125`) — and those are exactly the adapters where both copies land **in the same cached system block**:

```python
# src/lingtai/llm/claude_code/adapter.py:576-597
parts.append("# AGENT SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS")
parts.append(self._system_prompt or "(none)")   # contains "## tools"        (copy 1)
parts.append("# AVAILABLE TOOLS")
for t in self._tools:
    if t.description:
        parts.append(t.description.strip())      # the identical prose        (copy 2)
```

Verified byte-identical on a booted agent: the `### email` entry in `## tools` and `FunctionSchema.description` for `email` are the same 826-character string, both from `src/lingtai/tools/email/schema.py:20-21`.

**Measured on a live 18-tool `wen` agent running `provider: claude-code`: 27,735 of 190,159 characters — 14.6% of the composed system prompt — were the duplicate.** Projected to ~30 tools: ≈35k–46k characters ≈ 9k–26k tokens, resident on every turn.

## Change

New environment variable **`LINGTAI_TOOL_PROSE_SECTION_ENABLED`**, **default off**, named and parsed like the existing kernel opt-ins `LINGTAI_RISKY_ACTION_GATE` (`kernel/risky_action_gate.py:311-323`) and `LINGTAI_SOUL_FLOW_ENABLED` (`tools/soul/flow.py:20-44`) — `{1, true, yes, on}`, case-insensitive, default closed.

| | default (unset/falsey) | opted in (truthy) |
|---|---|---|
| `## tools` section | not rendered; any live copy deleted | rendered, unchanged (incl. glossary bodies) |
| provider wire top-level description | full `FunctionSchema.description` | `WIRE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION` pointer |
| nested parameter/property descriptions | untouched | untouched |
| `ChatInterface` tool snapshots | full prose | full prose |

Three edits:

- `kernel/config.py:139-181` — the gate (`TOOL_PROSE_SECTION_ENABLED_ENV`, `tool_prose_section_enabled()`), read live at every use so an `env_file` flip applies at the next rebuild without a restart.
- `kernel/base_agent/tools.py:73-75` — `_refresh_tool_inventory_section()` short-circuits and *deletes* any existing `tools` section, so flipping the switch off and rebuilding actually drops it.
- `kernel/llm/base.py:191-211` — new `wire_tool_description(description)`; the four wire builders in openai/anthropic/gemini call it instead of hardcoding the constant.

### Why the third edit is required, not scope creep

Gating the section alone would strand every API-backed agent: their wire carries `WIRE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION` — *"See the system prompt for tool usage guidance."* — a pointer **at that section**. Remove the section and they are left with a dangling pointer and no top-level tool prose at all. `wire_tool_description()` makes the invariant **"each tool's prose reaches the model exactly once, on whichever surface survives"**, which is pinned by a test. This *adds* description text to those wires; nothing is shortened or degraded anywhere.

### Known trade-off

The package-owned localized glossary bodies (`glossary-{zh,wen}.md`, the 名相对照 mappings) are **section-only** content — 7,080 chars across the 14 first-party packages in `wen`. With the section off by default, `zh`/`wen` agents lose that terminology mapping. That is precisely why this is a switch rather than a deletion: a deployment that values the mapping sets the variable and pays the duplication knowingly.

## Tests

- **`tests/test_tool_prose_section_gate.py`** (new, 20 tests) — the switch's parsing (6 truthy / 8 falsey spellings, default off, re-read per call); then end-to-end on a real `Agent`: the default prompt has no `## tools` and no schema description in it, the opt-in prompt has both, removing the gated block from the opt-in prompt reproduces the default prompt **exactly**, the schemas are byte-identical in both states, and for every tool the prose appears in the system prompt **xor** on the wire — never both, never neither.
- **`tests/test_wire_tool_description.py`** — pinned to the opt-in state its pointer contract belongs to (autouse fixture), plus new default-state coverage across all four wire builders and the empty-description fallback.
- **`tests/test_tool_glossary.py`** — the "glossary body never reaches a provider wire" invariant is now parametrized over both gate states.

```
tests/test_tool_prose_section_gate.py                       20 passed
+ test_wire_tool_description.py + test_tool_glossary.py    212 passed, 1 failed
+ test_architecture_documents.py + test_docs_governance.py
+ test_kernel_isolation.py                                  76 passed, 3 failed
```

All 4 failures are **pre-existing on clean `main`** (verified by stashing the branch and re-running): `test_openai_responses_preserves_daemon_backend_options_passthrough_schema` (asserts `backend_options.properties == {"config"}`; main already has `{"config","env"}`), `test_every_tracked_file_climbs_the_anatomy_graph` (`kernel/llm/ANATOMY.md` lists `reasoning_effort.py` twice — a duplicate that predates this branch; reported rather than auto-normalized, per the dev guide), `test_every_in_scope_doc_has_required_fields` (`IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` + three `mcp_servers/feishu/reference/*.md` lack frontmatter), and `test_all_four_notification_managers_preserve_exact_runtime_body` (sha256 pin drift).

**Full suite, apples-to-apples against a clean `origin/main` worktree:**

```
branch  feat/opt-in-tool-prose-section    85 failed, 8,986 passed, 31 skipped, 4 errors   (14:48)
main    0e291ec8 (separate worktree)      85 failed, 8,963 passed, 31 skipped, 4 errors   (14:36)
```

Diffing the two failure sets (89 unique ids each) turned up exactly **one real regression**, now fixed in `0f69e555`:
`test_browser_capability.py::test_web_real_agent_startup_and_complete_prompt_build` asserted `"### web" in prompt` —
i.e. it asserted the prose section renders. It is now pinned to the opt-in state, with a new default-state twin proving
the capability is not lost (no `## tools` in the prompt, but `web` still in the schemas carrying its full description).
`tests/test_browser_capability.py`: 6 passed.

The only other set differences are order-dependent flakes, two in each direction —
`test_daemon_email_mcp.py::test_daemon_email_reaches_parents_own_mailbox` fails in the branch's full run but passes in
isolation; `test_retroactive_history_compaction.py::…compacts_history_before_backoff` and
`test_wheel_sidecar_smoke.py::test_native_wheel_ships_and_runs_sidecar` fail on `main` and pass on the branch.
**Net regressions after the fix: zero.** The +23 passing tests are this PR's new and expanded coverage.

The 85 shared failures are pre-existing on `main` and unrelated to this change (Windows shims, WeChat/Telegram/Feishu
network paths, sdist packaging, plus the doc-governance items above).

## Documentation

Per `dev-guide-skill/SKILL.md`, Anatomy/Contract updated in the same PR: `ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md` (canonical registry row; version 1.0.1 → 1.1.0), `kernel/ANATOMY.md`, `kernel/base_agent/ANATOMY.md`, `kernel/llm/ANATOMY.md`, `llm/ANATOMY.md`, `prompts/ANATOMY.md`, `prompts/tools/tools.yaml`, and the "Provider wire" clause in all ten `src/lingtai/tools/*/CONTRACT.md` files.

## Not in this PR

author: smaug123
body:
`O_TRUNC` and `SystemNative_FTruncate`, which #1080 left behind as two curated refusals. `FileMode.Create` and `FileMode.Truncate` got through their open after that change and landed on the second one, so the commonest BCL creation call reached a `failwith`.

Measured on macOS 26.6/APFS and Linux 6.18.5 arm64, the latter as both uid 0 and uid 1000. Almost everything is unanimous: the length is validated before the descriptor (a bad fd with a negative length is EINVAL, not EBADF); a read-only, directory, pipe, socket or event-port descriptor is EINVAL; extension zero-fills; `O_TRUNC` on a directory is EISDIR and beats EACCES; a refused open truncates nothing; a truncation leaves the description's offset exactly where it was.

## Two rules that do not fall out of the existing code

* **`O_TRUNC` adds the write permission bit** to whatever the access mode already demands, and is not confined to a write access mode: `open(f, O_RDONLY | O_TRUNC)` empties a writable file, while the same call on a 0444 file is EACCES. Nine mode/flag rows pin it.
* **A truncation that changes no bytes is still a truncation**: it stamps mtime and ctime and clears the set-ID bits, where a write of no bytes is a complete no-op that the caller short-circuits. `truncateFile` must not copy `writeFile`'s shape here.

## The one divergence

The set-ID bits, derived from the flavour rather than crashed on because both sides are measured on every shape. Linux clears `S_ISUID` whatever the execute bits say and `S_ISGID` only alongside `S_IXGRP`; Darwin clears nothing at all. That is isolated rather than inferred: in one process, on one file, a one-byte `write` takes `04755` to `0755` on macOS while `ftruncate` leaves it `04755`.

| mode | Linux uid 1000 | Linux uid 0 | macOS uid 501 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `04755` | `0755` | `4755` | `4755` |
| `04644` | `0644` | `4644` | `4644` |
| `02755` | `0755` | `2755` | `2755` |
| `02644` | `2644` | `2644` | `2644` |
| `06755` | `0755` | `6755` | `6755` |
| `01755` | `1755` | `1755` | `1755` |

## A claim on existing code that this falsifies

`PermissionBits.afterContentChangingWrite` refuses the `S_ISGID`-without-`S_IXGRP` shape, saying macOS "was not measurable, a non-root user being unable to set S_ISGID on a regular file at all", and tells a future implementer to measure as root. Both halves are wrong. The earlier probe failed only because a file created in `/tmp` inherits group `wheel` under BSD semantics and `chmod` refuses the bit for a group the caller is not in — `chgrp staff` first and it sets fine at uid 501. And measuring *as root* would have shown preservation and hidden the answer entirely.

Measured properly, the platforms diverge for writes too: Linux keeps `02644`, macOS strips it to `0644`. So the refusal is right to exist and only its explanation changes here. Making that function flavour-aware is a change to the **write** path and belongs in its own slice.

## Not in this slice

`SystemNative_GetFileSystemType`, which is still the one native between here and an unmodified `File.WriteAllBytes`; `SystemNative_FAllocate`; any EFBIG modelling (a length above `Array.MaxLength` is a loud refusal, matching `FileWriteRefusal.WouldExceedMaxLength`, because real kernels *succeed* sparsely there and the EFBIG threshold that does exist is per-filesystem).

body:
## Architecture direction change

The previous plan — `SYSTEM StaticGameRegistry` + `CreatorGameRegistry` composing into a `CompositeGameRegistry` (PR #59) — is discarded. PR #59 was **closed, not merged**; its branch is preserved.

New target architecture: OwOGG official games and user-published games converge on the **same** deployment model — D1 (identity/runtime) + B2 (canonical/bundle) + `/play/:slug` + `GameHost` + `IframeRuntime` + Game Bridge. The only remaining real difference between "official" and "user" is publisher/permission/review policy — never storage or deployment mechanism.

```
                  Game Platform
                       │
                RuntimeGameRegistry
                       │
             ┌─────────┴─────────┐
             │                   │
            D1                  B2
     identity/runtime       canonical/bundle
             │                   │
             └─────────┬─────────┘
                       │
                  GameDefinition
                       │
                  /play/:slug
                       │
                    GameHost
                       │
                 IframeRuntime
                       │
                  Game Bridge
```

This PR (**Unified Game Platform U-1**) builds only the provider-neutral **domain foundation** for that eventual model. It is explicitly **not** a runtime switch — zero production behavior changes.

## What's added

**`GamePublisher`** (`modules/game/domain/gamePublisher.ts`)
```ts
type GamePublisher = { type: "OWOGG" } | { type: "USER"; userId: number };
```
Deliberately not derivable from `displayName`/`creatorName` — a user could set their own display name to `"owogg"`, so official-game identification must never be a string comparison. `OWOGG` carries no id (a platform-asserted fact, not a lookup); `USER` carries the same relational `userId` `CreatorGameOwner` already has. Not wired into `GameDefinition`/`PublicGame`/D1/any route. Existing `GameOwner`/`SystemGameOwner`/`CreatorGameOwner` are untouched.

**`GameCanonicalDocument`** (`modules/game/domain/gameCanonicalDocument.ts`)

Provider-neutral "what the game is" schema meant to eventually subsume `CreatorGameCanonicalDocument` — which keeps working exactly as today, untouched by this PR.

- Common fields: `schemaVersion`, `slug`, `title`, `shortDescription`, `description`, `policy`, `presentation?`, `difficulty?`, `supportsReplay`, `catalog`, `updatedAt`.
- `policy` reuses existing semantics (`score: ScoreConfig | null`, `leaderboard`, `xpPerCompletion`, `requiresAuth`). `score: null` is explicit "no score", distinct from an unconfigured score policy.
- `catalog` is a discriminated union distinguishing metadata **shape**, not publisher:
  ```ts
  type GameCanonicalCatalog =
    | { type: "GENRE_MODE"; genre: string; mode: SandboxGameMode }
    | { type: "TAXONOMY"; categories; tags; modes; inputMethods; minPlayers; maxPlayers; thumbnail; accent?; estimatedRoundSeconds? };
  ```
  `GENRE_MODE ≠ USER`, `TAXONOMY ≠ OWOGG` — publisher authority belongs to D1 identity, not canonical shape. A future user-published game should be able to use `TAXONOMY` too.
- Strict parser/serializer at the same safety level as the existing Creator parser: rejects malformed JSON, unsupported `schemaVersion`, slug mismatch, unknown fields at every level, NaN/Infinity, invalid score direction, invalid presentation, invalid catalog discriminant, missing required fields, duplicate difficulty level ids. Decimal score bounds are never truncated.
- `gameCanonicalObjectKey(slug) → "game-definitions/<slug>/definition.json"` — a new, non-colliding B2 prefix (verified distinct from `creator-games/`, `games/`, `uploads/`, `official-games/`). **No real B2 object is moved or written by this PR.**

**`gameCanonicalMigration.ts`** — pure, lossless converters:
- `creatorCanonicalDocumentToGameCanonicalDocument`: Creator canonical → generic. `genre`/`mode` → `GENRE_MODE`. `supportsReplay` restated as the same `false` already asserted elsewhere for Creator games (not fabricated).
- `systemGameDefinitionToGameCanonicalDocument(definition, updatedAt)`: SYSTEM definition → generic. Taxonomy fields → `TAXONOMY`. `status` is deliberately never read. `updatedAt` is a **required caller-supplied argument**, never generated via `new Date()` internally — migration provenance is never hidden.

Nothing calls these converters yet.

**`GameCanonicalRepository` port** (`modules/game/ports/gameCanonicalRepository.ts`)
```ts
interface GameCanonicalRepository {
  findBySlug(slug: string): Promise<GameCanonicalDocument | null>;
  save(document: GameCanonicalDocument): Promise<void>;
  delete(slug: string): Promise<void>;
}
```
Provider-neutral, no B2 knowledge in core. No adapter, no container wiring, `CreatorGameDefinitionRepository` untouched.

## Architecture guard (Section 11)

Satisfied at the doc-comment level rather than a new checker rule — `gamePublisher.ts` and `gameCanonicalDocument.ts`'s own top doc comments already assert, in force: publisher authority is never a displayName comparison; `GameCanonicalDocument` carries no relational publisher `userId`; runtime/editorial lifecycle (`status`, review, visibility) stays outside canonical; the canonical document is a Game concept independent of SYSTEM/Creator storage method; the future standard runtime is D1+B2. `pnpm architecture:check` passes with 0 violations. No new lint rule added.

## Zero production behavior change

Untouched by this PR: `StaticGameRegistry`, `CreatorGameRegistry`, `ScoreUseCases`/`GameSettingsUseCases` registry resolution, `PublicGame` API, `/api/games`, `GameHost`, `CreatorGameHost`, `transitionalCreatorGameResolver`, `/play/:slug`, `/official-games/*`, D1 schema, B2 production data, `apps/api/src/container.ts`. No `CompositeGameRegistry`. No PR #59 code merged.

## Tests

44 new (5 `gamePublisher`, 23 `gameCanonicalDocument`, 16 `gameCanonicalMigration`). Full `@owogg/core` suite: **646/646 passing**.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @owogg/core test` — 646/646 ✅
- `pnpm --filter @owogg/core typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @owogg/api typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @owogg/web typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck:scripts` ✅
- `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing unrelated warnings only) ✅
- `pnpm architecture:check` — 10 rules, 0 violations ✅
- `pnpm registry:check` — 0 stale registries ✅
- `npx prettier --check` on all changed files ✅
- No manual browser E2E (production behavior unchanged, per task scope).

## Explicitly not done in this PR

`CompositeGameRegistry` not built; PR #59 not merged (closed, branch preserved); `StaticGameRegistry`/`CreatorGameRegistry` not touched or deleted; no B2 object moved; no ball-dodge or official-4-games production migration; no D1 schema change; no `sandbox_games` rename; no route deletion; no `GameHost`/`CreatorGameHost` merge; no Score API unification; no Game Session change for SYSTEM; no admin official-upload UI; no real `creatorName="owogg"` DB record created; next Stage not started.

**Do not merge** — this PR is presented for review/CI verification per task scope; it stops here pending explicit instruction to continue.
